Undertale is by far one of the greatest and most unique games I have ever played. In fact, it is so good that I decided to write a review for it right away; I have not even completed it yet. First off, I have to say that the game has an absolutely amazing soundtrack. Some of the music is so catchy that I simply cannot get it out of my head. The story is very immersive and full of humorous elements. The great thing about Undertale is that you are free to do as you please. The game does give you a basic idea of what you should do, but you don't have to follow the rules! You are presented with many choices, and it is entirely up to you how you decide to handle them. I have had a great time so far, and I know it will only get better from here.

Oh yes, the acclaimed DayZ.
This is everything you wanted in a survival game:
[Almost] real simulation, zombies all over, giant map (Chernarus from Arma 2), PVP, full customization of everything, no horrible things like "free user and paid user", very fluent and usefull crafting (crafted itens do make sense), you can use and combine itens as you like (like looking through an unattached gun scope as binoculars)... even opening a noodles can with an axe can spill it`s content and ruining the meal. Nice graphics quality (compared to games like WarZ or Infestation, or H1Z1) and a lot of other things...
And also everything you didn't wanted in a survival game:
Everything is lagged (Zombies hit you and you take the hit seconds after, players are full lagged - they sometimes teleport), superbugs everywhere, almost no vehicles, itens suddenly disappear from your inventory (ok til here, because it's in alpha), stucked gameplay and interaction, and the most frustrating game engine of all times - the Arma 2 engine. Doesn't matter wich videocard you got, it's gonna be 10 fps. No kidding. Unless you open some notepad file in the preferences folder and change the object view distance to almost at your feet. Are you inside a cabin? Doesn't matter, the engine will process every tree in a range of 5 miles, and the bloom/ occlusion effects are so rorribly computated that will fry your GPU. And for those problem there will be nothing to solve, even on the final release, because Arma 2 was also like that forever. Arma 3 was released 2 years ago, and this game (that's in alpha stage yet and apparently is gonna be forever) is using the old engine yet. I don't get it.

The developers are working reeeeeeally slowly on this game apparently. While H1Z1 is going to beta soon, this one is at 0.5 for a whole year by now. But I think that, until now, this is the very best zombie survival game in existance. I just hope that the developers do a good job for now on, and solve the engine-core problems soon. Just remember that H1Z1 is gonna be a free game and you'll have to pay for ingame goodies. Just for this, DayZ is lightyears ahead.

I bought this game a year ago, and almost have 400 hours of play time. Its fun, had a lot of great memories with this game...but also had more TERRIBLE memories. The hacking is out of control, and I see the same bugs that have been in the game a year ago. Today I played with my friends, who also bought the game a year ago... and it got to the point where we just stopped playing because of the 20 FPS, slow/restarting servers, and incredible desync. The game really hasn't changed much from a year ago ... and the incredibly slow development doesn't give me any hope of it getting better anytime soon. New guns are great, but when you spend 5+hours getting fully geared, get an M4 with sweet attachments, and then venture into a high pop server only to get hacked, you will find it incredibly not worth it... I will keep playing this game periodically because its pretty fun with friends, but no longer on a daily basis.
In terms of development, there will always be controversy with this title. I have a degree in business management and marketing, and one of the first things you learn as a business student is that THE CUSTOMER IS ALWAYS RIGHT. Period. This is business 101. The devs at Bohemia refuse to acknowledge the concern of their early access players, and often fight back with rude and snarky comments on their personal twitter accounts. They often times halt status reports and patches. You can see a new stable patch about every 6 months.
I recommend it to people who are patient with the development, for the gun fights are sweet and the adrenaline rush you get from them is like no other game I've ever played. However to the gamer who typically plays CS:GO/BF4/COD, the often times long build up to that point might not be for you.
Pros:
-Great "survival" crafting mechanics
-Gun fights
-Every player run-in is different
-Awesome game if you run with a clan or group of buddies
-Great textures/detail
Cons:
-Very slow development (typically 1 patch a month, making little babysteps each month, and the devs suck at keeping community updated, when compared to other alpha titles like Star Citizen)
-Terrible Developer feedback on updates/status of DayZ
-Desync
-Lack of persistence
-New patches often bring new bugs (which is expected, but just another obstacle to surviving)
-"death by natural causes"    OR in other words: Desyncing off a building and dying, breaking your legs on second floor of prison, zombie glitching through the wall, falling through rocks, invisible zombie, and getting your V3S stuck in the ground.

Undertale....
It has colorful characters, an in-depth story, and a soundtrack to die for. The child-like wonder and excitement of a different world pushed against the dark truths behind battling an "enemy" in any game make for a roller-coaster of emotions that lead you to the edge of your seat, asking questions and searching for answers. The bullet hell battles are interesting, unique, and fun. All of them individualized per monster you battle and per monster groups, making them both difficult yet organized. The dialogue is detailed and meaningful, leaving no filler story. And while the map of the game is fairly linear it does hide it's share of secrets and mysteries that prove intriguing and leave the player wanting more. The multiple paths you may take hold an amazingly huge yet subtly hidden change in the scenery and dialogue, making multiple play-throughs contrast against each other making for extended game play. By far one of the most impressive independent games to come out in years, it is worth far more then ten dollars.

It's difficult to NOT recommend DayZ, especially given that I've spent large chunks of hours on this game. Unfortunately, despite the isolated instances of occasional fun, it's just not worth it.
For those of you familiar with Arma, you'll immediately recognize the rather unique engine. While Arma has been at the forefront of military simulators for years, the engine experiences some serious setbacks when thrusted into a scavenger hunt/zombie apocalypse narrative. Given that the engine was designed for massive scale, military missions, squad based firefights and gameplay focused on taking objectives, what you're left with in DayZ is a terribly inefficient inventory system, AI that doesn't quite know how to act irrationally (given that they're supposed to be military actors), and a looting system that's hit or miss. Essentially, the developpers are forced to fight and struggle against the engine itself, which greatly hinders any progress they are hoping to make.
And that brings me to the very reason why I can't bring myself to recommend this game: a complete lack of progress. While the devs attempt to give players the impression that the game is being updated by introducing goddamned berry bushes and new weapons, they have nevertheless been tiptoeing around some game breaking flaws such as♥♥♥♥♥♥poor physics (notice the amount of reviews complaining about the infamous 2 foot drop resulting in a broken leg), superhuman zombie senses that allow them to spot you miles away, complete disregard for obstacles and walls on behalf of the infected, and the list goes on.
While I've had some memorable experiences in this brutal yet occasionally rewarding game, those isolated instances don't merit a recommendation. Going on a full year of development—and 3 if you include progress made by the mod—the developers just seem to content themselves on delivering new gimmicky content rather than really tackling the issues that prevent this game from becoming great.

This is an account of events in DayZ since its original release date until January 2015.
I had high hopes for this game as it was the much anticipated sequal to the Arma 2 mod. I was informed of the Arma mod many times by friends but was never very optimistic as the concept seemed silly to me, but after months of refusing to purchase Arma I noticed that standalone was being released, so naturally I informed my friends who had originally recommended the mod to me. They proceeded to purchase the game and managed to persuade me to do so also.
At first glance DayZ seemed just like what I imagined, a boring survival game where there was few players to interact with as the map seemed so large. But after a few days I started to get the hang of it, with my friends inept knowlege of the map (which they claimed to know like our own town...) we proceeded to wander around the world of Chernarus, albeit taking rather strange routes, until we found the then capital of PVP; Electro. This was where DayZ started to make a profound impression on me as it showed that this game was not all about running around for hours with an FNX pistol looking for players to befriend and ultimately backstab, it showed that this game required a high level of concentration and tactical knowlege to successfully master the art of DayZ survival. So, many days where spent hunting down players within Electro, and also many days spent looking for gear after our inevitable deaths, this was also a key factor in the game as when you respawned it wasn't as simple as collecting some more loot from a nearby house, it actually took time to get geared back up and by that time the people who had killed you were most likely gone forever. Camping around Electro were definately some of the best times I have had in DayZ, spending hours on end in one house killing everyone who opened the door, collecting their gear then moving onto another house, only to do the same again, until eventually we became friendly and spoke to everyone who we met, until one day we met a group of people who later joined up with us and we formed into a group of players. I believe at one point we were the 80th best DayZ SA clan, that however had nothing to do with the review.
This magical experience of meeting new players and forming alliances is definately the best feature of DayZ, making the most unlikely friendships in the most unlikely ways is what makes this game great. However, the game then started to have some major problems in the development, every new release would fix one problem but create another three; zombies were incredibly fast and impossible to kill at one point I seem to remember. This was a real turning point as I started to see just how broken this game is, not at all helped by the then lead developer Dean Hall who was more concerned about climbing mountains that supporting his own games development, this coupled with the price increase makes me wonder why I played this game. Some times were good but most times were frought with arguements due to bugs in the game, stupid deaths or broken legs when you fell 1 foot from a staircase, not to mention the immense amount of hackers that glitch around somehow killing everybody on the server and sometimes taking the entire server down.
So, to conclude, I would definately reccommend DayZ to the individual who can put up with huge bugs and flaws in the game which lead to confusion and frustration, and sometimes downright unplayability, the person who can look past this and enjoy DayZ as I once did will have great pleasure from playing this and will most likely recommend the game to others, like myself. To others though, this game is far from complete, the departure of Dean Hall has definately improved the rate of progress but the game is still very badly made, it is unplayable on all but the best PCs and even then requires significant tweaking to increase FPS and decrease DeSync. But please don't take this the wrong way, DayZ
if fully released is sure to be one of the best survival games on the market, so if it is not your idea of a good game now, please do check towards the end of this year when it is due to be released, but be warned that this may come at an increaed price.
Thanks
~Sam

The concept of the game is great.  The graphics and shadows look awesome and it feels really immersive.
However, there are still a ton of glitches in the game.  The game failed six times in a few hours today.  Most of the servers are wonky and it can be hard to find one that actullly stays online.  If feels a lot like trying to play a hacked version of a game on a randome server; not a $38 game with more than a year in development.
The game play is frustrating most of the time.  It is hard to find food outside of cities.  If you venture into cities, you will likely be killed by a zombie.  If you can find food, and avoid the zombies - which you will not be able to find enough - you will freeze to death because it rains all the time and you can get warm again.  My first 7 hours with this game left me wishing I had not purchased it.  It is nearly impossible to survive long enough to get invested in the game.
Don't buy this game at $38 like I did.  At this price it is ABSOLUTELY a rip off. Once it goes down to $12, it might be worth it.  The reason they don't offer a way to try it before you buy it is because they know no one would pay for it.  Remember when people who wanted help with development would offer alpha testers free access until the game was polished enough to charge people for?  Shame of you Steam for letting all these people get ripped off like this under the precept that these are "In development".
This is the first and last early access game I will be buying.  If you are into this game, buy Arma 2 or 3.  I am sure there is a free mod somewhere that does what this is supposed to do, but for free.

DAYZ is a gritty, authentic, open-world survival horror hybrid-MMO game, in which players follow a single goal: to survive in the harsh post-apocalyptic landscape as long as they can. Players can live through powerful events and emotions arising from the ever-evolving emergent gameplay.
Chernarus
230 sq. km chunk of post soviet state, featuring deep forests, cities, villages, abandoned military bases, and more
Up to 40 players per server
Rich server / client architecture developed from scratch.
Persistent player profile
Key player data is persistent across all servers
Inventory
Combine various clothing items, equipment and carry all of the items that you will need to survive the harsh new environment in the open and intuitive inventory system developed to answer the needs of crafting and character customization.
Crafting
In the apocalyptic world of DayZ, resources are sparse and every useful bit should be utilized. Items or equipment can be improved, turned into something else or fixed using the new crafting mechanisms.
Weapon customization
Use customizable firearms with authentic ballistics and weapon characteristics as well as melee weapons to protect yourself against all the dangers a survivor may face
Customizable clothing
Customize your survivor with a multitude of new clothing items that can be scavenged from the remnants of civilization, which provide various degree of protection against the elements, infected, and other survivors.

Pros:
- The soundtrack is notably one of the best things within the game, featuring a wide variant of interesting music that fits flawlessly with the tone of this game.
- The settings although short are very impressive and differentiating from each other.
-The characters are extremely vivid, and in the pacifist run they will make you make you care for them
-The story itself is very deep, putting you on a winding path between a whimsical and sorrowful adventure, and even eery at times.(Especially in either true pacifist or genocide) The majority of AAA titles don't even come close to this excellence.
-The game creatively extends such systems created by the Shin Megami Tensei series, to the point where nearly every enemy can contact you in a different way.
-The True Pacifist Run will leave you very satisfied with completing the game, and even make you ponder most of it's life lessons it teaches you in the game
-The game creates a very unique world compared to other RPGs, similar to a fashion the wonderful Earthbound/Mother games have created
Cons:
-The RPG mechanics besides the pacifist mechanic leaves you with a shallow experience in fights, with only basic mechanics being in there otherwise.
-While all the characters are vivid, quite a few are static in terms of a developing personality(Although there are quite a few outliers of this though)
-Another problem with the game is that quite few of the characters have little to no flaws, making them at points very unrealistic (Although, you'll notice in the game a correlation with the developed and flawed characters)
-The Genocide Run is where the majority of these flaws are brought out. Also within this run, you'll find that the fun aspects of the game are mostly gone and the difficulty spikes greatly between two bosses. Despite this though, I suggest after completing your pacifist run that you play or watch someone do this run.
General: This game isn't as godly as some fans will say, but more or less of a "polished gem". I myself feel that this game is a close masterpiece that should be cherished in the gaming industry, but not to the point that some fans make. This game masterfully creates it's tone, and provides very satisfying content for the $10 it costs. The audience that will enjoy this game will not be the general one, but if you have a piqued interest in the game, try out the demo and if you need a further look JUST watch the beginning of Snowdin. This will give you a good enough analysis if you'll like the game or not, and if you are still interested STOP WATCHING and play it quickly.
My Rating: 9/10 (Masterful, but with some present flaws)
Realistic Rating: 8.25/10 (Great, but with quite a few noticeable flaws present in parts of the game)

It should be obvious to all that this game will go places even if it is unknown what the nature of said places will be. That being said, even if the game ended prior to going to these "places," it would had still been an incredibly memorable experience that I very much enjoyed and would had been recommended as is. Every major character is a great joy to interact with and have given me many a laughs… including one scene in particular which rendered me rolling with laughter for over a minute, unable to continue. Despite the many great jokes and comedy here, there is still a lot of heart in this tale. This is especially true in best ending. If there was anything to complain about, it is that backtracking can take a lot of time although its not strictly neccessary. Just wish some faster movement speed was available at some point. The begining of the game can also be a little rough, but once you get out of the ruins and start meeting some of the amazing characters of Undertale, the game really does comes around.
However once the game goes “places” the entire experience ascends into something quite special that you'll never forget. Both the journey and the payoff are worth it in this game. The music is also pretty good as well, so picking up the soundtrack with this is recommended. 10/10 spiders agree as they all clap along to the music.

At first as you start the game, everything seems confusing. You start with nothing, but a flashlight and a battery. In the new patch, you always spawn close to the water, pretty close to a city, but when I started you could spawn anywhere. At my first view, I thought it looked pretty nice. The graphics are awesome, despite it being alpha, and the animations too. But after a few hours, it all started to be pretty boring. I didn't meet a player, until I've played for 5 hours or so, and for the only reason him shooting me. I had found an axe and a backback and a few supplies, but nevermind I thought, because I thought I would have these things when I respawned again.
The thing with Dayz is, that when you die, you die. Litterally. So there, I spawned again with nothing but a flashlight and a battery. "What a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game" I thought. I placed it in my steam library as  "unfavored" games, and didn't play it for a few months. I gave it a shot again for a few months ago, and wow. Many things had changed. New animations, you spawn close to the water, not in a forest somewhere, and everything seemed to be so much smoother.
So here we go, 78.7 hours (ATM) in just a few weeks.
It just got so much more funnier. That tense feeling you get when you see another player, and for you just shouting "friendly friendly", for them to shoot you right after. That sucks, right? But after you have one of these moments, you just slowly start to be more careful when playing, because your next move, can determine wehter you're running into a group of bandits, or getting shot against.
To all you guys, who thought at first look, that this game seems like crap, give it a try again. I did, and I freaking love it !
Definitely recommended.

This is an incredibly charming game. It's short, sweet, cute, and will toy with your emotions. You will become emotionally invested in the characters and the storyline. You will become engrossed in the world and play through the whole game quickly. It is not a super difficult game. That was something I really enjoyed about it. I like games with puzzles and the like, but they shouldn't take me more than a few tries to figure them out. Undertale succeeded in making puzzles challenging enough that you have to pause and think for a couple of minutes, but not so challenging as to frustrate you and hinder gameplay. Fights are also scaled well. Make sure you always have some healing items on you, and you'll be able to beat the bosses without too much frustration.
It's also worth noting that this review is coming after I completed a True Pacifist run on the game. I highly recommend doing a pacifist run as your first playthrough of the game. The True Pacificst ending is considered the "true" ending, and it'll really pull at your heartstrings. It's sweet and makes you feel good. Honestly, I've become so attached to the characters and to my commitment to be a pacifist in the game world, that I'm no longer sure I even want to do a genocide run. I'm sure I will eventually, but that's just a testament to how much of a feel-good game it is when you go the pacifist route.
One additional note~ When I bought the game I was somewhat conflicted on the base price ($10) since I'd heard some people say it was totally worth it and others say it wasn't. I honestly do feel like it was worth it. Playing through the game once, I racked up over 15 hours of gameplay, and every second of it was very enjoyable. Given the different endings and the way the game changes after you've played through it, it also has very high replayability. That definitely adds to the value you get for $10. Obviously waiting for a sale can still be beneficial since then you'll get an amazing game for even less money, but I do not think you'll regret your decision to get the game for the full price, so long as you are interested in what the game has to offer: multiple play styles, sweet and engrossing story with quirky characters, a specific flavor of humor, a great soundtrack, and a lower level of difficulty.

Either disarmingly earnest or relentlessly macabre, Undertale does so much more with so much less. Three parts Earthbound to one part Homestuck, Toby Fox disassembles the RPG experience with the loving precision and biting insight of a fan-turned-creator.

Before getting Undertale I thought the game was being extremely overhyped, but I was wrong, the game absolutely deserve all the praise it is getting.
It's an extremely fun journey from beginning to end, no matter which path you choose. The rpg elements are really simple and easy to deal with. The bullet hell segments are just the right difficulty except for two fights in one of the routes. It's supported by great characters and an amazing soundtrack, every boss has their own track. There is enough silly stuff in the game to keep you entertained the entire time. The graphics and art are simple and unique, Undertale is the perfect example of how graphics don't make the game.
What got me the most though, is how story rich the plot and setting is. I'm not saying the plot is extremely deep that will leave you changed for life. I'm talking about how the game feeds you the perfect amount of plot while leaving enough lore drops in the form of flavor text in items and conversations with side characters. There is a LOT of stuff you can learn about what happened prior to the events of the game and if you love story as much as me, you'll try to find every detail.
Overall, this game offers a complete package you would want in a game. A very rich story despite appearances and graphics, great characters, simple gameplay easy to get into and the right difficulty, and an outstanding soundtrack.
If you're iffy about the game because of how hyped it is, worry not, it really is a great game.

It's an Alpha so obviously there are going to be some bugs, glitches, things that need optimized, etc.  That being said, the Rust team are doing a great job of getting the community involved and taking our feedback to heart.  There are weekly updates with items and featuers being added along with full patch notes describing what they're working on and whats coming soon.  I seriously can't wait to see what the finished product is.
This game is seriously one of the most addictive, fun, and immersive games I've ever played. It takes the best part of so many awesome games and puts them all into one cohesive package.  You have the survival/gathering feel of Minecraft, the building features of Halo's forge mode, the classic RPG feel of constatnly upgrading your character and equipment, and the thrill of a first-person shooter all rolled into one.  The truly awesome thing is the feeling of starting from nothing but a rock in your hands and eventually finding yourself in an armored fortress with assault rifles, rocket launchers, C4 explosives, and many other awesome pieces of gear.  With all the different admins and mods, as well, it truly is a different experience every time you play. And it just keeps getting better and better!
One thing I will say, though, is that this game is not for the casual gamer.  There is no chill mode. When you log out your character and stuff are still on the map. You can be raided and killed in real time while you're asleep in real life!  It forces you to be active if you want to be successful, which if you're an adult with real life priorities, can be a very hard thing to balance.  If you have the time, though, I highly recommend it.  No gaming experience like it.

Disclaimer: My opinion on current Alpha state. With over 2million copies sold, 1+ year following release and a successful Dayz Mod leading the way, what do they have to show for it?
I will over look the issues and bugs that are typical and are common with the territory of early access releases. This will be my honest review of what this game has to show at it's core and game play.
In a nutshell, If you enjoy mindless long walks and sight seeing in a zombie filled (with little amount of zombies) Post Apocalypse part of Russia, this game might be for you! You'll be walking for 20+min doing just that, Player encounters are they best, that is if you encounter any. All they want is your life and loot. There's no reason to cooperate with anyone. One of the best way to lose faith in humanity! Soon you too will turn to murdering as there's simply nothing else to do in this wonderful walking simulator with a hint of survival.
I'd say realistically most people spend 90% of the time trying to regroup with friends just to find food, then to die falling from three steps of stair or being player killed for no reason just to repeat this process. Dayz Standalone isn’t winning any awards! this is the current gameplay of Dayz Standalone. Once you've filled your stomach the only goal now is to find guns and terrorize everyone and anyone you come across.
Bit of warning for those looking to not support the alpha but looking for a game with direction. Better off to wait until this game is out of alpha. Go try some F2P in the mean time, at least they have content.
But not all is lost! Hopefully the Standalone will implement missions or a need for teamwork to keep it's player support, otherwise this game is just going to be about first impression which is drawn in by a very simple idea of exploration with no story and eventually becomes an open world death match of the last one standing. Good luck new players, better learn faster!
Pro: one of the best adrenaline rush you'll ever get when you enter a gun fight (~10mins to find a gun with ammo and another 15mins to find a player). Its because the game-play is so stale that any human interaction makes one paranoid. None the less, hands down my favorite experience of this game. This rush will beat any casual FPS game that’s out there.
Con: just about everything is hype and marketing from the success from the predecessor Dayz Mod, With no story or reason/goals, sadly this game is as fun as you are willing to believe it is.
I hope the Beta will be better since there are other competitors looking to monopolize on this niche genre and I would even venture to say onthe failures of delivery on this standalone.
On a side note Buddies of mine found Dayz Standalone to be a great past time for a drinking game. find a (insert item) ex: NotaCola Classic *everyone drinks* makes for a much more interesting night.
They already have our money, it'll never get out of Alpha </3

From the start, I had a good feeling about this game. It was reminescent of the older RPGs that I would play growing up. And I Have to say...WOW, for the 10 dollars that it costs, it's much more worth it than most games. So let me break it down as best I can.
The plot: The plot has been done before, several times. Seperation of races, constant warfare, one of the races hiding fear (Blah blah blah). However, what I didn't expect was to get so attached to the plot. It was as if I were the PC, and after going through the ruins, I was sucked in. Playing through Neutral and Pacifist ending, I found that the small differences were perfect. This game's plot has the capabilities to make a grown man cry, which is shocking in this day and age.
The characters: The characters had such personality that they were very much alive. From Toriel being the ever vigilant mother, to Alphys being the shy brainy type, I thoroughly enjoyed the characters. Depending on what you do and how you progress through the game, you will find that the characters seem to grow with you.
The mechanics: Ah! The fun part. The mechanics of this game are simply astounding. If parents had made kids play this, today's youth would learn the meaning of the consequences of your actions. During the game, one can choose to kill everything in sight, which majorly changes the direction in which the game goes. Or, they can choose to do things in a peaceful manner. Personally, I found being a pacifist was the way to go, as it takes more strength to be merciful than to be a genocidal lunatic.
Overall: This game is so akin to the Mother series that it almost hurts. The art style, the gameplay, the sprites! Seeing this gem in the middle of a time where graphics reign supreme is a breath of fresh air. I would recommend this game to anyone and everyone, from my worst enemy to my best friend. I literally have NO complaints. This game is an absolute masterpiece.

I don't often write reviews. Almost never, in fact. The only other game I have reviewed is To The Moon, because it was a game so beautifully made that I couldn't stop myself.  It's gameplay wasn't great, but that was ok because it wasn't meant to be. It was a game that was meant to tell a very poignant story in an interactive way. Thats a little bit of an understatement, but thats ok because this review isn't about that game.
Undertale has taken the place of To The Moon as my favorite game on my steam profile, and it will likely never budge. It is a better game. It excels at everything it attempts. Good rpg? Yes. Good bullet hell? Yes. Good soundtrack? Yes. Good story? Yes.  People are normally turned off by hype, and praises. They begin to question, "How can it possibly be that good?" This game deserves every good review it gets, every recommendation, and every praise. No amount of lauding will make this game overhyped. It has no right to be as good as it is. It has no right to be hilarious every time it makes a joke. It has no right to have a flawless OST. It has no right to be as meaningful and thought provoking as it is whenever it tries to be.  How is it that this little developer managed to reach a game at this level of perfection?
I have not really said anything specific about the game. That's intentional. The less you know about the game before hand,  the more enjoyable it will be.
One thing, however. This game nails the morality system. The idea that you do not have to kill things in this game. Dishonored's morality system is trash compared to this.  In Dishonored, you let people live because you want to get the good ending. In Undertale, you let things live because you have a heart. Please, human, show some MERCY. Especially on the first run.

Disclaimer: My opinion on current Alpha state. With over 2million copies sold, 1+ year following release and a successful Dayz Mod leading the way, what do they have to show for it?
I will over look the issues and bugs that are typical and are common with the territory of early access releases. This will be my honest review of what this game has to show at it's core and game play.
In a nutshell, If you enjoy mindless long walks and sight seeing in a zombie filled (with little amount of zombies) Post Apocalypse part of Russia, this game might be for you! You'll be walking for 20+min doing just that, Player encounters are they best, that is if you encounter any. All they want is your life and loot. There's no reason to cooperate with anyone. One of the best way to lose faith in humanity! Soon you too will turn to murdering as there's simply nothing else to do in this wonderful walking simulator with a hint of survival.
I'd say realistically most people spend 90% of the time trying to regroup with friends just to find food, then to die falling from three steps of stair or being player killed for no reason just to repeat this process. Dayz Standalone isn’t winning any awards! this is the current gameplay of Dayz Standalone. Once you've filled your stomach the only goal now is to find guns and terrorize everyone and anyone you come across.
Bit of warning for those looking to not support the alpha but looking for a game with direction. Better off to wait until this game is out of alpha. Go try some F2P in the mean time, at least they have content.
But not all is lost! Hopefully the Standalone will implement missions or a need for teamwork to keep it's player support, otherwise this game is just going to be about first impression which is drawn in by a very simple idea of exploration with no story and eventually becomes an open world death match of the last one standing. Good luck new players, better learn faster!
Pro: one of the best adrenaline rush you'll ever get when you enter a gun fight (~10mins to find a gun with ammo and another 15mins to find a player). Its because the game-play is so stale that any human interaction makes one paranoid. None the less, hands down my favorite experience of this game. This rush will beat any casual FPS game that’s out there.
Con: just about everything is hype and marketing from the success from the predecessor Dayz Mod, With no story or reason/goals, sadly this game is as fun as you are willing to believe it is.
I hope the Beta will be better since there are other competitors looking to monopolize on this niche genre and I would even venture to say onthe failures of delivery on this standalone.
On a side note Buddies of mine found Dayz Standalone to be a great past time for a drinking game. find a (insert item) ex: NotaCola Classic *everyone drinks* makes for a much more interesting night.

I have played through this game three times now.  It is the first NEW game I have felt compelled to complete since 2000-something.
My first playthrough, I explored everything and got to know the characters.  I read the ridiculous text and took the simple storyline at face value.  Then there were hints I should try playing the game without killing anyone.
2nd playthrough, everyone wants to be friends with me.  I had to figure out how to not kill...a very different experience for an RPG...I learn more about the characters and everyone lives happily ever after.
...but now I need to know what happens if I kill everyone...3rd playthrough is heartbreaking where I am the bad guy. Everyone flees in terror.  I know all of these characters now - their hopes, dreams, insecurities...and I have decided to murder them all.
Each gameplay route features the characters saying new things depending on your choices.  The first playthrough takes about 6 hours, and each recurring playthrough maybe another 4 hours.
This game reminds me of when I was a kid and I would wait all day in school thinking about getting home to get to the next area in whatever RPG I was playing - back when I needed to devour every piece of content in every game I could get my hands on.

rust was an amazing survival world. it gave you every opportunity to improve yourself as a player, and i dont care what anyone says legacy rust was the
of rust. it may of had its fair share of bugs but its what made the game fun. everyone i know was having an absolute blast playing the original rust legacy. you could do so much stuff. there was alot of skill and alot of luck it was a perfect balance, and the map was easy to memorize. everyone would have the chance to rule the server with there friends if they were good enough. there was no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t it was simple, fast, fun and was a way more polished verson of dayz
now lets look at rust when they decided to do the graphical overhaul of the game. it basically is what rust was, but added new graphics and made maps random with a few choices for weapons. you still had the blueprint system which was amazing simple and works perfectly. rust at this point looks almost to good to be true. sure there was no radiation yet like the previous, but it would all come in time.
that is. until like a complete ♥♥♥♥ing idiot facepunch decided that ya know hey lets just change rust into minecraft to please all our 12 year old fans of the game that complain about how bad they are at getting c4 to raid.
rust pulled a complete 180 and out of knowhere chaged the blueprint system into the XP system
the blueprint system was perfect, sure it required bit of luck to get good blueprints, but you need the element of luck in games like these to suprise, balance, and reward players who take the extra step in really searching for blueprints to craft better stuff. you still needed lots of skill in order to defend your self while looting these common places on the map to get the blueprints and raid. it was a perfect balance
why change something that isnt broken??
now the XP system. this ♥♥♥♥ing atrocity is what i like to call the
of rust.
not only could you not craft literally anything useful to even defend yourself from players ahead of you that grinded. you were only given tools to just grind your level up until you actually got to a bow or crossbow to even help yourself.
getting xp was a unessesary, massive, ridiculous waste of time. it took way to long to even get to level 20 where you could actually survive and build a decent base and have good weapons. it completly unbalanced the game
the game was super unbalanced. clans would just dominate buy abusing xp share on items to grind through levels extremly fast in 10 man crews.
it serverly seperated people who played on the server longer than you. at no point were you given a fair chance. you would allways be put down by higher level people who unlocked c4 before you . becuase you did not grind for 20 hours to even have a gun to counter raid or defend. casual players couldnt even play it was all competitive

thats the problem. facepunch forgot what fun is. graphic dont make the game better. they didnt need to make the graphics so fancey for the game to be good. before you make the game pretty. the game itself has to be enjoyable and fun. they stopped bug fixes and completly forgot that you must focus on the gameplay first before the graphics.

since then that has changed. rust has a new system. instead of going back to the blueprint system for some reason. they added in the component system.
the component system has its flaws, but it actually works, and you can have fun again, and do what your supposed to do in the game. this is what i call the
of rust. recovering from the dark ages of the xp system and massive amouts of players were unhappy with it.
you could now craft everything at the start of the game only the catch is you must have the resources and the components.
the component system works wonders as it allowed every player to have a fair chance at the start regaurdless of how long you played on the server. you just needed to go out and find the components using skill in killing others who already have some. raiding , looting barrels, traveling to places on the map that have some. it is great
that problem is that there are only 2 places where you are basically guaranteed rifle bodys and tech trash components. sure you still can get it from other places and shred some stuff in the shredders to get more components but the millitary tunnel and the mining outpost are by far the best places for high level components.
what this causes is a huge urge to build bases near these places on the map and take control of them. once a group of highly powered people takes that certain place. nobody else can loot from there to get ahead. they can still get ahead by going to the lesser areas and getting lucky. but its not as easy as the military tunnels, and mining outposts. the group that then controls these areas can continue to feed off of the components that spawn there. the longer they remain there the more powerfull they become until they get to the point of near invinicibility.
not to mention air drops that deploy aroud the map the contain good loot. whoever is the most powerful on the server has the best chance of taking them everytime. its not as bad though its pretty balanced.

This is probably one of my most favorite games I've played all year. Everything from the characters, story writing, gameplay and music is just so amazing. Undetale is an RPG, but with the added twist of being able to spare characters. Every choice you make in-combat sticks with you to the end of the game which makes battles much more intense. The way you defend yourself is by dodging enemys attacks in a black box with your arrow keys which makes battles much more interactive then watching numbers going up and down, it adds a certain difficulty to the game but keeps the pace going. This combat idea really made the game fun and found the right way of making it not too hard but not too easy. This game is a perfect combination of story telling and gameplay.
The music is amazing and perfectly fits the atmosphere you are in, either if your feeling dispair, fighting an intense boss just fighting a regular guy, or just in a funny situatuon. It's just done so well. I ended up getting the soundtrack so I can listen to the music on my phone.
The characters in this game are written so amazingly even down to the random encounters they are unforgettable. You get to see the personalitys of other characters in this game grow and you get to see what they stand for and what they want, you feel bad for fighting them. You get attached to the cast. If you're like me you want to help them and be able to achieve the best ending.
The ending in this game (depending on what you go for) is incredibly satisfying. It tied up the plot and the journey very nicely.
Honestly I could sit here all day and tell everyone what this game does great, this game really is worth the 10 dollars they price it at. If looking at the store page and reading some of the reveiws is enough to get you interested in buying the game do it, I can almost promise you it would be worth it. The best advice I can give you is too jump into the game without knowing too much about it, you will get the optimal experience out Undertale that way. If you were like me and knew a bit about the game before buying it, still buy it it's such a fun adventure.

the blueprint system was perfect, sure it required bit of luck to get good blueprints, but you need the element of luck in games like these to suprise, balance, and reward players who take the extra step in really searching for blueprints to craft better stuff. you still needed lots of skill in order to defend your self while looting these common places on the map to get the blueprints and raid. it was a perfect balance

I too, was a person who was hearing a LOT about this game and I was JUST at the cusp of being overwhelmed by the praise and simply dismissing it altogether.
But then my friend came to visit and we played and beat the game over the weekend.
I was enjoying the game with its impressive battle mechanics, amazing story and catchy music, but finally, a moment mid game involving a skeleton and thirty hot dogs was the moment I absolutely fell in love with the game.
This game has terrific replay value because characters will vaguely remember you and your choices you made in your previous journey. This can make some interesting or even heart-wrenching dialogue that you wouldn't see in your first play of the game.
After playing the game and achieving the true ending, I do recommend the No Mercy route, since it does augment the story and strengthen the feelings for these characters you've grown to call your friends. And it does a fantastic job in making you feel the weight of your choices, as well as a terrible person alltogether.
I've now lost track of how many times I've completed this game, and I'm addicted to a few of the boss battles, where I try to perfect the technique to dodge their attacks, all while jamming out to the music. It's loads of fun, and I have definitely enjoyed the hell out of this game!

of rust. recovering from the dark ages of the xp system and massive amouts of players were unhappy with it.
you could now craft everything at the start of the game only the catch is you must have the resources and the components.
the component system works wonders as it allowed every player to have a fair chance at the start regaurdless of how long you played on the server. you just needed to go out and find the components using skill in killing others who already have some. raiding , looting barrels, traveling to places on the map that have some. it is great
that problem is that there are only 2 places where you are basically guaranteed rifle bodys and tech trash components. sure you still can get it from other places and shred some stuff in the shredders to get more components but the millitary tunnel and the mining outpost are by far the best places for high level components.
what this causes is a huge urge to build bases near these places on the map and take control of them. once a group of highly powered people takes that certain place. nobody else can loot from there to get ahead. they can still get ahead by going to the lesser areas and getting lucky. but its not as easy as the military tunnels, and mining outposts. the group that then controls these areas can continue to feed off of the components that spawn there. the longer they remain there the more powerfull they become until they get to the point of near invinicibility.

Writing this review for Undertale at 5:45 AM fills me with determination...
Before I write this review, I just started playing this game. This is a story rich game which means that it has replay value.
Undertale is not your average RPG game, though I can't really say that because, well, this is the first RPG game I've ever played. But what I CAN say is that this game is not just an ordinary game, it's amazing! What I can ALSO say is that the combat bit of this game gives me a Pokemon vibe since random monsters want to fight you when you walk around. But the most important thing that you should know about Undertale is that you do NOT have to kill anyone, or anything. Whether or not you want to is completely up to you. You choose your path!
Anyway, let's get to the pros and cons of Undertale
PROS:
-You choose your path!
-Lots of dogs
-High replay value
-It's challenging but not impossible
I wish I could list more but I haven't finished the game yet. I will edit my review once I finish it though ^^
CONS:
-You will frequently encounter monsters, which gets annoying after a while, especially when it happens every 10-15 steps
-Checkpoints, which isn't entirely bad but it means that you can't save any time you want. But that's also what an RPG game is
-If you die, you have to start over from your most current checkpoint
Overall Rating: 9/10

UNDERTALE is a very unique RPG, with a combat system that is a mix of traditional turn-based combat, and a "bullet-hell" game. Another thing that makes this game unique is the fact that you don't have to kill ANYONE, and the story is affected by how many enemies you decide to kill and how many you spare.
The characters are really well fleshed out and the writing is phenomenal. It'll make you laugh, it'll make you cry, and it'll leave you wanting more. The soundtrack is great as well, with a nice mix of silly and serious, a nice mix of chiptune and more modern electronic instruments.
Toby Fox and the rest of the UNDERTALE team did an amazing job with this game, and I highly, highly recommend you pick up the UNDERTALE Game/Soundtrack Bundle. Well worth the $18 price tag.

Personally from the games of 2015, I would have to say that this is a serious contender for Game Of the Year. This is a work of art unlike most of the titles released today. Words cannot describe how wonderful the soundtrack is.  If this has not persuaded you enough, then I honestly do not know what will.

I'll be honest. I don't get attached to games that easily, nor do I get extremely attached to the game's characters. But upon playing Undertale, I found myself tangled in the plot, mysteries, and puns that this game had to offer. Within the first moments of starting up the game, the opening scene where they tell a brief story of what happened between monsters and humans was what initially dragged me in, of course. I mean, when it's the first thing that pops up when you load the game, you kind of have no choice but to let it drag you in. The game lets you decide between killing everything in your path (the fandom has called it Genocide Path/Run/Route) or sparing monsters and being innocent (Pacifist Run/Route/Path). Genuinely, either way, this game will truly toy with your emotions and make you cry. It literally does not matter which route you choose, at the end of the day, you will be drowning in your own tears. Depending on what path you choose, you also get different themes for each character, town, battle, etc. Let me tell you now, the soundtrack is absolutely beautiful. It will take you on a rollercoaster of emotions from happy, to confusion, to fear, sadness, anger and excitement overall. Throughout this game, you get certain little secrets/silly things depending on which route you choose. Phone calls, things you normally wouldn't be able to...er...interact with? There are a lot of easter eggs in this game which makes it even better to play through every single possibility. There is so much that Undertale has to offer, and I'd write an entire book about everything from start to finish, but this is supposed to be a short review. Not so short, eh?
*(But seriously, buy the game. If you've got the extra cash, buy the bundle of the game + soundtrack. You won't regret it.)

The only way it could've been better is if it never ended.
A relatively simple combat system, with an interesting dodging mechanic tied to a - at first glance - no more than easy to make art style may leave passerbys assuming this is yet another half-baked indie game, but it is so much more than that.
Having beaten one of the relatively short 10 hour playthroughs, the game had left me yearning for more. I haven't played a game that has impacted me in such a way in a long time, and even fewer games have made me feel bad for even thinking about taking the easier and shorter route.
From Toriel the "goat mom" to sans and Papyrus' infamous bad jokes, Toby Fox has created memorable characters that feel more alive than just pixels on a screen. A certain flower, lesser dogs and an angry fish girl; they each react differently to your decisions and actions, which are permanent and have a lasting effect on the world you inhabit in the game. Morals are a large part of the story, and at some point, you have to make a choice.
Whether you make a good one or a bad one, is up to you.
Whatever you do - whether you have an inkling of empathy or not - play this game. I am certain you will enjoy it.

I had heard a lot about this game and, from previous experience, I knew hype could be a dangerous thing. So, I approached it cautiously.
I looked at the game length vs the price. I read through the negative reviews for solid counterpoints and a difference of opinion against all the praise it was receiving (as much of it seemed to be bandwagon effect, joke reviews, etc.).
For a moment, I thought this would just be a passing fancy. I'd get over my growing curiosity about it, and it wouldn't be worth playing.
I have never been so wrong.
~
It's tough to write anything about this game without giving something away. It's an experience, no matter who you are or how you play it. This game allows you to be whatever you want to be, and is both frighteningly aware of that fact, and harbours no intention of letting you forget it, either. This game dares to do things no other game I've ever played has (and I've been gaming for a solid 15+ years), and certainly things no larger developers could get away with.
Are you the kind of person who is generally detached from a game's characters or story? The clever writing and insidiously genius morality system will leave you thinking about your every choice and action, and exactly what it has affected - past, present, and future - in the game. Things are always changing, and rarely is there anything repetitive to be seen or played through. It's not so long as to overstay it's welcome, and refreshingly different enough on the mechanics side to keep you interested even if you're not sunk into it for the story. Plenty of different options, music, and bosses to be experienced through playing different routes.
Ready to commit, get to know the characters, and immerse yourself in the story? Then get ready for an emotional roller coaster that will take you up, down, upside down, and every which way in between.  The gameplay is quaint, charming RPG fare with a truly unique battle system that is simple enough to pick up, but clever in it's execution, and doesn't pull punches with its bullet-hell madness later on. Pacing and difficulty curve are just right. The music is fantastic and thematic at all times. The characters (and interactions between them) are well-written, endearing, genuine, and deep, despite how nonsensical some may seem at first glance. I'd also argue there's a character for everyone to relate to in this game. There certainly was for me.
As for the story, well, that's something to be experienced and worked out yourself. It starts you off easy and leads you in to the very deepest and darkest of deep-ends. Or, rather, it lets you choose very freely, and of your own will, which deep dark you want to delve into.
The only counter point I can make note of is the game's humour. A good amount (though not all) of it is for a target, niche audience - very clearly a game for "gamers"; internet, video game referecnes and parodies,  pop culture, anime, etc. - so if you're not familiar with that, some bits may be lost in translation. However, chances are if you're even playing this, you should have no trouble keeping up pace with it. Even if you're not, missing the odd reference, pun, or jab will not detract from what the rest of the game has to offer.
~Closing~
If you're in for this as a story and experience, prepare to experience about every range of emotion available to our limited human shells. It will make you laugh. It will make you cry. It will make you furious one second, and fill you with hope, joy, and DETERMINATION the next.  No matter what, it will leave you with potent memories and a lasting impression.
There is much, MUCH more to this game than meets the eye.
And remember, it's always watching.

The gameplay is quaint, charming RPG fare with a truly unique battle system that is simple enough to pick up, but clever in it's execution, and doesn't pull punches with its bullet-hell madness later on. Pacing and difficulty curve are just right. The music is fantastic and thematic at all times. The characters (and interactions between them) are well-written, endearing, genuine, and deep, despite how nonsensical some may seem at first glance. I'd also argue there's a character for everyone to relate to in this game. There certainly was for me.
As for the story, well, that's something to be experienced and worked out yourself. It starts you off easy and leads you in to the very deepest and darkest of deep-ends. Or, rather, it lets you choose very freely, and of your own will, which deep dark you want to delve into.
The only counter point I can make note of is the game's humour. A good amount (though not all) of it is for a target, niche audience - very clearly a game for "gamers"; internet, video game referecnes and parodies,  pop culture, anime, etc. - so if you're not familiar with that, some bits may be lost in translation. However, chances are if you're even playing this, you should have no trouble keeping up pace with it. Even if you're not, missing the odd reference, pun, or jab will not detract from what the rest of the game has to offer.
~Closing~
If you're in for this as a story and experience, prepare to experience about every range of emotion available to our limited human shells. It will make you laugh. It will make you cry. It will make you furious one second, and fill you with hope, joy, and DETERMINATION the next.  No matter what, it will leave you with potent memories and a lasting impression.
There is much, MUCH more to this game than meets the eye.
And remember, it's always watching.

Undertale.... a game that i had never given much credit. When i first looked at it; the graphics seemed bad, monsters seemed  stupid, and the story didnt seem appealing. But i started seeing people talk more and more about this game... i had to give it a try, and to my surpise was one of the best games i've played in a long time. That said the worst thing about Undertale is its hard to decribe because your experience is different depending on how you play...
I have completed the Neutral and True pacifist routes so my experience/ review may be different then someone who:
*played the Genocide route
*Only played Neutral route
*Did not play through the entire game (Which is kind of a given)
-----
Undertale is a game where your choices matter.... that said there is really only 2 major choices that really effect the game. Kill all the monsters or don't. There is a 3rd ending but it requires you to complete the 'Neutral route' first. Anyway, even though the choice seems small it changes the way certain characters act, which ones you meet, which ones you wont, and how future run thoughs are played.
Neutral:
For me i found this route like every other rpg out there. Bond with certain characters, boss battles, dying to monsters a lot, and exploring a world of the creaters imagination. But the game has many things that set it apart from other rpgs. The jokes are perfect, interesting ways to fight creatures, amazing character development, and sometimes 'pee your pants creepy' moments. This route (when you dont kill any of the main characters or any monsters at all) really makes you fall in love with the friends you make on your journey. The ending to this route is creepy and funny all at the same time and makes you want to replay the game to get another ending and actually beat the game (this routes ending makes you feel that there is stuff undone).

Undertale is quite charming. It’s full of wit and humour and put a smile on my face at times. However, I’m not overly fond of the gameplay. During combat, you can attack opponents or interact with them in some other way. When you get attacked is where bullet hell mechanics come in and they really aren’t great. It’s basically a tiny box in the middle of your screen with your character represented by a heart and you need to move around to avoid objects that start moving through the box. I guess that’s technically what a bullet hell (minus the quite important ‘shooter’ bit) is, but it’s not fun or flashy and you have to move around with your keyboard. Ew.
Undertale’s big draw is that it subverts normal RPG tropes. The biggest one being that you don’t have to kill monsters – you can talk to them or interact with them in some way to make them surrender. However, without killing things you gain no XP so the no-kill route is the harder path. I’ve heard people complain when things get too tough that they don’t want to ruin their no-kill playthrough. There’s something very unnatural feeling about this – choosing how you’ll play a game beforehand. Placing these kinds of restrictions on yourself, and having gameplay that totally supports and even encourages this, feels  strange. Inorganic. My favourite parts of many RPGs are being able to use your character’s particular set of skills to complete an objective without combat. Often pumping skill points into things like Intellect or Charisma means you’re not as good of a fighter when combat is unavoidable. Undertale takes this to a whole other level by completely removing any measure of character progression, a very important part of an RPG, and replacing it with… feeling good about yourself for not killing monsters? It does raise questions about how much punishment you’re willing to take to do the “good” thing, but I’m still in the camp that thinks gameplay should be enjoyable.

So, at over 15,000 reviews at time of writing, with a score of "Overwhelmingly Positive", what can I add to the chorus of reviews? I can tell you why everyone is going bonkers for this game, without spoilers.
Undertale is a heck of a lot like certain "triple-A" franchises such as Bioshock, Mass Effect, and Fable. Except what they tried to do, Undertale does far, far better. The next closest franchise to successfully do something similar is Telltale's The Walking Dead series, and even then I think Undertale goes farther. Other games had whole teams of writers, millions of development dollars, and Toby Fox outdoes them all. "Choice and Consequence" like no game has ever managed before.
Oh, also it's a little bit like Earthbound crossed with a bullet hell shooter and there are lots of classic 16 bit RPG references.
Undertale is probably the best thing ever made with Game Maker. Regardless, it's certainly the best game on Steam for the price.

I'm a huge fan of dayz mod and I've probably put close to 1000 hours in it. It was the best game experience I've ever had, me and my friends absolutely loved it. It was a golden age of games for us.
DayZ standalone was the chosen one. It was supposed to fix every problem with the mod that we had - mostly the fact that it was clunky to control, laggy, and the zombies were glitchy.
This standalone has fixed none of these things and is - in every way that is important for having fun - inferior to the mod. It is a huge dissapointment and I can only imagine its success has been driven by a mixture of people who didn't experience the mod at its best and hardcore survival fans who want to be informed that their clothes are wet rather than having an intense man hunt.
This is the biggest gaming dissapointment of the decade for me, and it is far too expensive for the state it is in.

Thank you for stopping by to gather a little information on what it is to play rust!  Have you ever wanted to play with a community of 12 year olds running around with guns?!?  Ever wanted to try and talk to somebody to gain alliance directly before they shoot your naked body for no reason!?!  These questions might be difficult, so let's try some different ones.  Have you ever wanted to spend 25 hours on a game building up a base with 3 layers of walls made of metal only to have hackers jump over the first two layers, blow open the door, take your stuff and then place stone blocks everywhere inside your whole base ultimately trapping you in and then nonchalantly jump back out?
If you answered yes to any of these questions, RUST is the game for you!  You are guaranteed to experience all of the above!
On a serious note, this game is beautiful as far as graphics and gameplay is concerned.  The community is just full of garbage players.  Hackers rule over everyone as they speed hack and can jump over traps and obstacles.  I found that I could deal with the bad community by simply running around without anything on me whilst gathering.  If they kill me, they kill me, that's a part of it.  With that being said, the first time I saw a hacker jump over my walls, I got a pit  in my stomach.  I take all the time to build stuff and hackers can go download a file and instantly be able to negate all the effort I put in.  It really takes a 9/10 game and makes it 1/10 (if I dare give it 1 star.)
It's unfortunate I can't refund this game.  I will never play it again unless there is an announcement about a fight against the hacking.  I highly suggest you don't buy this game!
Thanks for reading!  - Sabethman

A strange, vaguely lightbulb-shaped creature asks me what a star is. “Can you touch it? Can you eat it?”,  it inquires. “Can you kill it?” There’s a pause. “Are you a star?” The monsters of the Underground haven’t seen the stars in generations, after all, so it’s unlikely this thing would know anything about them. Littering the walls of the jewel scrawled caves of Waterfall are many plaques, inscribed with the depressing history of monsterkind. They detail the sudden attack from the humans, the one-sided massacre of a war that ensued; the mystifying nature of the SOUL. Not long after, you bump into a monster. 'Wosh u leg' the birdbath-like creature exclaims; before swiftly and dutifully beginning to wash a pizza.
And that’s the general tone that Undertale sets from the get-go.
REVIEW
Undertale
GENRE
RPG?
Developed almost entirely by award-winning Earthbound mod creator and webcomic composer Toby Fox; Undertale is a (mostly) joyous romp through the otherwise depressing yet quirky land of monsters. The opening cutscene details the legend of Mt Ebott, a forsaken mountain whose travellers are said to never return from. The year is 201X, and a small child, presumably looking for shelter from the rain, wanders into an opening at the peak. Whilst exploring the inside of the cavern, they stumble on some vines, sending them tumbling far, far down into Ebott. As luck would have it, they land on a well maintained bed of golden flowers. It just so happens that this child is you, you blundering ninny! [Why would you ever climb a mountain like that? Really!] Thus, your tale begins; your, uh, Undertale! [I tried, okay?]
Moving on from my half-hearted attempts at humor, let’s talk about Undertale’s pull; its unique combat system and genuine, heartwarming humor. Sure, it has the usual RPG ensemble of combat mechanics; fight, items, flee, etc., but what truly sets Undertale apart from other games of its genre is the ACT menu. As you’ve probably seen from the trailer, the game’s description, or the blurb that sits alongside the game’s picture; the tagline of Undertale is: ‘The friendly RPG where nobody has to die!’ True to its word, Undertale is a game where not a single creature has to die; I repeat,
[That is, unless you want to have a BAD TIME.] This is where the ACT menu plays a part. Each enemy presents their own puzzle for you to solve during combat, and as the game puts it itself: “If you ACT a certain way or FIGHT until you almost defeat them (Monsters)... they might not want to battle you anymore.”
This also ties into the game’s humor quite well, as, aside from the many fantastic puns and brick jokes, the ‘hostile’ encounters with the residents of the Underground are usually chock full of it. In the aforementioned Waterfall, there exists a monster named Aaron; a deliberately creepy literal seahorse who is muscular beyond reason. All of his dialogue ends in winky faces, even when he’s as scared out of his mind as he is ripped. On the topic of Aaron’s veterinary need for his sick pythons, the ACT menu allows you to foolishly challenge this apparent god of muscles to a flexing competition. While I say foolishly, it’s the pacifist’s way of beating this beefcake. Flex thrice and the equine epitome of energy will flex so hard that he flexes himself out of the room. Yes, I’m being serious, and that’s just one of the many interactions with the monsters of Undertale.
“But what about the defensive side of the combat?”, you’d ask. “I was just about to start on that, you impatient little nerd.”, I’d respond. Much like you’d see in a game of Touhou [Or so I’ve been told, I’ve never played Touhou.], enemy’s attacks are presented as bullethell-esque challenge. You move your SOUL around a small boxed in region while your foe throws a variety of little, white ‘friendliness pellets’ which you must avoid; unless of course you
dying. Each monster provides its own unique pattern to dodge and adding more monsters to the equation only helps to further enhance the difficulty, as the monsters will combine their attacks into a completely new one. Heck, to take it another step further, the titular boss monster encounters can sometimes change the way you control your SOUL entirely. Sometimes you’ll be affected by gravity, forcing you to jump over dangerous obstacles; other times you’ll confined to a set of three pathways which you must swap in between to evade danger. Most importantly though, remember;
So that’s the end of combat, and segues sure are hard; aren’t they? Speaking of segues, I just made a half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥one into the soundtrack section of this review. Neat, right? The soundtrack of Undertale is
, and I can without a doubt say that Toby’s reputation as a composer utterly precedes him. From the subtle uneasiness of ‘Your Best Friend’ to the bombastic whimsy of ‘Nyeh Heh Heh!’, the many fantastic songs of Undertale could only be described as unique. Personally, my favorite song from the OST is ‘Dummy!’ a hyperactive remix of the uniquely Undertale ‘Ghost Fight’. [Yes, I described it as uniquely Undertale; it fits the style of the game to a T.] Each song fits its situation perfectly, and, if you’re unfortunate enough, you might just uncover a certain someone’s calling card.
Aside from the audible presentation of Undertale; the visual presentation, while not too terribly complicated, is utterly intriguing. When you encounter a monster, the world becomes monochrome, aside from your SOUL; still a warming shade of red. Color is scarcely used in combat; reserved for truly singular spectacles or small, oft unnoticed details. A dark shade of crimson can barely be seen in a particular monster’s eyes, though you
have to be looking to notice it. Outside of combat, the world is vibrant, colorful,
The lovingly-crafted pixel art paints a picture of an expansive underground community, lively and fun; although sometimes dark and ominous if need be.
And that’s the truly astonishing thing about Undertale, it knows what it wants to be;
Over the course of my journey I was thrown through a whiplash of emotions and events, each delivered with the utmost sincerity and expertise. Many a hearty laugh came from the surprises Undertale had cooked up for those expecting something they'd played before. You're expected it to play like you would any other RPG you've played, and the game decides to play
instead; to take your preconceptions and mess with their very being. I find that if you let the game take your hand, let it guide you down this archaic, joyful, tragic, melancholic, path of madness; you'll come out better for it. Not many games can make you truly
that child-like whimsy of playing your first game, of learning to love your hobby all over again; even fewer can make you truly attached to the characters of its world. I'll admit, I got a bit misty-eyed when my journey had reached its end, when I looked back at all the good times I had with these lines of code I’d come to know as friends. Undertale is a game that sets itself apart from the rest, a game that knows how to be how to be uniquely
One moment, I’m traversing a luminescent grotto; solemnly listening to the hopes and dreams of the species my kind has imprisoned for centuries.
The next, I'm getting lessons on hygiene from a washing machine and its bird.

It's okay if you don't want to play this game. But if you'd like to know about this game's quality first, hopefully I can help.
Gameplay: Undertale is an RPG where monsters' attacks are short, bullet hell sequences (think Galaga or Touhou), while your actions are either to attack or do something else entirely. The gameplay in battles aren't rewarding, and they aren't meant to be, because it's the dialogue during battles that are more interesting. If you're looking for a game where you can play really well and turn around and say, "Did you see that?", you might want to play something else.
What makes this game shine is the breadth of things you can do in battles. You can't cast magic or even attack in more than one way, but you can Hug your enemy, you can Pray to your enemy, you can even start a Flexing contest or play fetch with the enemy. In brief, the gameplay is all trying new actions and surviving bullet hell sequences.
There's also a great breadth of things to do in the overworld. The game is packed with extra dialogue and easter eggs, which you'll find if you explore (e.g. talk to NPCs multiple times, kill this enemy, spare that enemy in a certain way, etc.). Excuse me for being vague, but the game seems to "anticipate" a lot of the choices and actions you'll make. It remembers when you reload your save file, and will adjust dialogue accordingly.
Story:
You're a kid who fell into the underground world of monsters and have to travel to the castle to find a way out. Along the way, you'll meet, fight, and befriend several major monster characters, each with their own agenda, personality schtick, and recurring jokes. Undertale has moments meant to be funny, and it has moments meant to be emotional. It's subjective, but I think this game does these moments very well.
The story is deep. By which I mean, you'll probably miss quite a lot of it if you're not thinking while you play. For an indie game, Undertale has quite a lot of implicit lore and dots to connect.
Presentation:
Undertale has a mix of pixel-based art styles that, strangely enough, don't get tiring to look at. This game is based off of old RPGs like Earthbound with old graphics and simple music. But unlike Earthbound, Undertale CAN go above these graphics and low-bitrate music, and it does so at key points in the game. The sound effects are toony, but only for style. During more dramatic scenes, the sounds become as realistic as they need to be.
Replayability:
Each run of the game is 3-7 hours, depending on what you're doing. However, there are multiple "routes" you can take for very different gameplay, music, and stories, so players often play 2-4 runs. In each run, there are dialogue choices and flavor text that varies depending on what you've done in a previous run.
If you think this game sounds like a good time, you should buy it. If not, that's cool too.
