But then I watched the first episode again, how there was an alternate way to play, the Genocide Route.  On a whim, I bought the game, and, not only was I surprised in how much was changed, the ending is such a godsend that I'll now listen to Meglovania anytime I need friggin inspiration.  Undertale is not a game that is to be played, beaten, and discarded.  Every moment, every interaction, every bloody line of dialogue is to be cherished, because Toby Fox masters what David Cage, Peter Moleneux, Ken Levine, and countless others have tried, and that is having choices that mean something, a story that gels exceptionally with combat, and characters that you actually connect to.
Do not put this off as Earthbound Nostalgia Bait, because it isn't.  It plays at your heart, tugs at the strings, and it is one of the best games I've played.

Before playing Undertale, I had heard a lot of the hype surrounding it. As a result, I was expecting something overrated.
It completedly surpassed all of my expectations.
Undertale is an RPG in which you don't have to use violence. If that sounds appealing, you don't know the half of it. It's difficult to say why Undertale is so good without spoiling it, but part of it is how it's moral choice system actually works, and drives the game's entire narrative. The player's decisions can completely alter the later, and in some cases even the earlier, parts of the game, at least narrative-wise. Furthermore, it manages to marry turn-based and real-time combat in a very effective way, by having you evade enemy attacks in a bullet-hell manner. Every attack can be dodged this way.
It's difficult to come up with anything critical of the game. I haven't beaten it enough times for it to get boring, but it probably would after the fifth time. But that's just praising by faint damnation, isn't it.
Ultimately, Undertale is a simply fantastic game which, despite it short run time, contains multiple times more content than would be necessary to justify its price tag.

There's been a lot of hype for Undertale and there's a reason why.
Undertale is the perfect example of what all stories and games should be. Games and stories should make you connect with character. Games and stories should make you feel immersed into the narrative and universe. Games and stories should make you feel like you know what's going to happen, only to turn it all around at the end. Games and stories  should make you feel emotion: frustration, sadness, happiness.
THIS is what games and stories should be. Undertale is a phenomenal game and I'm afraid I won't look at RPGs the same way because nothing will ever be able to top this. There's a perfect balance between the gameplay and story. They complement each other. You weren't just getting story thrown at you as you sit back and watch and it wasn't an RPG where you necessarily had to be good at gaming to get anywhere. I will never come across another game that will make me question game design and morals than this game.
I've never bought music before but within a heartbeat I bought the soundtrack. The bullet hell battles for characters literally have personality--how does one even manage to do that? The characters were so lovable and endearing like they were real friends and were hilarious as heck. I felt like I wanted to protect them like they were family; like they were real.
It's a game you don't want to finish but you yearn the ending and never ever want to restart.
Just buy it. Buy it and play it for yourself because I can assure you it will be an experience you won't forget in a long time.

This game shows that you don't have to have a big budget or studio to craft a fantastic game. The gameplay mechanics and system are simple yet have a lot of variety and depth which keeps the game interesting throughout. The gameplay also used as a way of storytelling, informing you about the weird and wonderful monsters you meet in every encounter.
The story and the characters are interesting and while the characters personality can be very stereotypical at times you learn to love them. Untimely there the ones that motivate you to keep playing just to find out what happens too them. The humor is spot on for any RPG fans with plenty of small references that poke fun lovingly at the genre. As you progress through the story the light hearted nature of your romp through the underground starts to shift, this is when things get interesting and you start to wonder about the mysterys of the underground and the characters that inhabit it making you want to push on and continue the game.
Replayability is through the roof. There is so much to find and discover and so many ways to play. The game remembers various decisions you make throughout the game and will change dialogue and choices not only in the current playthrough but in your next playthrough as well.
The soundtrack is amazing and fits perfectly with the clean simple sprite look of the game.
Do yourself a favor and pick up this game, take a trip to the underground and discover this charming and humorous story for yourself.

As a long time player of the DayZ mod I was obviously excited about the standalone. As of now I have clocked about 70 hours in standalone and would like to provide some informative feedback for people looking into the game.
Pros:
* Fundamentally the same game as Dayz mod (this is a good thing.)
* Art assets have been expanded and improved (the map is more detailed and there is a large variety of clothing)
* More mechanical depth (blood types, improvised equipment, hunting etc.)
* Can now survive off the land by hunting animals and cooking them

Cons:
* Hackers (will speak about this later...)
* The engine sucks♥♥♥♥♥ The Arma II engine is great graphically but it is a pile of crap in every other regard:
* Melee is awful. It is basically 'simulated' by skinning a short range, high damage ballistic weapon with a melee model.
As a result it can be extremely difficult to land melee hits. Most of the time they won't even register. I suspect this is a fundamental limitation of the engine and 'true' melee won't ever be added.
* Animations are even worse than the melee system. Almost every action in the game requires a fixed animation cycle. What this means is that if you want to take out your weapon you have to enter an animation cycle. Once you enter this animation you can't do anything else. If you are running when you commence the animation you will keep running until it's complete. Jumping (yes, jumping) is also an animation. As a result, jumping is something I try to avoid like the plague. What else is one of these horrible animation cycles? Eating, drinking, attacking with a melee weapon, getting into a car, climbing a ladder etc. etc.  Basically this is the only game you will ever play where your in game character will feel less physically capable than your RL self.
* There are memory leaks up the wazoo. The fact that servers typically need to be restarted after a few hours is symptomatic of this (again, this may be a fundamental issue with the engine that will never be fixed).
* The netcode sucks♥♥♥♥♥ I'm a software engineer and I haven't looked at the source code but I suspect it is sucky. They recently added a vehicle after much waiting. It is just as prone to desyncs as the mod... (the server cannot update the position of the vehicle quickly enough and it rubber bands everywhere)
* AI. Wow. I suspect again this is a fundamental limitation of the engine. Arma II AI was meant to simulate troops who typically take cover and make precise, slow movements across open terrain. When they tried to adapt this to zombies in the mod the results were awful. Zombies are just a joke. They glitch through walls. They run erratically so  are next to impossible to hit. They also use the delightful melee system except clearly have what are effectively aimbots.
OK enough bashing on the engine. You get the idea. Hmm, what else:
* The updates are a joke. They think releasing a high poly model of a gun is an update. Bug fixes seem to just fix ridiculous shoddy coding errors that they introduced (mainly item dupes or other highly unexpected behaviour). They never fix actual limitations in the engine.

Oh yeah my special section about hackers. This game is full of them. Me and my friend have agreed not to play it until they sort this issue out. Every single time we join a high population server, within 10 minutes we are dead from speedhacking/aimbotting/teleporting/godmode hackers. It's your choice, either join a low pop server and loot♥♥♥♥♥ all day or join a high pop server for some actual action and 'get rekt' by 14 year old kids with £10 hack tools.
Conclusion: Do not buy this steaming pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥ It has been in development for quite a while now and progress is glacial. As I mentioned above, I suspect inherent limitations in the engine mean this game will never feel polished. They will just keep adding more art assets. In one year I predict this game will be just as full of hackers and annoying engine features (read bugs) as it is now. I'm not fugging surprised Rocket bailed on the dev team (I also suspect he isn't skilled enough to actually develop a standalone game as opposed to a novel but fairly trivial arma II mod).

Before playing Undertale, I had heard a lot of the hype surrounding it. As a result, I was expecting something overrated.
It completedly surpassed all of my expectations.
Undertale is an RPG in which you don't have to use violence. If that sounds appealing, you don't know the half of it. It's difficult to say why Undertale is so good without spoiling it, but part of it is how it's moral choice system actually works, and drives the game's entire narrative. The player's decisions can completely alter the later, and in some cases even the earlier, parts of the game, at least narrative-wise. Furthermore, it manages to marry turn-based and real-time combat in a very effective way, by having you evade enemy attacks in a bullet-hell manner. Every attack can be dodged this way.
It's difficult to come up with anything critical of the game. I haven't beaten it enough times for it to get boring, but it probably would after the fifth time. But that's just praising by faint damnation, isn't it.
Ultimately, Undertale is a simply fantastic game which, despite it short run time, contains multiple times more content than would be necessary to justify its price tag.

I like the Mother series well enough. I actually preferred Mother 3 over Mother 2 (a.k.a. Earthbound in the U.S.). Both of those games construct a fun and wacky world populated with lovably silly enemies but despite the goofy nature of their settings, they still both manage to pull off well written characters in an emotionally charged story. Underneath the layers of American culture parody and just general wackiness, there's still direct messages from the game's authors commenting on human life and friendships and other similar topics. Experiencing the wackiness and interesting stories of those games was my favorite thing about them. My least favorite part was the combat. Aside from the often humorous in-battle text, these games featured pretty standard and simple RPG combat systems. Mother 3 tried to mix this up a bit by awarding players bonus damage for attacking with the rhythm of the music (think Crypt of the Necrodancer), but I still didn't really find the combat system that interesting. Especially with the amount of grinding that these games practically require you to do before being able to advance to the next area. It felt like the combat was getting in the way of the excellent story, rather than complimenting it.
So now fast forward 10 years from Mother 3 to Toby Fox's Undertale which strongly evokes the Mother series visually, musically, thematically, and even directly at some points in the game. Like the Mother games, you play as a young kid wearing a striped shirt exploring a weird and dangerous world filled with wacky monsters. Thankfully, one of the big deviations from the Mother games is the unique combat system found in Undertale. Undertale's combat presents the player with an interesting twist which is that you actually don't have to kill any of the monsters in the game. If you choose to fight monsters, you'll be faced with a timing mechanic similar to something you might find in one of the Paper Mario games. But an alternative to fighting is using the "act" menu which allows you to talk to or interact with the monsters to finish the encounter without killing them. This usually plays out as a bit of a puzzle where you meed figure out the right combination of actions to pacify the enemy. Regardless of which of these two actions you choose, you'll be faced with a "bullet hell"-like system when you defend and the monster attacks. Different monsters have different attack patterns, so memorizing how to dodge them is it's own fun mini-game
Also created by Toby Fox, Undertale's soundtrack is an absolute delight. It's a mix of chiptunes, synths and the occasional live instrument and echoes various other RPG soundtracks from Final Fantasy to Earthbound. My favorites are Ruins which sounds like it could fit in any RPG ever, Another Medium which at times sounds like it's trying to evoke Thousand Year Door's X-Naut Fortress, Snowy, which perfectly sets the mood for walking through a winter forest, CORE which is a rockin' electronic dance tune, Death by Glamour which is a variation on the aforementioned CORE track, and ASGORE which sounds like appropriate epic RPG final boss music. For more examples of what I believe to be music references to other games, listen to Dummy! (which I believe to be an "Off" reference) Alphys' Theme (which I believe to be another Paper Mario reference), Amalgam (which sounds very Earthbound-y to me) and Oh! One True Love (which is undoubtedly a reference to Final Fantasy VI's opera scene). The whole soundtrack is really, really solid and I fell in love with it almost instantly
As neat as the combat is an even as lovingly crafted as the soundtrack is, the real star of Undertale is the story. The characters are very memorable and endearing and the quality of writing here is top notch. The way Undertale builds expectation and then throws you a twist just when you think you've got things figured out is masterful. It's rare when games can make me laugh, and I usually count it as a success if a game can tell a joke and even get me to crack a smile. Undertale had me laughing out loud on several occasions. It handles the serious, somber, relaxing, strange and horrifying moments in the story just as well as the humor. It's so rare when a game can hit all these narrative notes as well as Undertale.
Summary
Undertale is one of the best and RPGs I've played in years. I found it to be not only an homage to, but an evolution and improvement on blueprint established by the Mother series. It's not a systematically deep RPG with layers of strategy or anything like that. But what it does do is use game systems to tell a well written story with endearing characters full of memorable moments. It also has a soundtrack that leaves a lasting impact almost as big as its characters. Undertale's unique battle system keeps players engaged dodging various projectiles in a bullet-hell like frenzy on defense while giving the player an option of a timing based fighting system, or a non-violent puzzle to resolve combat. Depending on your actions in battle, Undertale adapts acknowledges your actions in the story as well, which gives real weight to the decisions you make in the game. It's such a smart game and I enjoyed every second I played of it. I finished my first playthough in one sitting and am currently halfway through a second. I'll likely play through this a third time as well since there's just so many cool easter eggs and little things to learn about the game's story that you inevitably miss in one single playthrough. All fans of RPGs and good storytelling need to play this game. This was one of my absolute favorites of 2015 so far this year.

Incredibly unique RPG. A game where - dare I say - your choices matter. Most of the time in a purely mechanical way, but ultimately the interactions and connections you build to the characters in the game, and how your actions affect those connections will rise above the simple GOOD CHOICE, BAD CHOICE, NEUTRAL CHOICE of so many other games that try to be what Undertale is.
And while I would claim that Undertale is mostly a game about story and how it makes you feel, underneath all of that is a very robust and incredibly enjoyable RPG system. The combat itself in the game is unique in almost every encounter whilst still maintaining the same basic principles. Each boss fight introduces new mechanics or a spin on old ones, always ensuring that it's fresh and thrilling. I didn't once find myself "grinding" or hung up on the same boring copy paste fights over and over.
And one can't talk about Undertale without discussing the music. In a nutshell? It's ♥♥♥♥ing awesome. It manages to invoke an array of emotions, but for me the boss music for every fight just made it so much more than it was. I think the music alone for Muffet's fight is what makes it my favourite encounter in the game.
Honestly, games for me are hardly ever worth a second playthrough - I always feel like I've exhausted the capabilities of the games storytelling after however many hours I sunk into playing it the first time, but Undertale will be my first exception. It's a nostalgic, well thought out and beautifully written game by someone who honestly just wanted to write a nice, compassionate story - there is no overbearing monologue or pretentious moral message that is being shoved in your face, it's just a story about humans, monsters, and you. And temmies.

This game has ups and downs depending on the patch that is released. Hackers wreak havoc in the public servers, whereas they seem to avoid private servers. The fact that we have private servers is a huge relief. If you're new to the game, ask for experienced players to play with you. As interaction within the game is poor, you have better luck receiving help on the forums.
This isn't about to buy or not, but more like when to buy it. The development is slow but do some research as to what each patch brought or what it fixed.
Calling this a game is actually a mistake in my opinion, as whether you like it or not this isn't a game. More like a simulator.  You make your own story, and you'd better be good at the damn game or have some luck where the opponent desyncs or you get a lucky melee headshot with an axe. If you don't have both of these requirements, all you're gonna be seeing is a black screen with a 30 second respawn, or if you're that kind of player, trees and empty houses wherever you go. Zombie distribution is pathetic, on some servers you don't even have zombies.
Loot distribution is also a laughable case, thanks to the adding of useless items. Yes, Bohemia, you are ruining this game by adding useless items such as P1 pistol, Derringer,Makarov etc. that are useless in PVP and more importanly have magazines that are impossible to find. I don't want to visit civilian houses to find an useless crossbow, a derringer, or a P1 pistol, not even a ♥♥♥♥ing 1911. Just let us loot that magnum, mosin, shotgun, repeater without having to deal with useless items that make us venture even deeper in order to arm ourselves and properly defend ourselves.
Another laughable addition that was not an occurence in the early development is the fact that you outrun people who have nothing with a ♥♥♥♥ing gun in your hand. I mean what the ♥♥♥♥ ? Guns made you slower in the early development, that made sense, but now you ♥♥♥♥ing outrun people who are bare-handed. I mean ♥♥♥♥ off. First of all in terms of balance, how do we catch these people who have guns out. And how the ♥♥♥♥ does it make sense for the sake of "realism" that they outrun us so easily ? Not to mention how they chase you down as if they were olympic runners.
TLDR; if you don't know what you're doing, black screen and 30 second respawn or empty world and no chance of defending yourself.
Even if you know what you're doing, looting even with proper knowledge takes a while because of all the useless items and if you rely on melee you're up for the who lags and gets 1shot game. Yes, desync. Not to mention the people with guns who outrun you cuz yolo.
Personally, recently I have been playing a lot and got my KDA back up. I usually either die like a retard for a stupid reason or kill geared people and take down 5-9 more before getting killed for another stupid reason..
This game would be interesting if you didn't have to deal with all the trash items through your looting process. 80% of the loot is useless.  I'm not even talking about guns but items in general. Some items have no use at all.
People say this game will get better, but it goes backwards with every patch. Bugs aren't fixed, more bugs come with every patch. A lot of new items are worthless or impossible to find, and remplace the other useful item's spawns.
Two things that made this game better : - Not able to look through the walls - Able to lock the zombies by closing the doors.
In early development you could actually use footsteps to locate your opponent or hear when somebody is near you, now footsteps are sometimes silent. People have become ninjas AND olympic runners. Now you sometimes can't hear gunshots and other stuff.
Also, please ! At some point you made zombies run faster, perhaps TOO fast. But it was a good idea. Give them appropriate speed, nerf survivors speed, and give zombies another use than making you stuck in houses, killing you while you desync, running around cows making 4-10 zombies disappear from the city in which they were supposed to be.
There might be a good time to join Dayz. And perhaps I'm mistaken when I say 0.52 isn't a good time to join, because it does have its ups and downs. For an experienced player (600+ hours) like myself, these issues are annoyances. But for a new player these issues will be game-breaking. If you're new, and don't know people in the game, look them up through the forums, and play with them. Safety in numbers works in Dayz.. Unless you encounter me fully geared and don't instantly kill me before I can see you.

Undertale is magnificent and brilliant game that satirizes and plays in familiar fashion to turn-based RPGs. I so VERY highly recommend it.
On one level, its story and writing are spectacular, weaving poignant themes and situations with laugh-out-loud comedy. I can't tell you the last time I found a game this funny. The characters are instantly loveable and the puzzles/challenges frequently irreverant.
On a deeper level, the game's satirization of standard RPG mechanics really touched me. I want to avoid specifics and spoilers, because so much of the meaning of this game, in my mind, comes from deciding for yourself what to do to progress. The game questions, though, whether our natural instinct in other games is realistic, and it explores what in my mind is a much richer experience if we eschew our training.
Radically inclusive and diverse, utterly loveable, and full of charm and true emotion, it's no wonder this game has already garnered a significant dedicated fanbase. Undertale is a marker of what a growing number of gamers want: subversive, smart, and meaningful experiences.

Dayz is a very good game. I like the whole idea of surviving in a apocalyptic world where you are going against zombies and players, i feel there is a few things i think should be fixed.
. Not being able to pick up some items
. I HATE when i find a good item (backpack, melee weapon, ETC) and i can't pick it up because of server lag.
. Zombie AI
. sometimes it could be kind of funny when you find a zombie in a wall and comes out and scare the s*** out of you, but when you are in a PVP situation ( which happens a lot in this game) and a zombie comes out and hits you, you start bleeding and you have to focus on that now so the player just comes in and kills you. it sucks sometimes...
. Optimization
. I know that most games made by bohemia interactive are not optimized (arma 3, arma 2, and many more) but in a game like dayz that revolves around PVP, you can't be trying to shoot someone when you have like 15 fps, you need to at least have like 30 to 45. I can give them credit though for optimizing the game a bit better compared to the mod. In some places i get up to 70 fps (small towns and fields.)
. Server Lag
. Im not sure if anyone else got this or its just my internet. When i play sometimes, a message comes up saying "No message received for __ seconds" and i would be on a server with 30 to 45 ping. It may just be my internet...
Overall: Dayz is a very fun game, despite all of these bugs. I just want you to know what some of these bugs are and how they can affect the game. Because me personally, im gonna be playing this game a lot, thank you for your time.

Undertale is magnificent and brilliant game that satirizes and plays in familiar fashion to turn-based RPGs. I so VERY highly recommend it.
On one level, its story and writing are spectacular, weaving poignant themes and situations with laugh-out-loud comedy. I can't tell you the last time I found a game this funny. The characters are instantly loveable and the puzzles/challenges frequently irreverant.
On a deeper level, the game's satirization of standard RPG mechanics really touched me. I want to avoid specifics and spoilers, because so much of the meaning of this game, in my mind, comes from deciding for yourself what to do to progress. The game questions, though, whether our natural instinct in other games is realistic, and it explores what in my mind is a much richer experience if we eschew our training.
Radically inclusive and diverse, utterly loveable, and full of charm and true emotion, it's no wonder this game has already garnered a significant dedicated fanbase. Undertale is a marker of what a growing number of gamers want: subversive, smart, and meaningful experiences.

Those short tense golden moments that come out of interactions between other players have stuck with me much more vividly than any survival game has given me. I can point to practically any town or city and recall a story that goes along with it. Whether the adrenaline felt right before lauching the perfect ambush, the sudden shortness of breath that follows when you notice a stalker just in time ready to end you with zero remorse, teaming up with people I thought about murdering shortly before and becoming friends instead, fighting off crazed cannibals in the cities, all the hold ups I've been part of, the times when I trusted the wrong people and paided dearly, overcoming of odds that would have lesser folk tuck tail and run off or just plain dead and most of all the silly♥♥♥♥♥♥inbetween. Even the stories that end badly with no closure leaving you unsure you did the right thing or not have a lession somewhere to be learned. There is no wrong style of play here and that big ugly mess of raw human nature is what makes Dayz.

Undertale has nice music (not mind blowingly good by any stretch, but not bad). The story is extremely compelling, and the chracters are funny, well written, and good.
(Keep in mind I'm trying a pacifist (no killing at all) run here -)
However, the rest of it totally sucks. Getting in a fight in this game is worse and more tedious than fights during grinding in Final Fantasy. Literally every time I have a fight, be it random encounter or boss fight, I just groan.
The only way to quickly end random monster fights is to just flee. Luckily, with monsters you've spared before, you can spare immediately. With others, you have to do the whole song and dance EVERY. TIME. Each time I run into Aaron I just want to..... not..... play anymore. He's good for a chuckle the first time or two you see him but after that it's like okay... I get it.
This game is fun if you like doing things over and over and over and over and over and over again. Or if you like having to look online for tips on how to beat bosses. Boy, nothing sure is better than having to spend 20 minutes repeatedly hitting "spare" and dodging the same 4 attacks while the same 5 phrases get repeated.
Honestly, the first time I looked into this game I took a hard pass. But because it's blowing up all over tumblr, I decided to give it a go. The only reason I even keep playing is 50% to understand all the posts and 50% to see what happens in the story. But even with those as motivation, if I don't beat Undyne soon, I'm just going to call it quits on this pretty overall "meh" of a game.
I don't know, I must not be smart enough or something, but even the good aspects of the game get lost when it's too frustrating and tedious to play.

Never before have I been happier to spend $10 to get sad.

This is very much a game in development but in it's current state still gives you the unique and chilling experience everybody talks about.

Gameplay is quite unforgiving and open ended in a way that really engages you and your character. you are given little more than a few starting supplies when dropped into the game world and then are left to find your own way. Survival, combat and exploration feel viceral and the game does not move an inch for you in a sticky situation - which only serves to further exemplify how engrossing a gameplay session can be.

It is hard to nail a good argument for this game's technical issues as it is still in development. Essentially the game is playable and enjoyable despite it's ongoing development. The team behind DayZ seem to have a good idea of where they are and what is coming so if the experience looks interesting to you it is worth picking up if only to keep up with development as it happens.

If however you feel the incomplete state of the game would stop you from fully enjoying the game, it will defiantly be worth purchasing after the game reaches a build closer to it's final release.

I thouroughly enjoyed Arma 2 DayZ in all variations, Overpoch to Origins to End and RP. Standalone is absolutely horrible compared to any of them.  Rocket (Standalone dev and original DayZ mod creator) will be leaving, which I believe will send this game to the pile of all the other abandoned Early Access games. And that really sucks too, because DayZ can be lots of fun, that is when you aren't constantly getting killing on sight by troll bandits, which btw are a large part of the community.  As far as content, Standalone has SO little variety, and yes it is early access, I get that, but it is inferior to DayZ mod. Also Standalone does not support custom maps or client sided mods ( idk if it is planned, check their website if custom maps or clients side mods like sound mods if those are your thing). Anyways, I will probably recommend DayZ Standalone IF it adds more content like weaps and vehicles to feel like there is a good variety. Sadly in its current state, I cannot recommend it unless you are absolutely dying (no pun intended) to try it out.

When I started playing this game I was skeptical it could live up to the hours of fun that I enjoyed in Arma 2: Day Z mod. The zombies were overpowered, there were about 2 guns in the entire game, and the dev diaries posted by (Then head of development) Dean "Rocket" Hall seemed like he was playing a different game entirely. An immediate perk I noticed was that this game is definitely optimized for low powered rigs (Which I owned when I started playing). You can tweak settings in the game files that make the game look like a Van Gogh painting but run at a nice FPS.
I break this review into another paragraph to explain the most crucial and amazing feature in this game which I will call "The  Stress Aspect". Now some of those who have played either the mod or the standalone game can attest to the pure stress you get when you so much as lay eyes on another nhuman player. After spending hours of acquiring food, tools, weapons, and other tools essential to your survival you're finally put to the test when you see a player with an equal or greater amount and quality of equipment than you currently possess and you're in the perfect position to sucker punch him and steal it all. But as soon as you see him you jump in surpise! Your hearbeat increases and your palms sweat as you try and calm yourself down and decide carefully how to attack this armed opponent you have stumbled across.
Cutting it off there I want to say that this is my experience, I've had friends who can keep their cool in any situation and some who just lose their absolute♥♥♥♥♥♥at the mere sight of another player with any form of weaponry. This game, as the creator intended it to be, was basically a huge experiment of how people would deal with an apocalypse scenario. Would they hide out in the city or flee to the country side? Would they be ruthless bandits or would they lend a helping hand? This is the great social experiment that is DayZ. This game is basically an amazing experience and will leave you with many tales of firefights, naked weirdos, and intense situations.

I have no words. There are no words to describe the masterpiece that is this game. Whether you're going down the surprisingly dark path that is the genocide run or embracing the pacifistic path, this is a game that will grab you by the heart and soul. Never once before have I actually cared about the NPC's in a game. Never once before have I gone down the evil road in a morally split game and actually, legitimately given up - not because of difficulty, but because I just felt so bad.
And never, EVER before have I thought "I am willing to petition to ADD DLC to a game just to save one more character." To those who have seen the true ending to this game... you know who I'm talking about.
In an industry that is becoming more and more obsessed with war and violence, where murder is justified and revenge glorified, Undertale is a sharp, emotional, and unbelievably immersive contrast. For the first time in years, I have gone through a game and come out of it having learned something - not in an academic sense, but in a personal sense. So many games have tried to do this, to help the player develop as a person alongside the character, but this is the first time I have ever seen such a goal fully realized.
Undertale isn't just a story about a land of monsters, it's about humans as well - showing that human nature and violence are not one in the same and that, given enough hope, effort, and determination, it is indeed possible to achieve peace. It is not an easy road, and often not even a road that some agree with, but it is still possible.
If you are looking for a fun and engaging game, buy Undertale. If you are looking for an incredibly emotional experience, buy Undertale. If you are looking for a story that will be not only memorable but inspirational, buy Undertale. If you have never, ever once played a video game and want to start off with the best possible experience to ever grace your screen, buy Undertale.
You may end up regretting HOW you play the game, but you will NEVER regret playing it.

This game is amazing.
I appreciate the various retro art styles, you can see an Apple II type style in-battle, and a sort of SNES/NES-esque style in the over world.
The characters, while not being overly thought out or dissected, are easily acquainted with and you can hardly help but seem to like every one of them for their quirky, humorous natures.
Battles, while being randomly chosen after a set number of steps which is a primitive way of doing encounters, are still fun despite this face. The music you have while fighting is upbeat when appropriate and sometimes dramatic and suspenseful. Which only adds to the dodging sort of mini game you play while enemies take their turns in battle.
The story is really good, if you can get into it and appreciate it. Which in certain circumstances could be a good OR a bad thing. You're a human who has fallen down into the perilous Mt. Ebott, you don't know why you are here not, but it seems like it was meant to be. You're definetly not the first human to fall down, but you'll be damned before you don't become the first to escape alive, no matter if you are a violent psychopath or kind and caring type.
If you love RPG's with an engaging story, crazy and addictive music, enjoyable bullet dodging scenarios, and a healthy combination of smiles and tears, Undertale is for you.

I was aware that this is an early access when I got the game. For me, the idea of an early access games is about the game developing new features and having occasional bugs here and there... But DayZ is so clunky I don't see it getting anywhere in near future. Maybe in 2-3 years something good will come out of this game. The engine seems very far from stable... Game runs choppy as hell on medium settings, even if I should be able to run it maxed out with no problems... Not to mention graphical artifacts I've had, like blinking textures. As for the gamplay itself,  running around a ghost town for over half an hour, I've just seen 1-2 zombies and no players (although I've joined a populated server). Game doesn't give any task to the player, there's no real threat... Survival seems far too easy... All you can do is walk aroun and look for stuff... The design of the interiors of the buildings leaves much to be desired. You'd imagine there'd be lots of trash, furniture, but they're mostly so empty with single items you can pick up spawned here and there... I don't know, it just looks wrong to me. I love post apocalypse, I love zombies, I love survival games. But DayZ really disappoints me. And as I said before, I know this is an early access game, but from what I've seen, I don't see any real hope for this game. And I'd actually be happy if I'm wrong and this game turns out to be amazing in future. We'll have to wait and see.

But DayZ is so clunky I don't see it getting anywhere in near future. Maybe in 2-3 years something good will come out of this game. The engine seems very far from stable... This game is amazing.
I appreciate the various retro art styles, you can see an Apple II type style in-battle, and a sort of SNES/NES-esque style in the over world.
The characters, while not being overly thought out or dissected, are easily acquainted with and you can hardly help but seem to like every one of them for their quirky, humorous natures.

The music you have while fighting is upbeat when appropriate and sometimes dramatic and suspenseful. Which only adds to the dodging sort of mini game you play while enemies take their turns in battle.
The story is really good, if you can get into it and appreciate it. Which in certain circumstances could be a good OR a bad thing. You're a human who has fallen down into the perilous Mt. You're definetly not the first human to fall down, but you'll be damned before you don't become the first to escape alive, no matter if you are a violent psychopath or kind and caring type.
If you love RPG's with an engaging story, crazy and addictive music, enjoyable bullet dodging scenarios, and a healthy combination of smiles and tears, Undertale is for you.

I have no words. There are no words to describe the masterpiece that is this game. Whether you're going down the surprisingly dark path that is the genocide run or embracing the pacifistic path, this is a game that will grab you by the heart and soul. Never once before have I actually cared about the NPC's in a game. Never once before have I gone down the evil road in a morally split game and actually, legitimately given up - not because of difficulty, but because I just felt so bad.
And never, EVER before have I thought "I am willing to petition to ADD DLC to a game just to save one more character." To those who have seen the true ending to this game... you know who I'm talking about.
In an industry that is becoming more and more obsessed with war and violence, where murder is justified and revenge glorified, Undertale is a sharp, emotional, and unbelievably immersive contrast. For the first time in years, I have gone through a game and come out of it having learned something - not in an academic sense, but in a personal sense. So many games have tried to do this, to help the player develop as a person alongside the character, but this is the first time I have ever seen such a goal fully realized.
Undertale isn't just a story about a land of monsters, it's about humans as well - showing that human nature and violence are not one in the same and that, given enough hope, effort, and determination, it is indeed possible to achieve peace. It is not an easy road, and often not even a road that some agree with, but it is still possible.
If you are looking for a fun and engaging game, buy Undertale. If you are looking for an incredibly emotional experience, buy Undertale. If you are looking for a story that will be not only memorable but inspirational, buy Undertale. If you have never, ever once played a video game and want to start off with the best possible experience to ever grace your screen, buy Undertale.
You may end up regretting HOW you play the game, but you will NEVER regret playing it.

I'm going to go a bit off topic to start off with but hear me out. I have loved and played games since I was 5 years old, the age I got a chance to play on the n64. I have broadened my horizons since then, playing titles from all kinds of consoles from nintendo, sony, and microsoft, both mobile and home. I picked up PC gaming really early in my youth playing games like Warcraft III, Vampire the Masquerade, but never was I serious about it until my buddy kyle showed me steam. My first steam game was the binding of issac and it was around that time I realized that games didn't need the best graphics to be spectacular. One game series had the best of both worlds, Kingdom hearts. This game was spread amongst many consoles and mobile devices and I brought myself to play them all, the story, gameplay and lovable characters (and enemies) made the game all worthwhile. When I first heard of Undertale, I was one of those "oh look, another Earthbound/Mother clone that completely misses the point of the original/fails to replicate the feel of it" folks. Boy, was I wrong when I finally got to play this game. It easily falls among those games which manage to reach to me on an emotional level.
....I'm sorry. Calling Undertale "a game" would be an understatement.
Undertale is not just a game. It is an experience. An experience of thoughts, an experience of emotions. An experience of a wonderful story about loss, tragedy, family, friendship, love, self-acceptance, and DETERMINATION. A story about growing up, a story about choices, a story about one child changing the lives of complete strangers for the better. Throughout the adventure, this experience will make you laugh, will make you cry, will make you feel all kinds of emotions and all in just a span of few hours. Some characters you will most likely adore upon first meeting them, others you will grow attached to as the story progresses; even the "random encounter" creatures have their own personalities and small stories tied to them, all which you can discover as you interact with them during battles.
And this is the element which I love the most about Undertale; the interaction during battles. By performing different actions, the beings you encounter will open themselves up to you and reveal who they are, and it all pays off by the end of the adventure, because you make a connection to all of them-as I mentioned above, your very acts of kindness change the lives of these creatures in ways they couldn't possibly imagine. And in return, you gain their friendship and love. You, a human, become one of them.
What also helps with getting into the atmosphere of the game is the soundtrack, which is quite possibly one of the best I've heard in years; a collection of chiptunes, orchestral music, synth/electronic music and occasional metal/rock compositions thrown in create a wonderful mix that you will most likely listen to for days on end.
I'm not just recommending this game to everyone who hasn't tried it yet; in fact, I highly encourage them to give it a try, to dive into this adventure, and live through the experience for themselves. I did, I will never forget it, and I will never regret it.
P.S.; never gonna do Genocide Run. Ever.

Rust can be described in many ways. Fun, hard, diffrent, bad, etc. These are all good words to describe rust. Rust is like any other survival game with a few diffrent things. For one the map is huge, one of the biggest I have ever seen for it's genre. There are forests ,desserts, snowy mountains, and even just fields of nothing. It gives you the choice to build your base wherever you desire. It has great mechanics and awsome features a lot of other games don't give. You need to find certain items to learn how to craft them or even build a research bench to learn how to make game changing items. You can craft c4's, and rocket launchers, or even grenades. All of them with their own unique and diffrent design. Grenades are basically bean cans filled with gunpowder and some guns are just you hitting the end with flint. While there aren't an extremely large ammount of guns, they all do diffrent things. Although as much as this sounds fun this game has an side you wouldn't see at first. The people who play rust can only be summed up in one sentence. Complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s. Now not everyone shall be this way but you will most likely spawn 5-25 times where you just get shot or beaten by someone with a stick. You may die multiple times in a row. Then the combat is very, bad. Atleast at first it is. You could build your first little pistol sort of thing. And while you may feel empowered with it you are not. No that gun is not as good as you think. It may do less damage than a spear thrown at you. You could shoot 5 shotgun rounds from it at someone and hit them each time but they live. But they grab a bow and kill you in one hit. That leads to the major bad part about the game. If you have no friends who play rust or can't then you are immediatly screwed. Without multilple friends (around 3 or more to start) then you won't get anywhere. You could have an assault rifle but three guys with rocks come up behind you and kill you. You could have a great base which would be great with multiple people. But 3 guys with some ladders and spears come in and immediatly kill you. While this is great allowing the game to be balanced and allow anyone to win a battle it doesn't do it well. If you have spent hours in the game just for you to lose it all in minutes by some noobies then it is unfair and very frustrating. So I only reccomend this game if you have friends.

When I first heard of Undertale, I was one of those "oh look, another Earthbound/Mother clone that completely misses the point of the original/fails to replicate the feel of it" folks. Boy, was I wrong when I finally got to play this game. It easily falls among those games which manage to reach to me on an emotional level.
....I'm sorry. Calling Undertale "a game" would be an understatement.
Undertale is not just a game. It is an experience. An experience of thoughts, an experience of emotions. An experience of a wonderful story about loss, tragedy, family, friendship, love, self-acceptance, and DETERMINATION. A story about growing up, a story about choices, a story about one child changing the lives of complete strangers for the better. Throughout the adventure, this experience will make you laugh, will make you cry, will make you feel all kinds of emotions and all in just a span of few hours. Some characters you will most likely adore upon first meeting them, others you will grow attached to as the story progresses; even the "random encounter" creatures have their own personalities and small stories tied to them, all which you can discover as you interact with them during battles.
And this is the element which I love the most about Undertale; the interaction during battles. By performing different actions, the beings you encounter will open themselves up to you and reveal who they are, and it all pays off by the end of the adventure, because you make a connection to all of them-as I mentioned above, your very acts of kindness change the lives of these creatures in ways they couldn't possibly imagine. And in return, you gain their friendship and love. You, a human, become one of them.
What also helps with getting into the atmosphere of the game is the soundtrack, which is quite possibly one of the best I've heard in years; a collection of chiptunes, orchestral music, synth/electronic music and occasional metal/rock compositions thrown in create a wonderful mix that you will most likely listen to for days on end.
I'm not just recommending this game to everyone who hasn't tried it yet; in fact, I highly encourage them to give it a try, to dive into this adventure, and live through the experience for themselves. I did, I will never forget it, and I will never regret it.
P.S.; never gonna do Genocide Run. Ever.

Undertale is a charming turn-based RPG, which you should really go into with as little foreknowledge as possible. The gameplay is simple yet varied enough to keep you engaged the entire way through, and probably into a second or third playthrough as well. However, it's real strengths are in it's wide cast of excellently written characters. Even the basic enemies show tons of personality in the short amounts of screentime they have.
There is a lot more to enjoy, like the incredible soundtrack which I would almost recommend buying this game just to hear. One could also mention the sheer level of detail present in the game, which only becomes more evident the more you see of the game. Or the fact that this game is only $10 right now. Honestly, you're practically a thief for buying it.
If you still aren't convinced, there's also a free demo available. It lasts around 30 minutes, and is a pretty good indicator of whether or not Undertale is your kind of game. It comes with a "read me" file to help with any technical issues that may arise, and I highly recommend you give it a look.
TL:DR You should buy Undertale as soon as possible. Even if you already have it. It's definitely my pick for GOTY, and probably the best $10 i've ever spent.

I've played the mod for many years.  I've loved DayZ in general for many years.  My clan and myself play it on a regular basis.
The game is an Alpha.  Most people understand that.  Due to it being an alpha, the game is unfinished and is generally speaking...terrible.  Glitches aren't really too bothersome since the game is new, but the amount of toxic people in the community is absurd.  Cheaters are everywhere and LOVE to ruin your day.
Just spent 8 hours getting that ghille suit? Ha, some guy teleports to you and kills you.  Nothing you can do.
Just spent par time gathering that loudout?  Nope.  Guy literally just took it off your body from a mile away.
The game is broken, which is fine.  The players who chose to play it, however, make it absolutely unplayable.  The devs don't seem to make anti-cheat a priority.
Now to be fair, I would normally say the game isn't about the loot; It's about the experience.  I enjoy running around towns with baseball bats and hitting people just as much as being a militant fighting in uncommon areas.  However, the experience is also ruined by people who cheat.  This game would be so good, so dang good f it wasn't for the cheaters who are winning by a longshot.
And for those of you that say I'm just giving the cheaters the attention they want: You're right.  But leaving it unmentioned is useless to those that may be purchasing the game.  To anyone wanting to purchase a zombie survival game, look into something else until this is at least kind of playable.

It's going to be alpha forever.  Don't believe it?  Check the things listed in the changelog.  Most of it is fixing typos and cosmetic issues.  A few thigns like "Polish this " or "Redo that"  All minor things and all cosmetic.  Meanwhile the game is fundamentally broken.  T
Changelog shows they added another zombie, yet the zombie mechanics...one of the most important aspects of a zombie apocalypse simulator, are broken.  Their changelog shows that it's much easier to fill up the changelog with non-value added tasks than to fix the game.
In a zombie apocalypse...there are what?  A dozen zombies?  5 or 6 per city.  And even then, killing them with a melee weapon?  It's man vs game interface requiring a bizarre mix of unintuiive aiming and completely indecipherable (sp?) attack distances.

The author of this game had a great concept for a game. In fact, when I heard about it, I was so excited I immediately purchased it. "There's a game where you can actually reason with your foes and fighting them isn't the only option? Wow! This will be great! I'm going to give this to my kids to play!" Sadly, the implementation of this game does not live up to the promise of its high concept.
Imagine a classic console RPG like FF7. You walk along and suddenly you get sucked into a random encounter. Your turn comes up and you have a list of actions to take. You can attack with your weapon, you could use a "special attack", you can use an item, you can study your foe to determine a weakness, you can cast a spell, and so on. Now imagine that this is a game like Mortal Kombat where, after you beat them down enough, your opponent gets stunned and dizzy. Then they're vulnerable to your "finishing move". Hit them with that and the fight's over. You win!
From that starting point, describing the actual gameplay of Undertale is very easy. Just cross out "special attack" and write "comfort". Cross out "finishing move" and write "spare". Congratulations, you just perfectly captured the mechanism through which "you don't have to kill anyone" in Undertale.
Changing the name of an action in the menu does not magically transform this into a game of meaningful choices. You still have no opportunity to negotiate with enemies. You still have no opportunity to try & go around or otherwise avoid a potential conflict. You still have no opportunity to learn why the enemy is so keen on killing you or what you might be able to do to resolve your differences. Nope, just hit them with your special move until they're dizzy, then FINISH THEM!
Ratings:
Concept?   Excellent!
Marketing and Hype?   Very effective!
Delivering on the Promise?   I want my money back. :(

After enjoying this game for some time and then reading people sh*t on this game, I think I needed to clear somew things up.
ONe thing that trumps most people's complaints is this: This game in pre-alpha. Think about that for a second. You know another game that was released in stages like this? Minecraft. How was minecrsaft different in Pre-aplha? Survival mode and any sort of AI's did not exist. And people can't ignore this fact either. Everytime you turn this game you have to say that you understand that this is an extremly early build, but in it's current state, it functions fairly well. Items spawn, zombies AGRESSIVELY attack players, and will chase them from one town to the next, easily auto-tracking them, guns work well, people can easily interact even if they speak a different language. For as early as this game is in DEV. it functions well enough that it's playable and even enjoyable.
Another thing that turns people away are people complaining about "game crashing glitches" and "Instant kill hackers" In my 40+ hours, I've found three glictches, two of which were items clipping into a surface and I couldn't pick them up, an the other was I droppped an item and it appeared in the next room over. I have never been killed by a player that was unreasonable. One was a headshot with a nagnum, another was I was clubbed to death, and the other the guy emptied an entire mag of 7.62's into me, more than reasonable cause of death.
While this game has things that need to be polished, it is worth the time to play it and get use to the mechanics and have a blast with some friends or make new ones.

The author of this game had a great concept for a game. In fact, when I heard about it, I was so excited I immediately purchased it. "There's a game where you can actually reason with your foes and fighting them isn't the only option? Wow! This will be great! I'm going to give this to my kids to play!" Sadly, the implementation of this game does not live up to the promise of its high concept.
Imagine a classic console RPG like FF7. You walk along and suddenly you get sucked into a random encounter. Your turn comes up and you have a list of actions to take. You can attack with your weapon, you could use a "special attack", you can use an item, you can study your foe to determine a weakness, you can cast a spell, and so on. Now imagine that this is a game like Mortal Kombat where, after you beat them down enough, your opponent gets stunned and dizzy. Then they're vulnerable to your "finishing move". Hit them with that and the fight's over. You win!
From that starting point, describing the actual gameplay of Undertale is very easy. Just cross out "special attack" and write "comfort". Cross out "finishing move" and write "spare". Congratulations, you just perfectly captured the mechanism through which "you don't have to kill anyone" in Undertale.
Changing the name of an action in the menu does not magically transform this into a game of meaningful choices. You still have no opportunity to negotiate with enemies. You still have no opportunity to try & go around or otherwise avoid a potential conflict. You still have no opportunity to learn why the enemy is so keen on killing you or what you might be able to do to resolve your differences. Nope, just hit them with your special move until they're dizzy, then FINISH THEM!
Ratings:
Concept?   Excellent!
Marketing and Hype?   Very effective!
Delivering on the Promise?   I want my money back. :(

Rust is both the best and worst game ever all at the same time. It provides you with a capable building platform similar to minecraft and a beautiful world to survive in and a huge community of players. While these things are great they also are the downside to themselves. The building mechanics are decent but not varied enough and limited for building components. There isn't much else to do but build simple structures and craft.  While there is huge community of players, many of them are not friendly even if they say they are and many of them are going to immediately kill you. That's just how it is. I have also watched players completely quit rust and never play again because of it. You work at your structure for hours and loose everything cause you log off and aren't there to defend it.
All of that put aside. I still really, really enjoy Rust. Even when I spend 20 hrs mining resources to have someone raid it and take it all away from me. Why would I enjoy this you say? Because that's how life is. You work really hard for things and struggle to make friends and trust people.  Even when you do make friends and are all working to gether it can still be hard and you have to work and fight for eveything you have. Then sometimes, maybe even several times, you will lose a lot. Maybe even everything. But that's how life just works. Then when you log off you have to go to work and school and basically do the exact same thing. And in the end things don't always work out as planned or you have to lose out on some things. Which is why I will never hate Rust even though it can very greatly frustrate me. Because of how it just so very closely mimics the real world. A very blood thirsty and impulsive world.
What does all this mean for you as the player looking to buy this reading this review? It means you should really only buy this game if you are ready to struggle tooth and nail for every scrap of material you have and then possible loose it. You can make friends, but it will be equally as hard. The best thing to think about when purchasing this is, 'Will you be able to make the game enjoyable for yourself if you get it?' Because that's what this game relies upon, is how you can make it fun for yourself while struggling against overwhelming odds.
Really think about it cause it will be a waste to spend $20, get mad, never play again. Alot of people play for ten minutes, post a review that says naked hits rocks. 10-10. It's sounds fun and funny and great. Then you play and you realize that it's not all fun in games. You will have to dedicate some time to this when you want to play. When you're not playing you have to realize that everything you have is at jeopardy. When you take a break from the game for any amount of time;days, weeks, etc. You will have to be willing to most likely give up all your work and start over because as the days go by all of your creations are exposed and at risk. People will try and raid them and sometimes they will succeed. The longer you wait to play again the higher the chance of a raid on your stuff.One thing you also really have to realize is this game is not updated very often since he is working on another much larger ip.
All that being said. I would totally give this game a 9-10. I really do enjoy it even when it's rough. I would recommend it to anyone who is willing and patient enough to play.

(DISCLAIMER) This game was not on steam when i played it the most. I would say i really have over 70 hours on this game. Core gameplay has not really changed
Gameplay
You start naked, in the woods, with a rock. Your goal is to survive. All the elements in survival games are here. (eating, drinking, shelter temperature etc) Of course with you on either a procedurally generated map or a set one, you've got other players. Player interaction really is the core meat of the game. You spawn and if you manage to get ahold of stuff before being bludgeoned by a rock, the next step logically is to slaughter your fellow man and take his things. On the way you will find things such as but not limited to: Naked men with rocks, racism, people with guns that do not care that you only have a rock, signs that dipicts male anatomy, and my favourite, black people.
Ok that all sounds well and good right? Not really. My main gripe with this game is how slow a start it has. That's not so bad, however late game things pick up to go very, very fast so your progression in this game is way up and down. Actually getting to a point where you have an established base and enough things that if you die you can recover easily, is difficult. Not all that it is functionally hard, but more so that it takes a long time. My experience is mostly playing with two or three people, and that certainley makes it easier, however it doesn't really eliminate the grind.
I would say that playing by yourself is a downright waste of time because of how ridiculously easy it is too lose hours of progress. As i said, the game is very slow paced at the beginning and then once you get guns and a base, things go very fast. There are many things that will stop from getting to that point. Theres a lot of things in the world to make things go fast, like rad zones and other peoples stuff. But all of those are artificially walled of when you have nothing. Walking into a rad zone is basically suicide because you can not really stay in there long enough to get what you need without dying from radiation. For some reason in new rust we have snow, which is just pure bull. unless you have clothes then you will freeze very easily. And on top of all the ridiculous enviromental hazards, players are also a huge hazard. Since once you actually have things the only thing to do is kill others, that's all they do. You will be killed by other players frequently.
So basically the game is just hard?
While the game is really challenging it doesn't feel "right" when you die, most of the time you will feel cheated. And be demotivated because you just spent 45 minutes trying to get established only to spend just a little too much time in a rad zone. And then you might spawn in an area where you can't get back to where you were because snow is everywhere. the only time i ever kind of enjoy the process of dying is when i'm fighting other players in a base raid. You will be doing a lot of building in rust. It is very fun. You would surprised at the ways people try to defend themselves. This is also where the game picks up a lot. Once you put down a simple sleeping bag, you can spawn at it. So once you have a base you can basically just spawn at home and as long as you have some gear in your house you're pretty much good to go. So base raiding happens a lot. That's really fun with your friends. By yourself, not so much. having someone to back you up is pretty much essential. So once you get to that point the game becomes loads of fun provided you have people to play with. One base can really put you far ahead of the competition. On the flip side, actually getting to this point really blows. To the point where i would seriously not recommend this game based on the amount of crap in between the fun and the start.
After a while playing this game you really figure out how tedious and linear the game feels. Even when you are playing with friends the game sucks to get started, and because of how terrible trying to do that without any, i don't recommend this game.
Theres really only one way the game goes from that start
Tryhard to get whatever you can
Die a lot for stupid reasons
Killed by snow
Killed by water
Killed by rock to head
Killed by bullet to head
Killed by radiation
Finally get a house and some stuff
Have fun!
Raided by dudes before you can defend yourself
Raided by dudes who bested you
Log off and get raided
Basically any death after getting established starts the whole process of grinding to get everthing again.
It makes starting a game really intimidating. I know that i'll have too make some dumb shack behind a boulder and kill pigs until i can make a jacket so i don't freeze to death trying to get through the snow. Or run in and out of a radzone trying to scavenge before radiation kills me in two minutes.
You see where i'm going with this? Theres way too much maintenance to get to a point where the game is actually fun, and when you get there it's pretty much 100% going to be gone when you log off. Also any point where your base is raided is basically game over. You can't really recover from having all your stuff taken without starting from the bottom. The game can be a lot of fun, but after a while of playing, the fun kinda wheres off when you realize that your stuff will be gone when you log on tommorow. Or when you get raided while online that the intimidating fact that you have to do everything over again will make you close the game. Bottom line here: If you decide to buy it, for the love of god play with as many people as possible to make things go faster.
Short Condensed Pros/Cons
Pros
(Provided you have stuff)
- Very fun pvp and base raiding
- Lots of fun with friends
- Great base building
- Lots of cool stuff to craft
- Getting picked on because your character model is black
really makes you fear the white man
Cons
- Progression to the point of fun is painfully slow
- The difficulty in some parts feels artificial and gimicky
(radiation, snow, water temperature, limits where you go and kills fast)
- Playing solo is a complete waste of time
- The pace at which you progress is stupidly slow and then very fast
- PvP is only fun/possible when you have guns and a base
- Death and raids on you can completley demotivate you from playing because of grind
- The anti cheat is a joke. Hackers are common
Final thoughts
I don't recommend this game now and i don't feel as if the gameplay will change enough in the future to make me reconsider that. The game is fun at times when you get going, until you realize the sinking feeling of apprehension you get after dying or before starting a game is not just "aww i died" or "oh this gonna be hard" its more because you know how much bull is inbetween you and your fun with this game. Enough to make you not want to play.
Early access - so things are bound to change. I don't think they will enough for me to recommend this game.
Graphics are fantastic, but if you ever see anyone with anything other than a rock you die.
all round a good game, one of the better survival games i have played.

More importantly, a game which seems silly on the outside was actually able to change how I think and feel about both the world around me, and myself.

As of Jan 2015 this is probably just about the least user friendly/worst game Ive ever played.
As soon as you open the game it displays in some miniscule resolution like 640, like how games that are 15 years old used to (is it that hard to auto detect res?), then when you try to select a res thats more fitting for the 21st century, there is no such option.  So after googling for 'dayz 1440/1080' - and its never a good thing to have to google to set the damn res - youll find that you have to tell the game what aspect ratio youre using which is buried under a couple of other menu.  At this point, make sure you have all of your other setting as you want them cos if you need to change them then youll be back to 640 res until you go set the aspect ratio yet again.
Finally youll get into the game, then run forwards and find a deserted barn, run up the stairs and all is well.  Then on the way down the stairs you may happen to run off the side of the stairs and drop the height of about 3 steps - then all youll be able to do is crawl, as in this farce if the player leaves the ground for more than a tenth of a second they will suffer lumb damage similar to that of a spaceman jettisoning a space shuttle just after re-entry into the earths atmosphere and then free-falling to the ground.
In any normal game thats been in development for longer than about 10 mins, expecially one which constantly uses its early-access shield to justify it being bug-ridden trash this wouldnt be a problem as youd just pull down a console and suicide or something, but oh-no, not in this game.  Instead youll have to crawl around until you can find a building high enough to throw yourself off to suicide.
But in the total lack of such a building at this point, theres a nearby shed that might have something in that can be used tokill yourself, so over you crawl and 5 mins later youve made the 10 meter distance and opened the shed door.  Now you cant actually crawl in.  The 1 centimeter high doorframe prevents you from crawling over it.  After randomly spamming standup and lunge, you might eventually manage to overcome this near-insurmountable beometh of a challenge and be in the shed.  Or tomb as it would be more accurately called, cos gl getting out of it as now youll be stuck on the side door frame as well as the miniscule bottom edge.
The game constantly puts up messages like 'You are cooling off', 'Your foot hurts', I kept waiting for a more accurate one like 'You should never have got this game'.
The early-access shield only goes so far, bugs/lack of content.. fine, to be expected.  But a game which has all of these and yet no method to actually counter them?  It seems like the devs have spent more time making things that can be used to sell the game rather than making thigs that make it usable.
If they were building a road, it would be lined with stores and signs and lots of nice looking things, but rather than asphalt the surface would be made of stone and caltrops.
The lack of vital things like a method of not having to just afk so you starve to death is inexcusible when the games in such an unplayable state.  Avoid, avoid at all costs.

Just got the game on the 2014 holiday sale.  I had looked into it first and knew it was going to be pretty intense and it is.  There are a ton of options in this open world game, which might seem daunting and complicated, but focus on staying alive for starters.  I'd suggest checking out some youtube videos on it to see if it's something you'd be interested in it.  There are a lot of ways to play it, a lot of people are bandits who go around and hold up or kill people for their stuff, and survive in the zombie infested world doing that.  It's not a great way to live, I don't just mean morally, but you'll make a lot of enemies, and make a lot of other sociopaths who will attemp to emulate you because that's their view of the world.  There is a chance you'll wind up having that newbie you just killed respawn not to far away from you, pick up the nearest hammer, and come break your arms, like I did to someone who killed me, and broken arms are a fate worse then death as you won't be able to interact with a damn thing or defend yourself from a single zombie.
Try to play this game with friends, both for protection, and your sanity.  You get very paranoid being out on your own.  For all of that I'm really starting to like this game.  There is a lot to learn and do, it only takes a little guidance to get you started and then you'll begin figuring things out for yourself.  You can join a PVE server like I did recently to help you learn the basics and give you a chance to explore.

Honestly, just play the mod for Arma II. I'm not going to complain about the bugs since they haven't really annoyed me or made the game unplayable, but some of the core features are just insane.
It rained. I got wet. I got cold. I became frozen and hypothermic. Even after getting dry clothes as well as wringing out my old ones and finding a dry place, still cold. Seems that you HAVE to make a fire to not get cold, even if you find a puffy winter jacket. Stupid. For fires you need an axe and matches (I think), then you get wood. That part is realistic, but the instant cold from the lethal rain is not. That's a dumb feature.
You start the game hungry. That's fine, except for the fact that in 45 minutes of going through buildings I didn't find any food.
If you have a melee weapon and you want to take down a zombie, just give up, because you're dead. They'll hit you once and you'll bleed out and die, end of story. At least in the mod bandages were easy to come by, so getting hit wasn't a big deal. It was actually possible to kill a zombie with an axe without getting hit at all. Can't do that in this game. Run if you encounter a zombie because apparently they have bear claws that will rip you to shreds.
I've played the mod for several hours and would rather play that than this game, despite all the new stuff they've added. The devs attempt at realism is laughable.

Pros
- Long amounts of playtime
- Development map looks amazing
- Already has the feels of a complete game
- You can tie people up and make them drink bleach.
Cons
- As with all early access, has its fair share of bugs
- Movement/melee attacks sometimes leave a lot to be desired
- Being tied up and fed bleach.

While everyone screams Fallout 4 and Witcher 3 as 2015's GOTY, I sit here with Undertale. This is easily my GOTY. A spiritual successor of sorts to the Mother series, Undertale is a gimmicky RPG with pulling points being it's bullet hell style combat system and the fact that you don't have actually have to kill any enemy you come across. But beyond that, Undertale is a very finely crafted game. Toby Fox put every last ounce of his love into this masterpiece.
Pros
- Incredibly catchy soundtrack
- Unique twist to RPG combat
- Fantastic memorable characters
- The game actually remembers what you do in future playthroughs
- Tons of replayability
- You can date a skeleton
- Surprisingly deep and convoluted story with amazing morality system
Cons
- The game is pretty short (my first playthrough took about 8 hours, but I have seen runs only lasting 2 hours)
That's seriously the only con I can think of off the top of my head. Undertale is a game you won't regret buying and playing. I assure you. It met all my standards and filled me with determination.

This game is a 2 sided game. On one hand, while the game play is quite enjoyable, more often than not, there are still issues, a prominent one being that zombies clip through walls/floor/etc, and other minor bugs. While still in alpha, there seems to be very slow progression of these bugfixes, considering the first issue I pointed out was a day-1 issue. This is compounded by what seems to be conflicting interests, as instead of fixing game problems they work on other things, like new weapons or clothing or mechanics. This would be fine if not for the other issues going seemingly untouched, or minor improvements. Moving on, hacking is a MASSIVE ISSUE. Battleeye does not do a good job of detecting or punishing cheaters, and the bans are not IP. While IP banning has its flaws, it is still more effective.  Another thing to look it is the potential "moneygrabbing" by the developers, chiefly Dean "Rocket" Hall, after an incredible amount of sales and profit, is abandoning the game development, after having created it, and not making much progress into developing it beyond the state it started in. Also, the price was raised to 35$ during the steam winter sale, then put on a 15% discount, moving the price down to what it was before, but that is just an effort to make you think you're getting a "deal" on the game when rather before this was the normal price.
TL;DR
Game is good, fun, but still has major "ironing out" to do.
My advice? Play the Dayz mod for arma 2 or Arma 3's Breaking point, do not buy.
