In Undertale, you play as this young character who fell into the cave into a worlds under a world. Your quest is to find a way back home and during your journey, you meet these peeps that become your friends, and those friends can be memorable. During your journey, you can also find some humor in the game as it progresses, BUT YOUR CHOICES CAN AFFECT THE GAMEPLAY BY ALOT. When you finally reach the end you have to make a choice to fight the "final" boss, but after that, THERE IS A PLOT TWIST. The story line can affect the ending when you DID or DIDN'T KILL. When you made the right choice, lets just say, the "true ending" will really get you. TRUST ME, It did.
My opinion of this game is that this game is a game that is well worth playing. You get to meet friends that you will remember. The story line is really good, the music is really nice, and the graphics ARE NOT REAL, but its retro and it fits well. Rust has to be one of my favorite games I've played on Steam.  That being said, it is NOT all fun and games.  If you're looking for something to hold your hand and ease you into the experience, as I'm sure you already know Rust is not for you.  You're immediately thrown into a pot of complete social chaos, which I can easily say makes the game.  You really never know what you'll run into with the endless number of wackjobs and jokers playing alongside you.  Without any friends to play with you may not survive the experience.  To be quite honest you'll probably find the game quite boring and most likely rage quit due to hours of time wasted only to be brutally murdered, raided, etc due to lack of protection...  But once you do get a crew going, this game can be a hell of a lot of fun (which my hundreds of hours of gameplay can attest to.)
-Great, hilarious, downright awesome player interaction
-Beautiful game
-Updated weekly with great new stuff!
-Also A LOT of terribly rude, hair-tearing and rage-inducing player interaction
-No fun without friends (that's to be expected)
-Steals hours upon hours of your life, both good and bad
In the end, Rust is basically what you make of it.  If you're the type who enjoys smashing your expensive computer hardware when upset...  Probably not the game for you.  However, if you've got a few buddies to play with and think you can take a bit of a beating, then in my opinion the game is
worth it.  I'll put it this way - I've had countless experiences in Rust; both good and bad; and I honestly only remember the good.  So that's why I recommend Rust 100%.  Thanks for reading my review.

I'm going to have to go against the tide here and say that Rust was something of a disappointment for me. Although there are some verifiably comical moments to be had (such as being stoned to death by someone in the buff upon attempting to purloin their torch as they sleep), there unfortunately isn't a lot of substance beyond that.
First is the incessant crashing to desktop. Okay, okay, I know it's an alpha and such things are to be expected, but Rust is probably the first game I've played that does it literally every twenty minutes. I've been playing for less than an hour and the game crashed three times in that short period. And just to rub salt in my eyes, I'll find that once I've returned to the server to start playing again, everything I've spent the past half-hour gathering has been robbed by a passer-by, putting me straight back to square one.
Speaking of "gathering", survival is extremely difficult even for a walking simulator (not least because of the looming threat of crashing to desktop and having everything you own burgled). Getting off of the beach where you first spawn is easy enough, but after that it just becomes a pain: usually the biggest threat in a walking-sim is having your food stolen by a pack of bandits, but in Rust the issue lies in getting food in the first instance. My first thought was to harvest fruits and the like, of which there are precisely none in the starting area. Hunting is also frustrating, especially given that the first proper weapon you get in the game will barely tickle the creature being hunted, which is also faster than you. Fishing is also a non-thing, so literally the only way for a newbag to procure food and drink (here I should think I could drink from the river, but apparently not...) is to overpower some unsuspecting adventurer and rob his stuff. Or, if he has no food, eat
instead (cannibalism is a thing in Rust).
So we move on to what I found to be the only good thing about Rust (and let's face it, the overwhelming majority of positive reviews here are about this), that being the fact that one can strut around in one's birthday suit and beat one another to death with rocks. However, other than this bit of humour, the game has little else to offer in the field of actual gameplay. Like I said, I've only played for an hour or so, and I'll probably play it a little more to see if it gets any better (in which circumstance I'll write a considerably less damning review). But, frankly, I don't have a very good first impression of Rust.

You know what? I bought this game a while back due to the hilarious reviews of it. But in reality there is nothing in this game that makes it worth $30. It's glitchy as hell, and there is no real gameplay. There are > 100,000 reviews for it on Steam, assuming every reviewer had paid $30, that gives the devs > $3,000,000. With all that revenue they still haven't managed to create a functional game.

Bottom line: I got my money's worth but I also don't mind throwing away my money at short-lived experiences. Once I got the basic experience down, I never played the game again.
I love survival games and DayZ had a ton of hype behind it when I bought it. I played for about a week with a friend (this is important) and had some decent fun.
In retrospect, the fun came from the simple goal of surviving long enough to meet up with my friend, which is a pretty lame way to have fun. That said, fun is fun and those couple of hours were simple fun. Being on Skype with my friend was a huge plus to this experience. If this is all you're looking for and money isn't an issue, give it a shot.
As the initial "cool" factor started to wear off and my friend stopped playing (a few days into buying the game), I began to realize how hollow this game really was, even though it was in alpha. There's something beyond optimization, better graphics and general gameplay mechanics that DayZ was missing; something that can't really be fixed by its final release.
DayZ is an empty world with some survival elements where your only real enemy/friend is the community. As it stands, the community is pretty unbalanced and full of griefers. If you like cut-throat communties, maybe this is your game.
If you're looking for a cool experience where you really feel like you're surviving with a dozen other humans in a world infected by zombies, this game isn't it unless you've got a bunch of friends who play.
VERDICT: Don't buy it at its retail price. Its fun with a friend for a while but it becomes stale quickly.

This is a game that is dangerously close to overhype for some people, so I'm going to try to keep this very simple.
This game is made for people who :
-Grew up with SNES-era RPGs, especially (but not limited to) the Mother/Earthbound series
-Appreciate well-designed and well-written characters
-Enjoy (or at least are willing to put up with) quirky humor in a game
-Find meta-commentary on the RPG genre interesting (or at least tolerable)
-Are willing to have their emotions tugged on
-Are looking for a unique twist on the normal JRPG gameplay style
-Enjoy catchy chiptune-esque music
-Want to date a skeleton
If at least two of the above apply to you, you'll get at least a little (and probably far more than that) enjoyment out of Undertale.  Even if they don't apply, I strongly recommend at least grabbing the free demo and giving it a shot.  You might find yourself surprised and wanting more.

I bought this game when it got released as a zombie game in early access, over a year ago. And the game is still early access and in alpha.
BASIC OVERVIEW:
Rust is a survival game that features scavenging, schematics, buildings and plenty of PvP situations. You start with a simple rock which can be used to gather modicum amounts of rock and wood. It's shining point lies in the ability to build your own base which is fairly innovative and really easy to use.
This review will mostly contain negative remarks from someone whom is basing a lot of it upon first impression, with a moderate amount of research into the background of the gameplay and development.
GAMEPLAY:
I'll admit that there has been small improvements here and there, but overall it still runs horribly on certain specs (mine included, I can't play above lowest graphics without the game lagging out) and a part of improved building and crafting, there hasn't really been any update of note.
As it is right now the only real enjoyment you can get out of this game is if you're as toxic as most of the people on the official server chats or if you're part of a large, geared group that have no problems in running raids.
On top of this, the game is riddled with graphical bugs, animals that glitch out, runs around underwater, players using the wrong animations when holding certain things, or sometimes flat out the items holding in their hands being way out of place.
TECHNICAL:
My main issue however is that I question the motivation and planning of the developers. As I said this game was released over a year ago and it is still Early Access, still Alpha, and the overall gameplay has seen changes (such as upped graphics) but nothing that redefines the game. They also revamped the entire theme of the game (from Zombie Survival to PvP Survival, scrapping the entire zombie concept) AFTER releasing early access. Which is a questionable act from the developers part, and a huge issue for people who got a completely false description of the game early on.
On top of this, the menu design is incredibly lazy. There is no in-game options screen. When you start the game, you get a launcher with some basic options (change resolution, apply window-mode) but little else. There is not even an option either in-game or in the launcher to change the game's volume, forcing you to alter it on your own computer.
Final verdict:
Be careful if you intend to purchase this game. It's been in Early Access & Alpha for over a year without major development, got visual glitches here and there and the enjoyment is mostly limited to groups of players. There are also cases of lazy design, which might not matter much but it shows a lot about the development of the game and time taken in consideration.

I love survival games and DayZ had a ton of hype behind it when I bought it. I played for about a week with a friend (this is important) and had some decent fun.

There's something beyond optimization, better graphics and general gameplay mechanics that DayZ was missing; something that can't really be fixed by its final release.
DayZ is an empty world with some survival elements where your only real enemy/friend is the community. As it stands, the community is pretty unbalanced and full of griefers. If you like cut-throat communties, maybe this is your game.
If you're looking for a cool experience where you really feel like you're surviving with a dozen other humans in a world infected by zombies, this game isn't it unless you've got a bunch of friends who play.
VERDICT: Don't buy it at its retail price. Its fun with a friend for a while but it becomes stale quickly.

Normally, I do a "pros/cons" type of review. I am not doing this for Undertale. Because there ARE no cons. I'll try to keep it as spoiler-free as possible.
The music: Just pure greatness. Each song is catchy, some are emotional, some make you want to dance, others are fun to listen to for motivation. For every character, place, or occasion, there will be the perfect tune for everything.
The characters: The best group of video game characters I have seen in years. They all have unique designs, personalities, and even different talking sounds. They feel like you are right there in the game, next to them, like they're your friends, or even family.
The gameplay: What makes Undertale so special. You don't have to hurt anyone in battles, unless you want to. You don't have to backtrack, unless you want to, i.e for different events or wanting to see scenery again. You don't have to farm for money/EXP, unless you want to. The whole game is whatever YOU want it to be. It's YOUR choice of what you want to happen. Your choices actually matter. (Unlike Telltale...)
The story: So beautiful, it will make the tears flow. From the very beginning with Toriel to the very end with Asgore, each twist and turn is placed so delicately, you will love each one. There are a total of, I believe, 4 endings to the game. Each one is completely different, with it's own feels. Even resetting the game to get another ending is hard to do.
The graphics: If you SERIOUSLY need to know about the graphics before getting this incredible game, shame on you.
This is the perfect game to me. It was always Portal 2, but then this game came. I had never been so emotionally moved by a game so tiny. Every single element of this absolute beauty is just perfect. Fallout 4 and Black Ops III are not Game Of The Year 2015, it's this.
My final rating for Undertale is 11/10. You need this game. NOW.

Maybe I should actually elaborate on this...
Undertale is a pretty unique RPG. Depending on how you play it, it can be funny, sad, scary, or just about anything in between. The breadth of this game's tone is actually quite astounding, and only one of the many great things about it. I found myself way more engaged in this game's setting, story, and characters than any other game I've played in quite a while, not only due to the quality of the characters themeselves, but also its brilliantly deconstructive sense of humor. This game uses the player's knowledge of common RPG tropes to its advantage to produce some really clever moments. On top of this, when it's not making you laugh, it's being incredibly heartwarming or sad. Fans of Earthbound and other such games will feel right at home here.
The music is freakin astounding and that's all I really have to say about that.
Gameplay wise, this game includes some rather unique battle mechanics for an RPG as well, forcing you to actively dodge enemy attacks in a fashion reminiscent of a bullet hell game, spicing up the combat and giving it a more involved feel. And, well, as far as actually attacking goes, you don't really have to. Every enemy encounter can be resolved peacefully with the correct actions, almost like a small puzzle. It's something most games like this just don't do.
As you may know, though, not every game is made for everyone. This is less a crtique of the game itself and more of a heads up for those entertaining the idea of diving right in: if you (somehow) don't like the characters, or the story of the game doesn't grab you, you're really going to be missing out on a big part of why the game is considered so great. Sure, the gameplay is pretty cool, interesting, and well-developed as far as the battles go, but it clearly is not the game's major focal point. This game is all about the narrative, and it absolutely requires you to connect with the characters in order to be successful. Fortunately, everything concerning that in particular happens to be incredibly good, so, uh, yeah. Have I mentioned how amazing the music is yet?
Really, all you need to know is that Undertale is an fantastic experience. Honestly, I've been really holding back from gushing incessantly for most of this review. The truth is, this game is something special. It makes you think. It makes you smile, sometimes without even realizing it. The characters are amazing, the humor is almost always on point and well thought out, the attention to detail is genuinely difficut to fathom, the battle system is actually unique, and it has a totally kickass soundtrack to boot. This game oozes so much heart and hard work that I'm still trying to scrub the stains out of my couch, and it's very likely going to be remembered for a long time. If you decide to get it, do yourself a favor and don't spoil ANYTHING. You'll be rewarded for your restraint.

Undertale is a unique game, I'm not entire sure how to describe it. It is essentially an RPG that uses bullet hell mechanics, and gives you the option to fight or spare enemies, adding a great deal to what the player can do to impact the story. Just saying that doesn't really do it any justice, and the vast majority of positive reviews simply say "BUY THIS GAEM!!!!1! 1" with no further detail. Not really helpful.
Chances are you'll like undertale if you like charming characters, heartwarming (or if you're a genocidal maniac, terrifying) moments, gameplay that involves interaction (no mashing enter to skip through fights), a quirky, seemingly earthbound-inspired world and visuals, a beautiful soundtrack  and plenty of other things I can't particularly put into words.
As much as I love it though, it's not perfect. The tutorial is clever in how it pokes fun at tropes, but at the same time it still retains the sort of boing tutorial-type feeling, which is hard to avoid. One fair warning: if you don't like the characters, the experience may not be as enjoyable, although I'd argue most of the characters are at best, fantastic, and at worst, bearable. The game also gets sorta meta towards the end, which some people may not like, but the way it handles the meta is actually creative and well-done.
Regardless, if you like traditional RPGs, Good story and soundtrack, bullet hell, choices that impact the story, you'll like Undertale. (Probably.)
TL;DR: Undertale is great.

So I have owned this game for quite a while and have put a decent amount of time into it so I think I now have the priviledge of expressing my opinion. Anyway. First thing's first, DO NOT buy this game if you are not prepared to deal with bugs. I know it's hard to believe that an early access game might not be complete, but just bare with me for a second. I had a look through the other reviews and what seems to be the running trend is that people are angry with the state the game is currently in, which is understanable to an extent. In my opinion, the current problem with the game is the progress and order in which it's being updated. For instance, some people would rather have major bugs fixed before the devs add things like new textures for pain killers and farming hoes. However, the important thing to remember is that this game is still in early access, and while this isn't an excuse for completely ignoring updating the game, it's still something that the devs have EVERY right to do. You click the button every time you open the game saying you understand that you understand you are entering an Early Access Game. And we have to commend the devs of DayZ for even bothering to continue updating it, because they really don't have many reasons to do so because of all the money they've made off of people unprepared for what is technically an alpha.
In conclusion, only buy this game if you are fully prepared to deal with the constant changes and bugs that will show, but if you are buying this game with a complete intolerance to the bugs you are:
1. Clearly misunderstanding the entire point of the game being on Early Access.
2. Not going to have a good time
3. Ruining the game for people who would genuinely like to take part in the testing proccess and see the potential.
So yeah, go ahead and do what you want now.

They have now updated the system specs on the store page to a more realistic level, I assume the original specs were for Legacy Rust. People are still complaining about crashes and instability but thankfully mine have cleared up simply by using DX9 and window mode. It's not ideal but it has at least made the game playable again for me.
Some info for people thinking about getting rust:
They are pushing pretty regular updates around once a month although this also comes along with a mass server wipe most of the time.
Most PvP servers will have people that just kill you on sight even if they're fully armed and you're naked with a rock. There are PvE servers though, so it's an option if you just like building and hunting.
You never really log out of the game, your character simply drops to the floor asleep. While this is a good way to stop people combat logging, it does leave you open to people not only destroying your base and all your hard work but also killing and robbing you all while you are logged out at work or sleeping.
A lot of the official servers are plagued by hackers. The devs are fighting back and people are getting VAC banned but it's still a pretty big problem. Thankfully there are community servers that you can play on and they don't have that many hacker issues.
There is no character customization, your characters look is given to you at random based on your Steam ID, you could very well end up as a tall black guy with tiny junk and a huge head or an equally weird white guy variant. Some people don't like this and some don't mind, but it's worth knowing before you decide to buy the game.
The Female character has now been added, although it's still given out at random, depending on your Steam ID.
All in all I do enjoy playing the game with my girlfriend on a community server as the people are nicer, help each other out and I don't have to worry too much about being murdered in my sleep.

Probably not the game for absolutely everybody, but for anyone who enjoys Role-Playing Games, this is a definite buy. This game takes and challenges just about every trope present in RPGs from grinding enemies to level up to abusing Save/Load to ensure proper outcomes. The game is chock full of little details such as mentions to things you've done in previous playthroughs and even things you've saved/reloaded to change in the same one.
My first run through took me about 8 hours standing around to smell the roses.. I still take a similar time in further playthroughs because things change subtly from run-to-run, and the developer encourages and rewards experimentation.
The gameplay is not the core focus, but for those wondering, it's turn-based friend-making with intermittent bullet hell thrown in there. However, more depth is to be had in the secrets, story, and lore surrounding the UNDERGROUND...

Wow.
Just, wow.
I'm at a loss of words. This game...
...It's an absolute MASTERPIECE.
For my loyal readers, do you remember my Shovel Knight craze last year?
The graphics are a simple 8-bit style, and although it's considered "generic" because of the whole "8 bit indie game made by one guy" sort of thing, this game uses it properly. I know, that seems really weird, but it's true. If you play the game and take a certain route, the final boss WILL blow your mind with the visuals. Not much here to say, it's not what's supposed to make this game so noteworthy, but it's still acceptable nonetheless.
Undertale is a lot like Earthbound in many ways, the most notable trait being the turn based combat and how it's portrayed. Nowadays, LOTS of games have opportunities where you can spare or kill a certain character and decide their fate. Their flaw, however, is that the said death often is just shrugged off, both in the game's world AND in real life. Undertale takes this concept and cranks it up a notch, leaving literally every single character's fate in your hands. You can go for a pacifist run and kill no one, and this is the one I would
recommend going for if you do decide to purchase this masterpiece. There's also the neutral ending, which is the most common of the bunch but has one of the most creative final bosses I've ever seen in video games. I won't spoil much, but it will BLOW your mind, you can trust me on that. There's also the genocide run, which is incredibly difficult to pull off because of how emotionally difficult it is to actually kill this lovable cast of monsters. The combat itself is like Earthbound's, as said earlier. This being said, Undertale takes yet another step forward, adding bullet hell and platforming to the mix and blends the two perfectly, making the game far more exciting, while keeping the original RPG elements.
This is the very core of why Undertale is such an unforgettable experience. Of course, though, you shouldn't be shocked at this point, because most of the internet will agree with me on that. The cast of characters is so diverse and unique, each one having traits to make them likable or the one you'd love to kill on a genocide run. For example, you have Sans, my favorite of the bunch. He's a laid back, prankster, and easy going skeleton who has a brother named Papyrus. What Papyrus lacks in intelligence, he makes up for with a big heart for humans. You also have Flowey, who immediately will creep you out because of how ruthless he is. As for the plot itself, it's one big emotional rollercoaster you would want to ride over and over and over again. It has its hilarious moments, since the writing is surprisingly well done, while it has its sad moments, too. What takes the cake on all of this, though, is that it literally makes you rethink everything you knew about video games. The fourth wall is also broken often, and this is done in the most clever and creative ways. It's like Kid Icarus: Uprising, except Undertale does it far better. I almost forgot, too, but every action in this game will be remembered by the characters, long after you actually beat it. People have called this game a "sentient being" and I can actually agree with them on that. Trust me, Undertale is literally perfect for storytelling, and I won't be shocked if you cried a bit. It's hard not to, and with such a unique cast of lovable characters, it further justifies my point.
I have a friend who also loves Undertale, and the one thing he seems to point out about it is the soundtrack. I can't blame him, because it's really catchy. Remember how I said this game was my Shovel Knight of 2015? I wasn't kidding about that, it has the awesome soundtrack to go with it. You have Bonetrousle, the sinister, yet lighthearted and catchy tune that fits Papyrus. There's the Spider Dance, Muffet's theme. This theme is a lot more evil but far more catchy, and is one of my personal favorites. The king of the bunch, however, is one that didn't directly originate from Undertale: Megalovania. Sans' theme is slowly becoming an iconic boss theme, as it has been used in two different times in the past, and this variation is definitely my favorite of the three. You also have some humorous songs, namely the Dogsong. I won't get too in-depth with that one, but I need to say this now: GEEEET DUNKED ON! There is no voice acting, but why does that even matter? This game doesn't need it. Overall, this game has some high quality music, and I love it that way.
As I said earlier, this game has multiple endings. Want to know what makes it interesting, though? The characters will remember EVERYTHING you've done. I mean that, too. Mess with the game's files and try to beat it that way, I dare you. With the multiple endings, the replayability is far more dependent on you. If you have no soul, you'll probably try and do a genocide run while doing the other two runs as well. Maybe you'll try and do a pacifist one so you don't have to go through the pain of killing anyone, then do a neutral, and finish with a genocide ending. Just remember, EVERY choice will be remembered permanently.
Undertale is easily my GotY at this point in time, but it's also one of the most creative games I've ever seen. This is an absolute masterpiece, and I really hope it wins a LOT of awards. Do I recommend this game? Well, I'll join the internet on this one and say, "Of course!" Just be ready to stock up on spaghetti, because you'll need it while you stress-eat and do a playthrough of this gem.

Probably one of the best RPG's to come out of the past 5-6 years, give or take.
Why, you may ask? Well here's why it holds a special place in my heart; why it might hold a special place in your heart as well:
+ A majority of the game was produced by a two people--Toby Fox and Tem Chang. The art, music, characters... almost everything you see/hear  were probably created by him and Tem. Regardless of how you feel about this game, you have to admit that's not a simple undertaking.
+It's an RPG which promotes the use of complete pacifism or inaction in some scenarios. Not just for major characters you encounter, but for almost any mob found in the game. Other games will not actively encourage you to always flee from batte, or to find other means to disable hostile characters/mobs. Following the path of pacifist has its own rewards for you to reap. Maybe not monetary rewards, granted, but other interesting rewards. I could go on, and on, and on about this feature.
+/- The game has almost no fourth-wall; so, take that as you will. If you're an Earthbound nerd, like me, you'll probably love this.
+ Combat system which allows you utilize pacifism; flirtation; brawn (I know I mentioned this before, but it is a significant feature in this game).
+ Strong character development for every major character. Hell, it even has some development for recurring minor characters after you play through the game once or twice.
+Humorous writing
+ Undertale has some superb music. I'd dare to say that it is currently unrivaled in this department.
+Beautiful overworld to accompany the music.
+ Only $10 for something that will probably give you 20+ hours of enjoyment.
+Some boss fights can be quite challenging depending upon the run you do/your actions during the fight. If you intend to buy this game, you'd be wise to remember this.
- Backtracking through levels might annoy some people.
- There's a typo or two. I guess this might detract a select few individuals.
- The game can feel incredibly short if played in a single sitting. So seriously take your time with this gem.

So let's get started. If you are planing on buying DayZ you probably seen people saying "Don't buy DayZ Standalone go play Arma 3 Breaking point mod it's better and free.". I'm here to clear things up.
So what is better in Arma 3 ( Breaking point MOD ) than in DayZ SA? Well Arma 3 ( Breaking point MOD ) runs better and has less bugs but that is because this game ( Witch is Arma 3 ) was polished over several years the mod only added "zombies".
I've spent few days playing Breaking point mod to get an idea of what it is and see for my self if it's true.
I would say that "Breaking point" is hardly better than DayZ SA. People will say that zombies are better, less hackers, there are classes to chose from, every building is enterable, there are cars, better graphic etc. While it is some what true but peoples ignorance make it sound too good and tend to misslead other people.
This is how it is:
1. Zombies are not better they are actually worse than in the DayZ SA. You have a bunch of poor AI zombies walking back and forth, you can walk around them with no danger the only time they would hit you is if you would be standing still. You used to be able to track people down using zombies now you can't because they are buggy and useless they only give you nice feeling of zombie apocalypse ( Only in cities ).
2. Yes there is less hackers but when you only have 15 servers witch 4-6 of them get decent amount of players it's not that hard to monitor your server with some anti-cheats and some dedicated admins.
3. Going to talk about the gameplay, maps and classes.
1) While yes there are classes like Ranger ( Hero, helping everyone ), Hunter ( Bandit, killing everyone ), Survivalist ( Neutral, helping few factions ) and more. There is no depth into classes besides them having few bonuses while leveling up.
2) Having classes is a unique idea but everyone just plays the same just some have more friendly people. You can talk via "Ranger chat" or your faction chat witch is immersion killer when the chat always is "Is anyone in <Insert City Name>".
3) There is no in-depth looting you can find a weapon in less than 5 min so this only encourages you to be hostile to everyone you meet. Food and water has almost no purpose in the game I was running around for hours and I didn't need to eat or drink.
4) You don't need to loot cities for resourses you get everything you need from shacks that you come across in your journey. There is no real reason to team up with anyone, there is nothing to do team based besides of crafting some stuff. The entire gameplay is get a weapon and go kill some one even rangers get guns team up and go kill some one. It is not a zombie survival mod I coudn't get a conversation with anyone from another faction they just shoot you on sight even if you play as none and try to be nice ( I don't blame them because it's a pain to encounter anyone unless you go to hot spots ).
5) Maps aren't that great. Altis map is terrible, it's dull desert, has nothing interesting in it. The rule of who sees who first, wins is insane you can't locate your target and then try to fight back you will die there is nothing you can do about it unless you're near a building or bushes. Takes ages to get somewhere on this map.
Thirsk Summer/winter map is small Deathmatch island full of unfair action if you get a weapon or sneak up on someone good for you but other than that there is nothing to do there.
New haven kind of like Thirsk haven't played it much because the servers barely had any players in them.
Stratis map is one of the better ones because it has more forests and is smaller so encountering people is more common.
4. You'll hear that every building is enterable but when every single one is like a cartboard box that has no furniture and looks the same like the last one you will change your perspective on the entire "Everything is enterable" fiasco . The worst part is the loot spawns only in bag, trash can, lugagge box form that is just sitting in the middle of an empty room.
5. Vehicles. I personally don't care about them that much I like to go on foot but I found quite a few of them and a helicopter that were in great condition just needed fuel (This is how everything spawns after restart).
6. The good graphic thing is arguable the look of your game will depend on the rig you have. I can play it on high/ultra and there is nothing much to look at unless you want super realistic looking sand on a desert...
There is a lot more to tell why it's not better than DayZ SA. For me I can't stand the DayZ sometimes because it runs like steaming pile of dong but still wierdly I want to come back and play it some more. I'M NOT DISCOURAGING people buying Arma 3 or DayZ SA just clearing things up.

THIS INFORMATION IS FOR PEOPLE THAT ARE PLANING ON BUYING DAYZ! ( Date 2014-12-25 )
________________________________________________________________________________
So let's get started. If you are planing on buying DayZ you probably seen people saying "Don't buy DayZ Standalone go play Arma 3 Breaking point mod it's better and free.". I'm here to clear things up.
So what is better in Arma 3 ( Breaking point MOD ) than in DayZ SA? Well Arma 3 ( Breaking point MOD ) runs better and has less bugs but that is because this game ( Witch is Arma 3 ) was polished over several years the mod only added "zombies".
I've spent few days playing Breaking point mod to get an idea of what it is and see for my self if it's true.
I would say that "Breaking point" is hardly better than DayZ SA. People will say that zombies are better, less hackers, there are classes to chose from, every building is enterable, there are cars, better graphic etc. While it is some what true but peoples ignorance make it sound too good and tend to misslead other people.
This is how it is:
1. Zombies are not better they are actually worse than in the DayZ SA. You have a bunch of poor AI zombies walking back and forth, you can walk around them with no danger the only time they would hit you is if you would be standing still. You used to be able to track people down using zombies now you can't because they are buggy and useless they only give you nice feeling of zombie apocalypse ( Only in cities ).
2. Yes there is less hackers but when you only have 15 servers witch 4-6 of them get decent amount of players it's not that hard to monitor your server with some anti-cheats and some dedicated admins.
3. Going to talk about the gameplay, maps and classes.
1) While yes there are classes like Ranger ( Hero, helping everyone ), Hunter ( Bandit, killing everyone ), Survivalist ( Neutral, helping few factions ) and more. There is no depth into classes besides them having few bonuses while leveling up.
2) Having classes is a unique idea but everyone just plays the same just some have more friendly people. You can talk via "Ranger chat" or your faction chat witch is immersion killer when the chat always is "Is anyone in <Insert City Name>".
3) There is no in-depth looting you can find a weapon in less than 5 min so this only encourages you to be hostile to everyone you meet. Food and water has almost no purpose in the game I was running around for hours and I didn't need to eat or drink.
4) You don't need to loot cities for resourses you get everything you need from shacks that you come across in your journey. There is no real reason to team up with anyone, there is nothing to do team based besides of crafting some stuff. The entire gameplay is get a weapon and go kill some one even rangers get guns team up and go kill some one. It is not a zombie survival mod I coudn't get a conversation with anyone from another faction they just shoot you on sight even if you play as none and try to be nice ( I don't blame them because it's a pain to encounter anyone unless you go to hot spots ).
5) Maps aren't that great. Altis map is terrible, it's dull desert, has nothing interesting in it. The rule of who sees who first, wins is insane you can't locate your target and then try to fight back you will die there is nothing you can do about it unless you're near a building or bushes. Takes ages to get somewhere on this map.
Thirsk Summer/winter map is small Deathmatch island full of unfair action if you get a weapon or sneak up on someone good for you but other than that there is nothing to do there.
New haven kind of like Thirsk haven't played it much because the servers barely had any players in them.
Stratis map is one of the better ones because it has more forests and is smaller so encountering people is more common.
4. You'll hear that every building is enterable but when every single one is like a cartboard box that has no furniture and looks the same like the last one you will change your perspective on the entire "Everything is enterable" fiasco . The worst part is the loot spawns only in bag, trash can, lugagge box form that is just sitting in the middle of an empty room.
5. Vehicles. I personally don't care about them that much I like to go on foot but I found quite a few of them and a helicopter that were in great condition just needed fuel (This is how everything spawns after restart).
6. The good graphic thing is arguable the look of your game will depend on the rig you have. I can play it on high/ultra and there is nothing much to look at unless you want super realistic looking sand on a desert...
There is a lot more to tell why it's not better than DayZ SA. For me I can't stand the DayZ sometimes because it runs like steaming pile of dong but still wierdly I want to come back and play it some more. I'M NOT DISCOURAGING people buying Arma 3 or DayZ SA just clearing things up.

Rust has to be one of my favorite games I've played on Steam.  That being said, it is NOT all fun and games.  If you're looking for something to hold your hand and ease you into the experience, as I'm sure you already know Rust is not for you.  You're immediately thrown into a pot of complete social chaos, which I can easily say makes the game.  You really never know what you'll run into with the endless number of wackjobs and jokers playing alongside you.  Without any friends to play with you may not survive the experience.  To be quite honest you'll probably find the game quite boring and most likely rage quit due to hours of time wasted only to be brutally murdered, raided, etc due to lack of protection...  But once you do get a crew going, this game can be a hell of a lot of fun (which my hundreds of hours of gameplay can attest to.)
-Great, hilarious, downright awesome player interaction
-Beautiful game
-Updated weekly with great new stuff!
-Also A LOT of terribly rude, hair-tearing and rage-inducing player interaction
-No fun without friends (that's to be expected)
-Steals hours upon hours of your life, both good and bad
In the end, Rust is basically what you make of it.  If you're the type who enjoys smashing your expensive computer hardware when upset...  Probably not the game for you.  However, if you've got a few buddies to play with and think you can take a bit of a beating, then in my opinion the game is
worth it.  I'll put it this way - I've had countless experiences in Rust; both good and bad; and I honestly only remember the good.  So that's why I recommend Rust 100%.  Thanks for reading my review.

Probably one of the best RPG's to come out of the past 5-6 years, give or take.
Why, you may ask? Well here's why it holds a special place in my heart; why it might hold a special place in your heart as well:
+ A majority of the game was produced by a two people--Toby Fox and Tem Chang. The art, music, characters... almost everything you see/hear  were probably created by him and Tem. Regardless of how you feel about this game, you have to admit that's not a simple undertaking.
+It's an RPG which promotes the use of complete pacifism or inaction in some scenarios. Not just for major characters you encounter, but for almost any mob found in the game. Other games will not actively encourage you to always flee from batte, or to find other means to disable hostile characters/mobs. Following the path of pacifist has its own rewards for you to reap. Maybe not monetary rewards, granted, but other interesting rewards. I could go on, and on, and on about this feature.
+/- The game has almost no fourth-wall; so, take that as you will. If you're an Earthbound nerd, like me, you'll probably love this.
+ Combat system which allows you utilize pacifism; flirtation; brawn (I know I mentioned this before, but it is a significant feature in this game).
+ Strong character development for every major character. Hell, it even has some development for recurring minor characters after you play through the game once or twice.
+Humorous writing
+ Undertale has some superb music. I'd dare to say that it is currently unrivaled in this department.
+Beautiful overworld to accompany the music.
+ Only $10 for something that will probably give you 20+ hours of enjoyment.
+Some boss fights can be quite challenging depending upon the run you do/your actions during the fight. If you intend to buy this game, you'd be wise to remember this.
- Backtracking through levels might annoy some people.
- There's a typo or two. I guess this might detract a select few individuals.
- The game can feel incredibly short if played in a single sitting. So seriously take your time with this gem.

They have now updated the system specs on the store page to a more realistic level, I assume the original specs were for Legacy Rust. People are still complaining about crashes and instability but thankfully mine have cleared up simply by using DX9 and window mode. It's not ideal but it has at least made the game playable again for me.
Some info for people thinking about getting rust:
They are pushing pretty regular updates around once a month although this also comes along with a mass server wipe most of the time.
Most PvP servers will have people that just kill you on sight even if they're fully armed and you're naked with a rock. There are PvE servers though, so it's an option if you just like building and hunting.
You never really log out of the game, your character simply drops to the floor asleep. While this is a good way to stop people combat logging, it does leave you open to people not only destroying your base and all your hard work but also killing and robbing you all while you are logged out at work or sleeping.
A lot of the official servers are plagued by hackers. The devs are fighting back and people are getting VAC banned but it's still a pretty big problem. Thankfully there are community servers that you can play on and they don't have that many hacker issues.
There is no character customization, your characters look is given to you at random based on your Steam ID, you could very well end up as a tall black guy with tiny junk and a huge head or an equally weird white guy variant. Some people don't like this and some don't mind, but it's worth knowing before you decide to buy the game.
The Female character has now been added, although it's still given out at random, depending on your Steam ID.
All in all I do enjoy playing the game with my girlfriend on a community server as the people are nicer, help each other out and I don't have to worry too much about being murdered in my sleep.

Maps too large, server population too sparse, zombies that are only killable through bugged AI, and characters who were born with glass bones and paper skin. These are all some of the things you will encounter in the bug ridden alpha known as DayZ stand alone.
Falling any distance more than a foot =1-2 broken legs and your pants turning into rusted iron. All clothing seems to be made out of dyed metal and once damaged though any means reverts to rusted metal. Jackets, pants, and vests possess the ability to hold a void gate within them that stores another void gate vest and then some. Making it possible to store an endless number of items in the further that you can handily access though the one vest still present in the physical realm.
Combat in the game goes as follows,
Zombies: Run around in a circle and hit them in the back OR run to a hill and watch them fly into the air only to learn that they too were born with Paget's Disease. Sometimes zombies will turn to the sky and howl with rage before being eviscerated by some divine force. As for trying to fight them head on, don't. Do not assume the slow zombies can be easily eliminated by simply walking backwards and swinging like any other game for these are no ordinary zombie, they are Dota 2 creep zombies. Once an attack animation is started it is almost bound to hit if you move in a straight line. I have even seen a zombie kill a trucker who was a good 40 feet away. Let’s assume they are just superhuman zombies and not a crippling gameplay flaw that was ignored so the developers could add in another way for you to kill yourself.
Players: Fighting players opens up the possibility for inhumane torture by incorporating a blinding and binding mechanic. This mechanic is 110% ignored in the game and only used in videos for pre staged situations as 10/10 you will either be shot on site or handcuffed from behind, looted, and killed with your own weapon.
Suicide: because we were not ♥♥♥♥ed enough in this hellish world of telepathic zombies with bone disorders. At first I was willing to look past all the flaws because hey, it IS an alpha. Something a lot of my friends kept reminding me. Then they go and add this in here while completely IGNORING the bugs. Which leads me to believe that the devs are either ignorant these problems or consider them a good part of the game. Perhaps it’s a problem with the game engine, either way it still ruins the game.
Having a map so vast one would think that there are plenty of ways to get around right? Wrong. Currently there is only one time of vehicular transport in the game (a truck) that is rarer than a black republican. And with half the efficiency! It really explains why this has come to be known as "WalkingSim2014™".
Looting is considered a vast part of open world survival games like DayZ. So how is the loot system? Besides the previously discussed void storage system loot seems to be pretty straight forward. Items were left scattered on the floor in random places by some unknown entity. Most loot one finds in towns is decent to useless with the best stuff coming out of airports and crash sites. The only real way to get decent loot in that game is to hack it in with a .dll or kill a hacker and steal his stuff as seen here
. And then proceed to stuff EVERYTHING of value you find into your pants, including more pants.

Probably one of the best RPG's to come out of the past 5-6 years, give or take.
Why, you may ask? Well here's why it holds a special place in my heart; why it might hold a special place in your heart as well:
+ A majority of the game was produced by a two people--Toby Fox and Tem Chang. The art, music, characters... almost everything you see/hear  were probably created by him and Tem. Regardless of how you feel about this game, you have to admit that's not a simple undertaking.
+It's an RPG which promotes the use of complete pacifism or inaction in some scenarios. Not just for major characters you encounter, but for almost any mob found in the game. Other games will not actively encourage you to always flee from batte, or to find other means to disable hostile characters/mobs. Following the path of pacifist has its own rewards for you to reap. Maybe not monetary rewards, granted, but other interesting rewards. I could go on, and on, and on about this feature.
+/- The game has almost no fourth-wall; so, take that as you will. If you're an Earthbound nerd, like me, you'll probably love this.
+ Combat system which allows you utilize pacifism; flirtation; brawn (I know I mentioned this before, but it is a significant feature in this game).
+ Strong character development for every major character. Hell, it even has some development for recurring minor characters after you play through the game once or twice.
+Humorous writing
+ Undertale has some superb music. I'd dare to say that it is currently unrivaled in this department.
+Beautiful overworld to accompany the music.
+ Only $10 for something that will probably give you 20+ hours of enjoyment.
+Some boss fights can be quite challenging depending upon the run you do/your actions during the fight. If you intend to buy this game, you'd be wise to remember this.
- Backtracking through levels might annoy some people.
- There's a typo or two. I guess this might detract a select few individuals.
- The game can feel incredibly short if played in a single sitting. So seriously take your time with this gem.

Note that I haven't even started to plumb the depths of this game but I feel compelled to leave a review anyway.
This game had so much buzz online that I was immediately resistant to trying it, out of a weird defiance, so when I did start playing this game, it was with preconceived expectations that I wouldn't like it and that it would not live up to the hype.
I was wrong.
This game slowly and completely immersed me in its  little world. The music is simple yet brilliant. The characters are vividly imagined and their dialouge is cleverly written.
You aren't told too many rules explicitly, you learn how to play as you go along. When you equip different weapons, for example, you don't realize how to fight with them until you get into your next encounter. I found this interesting and engaging, and for that reason, it made me want to try out a variety of weapons rather than sticking with the first thing I equipped.
As for the story itself - you make many choices as you go along, and they do impact how the plot develops. You feel the consequences of some choices you make, and you sometimes feel like you are the villain in the game after all. The monsters become more human by the minute, and you feel like your 'human' character is not much different from them.
I will not lie, I felt increasing regret for killing a specific character in a boss fight. As I kept playing and learned that there are various ways to lead encounters so that you can Spare monsters (and as such, don't have to kill them), I ended up resetting the game so I could start all over again and spare that character.
Normally, video games have bosses that you are supposed to defeat and they are set up so that they are clearly a villain and obstacle that you, as the hero, need to get rid of. In this game, the 'boss fights' are monsters just doing their jobs, leading their lives, and often times have nobler motivations than you as the main character.
This leads to surprising levels of introspection and thoughtfulness, and at least for me, formed a desire to replay the game from the start to try to do things differently a second time around.

If the developers decided to put work into this game rather than take the money they made from selling the alpha version to create a console version, when this isn't anywhere near finished, I wouldn't write a negative review.
It's been over a year, they aren't improving it, they haven't fixed anything, they're taking money from people who believed in the game and slapping them across the face. F**k the team behind this game, play the mod if you want DayZ, but don't give these people your money. They're just screwing people over.

In the current state that this game is in, I feel as if I should do an updated review on this game. DayZ in its current state is quite horrible and repulsive to play. The amount of issues, bugs, lack of content and other various things makes the experience of playing DayZ like literal cancer. To be frank, there is no real good experiences to be had in this game currently. It has no play value to it because of all the cons that outweigh the pros.
However I will come to DayZ's defence in some regards. I truly appreciate the people working on this game. God knows its been a rough ride. I appreciate everything Bohemia Interactive is doing to improve the game expereince and overall quality. I hope that Bohemia will go through with this game and complete it fully, with minimal bugs and such. I truly belive that they have it in them to do it. The fact that the dev cycle is taking quite long should not enrage you to any form. Games take a long time to make and have many phases to go through.
Pros:
- Gun fights are very intense, and enjoyable. Only thing that makes this game enjoyable
- Good enviroment
- Extremely Large map
- Good Time killer
- Fun game to play with friends
Cons:
- Extremely Glitchy
- Plagued with bugs
- Frame lags constantly (Not so much anymore because of the new engine)
- Game is not a survival game, more so a large scale pvp game
- Zombies are god awful and not even in the slightest dangerous

- No form of alliances or point of teaming with people, you gain nothing allying with other people
- Extremely Grindy
- Can take hours to get geared
- Game is a walking sim
To conclude, I would give this game a solid 4/10. It is really not worth playing at this time, and the changes that were implemented were the main reason that I stopped playing this game. I would wait until this game is years more in development until considering looking at what it has to offer right now. I truly want to love this game but I cannot in the horrendous state that it is in.

I can't express how much I loved playing through every minute of this game. It toyed with my emotions more than any other game, movie, books, story, and form of entertainment. I went into this game expecting a quirky little RPG with me quitting after thinking, "Eh, that was cool I guess."
By the end of this gem of a game, I fell in love with it. I completed a perfect pacifist run and was so happy I did it. I found myself liking all the characters far to much to ever want to lay a finger on them.....except one.....
This game had me bawling more times than I'd like to admit. From an emotional standpoint. This game hits hard. I got happy, I got sad, I got angry, I got frustrated, and everytime I thought I found a character I didn't want to have mercy on. The game proved I did.
Gameplay wise, the combat system is really unique and a novel idea to me. The combat system itself is a mini-game in a game. And by the late game it becomes a BULLET HELL. I found it fun, albeit frustrating sometimes. So if gameplay is the reason your buying, it's good in that regard. But that reason for buying will change....I bet you.
Story wise, I've halfway already stated. The characters are distinctly written, and I grew to love them all.....except one.......It's a super emotional experience that is one large journey to go through.
I give 200/10. Would buy so many times over. Do yourself a favor. If you've never seen a walkthrough of this game, or don't know any of the events of this game. Don't look into them. Do NOT spoil this game for yourself. It is a game you need to experience for yourself without the impression of others thoughts. Go into it knowing nothing about the events that happen and roll for the ride.

I've played so much of this game and I just can't escape its many charms
Many people wanna look at this game and just see it as another one of those niche old game nostalgia inducers, but it is hardly that. The game seems to go out of its way to AVOID being a mass of silly references.
On top of having the best soundtrack I've heard in years (there are like 70 songs in this game that takes 4 hours to beat, that's more than many much larger games!), it offers a rich story with lovable and magnificent characters, and might be the best feel-good game I'v eever played.
A lot of the Feel-good elements come from the fact that this game can at once be deep and meaningful and complex while still managing to make me feel extremely positive emotions (though Undertale isn't without a few creepy moments). Between "innovation" and "improvements" so common in today's gaming market, triple A, and many others with them, Undertale is a breath of fresh air, which manages to be unique not by improving the things that exist already, but by being an original idea with what has existed for years.
All in all, there is no game I could recommend more than undertale, it's a little game with lots of heart.

(Game Is Alpha 50% as of December 2014, Remember That!)
Pros;-
You like survival? Good, this game has it. First thing to do is find food and water, backpack, new clothing with more pockets and your on your way to surviving. Oh and a weapon! :)
You like zombies? Good, there isn't many yet as its alpha but in time there will be more.
You like PVP? Good, there is much, friendly people are about, just act like it and you'll be fine but always watch your back.
You like weapons? Good, from knifes you make out of rocks on the beach, to pistols, to rifles and machine guns. (More weapons to come in the new year)
You like the feel of being hunted but want to become the hunter?... Good, you can, join your friends or other friendly people (rare) and hunt out the bandits killing bambies (New people/Fresh spawns).
You like driving? Good, first implementation of cars have been added, this being a V3S truck. (More to come in New Year)
You like building a campfire with a tent and feeling at home? Good, you can, just don't forget to look for persistent servers that will allow your tent to be in the same place as it was pitched by you until the following Wednesday as server maintenance will happen and your tent will be gone. (For now).
You like being your own person? Good, you can by dressing as whoever you want to be. That being a Hobo, a Cop, part of the Military, a Sniper, a Bandit, a Cross-dresser, a Prisoner, a Medic, a Farmer, a Fisherman, a Traveler and much more.
You want to just end it all in game as you've seen enough to even send your self to the grave? Good, you can now kill your self in game in the most brutal way ever. Grab a knife, can opener or a gun and press F11. A new start, a new life. But your still in the apocalypse, just remember that.
You want to help the devs on finding bugs and reporting them to help make the best survival zombie game ever for full release next year? Good you can. Be apart of a big community on making a game that you guys want to see! The devs show a lot of interest in what you want in game and how to go about doing things and not many devs allow this but these guys do!
cons;-
You like KOS? Good, this game has a lot of it since the game isn't finished, people will kill for your gun or just because you looked at them...No seriously, don't even look in there eyes!
You like admins kicking you for joining there servers? Good this game has it big style. It is however against the Dayz Devs rules and regulations for the game and server owners can be punished by reporting them to the server operators. But this doesn't stop them and we don't have time to report 30-40% of the servers. Stick to official Dayz servers when looking.
You like in game bugs/glitches? Good, this game has some, not many in all fairness but some, like any alpha state game.
You like people walking up to you acting friendly then knocking you out and taking your cloths? Good, this game has it. Be weary, always!
Final Note:
Now with that out the way, enjoy the game, don't expect your character to save all the time, it will reset but rarely, so don't get attached to what you have, just have fun, live for the moment and enjoy your survival experiences in the zombie apocalypse! See you out there!

*SLIGHTLY SPOILER-Y*
As silly as it sounds, my experience playing Undertale was just that: an experience. Gameplay-wise, it's incredibly simple. Walk, talk, battle enemies. But it's how it utilizes those simple elements and creates a powerful story centered around it. As you walk from point A to point B, you can feel that you have made a journey. You're exploring this foreign, perilous world, you grow attached to the interesting and quirky characters you meet, and the way you face against your enemies is actively shaping the outcome of your adventure. This is a game were, like in real life, everything has powerful consequences that you can't just run away from (even if you try the age old habit of save scumming, something that Undertale LOVES to pull apart and analyze).
A lot can be taken from Undertale, and very rarely does a game succeed in so many ways on leaving a mark on its player. Many of the game's concepts (the deconstruction of the rpg, the psychology of in-game characters and the godlike powers of a player to manipulate the game's world) can of course be preached by lesser artist's, but TobyFox has combined visuals, gameplay, story, music, and character and shaped them all into such a unique game that has proven it deserves all the recognition it gets.
While I may not have the heart to play the game again, I absolutely want to see other players experience it for the first time like I did. Please pick up this game if you have the chance. It's worth it.

Oh boy, how do I begin describing this game? It is very hard to do so without spoiling, and if it is spoiled, then a great part of the experience will be ruined. It is incredibly important to approach this game as blind as possible.
Undertale at first glance might look like a rather simple looking RPG, with a gimmick added to the typical JRPG formula. You can either kill or spare your enemies, and who and how much you kill affects the outcome of the game. Instead of directly receiving attacks from enemies that automatically lower your HP, defending works as some sort of small scale bullet hell, and each boss adds its own little twists to it. It is rather fun although the random encounters don't offer too much by themselves. Gameplay wise, it is fun and enjoyable, and while there is certainly not a lot of "challenge" (except for some of the bosses) it's still entertaining enough to carry the game and narrative well.
But really, it is a whole lot more than that. Undertale tackles narrative in a way that reminds us of how powerful storytelling can be in videogames, in a way only videogames are able to. Gameplay and story tie together very damn well, and your actions for once, have real importance. It is truly a great experience, and a real ♥♥♥♥ing ride all the way through.
And did I mention the soundtrack? Holy damn, it's god tier stuff and one of my favorite soundtracks ever. Phenomenal use of motif and wide variety of styles and genres.
So my verdict? Go buy it now. Seriously. It's a really fantastic game and an experience worth going through.

A wonderfully charming journey through an unusual world inhabited by strange creatures. I could never have predicted what exactly I was getting into. All I'd seen before playing was some fanart of two skeletons and some blue chick with big teeth. These characters, and others, are popular for very good reason and I too soon found myself falling in love with them.
The conclusion is thrilling, full of surprises, and in an unusual turn did not leave me longing for more. I was satisfied with how things turned out in the end and couldn't have asked for anything better.
So have a look, spend some time with Undertale, and enjoy it.

Oh boy, how do I begin describing this game? It is very hard to do so without spoiling, and if it is spoiled, then a great part of the experience will be ruined. It is incredibly important to approach this game as blind as possible.
Undertale at first glance might look like a rather simple looking RPG, with a gimmick added to the typical JRPG formula. You can either kill or spare your enemies, and who and how much you kill affects the outcome of the game. Instead of directly receiving attacks from enemies that automatically lower your HP, defending works as some sort of small scale bullet hell, and each boss adds its own little twists to it. It is rather fun although the random encounters don't offer too much by themselves. Gameplay wise, it is fun and enjoyable, and while there is certainly not a lot of "challenge" (except for some of the bosses) it's still entertaining enough to carry the game and narrative well.
But really, it is a whole lot more than that. Undertale tackles narrative in a way that reminds us of how powerful storytelling can be in videogames, in a way only videogames are able to. Gameplay and story tie together very damn well, and your actions for once, have real importance. It is truly a great experience, and a real ♥♥♥♥ing ride all the way through.
And did I mention the soundtrack? Holy damn, it's god tier stuff and one of my favorite soundtracks ever. Phenomenal use of motif and wide variety of styles and genres.
So my verdict? Go buy it now. Seriously. It's a really fantastic game and an experience worth going through.

The conclusion is thrilling, full of surprises, and in an unusual turn did not leave me longing for more. I was satisfied with how things turned out in the end and couldn't have asked for anything better.
So have a look, spend some time with Undertale, and enjoy it.

Now is the time to start picking this game up, with the new engine overhaul and massive updates coming weekly.
This game right here is one of the most promising sandbox games currently out there, with little competition, and one of the best Early Access games to follow right now. The talented team, with king Garry from Garry's Mod in the front are constantly delivering plenty of updates right now that you can watch in

The old engine (legacy) is what is being showcased in the videos/screenshots on the steam page right now, and it's probably the version many people played when they first bought the game. Now it's way, way different and better and it's getting more work done.
Not to mention, the graphic and random terrain generation overhauls are superb.
In rust, the focus is on three things:
- base building
- resource gathering and hoarding
- base raiding
If any one of those is something you are interested, you'll have a blast.
What you want to have to get the best out of the game:
- friends
- time around the clock
The experience is hardcore, and basically requires you to play it regularly to keep what you build.
The map is either custom made or randomly generated, and really varied.
There are other players on the server, and when you log out your character sleeps where he is and can be killed/looted.
You have needs like hunger, thirs, cold, wetness, comfort and more to be added.
You gather resources by utilising tools on the resources in the map (tress, rocks) and hunting animals.
You build bases in a modular fashion, where you place foundations, then pillars, then walls, then doorways, then doors, then locks on those doors. Bases modules can be square or triangular. Door locks can be key based (where you craft the key to the door) or pin code based.
You can destroy buildings by hitting them with axes/pickaxes (it takes maybe an hour to do so on high upgrades) or use explosives like C4 detonation or rocket launchers (that are hard to craft or find).
Bases modules can be upgraded by hitting them with tools and using up resources in your inventory. I think the stages at the moment are: twigs, woods, stone, iron, reinforced. Each of them can withstand more punishment before going down.
There are some objects called cupboards that authorize building in an area around them. Meaning if you click on them, only if you're authorized you can build around it (to prevent grief building around a base you own).
There are plenty of weapons and gunplay is fairly hardcore. Need to aim down sights. Shotguns, tommyguns, pistols, AKs, bolt actions, all of them really artisanal and rusty looking.
Most items have durability and degrades / can be repaired.
There are random air drop events around the map where a rare package gets dropeed with supplies and weapons. Encourages PvP.
Friendly fire is of course enabled.
When you die, you spawn to a bed you own (there is a 200+ second cooldown on respawn on bed atm) or you can just spawn randomly along a coast.
You can request a friends bed so that you can spawn on it through a command. (so you can meet up with friends if you just joined on a server).
There are radiation zones, with buildings that spawn loot barrels, but you receive damage over time if you are not protected in those areas.
You have to research items if you want to KNOW how to craft them. Either find the blueprint as a drop, or research at a research bench for a chance to gain the items knowledge, and destroy it in the process.
There are plenty of flavourful items in the game right now, like paintings, guitars, signs, campfires, roofs.
Roleplay as much as you want, since people are generally really fun to play with. Set up a shop, be a militant general, be a hunter, be a city manager, be a lone wolf, be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Whatever you want, you can play however you want.
People start naked, and if you deactivated censoring you can see pinis in front of your eyes while you're hurled up in your base.

Might as well give my two cents on this.
Let me preface this by saying I love DayZ. I love ArmA and its community.
With that out of the way, lets begin. I spawned in first to DayZ when it hit early access. The game was nigh unplayable. Bugs amok; terrible, terrible framerate; and a bunch of ruined hats and motorbike helmets.
Flash forward to December 22nd, 2014. I spawned in for an extended period after the game would run at an acceptable resolution, (Why the ♥♥♥♥ do you have display resolution and interface resolution separate? I want it at 1920x1080 for both.) and what I found appalled me. Finally there was more than just ruined hats and motorbike helmets: THERE WERE RUINED GLOVES NOW!!! In all honesty though, there are just as many bugs, to the point that I am reminded of WarZ's launch (Infestation Survivor Stories for those of you born yesterday). Glitching through walls, flying hackers, lag (despite single digit ping on my end and the servers end), and an unapperent lack of added content. I look at the update files going back to the first days of early access, and it seems that other than items everything is the same. Also it rains too much. To the point that you should just change servers if its raining because the rain is more of a death sentence and waiting game than a fully kitted bandit.
TL;DR Don't buy until such time as this is actually playable. Please don't. The devs have done very little to fix performance issues and bugs. Don't buy this because in its current state, DayZ is essentially WarZ.

Might as well give my two cents on this.
Let me preface this by saying I love DayZ. I love ArmA and its community.
With that out of the way, lets begin. I spawned in first to DayZ when it hit early access. The game was nigh unplayable. Bugs amok; terrible, terrible framerate; and a bunch of ruined hats and motorbike helmets.
Flash forward to December 22nd, 2014. I spawned in for an extended period after the game would run at an acceptable resolution, (Why the ♥♥♥♥ do you have display resolution and interface resolution separate? I want it at 1920x1080 for both.) and what I found appalled me. Finally there was more than just ruined hats and motorbike helmets: THERE WERE RUINED GLOVES NOW!!! In all honesty though, there are just as many bugs, to the point that I am reminded of WarZ's launch (Infestation Survivor Stories for those of you born yesterday). Glitching through walls, flying hackers, lag (despite single digit ping on my end and the servers end), and an unapperent lack of added content. I look at the update files going back to the first days of early access, and it seems that other than items everything is the same. Also it rains too much. To the point that you should just change servers if its raining because the rain is more of a death sentence and waiting game than a fully kitted bandit.
TL;DR Don't buy until such time as this is actually playable. Please don't. The devs have done very little to fix performance issues and bugs. Don't buy this because in its current state, DayZ is essentially WarZ.

I'm going to try to make this simple. Rust is a harsh, non-forgiving survival game. You are going to die a lot. You are going to get raided, starve, killed, etc. A majority of the community is not friendly. I like this more preferably, as it's more realistic. Anyway, you can build a shelter, explore and conquer with friends, and have a blast. There are supply drops and radtowns (radiated towns with good loot usually, risky but the payout is big.) which give more things to do. Also note that this game is not perfect. Graphics are tweaked to be better yet, and there are a handful of bugs (horses run through walls and do Halo jumps for me). If you are willing to take the minor bugs along the way for a great game, I would recommend this game. Worth every dollar.

A pretty fun game with a bit of clever dialogue and gameplay.
Adds a nice mix of RPG with a feel to a bullet hell when avoiding attacks and heck it's got a bit of every game genre hidden in it. Good music and and an art aspect reminiscent to old RPGs, but my favorite part about the 'visuals' is the battle system.. The game also seems to pay some homage to older games and such with references here and there.
I only had a few problems with it. Such as the Temmie character and Alphys' constant calls and text. She was almost worse than Roman Bellic... I understood what the game was going with for them, but it just rubbed me the wrong way. I didn't mind the bad puns too much, but what really did bother me was too many references of anme that kind of got bothersome and also the sounds for some of the character's dialogue got a bit annoying, but other than that it's been a pretty good game.
*Possible spoilers, so you've been warned*
My only real regret was killing Toriel and restarting only to have the regret haunt me and never being able to see her again and the fact that I showed my 'undying' love for a skeleton.
Finally as much as I enjoyed the game, I didn't understand the major hype it had. That being everyone would praise it as "Game of the year" or "Best game ever made" and even saying it made them cry. The only time I felt "emotional" towards the game was when I felt bad for hurting Asgore and thinking of hurting Papyrus, but to each their own I guess.
All in all I found myself enjoying the game and will come back to it sometime to do a genocide and pacifist playthrough.

One of the few recent examples of games doing moral choice correctly.
I personally went into Undertale with a bit of skepticism on my part, after I was asked to try it out by a friend of mine. As long as you allow it to, the game will surprise you with the kind of depth that you would not otherwise expect from a 10$ title. While the game's core interaction is an RPG-like fight system, you quickly realize that it is not the focus of it. This seems to be one of the few recent titles where choice does indeed matter and the game itself does a good attempt to restrict the player from avoiding consequences, and while most tech savvy (or google-knowing) people will find ways around it, it is highly advised that you do not try to fix your mistakes in such a manner but rather try to deal with them as the game progresses.
The only negative aspect of the game is that it might prove a bit too challenging to players who are not used to bullethell titles such as Ikaruga and other reflex-based examples. Getting stuck on the games bossfights tends to happen a fair bit and can only be solved via trial and error and DETERMINATION as the game lacks a difficulty setting or cheat codes. But for a very good reason, mind.
What the game lacks in terms of gameplay it more than makes up with a story which quickly becomes quite meta the deeper you get into it. Likable characters, decent humor and a rollercoaster of emotions with all of the ups and downs. All of that you will find here.
