---You are about to read a short story of on my experiences in Rust. A note to consider, this might never happen to you. However I'm hoping that such a 'review' will help you decide to buy this game because never will you experience anything, like what you will in rust, in any other game. ---
There I was standing. Thinking that I must be the luckiest person on earth. A player with full clothing (you don't see that a lot in rust) and a bolt action rifle in hand. You must be thinking 'how on earth is that considered lucky?'. But did I forget to mention that he was AFK. So exited, I ran towards him with my makeshift spear and was about to rip him to bits until I saw his name tag. It read 'BDB'. It took me a few seconds to remember the name, 'Have I ever met you before'. Then I remembered.
Two days earlier I had met two complete beginners at the game. They were running towards me, rocks in hand, shouting 'FRIENDLY' to assure the fact that they weren't going to attack me on sight. I shouted the same word back to them but took out my spear to take precaution. After a few  seconds of dark silence I thought I should offer them food. I would always to that to the 'friendly' so that i  could make more friends than enemies. As they thanked me and ate some food they explained how they were quite new to the game and were looking for some place to mine some rock. I told them that I was making a Noob (as us gamers call beginners)  shelter up in the mountains and was willing to teach them the ropes. I also gave them the rock they needed. After that we started to improve the base together, and make it a home for all of us. I was also quite a Noob at the time so they also taught me things I didn't know. We became a strong trio who had a nice fortified base until the day where i decided to sep out the front door of our house at the wrong time.
I told my two friends (one of them was away) that I was going out to fortify the base with a few more barricades. However the moment I opened the front door to our base I was shot done. Raiders. The screen read 'You were killed by BDB'. They were listening to our conversations and looking for just the right time to raid us. I shouted at one of my friends to take cover inside the base, while I was given the option to respawn at my sleeping bag also inside the base. It was hopeless. My friend with just a bow to fight off pesky raiders with full protective clothing. I had nothing to fight with and the raiders looted my previous body and gained access to the house using my key. My friend with the bow fought hard and dealt a good amount of damages but soon enough, the bullets had finally ripped through his skin. They killed me once again with my friend and renamed our sleeping bags to prevent us from respawning. BDB... never have i had so much hatred for another player in a game. BDB. Never did i see my two friends ever again. All because of that raider. BDB.
I got my spear in hand and started to pierce through the skin of the AFK raider. Such joy filled my heart like never before. Revenge had never felt so sweet. BDB was no longer. I started to loot through his dead body and steal all the valuables. I equiped my self in my dead foes armor and help his gun in my hands. Though that wasn't the end. I was running away from the murder scene when the message from a very angry player came onto the message section. BDB was looking for revenge and considering the fact that he was apart of the the servers currently biggest (and strongest)  clan, there was no doubt he was going to get it.
I was running as fast as I could, from the dead body of the raider, when I saw another player dressed in full burlap armor ( the weakest in the game). It was the same guy who had killed me prior to myself finding AFK BDB. I thought that, now that was equiped with things that were vastly better than his, i should probably take my second revenge for the day. So I did, using 'only' two bullets. He was laying on the floor, pleading for me to revive him. I thought to myself that 'I am better than this' so i had just taken his weapons for precaution. As he got up he thanked me and had also invited me to his base. Or should I say bases. He had two, one of which was raided so after inspecting that we went to his second base. Both bases were fairly large and fortified so I had thought that he must have been in affiliation with another strong clan, especially considering the fact that he was Russian himself.
We had finally arrived at his second base. I was at the front of his base, admiring it, when all of sudden a bullet came flying across my head. I shouted at the Russian to take cover at a giant rock opposite the front of the house. Bullets were flying everywhere meaning the were clearly well stocked. I tried to shoot back at them but we were pinned down. The Russian quickly ran into the house through the front door, and got shoot in the back while trying to do so. Fortunately he made it in and he was shouting at me to also come so he could fortify it. I considered whether I should trust him or not, but then I thought 'I have also attacked a fair share of naked's ,for no good reason, in my time playing rust'. So i eventually complied and ran towards the door while, luckily, dodging two. bullets.
We made our way to the top floor, where there was a window to get a good view on our opponents, and started to discuss what we should do. We tried to look through the window and shoot them, though every time we attempted so bullets would start to fly from our opponents guns. I decided eventually, that i should try talking to them. I asked them to put there guns down. It wasn't the reply that had devastated me but the player from whom I had received the reply from. Chistine. She was apart of the the biggest and strongest clan in the server. The same clan BDB was from.
Half an hour had passed. Much discussion had taken place. We had no hope in just running outside the base and trying to shoot them. Our opponent was obviously more trained than us, and her and her other partners had more firepower than my Russian friend and I. Also if we had really been a threat to them they would have called for back up. There base was no too far from ours so it would be no problem for them. If we wanted to leave this situation alive we had to play it smart. Christine had told us to come outside of the house naked with no weapons so that we could discuss further. Many other random players hearing this conversation warned me not to trust her. I had already figured that out by myself.
Now I could continue my story and start to talk about my mastermind plan and a big battle, but not much really happens. Nothing really goes in my favour. I end up randomly dying and my both Christine and my Russian friend both join forces with me out of the picture. The End.
--- Sorry about the flat ending. Also sorry if this wasn't what you'd be expecting from a review. Though I thought that this story would have done much justice to this magnificent game than a general review. Though if your still looking for a more traditional review...

A pretty fun game with a bit of clever dialogue and gameplay.
Adds a nice mix of RPG with a feel to a bullet hell when avoiding attacks and heck it's got a bit of every game genre hidden in it. Good music and and an art aspect reminiscent to old RPGs, but my favorite part about the 'visuals' is the battle system.. The game also seems to pay some homage to older games and such with references here and there.
I only had a few problems with it. Such as the Temmie character and Alphys' constant calls and text. She was almost worse than Roman Bellic... I understood what the game was going with for them, but it just rubbed me the wrong way. I didn't mind the bad puns too much, but what really did bother me was too many references of anme that kind of got bothersome and also the sounds for some of the character's dialogue got a bit annoying, but other than that it's been a pretty good game.

My only real regret was killing Toriel and restarting only to have the regret haunt me and never being able to see her again and the fact that I showed my 'undying' love for a skeleton.
Finally as much as I enjoyed the game, I didn't understand the major hype it had. That being everyone would praise it as "Game of the year" or "Best game ever made" and even saying it made them cry. The only time I felt "emotional" towards the game was when I felt bad for hurting Asgore and thinking of hurting Papyrus, but to each their own I guess.
All in all I found myself enjoying the game and will come back to it sometime to do a genocide and pacifist playthrough.

I could sit here and talk through the positives and negatives of DayZ but we all know what they are. One the one hand development is slow, the game is still buggy and looks a long long way off of a final product. The other, it is a very enjoyable game with arguably one of the best PvP expereinces you can get. But we all know this and neither of these factors are important in a way.
The most important thing is to know early access is a gamble. If you bought DayZ a year ago or you bought it a week ago you're gambling on whether the game will progress, and whether it will be an amazing game.
In the reality of it when you bought/If you are going to buy DayZ you need(ed) to ask yourself "Am I willing to spend £20 on what it currently is?" Because ultimately thats what you may end up with. For me I was happy to spend £20 a year ago and only get what was there, anything on top of that is a bonus for me personally.
You shouldn't buy DayZ on what you think it can be. If you think it can be amazing then buy it when it is, or if you buy it for what it is now you need to be prepared to accept it may not get any better.
To sum up if you don't think the current product is good enough for the price don't buy it expecting it to become good enough.

I have never been a big PC Gamer. I plan on getting a powerful enough PC that I can at least attempt to play some of the bigger games, but even then, I have a very mixed opinion of games on PC, with most of my experience on PC being browser games on Cartoon Network and those games you got from cereal boxes. I have also been console gamer, and still am. Added with the fact I'm working a part-time job trying to pay school debt, I need to learn to be extremely cautious when it comes to buying games, especially on this site, when hundreds of games are on sale every week. If there are any PC games that I do buy, they're cheap, and not always that impressive, just mindless time.
So when I heard all the praise this simple-looking game was getting, I was very skeptical. but at least willing to try. An RPG that can play even on toasters without problems with a $10 price tag (even with no sale) was appealing. So I bought it.
And then I fell in love.
Undertale somehow captures a torrent of feelings that I never felt playing video games since I played Banjo-Kazooie for the first time on N64. It opened me like nothing else that came before it. Sometimes it made you feel young, made you feel loving, made you cry, laugh, worried, regretful, accomplished. Determined.
Even when you get past the slap fest that your amygdala puts you through, it is a deceptively clever game. A turn based combat system that combines logic puzzles, action commands ala Mario & Luigi RPG's, and a bullet hell-like dodge system, each battle and enemy has a unique experience that leaves a lasting impression. The designs of the monsters you find in this game aren't overly complicated, but have a loving charm to them, like Mickey Mouse or Bugs Bunny, and while the overworld sprite art is the main issue I have with this game (my own nitpick if you will), it was never something that made the game unplayable, just that it caused confusion, such as where a mouth was positioned in relation to the rest of the face, etc., and was only a slight issue with some sprite art, not a reflection of the overall quality of the artstyle.
The story, much like the battle system, is also deceptively clever, and branches out in a way that only a video game could ever accomplish. I won't spoil too much on how the story unravels, but you WILL get invested. There is no doubt in that. The way that it sets the mood in each specific part and succeeds in getting the reactions it wanted from you shows how well crafted the story is. The soundtrack (which I bought here shortly after) is fantastic, not just 8-bit music, but a combination of styles that fits each situation they are heard in. When you feel happy, sad, scared, or just want to laugh forever, the music let's you know your feelings are justified.
When I got to the end of my own personal journey, I felt like a giddy little kid and just wanted to never stop playing and  replay it over and over again, but every adventure needs to end. I will always cherish the time I had with this game, giving me a sense of curiosity that I never felt in years when it came to video games. It reminded me to never be too judgmental on games and just experience it. To enjoy what I have in front of me. To be willing to try something new.
Congratulations, Toby Fox, and the rest of your team. You made the Game Of The Year 2015.

How does one put UnderTale into words? Well, there's a decent amount I want to say, but I don't want to go too in-depth, because I want to let the game to all of the talking. Or typing. Or whatever. Undertale is an RPG where you are a human trying to escape a world of monsters, and you can either fight the monsters that get in your way, or you can interact with the monsters in unique ways to negotiate with them to make them stop attacking you.
Now, the developers (mostly one person, by the way), COULD have shoehorned this idea into a regular RPG to make it a subpar game. But they said "YOU THINK YOU'RE TALKING TO A LOSER, FOOL?" and made it so then your actions change how the characters interact with you and how the plots progresses. Changing small details in your playthrough will change small details about the plot, and same with large variations. It remembers EVERYTHING you do, not only through your playthrough, but sometimes even WHEN YOU QUIT and ACROSS DIFFERENT PLAYTHROUGHS. This works especially well because of how good the story is in general.
This is certainly a game that is much better when you play it more than one time. Not only to get the different endings, but to also pick apart the tiny bits of dialogue that foreshadow the rest of the game. There is some VERY clever and subtle foreshadowing hidden away in the very specific wordings of the characters' sentences. I've completed the game twice, and looking back on all of the dialogue I can still find little tidbits that I haven't notice before, as there are also some minor subplots that are actually really interesting most of the time.
Now,this is probably obvious, but just remember, AVOID SPOILERS AT ALL COSTS. I had a couple things get spoiled for me, but luckily it was nothing too major. But please don't even look up something about undertale on youtube if you are in the middle of a runthrough or want to playthrough another time, and if you need walkthrough, either asked a friend who has played it or google it and be VERY careful searching.
The little touches are great too. The music is PHENOMINAL (or however you spell it), I recommend picking up the soundtrack as you pick up the game as you will save a little and if you have an interest in video game music, chances are you'll pick it up in the end anyway. The sprite is also simple (for the most part), but still looks nice.
Like I said, I don't want to give away too much, because this game is truly something to play for yourself. And if what I had to say hadn't convinced you, let me say this.
This is the one video game, heck, the one ANYTHING,that I believe that everyone, EVERYONE in the world, on this very earth, should experience. I'm not exaggerating. I've already considered ways to get my irl friends to play it (like possibly paying for their copy), I've already talked about it with one of my brothers about having them play it and I plan on talking to my other siblings who live nearby. I want to spread this game even further than it's gotten. This can't be something that is simply lost to history. Not just "another thing".
So please. Try it if you haven't yet. And when you're done, tell your other friends. I hope you'll see why I put this game on such a high pedestal.

---You are about to read a short story of on my experiences in Rust. A note to consider, this might never happen to you. However I'm hoping that such a 'review' will help you decide to buy this game because never will you experience anything, like what you will in rust, in any other game. ---
There I was standing. Thinking that I must be the luckiest person on earth. A player with full clothing (you don't see that a lot in rust) and a bolt action rifle in hand. You must be thinking 'how on earth is that considered lucky?'. But did I forget to mention that he was AFK. So exited, I ran towards him with my makeshift spear and was about to rip him to bits until I saw his name tag. It read 'BDB'. It took me a few seconds to remember the name, 'Have I ever met you before'. Then I remembered.
Two days earlier I had met two complete beginners at the game. They were running towards me, rocks in hand, shouting 'FRIENDLY' to assure the fact that they weren't going to attack me on sight. I shouted the same word back to them but took out my spear to take precaution. After a few  seconds of dark silence I thought I should offer them food. I would always to that to the 'friendly' so that i  could make more friends than enemies. As they thanked me and ate some food they explained how they were quite new to the game and were looking for some place to mine some rock. I told them that I was making a Noob (as us gamers call beginners)  shelter up in the mountains and was willing to teach them the ropes. I also gave them the rock they needed. After that we started to improve the base together, and make it a home for all of us. I was also quite a Noob at the time so they also taught me things I didn't know. We became a strong trio who had a nice fortified base until the day where i decided to sep out the front door of our house at the wrong time.
I told my two friends (one of them was away) that I was going out to fortify the base with a few more barricades. However the moment I opened the front door to our base I was shot done. Raiders. The screen read 'You were killed by BDB'. They were listening to our conversations and looking for just the right time to raid us. I shouted at one of my friends to take cover inside the base, while I was given the option to respawn at my sleeping bag also inside the base. It was hopeless. My friend with just a bow to fight off pesky raiders with full protective clothing. I had nothing to fight with and the raiders looted my previous body and gained access to the house using my key. My friend with the bow fought hard and dealt a good amount of damages but soon enough, the bullets had finally ripped through his skin. They killed me once again with my friend and renamed our sleeping bags to prevent us from respawning. BDB... never have i had so much hatred for another player in a game. BDB. Never did i see my two friends ever again. All because of that raider. BDB.
I got my spear in hand and started to pierce through the skin of the AFK raider. Such joy filled my heart like never before. Revenge had never felt so sweet. BDB was no longer. I started to loot through his dead body and steal all the valuables. I equiped my self in my dead foes armor and help his gun in my hands. Though that wasn't the end. I was running away from the murder scene when the message from a very angry player came onto the message section. BDB was looking for revenge and considering the fact that he was apart of the the servers currently biggest (and strongest)  clan, there was no doubt he was going to get it.
I was running as fast as I could, from the dead body of the raider, when I saw another player dressed in full burlap armor ( the weakest in the game). It was the same guy who had killed me prior to myself finding AFK BDB. I thought that, now that was equiped with things that were vastly better than his, i should probably take my second revenge for the day. So I did, using 'only' two bullets. He was laying on the floor, pleading for me to revive him. I thought to myself that 'I am better than this' so i had just taken his weapons for precaution. As he got up he thanked me and had also invited me to his base. Or should I say bases. He had two, one of which was raided so after inspecting that we went to his second base. Both bases were fairly large and fortified so I had thought that he must have been in affiliation with another strong clan, especially considering the fact that he was Russian himself.
We had finally arrived at his second base. I was at the front of his base, admiring it, when all of sudden a bullet came flying across my head. I shouted at the Russian to take cover at a giant rock opposite the front of the house. Bullets were flying everywhere meaning the were clearly well stocked. I tried to shoot back at them but we were pinned down. The Russian quickly ran into the house through the front door, and got shoot in the back while trying to do so. Fortunately he made it in and he was shouting at me to also come so he could fortify it. I considered whether I should trust him or not, but then I thought 'I have also attacked a fair share of naked's ,for no good reason, in my time playing rust'. So i eventually complied and ran towards the door while, luckily, dodging two. bullets.
We made our way to the top floor, where there was a window to get a good view on our opponents, and started to discuss what we should do. We tried to look through the window and shoot them, though every time we attempted so bullets would start to fly from our opponents guns. I decided eventually, that i should try talking to them. I asked them to put there guns down. It wasn't the reply that had devastated me but the player from whom I had received the reply from. Chistine. She was apart of the the biggest and strongest clan in the server. The same clan BDB was from.
Half an hour had passed. Much discussion had taken place. We had no hope in just running outside the base and trying to shoot them. Our opponent was obviously more trained than us, and her and her other partners had more firepower than my Russian friend and I. Also if we had really been a threat to them they would have called for back up. There base was no too far from ours so it would be no problem for them. If we wanted to leave this situation alive we had to play it smart. Christine had told us to come outside of the house naked with no weapons so that we could discuss further. Many other random players hearing this conversation warned me not to trust her. I had already figured that out by myself.
Now I could continue my story and start to talk about my mastermind plan and a big battle, but not much really happens. Nothing really goes in my favour. I end up randomly dying and my both Christine and my Russian friend both join forces with me out of the picture. The End.

I have never been a big PC Gamer. I plan on getting a powerful enough PC that I can at least attempt to play some of the bigger games, but even then, I have a very mixed opinion of games on PC, with most of my experience on PC being browser games on Cartoon Network and those games you got from cereal boxes. I have also been console gamer, and still am. Added with the fact I'm working a part-time job trying to pay school debt, I need to learn to be extremely cautious when it comes to buying games, especially on this site, when hundreds of games are on sale every week. If there are any PC games that I do buy, they're cheap, and not always that impressive, just mindless time.
So when I heard all the praise this simple-looking game was getting, I was very skeptical. but at least willing to try. An RPG that can play even on toasters without problems with a $10 price tag (even with no sale) was appealing. So I bought it.
And then I fell in love.
Undertale somehow captures a torrent of feelings that I never felt playing video games since I played Banjo-Kazooie for the first time on N64. It opened me like nothing else that came before it. Sometimes it made you feel young, made you feel loving, made you cry, laugh, worried, regretful, accomplished. Determined.
Even when you get past the slap fest that your amygdala puts you through, it is a deceptively clever game. A turn based combat system that combines logic puzzles, action commands ala Mario & Luigi RPG's, and a bullet hell-like dodge system, each battle and enemy has a unique experience that leaves a lasting impression. The designs of the monsters you find in this game aren't overly complicated, but have a loving charm to them, like Mickey Mouse or Bugs Bunny, and while the overworld sprite art is the main issue I have with this game (my own nitpick if you will), it was never something that made the game unplayable, just that it caused confusion, such as where a mouth was positioned in relation to the rest of the face, etc., and was only a slight issue with some sprite art, not a reflection of the overall quality of the artstyle.
The story, much like the battle system, is also deceptively clever, and branches out in a way that only a video game could ever accomplish. I won't spoil too much on how the story unravels, but you WILL get invested. There is no doubt in that. The way that it sets the mood in each specific part and succeeds in getting the reactions it wanted from you shows how well crafted the story is. The soundtrack (which I bought here shortly after) is fantastic, not just 8-bit music, but a combination of styles that fits each situation they are heard in. When you feel happy, sad, scared, or just want to laugh forever, the music let's you know your feelings are justified.
When I got to the end of my own personal journey, I felt like a giddy little kid and just wanted to never stop playing and  replay it over and over again, but every adventure needs to end. I will always cherish the time I had with this game, giving me a sense of curiosity that I never felt in years when it came to video games. It reminded me to never be too judgmental on games and just experience it. To enjoy what I have in front of me. To be willing to try something new.
Congratulations, Toby Fox, and the rest of your team. You made the Game Of The Year 2015.

DayZ in many ways is less a game and more of a psychological experiment. It shows without question that there is a large contingent of society when placed in a situation where there is no reprecussions for evil or selfish acts, they will jump at the chance to commit said act. People complain of Shooting on sight. However, in reality if you were in this situation, should you choose not to shoot someone you dont know imediately you are taking a very high risk of getting shot yourself.
The most difficult thing to realize with this game is, that it isnt Hollywood. There are no hero's, and you are not invincible. Getting shot in the back of the head from a guy 700 meters away just happens sometimes. As careful as you are. Eventually, someone will get you. Unless, you have friends.
Some of the bugs in this game are absolutly INFURIATING! The Zombies should be taken out of the game entirely untill they can get them working even halfway decent. Currently, they are all seeing, heat seeking, wall passing, lag monsters. They hit you from WAY to far away. Their ability to hit you through walls....really....Zombies need A LOT of work.
Player to player interaction is second to none. I have had some of the most tense standoffs, as well as interesting encounters with other players. Nobody trusts anybody, and it makes for some very dynamic events ingame. Some of the most memorable moments in gaming I have ever had have been in this game. DayZ is in a class of its own when it comes to atmosphere, and player to player interaction.
With that said, when your character has been alive for a long time, and you have alot of really nice gear. It is very painful to suddeny see a black screen saying your dead. All because some chickenshit is hiding in a bush with a shiny rifle just randomly shooting people.
Perfect example: I just logged off as I was a new spawn. I had a tshirt, blue jeans, a baseball hat, and a kitchen knife. I was happy to have found a well out back of a house and I was greedily drinking water from the well to quench my thirst and get hydrated for the hike north when BANG. Black screen, dead....Now you tell me...You saw me. I had on a tshirt and jeans....I had a knife in my hand...was I threat to you? I was drinking water for crying out loud....why shoot me...
I LOVE THIS GAME! I ABSOLUTLY HATE THIS GAME!
It does so much right, but it kicks you in the balls repeatedly for enjoying it. This game is not for the light hearted. If you are the kind of guy that always plays the hero. You arent going to like this game. Society has fallen, and so must you. Be prepared to kill perfectly innocent people. Because if you dont, they're going to kill you.
Make some friends and play this game. I guarntee you will have experiences that will seem so real, your heart will pound. No other game has ever made my hands shake after killing another player. I was genuinly shaking after one of my first encounters....
Atmosphere? This game has it in SPADES!!!

People complain of Shooting on sight. With that said, when your character has been alive for a long time, and you have alot of really nice gear. It is very painful to suddeny see a black screen saying your dead. All because some chickenshit is hiding in a bush with a shiny rifle just randomly shooting people.

I was happy to have found a well out back of a house and I was greedily drinking water from the well to quench my thirst and get hydrated for the hike north when BANG. I have never been a big PC Gamer. I plan on getting a powerful enough PC that I can at least attempt to play some of the bigger games, but even then, I have a very mixed opinion of games on PC, with most of my experience on PC being browser games on Cartoon Network and those games you got from cereal boxes. I have also been console gamer, and still am. Added with the fact I'm working a part-time job trying to pay school debt, I need to learn to be extremely cautious when it comes to buying games, especially on this site, when hundreds of games are on sale every week. If there are any PC games that I do buy, they're cheap, and not always that impressive, just mindless time.
So when I heard all the praise this simple-looking game was getting, I was very skeptical. but at least willing to try. An RPG that can play even on toasters without problems with a $10 price tag (even with no sale) was appealing. So I bought it.
And then I fell in love.
Undertale somehow captures a torrent of feelings that I never felt playing video games since I played Banjo-Kazooie for the first time on N64. It opened me like nothing else that came before it. Sometimes it made you feel young, made you feel loving, made you cry, laugh, worried, regretful, accomplished. Determined.
Even when you get past the slap fest that your amygdala puts you through, it is a deceptively clever game. A turn based combat system that combines logic puzzles, action commands ala Mario & Luigi RPG's, and a bullet hell-like dodge system, each battle and enemy has a unique experience that leaves a lasting impression. The designs of the monsters you find in this game aren't overly complicated, but have a loving charm to them, like Mickey Mouse or Bugs Bunny, and while the overworld sprite art is the main issue I have with this game (my own nitpick if you will), it was never something that made the game unplayable, just that it caused confusion, such as where a mouth was positioned in relation to the rest of the face, etc., and was only a slight issue with some sprite art, not a reflection of the overall quality of the artstyle.
The story, much like the battle system, is also deceptively clever, and branches out in a way that only a video game could ever accomplish. I won't spoil too much on how the story unravels, but you WILL get invested. There is no doubt in that. The way that it sets the mood in each specific part and succeeds in getting the reactions it wanted from you shows how well crafted the story is. The soundtrack (which I bought here shortly after) is fantastic, not just 8-bit music, but a combination of styles that fits each situation they are heard in. When you feel happy, sad, scared, or just want to laugh forever, the music let's you know your feelings are justified.
When I got to the end of my own personal journey, I felt like a giddy little kid and just wanted to never stop playing and  replay it over and over again, but every adventure needs to end. I will always cherish the time I had with this game, giving me a sense of curiosity that I never felt in years when it came to video games. It reminded me to never be too judgmental on games and just experience it. To enjoy what I have in front of me. To be willing to try something new.
Congratulations, Toby Fox, and the rest of your team. You made the Game Of The Year 2015.

Don't like RPG's? This is the game for you.
Don't like puns? This is the game for you.
Don't like humor or amazing characters, you soulless monster? This is the game for you. (P.S. Get dunked on.)
Don't like anything that happens to give other, normal people pleasure? I don't care; just play it.
Seriously, though. This game is a masterpiece. I first learned about only a week ago and fell in love with it the moment I saw it. It has amazing music that has me jamming out in the middle of a hard boss fight (MEGALOVANIA), lovable characters that make you smile, and brilliant dialogue that can be witty, heartfelt, and just downright hilarious.
The best part, though, is this. You know all that stuff that I just mentioned? Yeah, you have the power to destroy it all if you so choose. You can ravage the world, kill every character, and even lose that amazing, jamming music when it is replaced by that dark ambience thet gets ME scared. You can be an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to everyone or befriend everything and have some good fun. But the moment that you start to kill everything.....well...
Let's just say you're gonna be in for a BAD TIME.
Unless you enjoy being a soulless monster and a murderer, chances are, you're gonna be kind to everyone. Which is good.
On the off chance that you ARE a murderer, you are in for a treat. While the regular game (Pacifist Run) has a serene and lighthearted atmosphere filled with laughs and nice friends, the Genocide Run is not so happy. The atmosphere change is huge, and it is definitely somethng that you'll notice. In the Pacifist Run, the boss fights are hard but doable, and you get many different ones that usually will only take you one go. In the Genocide Run? Well... You're not so lucky. You get two boss fights. The catch? Holy jhsauighdsgfdsvjxchgvyxcfyds, they're THE HARDEST BOSS FIGHTS EVER. It took me hours to defeat the first one, and I still am having a VERY BAD TIME with the other!
My only hint for you future players is: Look for the patterns on the boss fight (of the Genocide Run) and memorize when they use what attack. Know when to heal and when to attack, and hopefully things will be a bit easier.
Anyway, if you want a game where your choices matter, this is also a very good game for you.
Every (and I mean EVERY) choice matters. Each one has some sort of importance, and the game remembers all of your choices, sometimes even in differing playthroughs. Let's say you play Genocide and then Pacifist. That Pacifist Run will be tainted from the leftovers of your killing spree, even though you already restarted the game and played with a blank slate.
Although this may seem like a bad thing, it hugely opens up the amount of possibilities of endings that the game has, so have a lot of fun trying to find them all (along with all of the secrets of the game).
Overall,

---You are about to read a short story of on my experiences in Rust. A note to consider, this might never happen to you. However I'm hoping that such a 'review' will help you decide to buy this game because never will you experience anything, like what you will in rust, in any other game. ---
There I was standing. Thinking that I must be the luckiest person on earth. A player with full clothing (you don't see that a lot in rust) and a bolt action rifle in hand. You must be thinking 'how on earth is that considered lucky?'. But did I forget to mention that he was AFK. So exited, I ran towards him with my makeshift spear and was about to rip him to bits until I saw his name tag. It read 'BDB'. It took me a few seconds to remember the name, 'Have I ever met you before'. Then I remembered.
Two days earlier I had met two complete beginners at the game. They were running towards me, rocks in hand, shouting 'FRIENDLY' to assure the fact that they weren't going to attack me on sight. I shouted the same word back to them but took out my spear to take precaution. After a few  seconds of dark silence I thought I should offer them food. I would always to that to the 'friendly' so that i  could make more friends than enemies. As they thanked me and ate some food they explained how they were quite new to the game and were looking for some place to mine some rock. I told them that I was making a Noob (as us gamers call beginners)  shelter up in the mountains and was willing to teach them the ropes. I also gave them the rock they needed. After that we started to improve the base together, and make it a home for all of us. I was also quite a Noob at the time so they also taught me things I didn't know. We became a strong trio who had a nice fortified base until the day where i decided to sep out the front door of our house at the wrong time.
I told my two friends (one of them was away) that I was going out to fortify the base with a few more barricades. However the moment I opened the front door to our base I was shot done. Raiders. The screen read 'You were killed by BDB'. They were listening to our conversations and looking for just the right time to raid us. I shouted at one of my friends to take cover inside the base, while I was given the option to respawn at my sleeping bag also inside the base. It was hopeless. My friend with just a bow to fight off pesky raiders with full protective clothing. I had nothing to fight with and the raiders looted my previous body and gained access to the house using my key. My friend with the bow fought hard and dealt a good amount of damages but soon enough, the bullets had finally ripped through his skin. They killed me once again with my friend and renamed our sleeping bags to prevent us from respawning. BDB... never have i had so much hatred for another player in a game. BDB. Never did i see my two friends ever again. All because of that raider. BDB.
I got my spear in hand and started to pierce through the skin of the AFK raider. Such joy filled my heart like never before. Revenge had never felt so sweet. BDB was no longer. I started to loot through his dead body and steal all the valuables. I equiped my self in my dead foes armor and help his gun in my hands. Though that wasn't the end. I was running away from the murder scene when the message from a very angry player came onto the message section. BDB was looking for revenge and considering the fact that he was apart of the the servers currently biggest (and strongest)  clan, there was no doubt he was going to get it.
I was running as fast as I could, from the dead body of the raider, when I saw another player dressed in full burlap armor ( the weakest in the game). It was the same guy who had killed me prior to myself finding AFK BDB. I thought that, now that was equiped with things that were vastly better than his, i should probably take my second revenge for the day. So I did, using 'only' two bullets. He was laying on the floor, pleading for me to revive him. I thought to myself that 'I am better than this' so i had just taken his weapons for precaution. As he got up he thanked me and had also invited me to his base. Or should I say bases. He had two, one of which was raided so after inspecting that we went to his second base. Both bases were fairly large and fortified so I had thought that he must have been in affiliation with another strong clan, especially considering the fact that he was Russian himself.
We had finally arrived at his second base. I was at the front of his base, admiring it, when all of sudden a bullet came flying across my head. I shouted at the Russian to take cover at a giant rock opposite the front of the house. Bullets were flying everywhere meaning the were clearly well stocked. I tried to shoot back at them but we were pinned down. The Russian quickly ran into the house through the front door, and got shoot in the back while trying to do so. Fortunately he made it in and he was shouting at me to also come so he could fortify it. I considered whether I should trust him or not, but then I thought 'I have also attacked a fair share of naked's ,for no good reason, in my time playing rust'. If you care about video games as a serious form of art, you really should play this game to completion.  You will only understand what all the fuss is about when you see the best ending.
It's difficult to talk much about Undertale without spoiling things.  If this review seems vague, that is the reason.
There are many good things about Undertale.
It deals with some serious subject matter, and gives it the complex and detailed coverage it deserves, instead of resorting to simplistic, unworkable or even harmful, political tripe.  It does this without becoming depressing by mixing in lot of comedy, like the practice of performing comedies after tragedies in Shakespeare's day.
It does not have a plot in the conventional sense.  Every playthrough is likely to be at least a little different.  A vanishingly small number of other games (e.g.
) have achieved this with extremely deep simulation.  Undertale achieves this by making almost everything you do, even seemingly minor things, impact a large number of other things you will encounter later in the game.
The best ending is fully interactive, and if you do everything you can it will probably take you an hour or more.  I can't praise this highly enough!  Not only is it something I've never seen done before, but many other games have short, unrewarding endings, or even ones that punish the player for winning by having something bad happen to their or other loved characters.
I love the “Act” and “Mercy” parts of the combat system.
I really like the soundtrack.  It's quirky, but very listenable.  It's also long enough to leave playing for quite a while without becoming repetitive.
Even some things I do not like (like some aspects of the combat system) could be argued to be ‘part of the message’.
Undertale is not perfect, in my opinion.  However, it comes closer than most other games.
I am personally not a fan of the action aspect of the combat system.  The boss fights in the last half of the game would require someone to react with the speed and precision of a computer without certain items that they are unlikely to have.  This is too difficult to be fun.  At least the game does include a workaround (the necessary items) for those of us who cannot react that quickly and accurately.
Undertale misleads you into thinking you should avoid picking up or buying items because your inventory will be too limited with some bad advice in the beginning.  Further, it punishes you for using up certain consumables by making them unique or unavailable (because part of the world becomes inaccessible) later on.  One of almost every consumable is needed to complete a quest, or end a fight quickly, somewhere in the game.  The strangest thing is there seems to be no reason for this.
There also appears to be one bug in the game.  The solution to the piano puzzle sounds nothing like the hint.
Undertale lacks the settings PC gamers have come to expect.  There are no graphics or sound settings.  You can run the game in fullscreen mode or in a tiny window that cannot be resized.  It would be really nice to be able to resize and maximize/restore that window.  It would also be really nice to be able to set the music and sound effect volume.  There is no way to remap the keys, which default to the arrow keys (movement and selection) and Z (confirm), X (cancel), and C (menu).  Given that the game demands speed and precision, it would be really nice to be able to change those key bindings to something more comfortable.
I was gifted this game by a friend, and am very grateful.  This is one of the most enjoyable, and important, games I own.
I hope this game will fill others with determination to confront serious subject matter in their games, and provide such impressive replayability.

Undertale is without a doubt the best game I have ever played in which I have no intentions of ever playing again.
Okay, so where to begin?
In all honesty, I was near the end of typing out a massive review covering every mechanic and facet of the game in extensive detail. But reading it, I don't think I was doing the game justice.
With the popularity Undertale is reiceiving, if you are reading this then you have likely heard a bit about it already and are wondering what the fuss is about.
All that can be said is that Undertale is a game that you need to experience for yourself and it is far more then the sum of its parts. A written review simply cannot convey what makes Undertale such a beautiful game. I will probably fail to do Undertale justice in continuing the attempt, but alas.
The battle systen is very fun, combining bullet hell sequences in which you must dodge enemy attacks, dialogue based puzzles in which you figure out how to pacify the enemy and a simple timing minigame to attack your foes (This being something you may wish to forego entirely) but the storyline, characters and raw emotional responses this game evokes from the player are what truly define it.
The game manages to balance different tones and moods beautifully. This game will make break your heart one minute, then have you laughing out loud the next and then might decide to follow up for creeping the F*** out of you.
It balances the clashing tones and emotions in an effective manner that doesn't feel out of place in the slightest, and does it a way few developers can match,
Its also one of the few games in which the storyline is combined with the gameplay to such a strong level. This is one of those few game stories that could only work as a game; what are first presented as your standard RPG cliches are torn apart and dissected as the game goes on. Whilst this cannot be discussed in detail without delving into spoilders, lets just say that playing may seriously make you think about the implications of Levelling, EXP and saving in future games you play.
Undertale is a game I cannot recommend enough and a strong contender for GOTY 2015 and one I see scoring very highly on "greatest game of all time" countdowns for years to come.

Don't like puns? This is the game for you.
Don't like humor or amazing characters, you soulless monster? This is the game for you. (P.S. Get dunked on.)
Don't like anything that happens to give other, normal people pleasure? I don't care; just play it.
Seriously, though. This game is a masterpiece. I first learned about only a week ago and fell in love with it the moment I saw it. It has amazing music that has me jamming out in the middle of a hard boss fight (MEGALOVANIA), lovable characters that make you smile, and brilliant dialogue that can be witty, heartfelt, and just downright hilarious.
The best part, though, is this. You know all that stuff that I just mentioned? Yeah, you have the power to destroy it all if you so choose. You can ravage the world, kill every character, and even lose that amazing, jamming music when it is replaced by that dark ambience thet gets ME scared. You can be an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to everyone or befriend everything and have some good fun. But the moment that you start to kill everything.....well...
Let's just say you're gonna be in for a BAD TIME.
Unless you enjoy being a soulless monster and a murderer, chances are, you're gonna be kind to everyone. Which is good.
On the off chance that you ARE a murderer, you are in for a treat. While the regular game (Pacifist Run) has a serene and lighthearted atmosphere filled with laughs and nice friends, the Genocide Run is not so happy. The atmosphere change is huge, and it is definitely somethng that you'll notice. In the Pacifist Run, the boss fights are hard but doable, and you get many different ones that usually will only take you one go. In the Genocide Run? Well... You're not so lucky. You get two boss fights. The catch? Holy jhsauighdsgfdsvjxchgvyxcfyds, they're THE HARDEST BOSS FIGHTS EVER. It took me hours to defeat the first one, and I still am having a VERY BAD TIME with the other!
My only hint for you future players is: Look for the patterns on the boss fight (of the Genocide Run) and memorize when they use what attack. Know when to heal and when to attack, and hopefully things will be a bit easier.
Anyway, if you want a game where your choices matter, this is also a very good game for you.
Every (and I mean EVERY) choice matters. Each one has some sort of importance, and the game remembers all of your choices, sometimes even in differing playthroughs. Let's say you play Genocide and then Pacifist. That Pacifist Run will be tainted from the leftovers of your killing spree, even though you already restarted the game and played with a blank slate.
Although this may seem like a bad thing, it hugely opens up the amount of possibilities of endings that the game has, so have a lot of fun trying to find them all (along with all of the secrets of the game).
Overall,

...

This game is one of the best games that I have ever played, and I fell in love with it almost instantly.
It draws you in through its story, makes you feel empathy for characters on a computer screen, even from the get go.
You can play the game however you want, even by not killing a single thing in your entire game, and you'll always want to try and get a better ending.
Drawing inspiration from Earthbound, Undertale reinvents the JRPG for the modern day, and it's truly astounding to think that this game was made by one guy, Toby Fox.
From the wacky game design to hilarious dialogue, this game will make you laugh out loud from the scenes inside, even during fight scenes, I couldn't help but chuckle at the fact that you could attempt to date the person that you're fighting midway through.
All in all, it's a game that you may think "oh, but once I've got the best possible ending, I'll never need to play it again", but I assure you, you'll be back to play it again time and time again.

Rust, throughout it's ups and downs of development, has proven to be my favorite game, and will remain it for time to come.
Rust is a hardcore survival game with a heavy focus of player interaction and raiding. The game revolves around talking to people and forming relations, whether good or bad. These relations may result in becoming allies or having a potential raid. Having 300+ hours in the game, I can tell you raiding is a blast, and defending from raids is nerve-racking and tense. I love Rust, and the developers behind the game, while not entirely graceful, get the job done and provide what they know is best for us players.
Rust has undergone a lot of development changes, including a full reboot to optimize the game's code and mechanics. The older version is referred to as "Legacy", and while a select few rant about the new version and how the "good ol' days" in Legacy were superior, the new version has proven itself stable and completely playable, and in my eyes is much better than Legacy ever was or could be.
And please, don't let this game's nudity turn you away. Many complain about the game's themes being "gross" and "rude", but nudity is a part of life, it's natural and people need to stop being sensitive. Rust is a game about survival, and if you can't handle a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥or two, you can't handle survival within this game.
Overall, to put it in simple terms, Rust is my favorite game of all time. It can create intense feelings and attachments, spawning fear and nerve-racking tension in your mind throughout game-play. Any game that has the power to evoke such emotion into it's players, making you feel truly naked and afraid, is worth my money and worth your's as well.
Buy Rust, you will not regret it.
Remember to tRUST no one. (Except me, because this is a damn awesome game! XD)

Latest version is unoptimized, so I recommend the legacy version that is included with Rust (just use the legacy beta version after downloading). Since I've played legacy more, that's what this review will be about.
Rust has a great concept: gather resources and just try to survive. Gathering wood and stone is easy since you can find them nearly everywhere, but finding animals to kill for food is a little challenging since they are relatively hard to find. If more animals were spawned in worlds then it would make the game a little easier.
Playing by yourself will get boring quick, so you should either get some friends to play with you or join a public server. Keep in mind that other players are usually hostile on sight, so it may be hard to actually find someone to hang out with. If anything, you can download the server files and host a server yourself; that way you can set it up to your standards and likings.
The game itself is good. I'd just recommend that you make sure you have trustworthy people/friends to play along with before you buy it. Undertale is without a doubt the best game I have ever played in which I have no intentions of ever playing again.
Okay, so where to begin?
In all honesty, I was near the end of typing out a massive review covering every mechanic and facet of the game in extensive detail. But reading it, I don't think I was doing the game justice.
With the popularity Undertale is reiceiving, if you are reading this then you have likely heard a bit about it already and are wondering what the fuss is about.
All that can be said is that Undertale is a game that you need to experience for yourself and it is far more then the sum of its parts. A written review simply cannot convey what makes Undertale such a beautiful game. I will probably fail to do Undertale justice in continuing the attempt, but alas.
The battle systen is very fun, combining bullet hell sequences in which you must dodge enemy attacks, dialogue based puzzles in which you figure out how to pacify the enemy and a simple timing minigame to attack your foes (This being something you may wish to forego entirely) but the storyline, characters and raw emotional responses this game evokes from the player are what truly define it.
The game manages to balance different tones and moods beautifully. This game will make break your heart one minute, then have you laughing out loud the next and then might decide to follow up for creeping the F*** out of you.
It balances the clashing tones and emotions in an effective manner that doesn't feel out of place in the slightest, and does it a way few developers can match,
Its also one of the few games in which the storyline is combined with the gameplay to such a strong level. This is one of those few game stories that could only work as a game; what are first presented as your standard RPG cliches are torn apart and dissected as the game goes on. Whilst this cannot be discussed in detail without delving into spoilders, lets just say that playing may seriously make you think about the implications of Levelling, EXP and saving in future games you play.
Undertale is a game I cannot recommend enough and a strong contender for GOTY 2015 and one I see scoring very highly on "greatest game of all time" countdowns for years to come.
Oh, and buy the soundtrack too. It's frickin' brilliant.

Every few months, if not every year, there comes along a game that absolutely annihilates the idea that triple A games are the best in the market. In fact, they prove that triple A games have nullified our ideal gaming scenario: a somewhat immersive environment where no characters are even noteworthy. Undertale is an indie game that truly mocks triple A games -- a short experience, but an extremely memorable one, and completely immersive.
There are few games, especially triple A, where there are any standout characters. In Undertale, every character, even those shown for only small sections of the game, are interesting and aren't just white husks sitting on the screen. It's why I couldn't bring myself to kill all of them in a Genocide Run. (In fact, I've only ever killed one of the lead characters, and that was only on my first run of it.)
The emotions in Undertale are legitimate. The game starts off with humor that always hits on its mark. It'll have you laughing at every encounter, and want more and more. Then, depending on your choices, it can make you hate yourself, hate a certain character (you know who I'm talking about), and/or feel generally awful for the circumstances the monsters in the game are in. If you play Undertale and finish the True Pacifist ending, you WILL be in tears. It's depiction of loneliness, compassion, and grief will make you mourn for the character in question. It's an absolute masterpiece when it comes to the emotions presented in the game.
Above all, the game is all-immersive. I can't give out exactly why, because of spoilers (and I don't want to spoil this game at all, not even with a spoiler block), but you will be part of the game. At first, you won't notice it...but slowly and surely two characters will put you into the spotlight. And its those two characters who drive all the endings of the game.
Undertale has no plot holes, it's narrative is the best in any game I've ever played in my life. The amount of motivation the game creates is outstanding, and nothing is black or white (except for the characters that is). It's a complex narrative that drives you to finish it, and depending on how you play, the ending will either be the most satisfying conclusion, or it will be a devastation loss for no purpose. It's up to you.
Overall, Undertale truly slaps triple A gaming. It's a testament to why I almost never play any anymore. It only has three distinctly different endings (albeit there can be many different endings, but there are three truly different ones), but it is able to do what no triple A game has ever done: create a narrative solely focused on player choice without sacrificing gameplay to it.
Instead of dropping $60 for Fallout 4, take $10 to Undertale. (I hear Fallout has some serious problems. Too much hype, maybe?)
Oh, and the music is good too.
If you doubt the humor of this game, check the specs required on the soundtrack.

This game is one of the best games that I have ever played, and I fell in love with it almost instantly.
It draws you in through its story, makes you feel empathy for characters on a computer screen, even from the get go.
You can play the game however you want, even by not killing a single thing in your entire game, and you'll always want to try and get a better ending.
Drawing inspiration from Earthbound, Undertale reinvents the JRPG for the modern day, and it's truly astounding to think that this game was made by one guy, Toby Fox.
From the wacky game design to hilarious dialogue, this game will make you laugh out loud from the scenes inside, even during fight scenes, I couldn't help but chuckle at the fact that you could attempt to date the person that you're fighting midway through.
All in all, it's a game that you may think "oh, but once I've got the best possible ending, I'll never need to play it again", but I assure you, you'll be back to play it again time and time again.

Every few months, if not every year, there comes along a game that absolutely annihilates the idea that triple A games are the best in the market. In fact, they prove that triple A games have nullified our ideal gaming scenario: a somewhat immersive environment where no characters are even noteworthy. Undertale is an indie game that truly mocks triple A games -- a short experience, but an extremely memorable one, and completely immersive.
There are few games, especially triple A, where there are any standout characters. In Undertale, every character, even those shown for only small sections of the game, are interesting and aren't just white husks sitting on the screen. It's why I couldn't bring myself to kill all of them in a Genocide Run. (In fact, I've only ever killed one of the lead characters, and that was only on my first run of it.)
The emotions in Undertale are legitimate. The game starts off with humor that always hits on its mark. It'll have you laughing at every encounter, and want more and more. Then, depending on your choices, it can make you hate yourself, hate a certain character (you know who I'm talking about), and/or feel generally awful for the circumstances the monsters in the game are in. If you play Undertale and finish the True Pacifist ending, you WILL be in tears. It's depiction of loneliness, compassion, and grief will make you mourn for the character in question. It's an absolute masterpiece when it comes to the emotions presented in the game.
Above all, the game is all-immersive. I can't give out exactly why, because of spoilers (and I don't want to spoil this game at all, not even with a spoiler block), but you will be part of the game. At first, you won't notice it...but slowly and surely two characters will put you into the spotlight. And its those two characters who drive all the endings of the game.
Undertale has no plot holes, it's narrative is the best in any game I've ever played in my life. The amount of motivation the game creates is outstanding, and nothing is black or white (except for the characters that is). It's a complex narrative that drives you to finish it, and depending on how you play, the ending will either be the most satisfying conclusion, or it will be a devastation loss for no purpose. It's up to you.
Overall, Undertale truly slaps triple A gaming. It's a testament to why I almost never play any anymore. It only has three distinctly different endings (albeit there can be many different endings, but there are three truly different ones), but it is able to do what no triple A game has ever done: create a narrative solely focused on player choice without sacrificing gameplay to it.
Instead of dropping $60 for Fallout 4, take $10 to Undertale. (I hear Fallout has some serious problems. Too much hype, maybe?)
Oh, and the music is good too.
If you doubt the humor of this game, check the specs required on the soundtrack.

Great RPG, very reminiscent of Earthbound but with a really interesting approach to pacifism. I'd say that where other games make pacifism into a simple achievement, this is the first game I know that uses it as an integral part of the game design and the story.
Having completed the game twice with different endings, I don't think I could bear to go for the remaining ending. The characters are just too loveable to do that :-/. It's been a long time since I felt this attached to the setting of a RPG. While the graphics are simple, they are an excellent match to the game and they are well animated in my opinion. The soundtrack is also very fitting.
I wouldn't recommend this game if you're not very good with a keyboard, though: some of the "bullet hell"-style bosses can be challenging. There are some items which should make it easier if you keep dying, but it's something to take into account.
Another tip: do *not* read any guides and be very careful with spoilers for this game. Half of the fun is being surprised at all the twists!

Undertale is a game made by an Earthbound fan, for Earthbound fans. If you liked any of the Mother/Earthbound games, you will like this game. If you don't like those games, you have obviously never played them.
This game has great characters, a catchy soundtrack, ingenious battle system, and a story that perfectly combines "Laugh your head off" with "Cry your eyes out".
Not only that, but this story is affected by how you play the game. Unlike many other games, death is permanent and has serious consequences. Kill someone just because they attack you? They are dead for good now. That person you just killed might have been someone's friend or family. This can drastically change your story.
Due to this principle, the game can end differently each time, depending on what you do. I would suggest playing this game at least 3 times, for the 3 main endings: Pacifist, Neutral, and Genocide.
Overall, Undertale is a great game, certainly worth the $10.

Firstly: I will say this, don't let the appearance of this game decieve you. The story that this game tells, and even the way that it's told really is something that HAS to be seen.
Second: Sadly I feel this Review must be kept short, as spoiling the game even a little I feel takes away too much from the experience.
Now then... This game has had a profound way of how I even normaly play, from changing my own play-style to even causing me to really think on what's going on and of my choices.
Because this game actually does choices that mater, it actually reacts to your decisions and even actions there-after, and I can't even stress how strongly I mean that.
Where as most games end up giving you a choice, where it ultimatly just changes the flavor slightly here and there, the choices done in this game can range from...
Without spoiling it: Just like how the Day, Nights, and even Dawn / Dust are different in their own ways, so are the outcomes to the decisions that you'll be doing when it all comes together.
Really think on what you'll be doing, as the ripples of your choices can reach farther and affect much more than what you might expect, even the smallest of decisions you make can have the most drastic of outcomes down the line.
Now, the sound design ranges from what you'd come to expect in a RPG of this kind, certain flare added in as well to the sound effects that make the experiences even greater and more inpactful.
But hands down the Music, I could gush about this for hours so I will just say this: The music is some of the best composed I've heard in that it always sets the mood, the pace, and the depth of feeling in every area that you venture into.
Really bringing home what's going on in the situation, from the calm down times to the nightmarish
scenarios that you could be thrust into, even moments where the music ALONE is able to cary the scene and the feel of what's happening.
Now as you can see I am regarding this game very highly, and if you saw what I have, learned what I did, and even compaired it to many games, even AAA games, you would see that this game actually went far above what it needed to be.
It took game mechanics that are rarely practiced, an interesting story-line, and many unique and drastically distinct characters and turned it all into something that is truly beyond what any words could bring it justice to describe it as.
For certain though it is this: It's an experience unlike many games over the recent years, and to me: This is a Game of a Lifetime, definetly in my top three if not THE best game I've EVER played because of how it all comes together.

My best gaming experience ever was way, way back when I popped my online cherry running up the beach in Enemy Territory (you never forget your first time!). DayZ however comes a very close second, and is head, shoulders, body and legs above anything else I've played in the intervening years. This game really creeps me out, but I just love it - I've gotten used to the zombies now, but nothing quite makes my blood run cold and gets the pulse going as when I come face to face with another player or hear a not too distant gunshot. The perma death aspect makes you play like your 'life' means something, which I've found a refreshing change (although you do have to accept that death is inevitable).
It is still in Alpha so you may want to wait a bit before buying, but I've enjoyed dipping in and out as they've developed the game and it's been good to get familiar with things as they come online. I've always been a fan of Zombies and end of the world scenarios. Every time I log on I feel that I'm starring in my own personal episode of the Walking Dead:
"...How many walkers have you killed? How many people have you killed? Why?..."

This game gets a lot of criticism for slow updates and glitchy gameplay. I like to believe that this is because people have an idea of what this game is going to become and want it now.  My biggest wish was that there were more zombies...Like a lot more, and I am fearful that the engine might not be able to take the stress, or that the devs believe this is a major pillar as it is player focused (zombies are there for background noise).
Overall this is my favorite video game to date.  The freedom and huge world to explore can make for some interesting situations unlike any other game I have played.  This is the only video game that I find myself watching youtube videos of other people playing it, its that good!
Regardless of what I say you are going to get this or your not.  If you want a finished polished title, give it time and pick it up later.  If you love zombies and dont mind a few bugs like me then go for it....The choice is yours!

Great RPG, very reminiscent of Earthbound but with a really interesting approach to pacifism. I'd say that where other games make pacifism into a simple achievement, this is the first game I know that uses it as an integral part of the game design and the story.
Having completed the game twice with different endings, I don't think I could bear to go for the remaining ending. The characters are just too loveable to do that :-/. It's been a long time since I felt this attached to the setting of a RPG. While the graphics are simple, they are an excellent match to the game and they are well animated in my opinion. The soundtrack is also very fitting.
I wouldn't recommend this game if you're not very good with a keyboard, though: some of the "bullet hell"-style bosses can be challenging. There are some items which should make it easier if you keep dying, but it's something to take into account.
Another tip: do *not* read any guides and be very careful with spoilers for this game. Half of the fun is being surprised at all the twists!

Undertale is a game made by an Earthbound fan, for Earthbound fans. If you liked any of the Mother/Earthbound games, you will like this game. If you don't like those games, you have obviously never played them.
This game has great characters, a catchy soundtrack, ingenious battle system, and a story that perfectly combines "Laugh your head off" with "Cry your eyes out".
Not only that, but this story is affected by how you play the game. Unlike many other games, death is permanent and has serious consequences. Kill someone just because they attack you? They are dead for good now. That person you just killed might have been someone's friend or family. This can drastically change your story.
Due to this principle, the game can end differently each time, depending on what you do. I would suggest playing this game at least 3 times, for the 3 main endings: Pacifist, Neutral, and Genocide.
Overall, Undertale is a great game, certainly worth the $10.

Played like any old RPG, Undertale would be standard fare.
Play it like you would life, though, and it becomes a truly amazing exercise in storytelling and raw emotion. Undertale is a thought-provoking game that builds into something more than the sum of its mechanics and its characters-- 10/10, would recommend.

An amazing game full of amazing characters, an interesting storyline based on your decisions, and beautiful pixel art topped with an incredible soundtrack. Loved every second playing it, and look forward to playing it again and again.

The bottom line is that you should buy this game just to try it out for yourself. It's the only way to REALLY know if you'll like it. The following "review" is only a list of afterthoughts and forewarnings gathered from experience and other people who don't enjoy the game. It'll probably give you a good idea on if you'll be rubbed the wrong way.
- Photosensitive epilepsy warning! There are instances of vibrating text and certain late battles can be visually overwhelming.
Though, I think the store page already says this by now.
- The game is really fond of long, featureless hallways. I'm very patient, so whenever I go through one of them, I actually worry that other people might be really put off by this boring hallway. I'm weird.
- The battles' main genre is ultimately Bullet Hell with simplified controls and mechanics. With exceptions, you're either moving or not moving; you either got hit or didn't get hit. It starts off easy, but it does get harder, so it expects you to have some skill. However, it is very kind in what counts as getting hit. Usually.
- The game knows if you get a game over. It's a selling point, yes, but some people really don't like being mocked or pitied for that kind of thing. Some people just don't like being told to be merciful, while others don't need to be talked down to.
- It has functional controller support, but don't expect any control stick sensitivity. You're better off using the d-pad/POV hat...or just going keyboard.
- Most say that the jokes don't overstay their welcome. In truth, some can. If you don't like its brand of humour, well... Nearly every joke comes back in some way, or at least runs for a little while. It's great if you love 'em, bad if you don't.

Rust is a game about survival. But that takes time. Initially, it's just about death. It's about freezing to death, and starving to death, being shot to death and getting bitten to death; occasionally mixing things up a little by slipping on a warm radiation coat and fading faster than your faith in humanity after being stabbed in the back by a supposed friend's hatchet. Sometimes you get gored to death. Other times, bored to death. It's not easy, surviving post-apocalyptic civilisation with nothing but a rock - especially when your enemies have guns, and double-especially in a game that makes you work just to earn a pair of basic trousers.
Even this early into development, Rust's mix of DayZ and Minecraft (the easiest comparison, though Wurm Online is more apt) has won it no shortage of fans - some of them not even psychopaths, hackers and trolls on the hunt for new victims to murder and mock over voice chat. It's the kind of game that's less a shooter than an engine designed to tell stories. Those stories are mostly, as ever, in the field of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥om, but there's scope for some humanity amongst all the pranks and murder. It's also a world that focuses on demanding effort rather than promising to reward it: starting players out naked and hungry and alone, dangling the potential of going on to build forts, craft weapons, and finally savour the air at the top of the food chain.

The bottom line is that you should buy this game just to try it out for yourself. It's the only way to REALLY know if you'll like it. The following "review" is only a list of afterthoughts and forewarnings gathered from experience and other people who don't enjoy the game. It'll probably give you a good idea on if you'll be rubbed the wrong way.
- Photosensitive epilepsy warning! There are instances of vibrating text and certain late battles can be visually overwhelming.
Though, I think the store page already says this by now.
- The game is really fond of long, featureless hallways. I'm very patient, so whenever I go through one of them, I actually worry that other people might be really put off by this boring hallway. I'm weird.
- The battles' main genre is ultimately Bullet Hell with simplified controls and mechanics. With exceptions, you're either moving or not moving; you either got hit or didn't get hit. It starts off easy, but it does get harder, so it expects you to have some skill. However, it is very kind in what counts as getting hit. Usually.
- The game knows if you get a game over. It's a selling point, yes, but some people really don't like being mocked or pitied for that kind of thing. Some people just don't like being told to be merciful, while others don't need to be talked down to.
- It has functional controller support, but don't expect any control stick sensitivity. You're better off using the d-pad/POV hat...or just going keyboard.
- Most say that the jokes don't overstay their welcome. In truth, some can. If you don't like its brand of humour, well... Nearly every joke comes back in some way, or at least runs for a little while. It's great if you love 'em, bad if you don't.
"If you're not laughing, then the joke is on you."
- In general, you don't really see a lot of character development with one normal playthrough. If you really want character development, you'll have to play it once, then see the polar opposite of the pacifist run. It's depressing, but...you really do see their best sides.
- The game expects you to be at least decent at dodging like it expects you to at least kinda get its references. It ranges from small things like missing a few referential jokes because you don't know what "tsundere" means, to possibly not being phased at all by certain scenes because you never experienced one of the games this takes inspiration from. It's one out of one-hundred, but they can add up if you miss a lot of ones.
If you're still reading and on the fence regarding this game, then I must conclude that you should try out the game for as long as you can. The most time you'll waste is around eight hours.
