(TL;DR AT THE BOTTOM)
Undertale is an "un-game". Yeah, yeah, I know that most games which are called that are crappy Hipster SJW garbage, but I mean it here. It's to JRPGs what Default Dan is to platformers, except with charm and an identity.
Even when you take the non-violent route of standing there doing nothing there's a challenge. The combat system (which you probably already know of) is similar to a bullethell, or shump, which means actively dodging enemy attacks. The mechanic itself is difficult in it's own right, and basically puts up two different experiences. RPG and story-rich bullethell.
The characters are memorable. Almost every NPC you see has something to say that will warrant at least a smile, if not a hearty chuckle. Out of all the games I've played, I can say that the main characters of Undertale (should you choose not to murder them) stand out the most among every other Western-developed franchise I can think of. '
Music is fantastic. Even people who hate this game acknowledge that much. Not much to say here.
All that said, I don't want to suck Toby Fox off too much. The game has flaws, but only one of them is thematic.
I've heard it said so many times that this game is an "Earthbound Wannabe", which couldn't be farther from the truth. As much as I love Earthbound (my second favorite game of all time), this game just frankly does story better. The characters in Earthbound weren't developed at all sans (badum tss) one or two lines of dialogue. Aesthetically and thematically it's kind of similar, so since other people consider that a con I'll list it as one too to play devil's advocate.
On a technical level this game is near abyssmal. It plays in 4:3, can't be stretched, lacks even a "Quit Game" button (ESC is all you get), can't even close right, and has the bare minimum of an options menu. It's a 2D RPG, but that doesn't excuse the lack of antialiasing (it can be a problem in battles on lower-end systems), a functioning sensitivity slider for joypads, RESOLUTION OPTIONS (AHEM AHEM AHEM), or a volume slider. At the very least it doesn't crash. It's stable, but light on the options menu TO SAY THE LEAST.
---TL;DR---
Pros:
>Memorable characters
>Unique and fun combat (or lack therof) system
>Great music
>Pleasing aesthetic
>Humor that wavers between Monty Python sarcasm and contemporary "randomness"
>$10 for an experience that will surely stick with you for a lifetime
Cons:
>INCREDIBLY light options menu
>Tiny windowed mode that can't be changed
>No resolution settings (see both above)
>Thematic similarities to Earthbound may put some people off (but they're pretty minute)

It's difficult to describe my favorite parts of this game without spoiling it so please keep that in mind if my review sounds vague. I recommend playing this game without spoilers and if possible to go with as little information as possible.
This game offers a lot of choices and reacts to many of them. It might be as simple as killing instead of sparing or using certain items in battle or in the overworld along with more obvious ones during dialogue. The game will react to player actions throughout and have minute changes accordingly. Thanks to this it felt more like it was a personal story rather than following a character through their journey. I should mention that most of these changes have little effect on the story as a whole but they level of detail in how the game reacts was impressive. For a better effect consider inputting your own name.
The writing was a definite strong point with characters being enjoyable and the story did a great job evoking the emotions it intended. That said, some running jokes got a bit old although the majority were amusing.
The music was especially good. I don't know how to describe music well but in most games I will only remember a specific track or two unless it is the main theme and only vaguely recognize other tracks. For this game, I remember actively liking them and thinking that I had to look up certain tracks later or remembering them because of how well it fit with a scene.
Now for a few non-spoiler tips: there's a some battle text that can be seen if you continue after the spare option is available, the phone will also get you extra comments in the game, and stay determined.

I follow the philosophy that there is no such thing as a perfect game. All games have at least one flaw.
The only flaw I have with Undertale is that it can be fairly cryptic. But is that really a flaw?
We live in a day and age where secrets are spread over the internet in a matter of minutes post-release.
NES Zelda's map went from being an endless realm of discovery to just being another map to go through on the internet.
Undertale is a game that let me discover secrets at my own pace. It made me question every desicion I made. Heck, I nearly died fighting multiple bosses before I discovered what I was supposed to do.
But exploring a boring world yields little reward. Luckily, Undertale had one of my favorite casts of characters in a game. Heck, they made regular enemy encounters a joy to experiance. That may also be because of the entertaining battle system. On defense, you are a tiny heart dodging enemy attacks. It sounds simple, but the battles get more complex as you encounter more enemies with different patterns or attack effects. On offense, you can either attack (line up lines to determine damage) or attempt to perform an act to end the fight without conflict. This makes it a joy to fight new enemies, as you have new attacks and acts to adapt to.
Finally, the music. Due to the pixelated art style, you may expect to hear a lot of chiptune. Yes, there is a lot of chiptune, but it's also combined with symphonic rock, jazz, accoustic, and an assortment of other musical styles. Of course, variety doesn't matter if all the songs are garbage. Luckily, I have found myself hard-pressed to think of one song that I wouldn't listen to for a second time, ESPECIALLY the boss themes, which are some of my favorite songs in the game.
Bottom line: If you like RPG's, you will like Undertale. If you like music, you will like Undertale. If you like good stories and characters, you will like Undertale. If you enjoy making choices that actually matter, you will like Undertale.
Basicly, it's a good game. But most likely, I'm not the first person you heard gushing about it. ;)

Undertale is a wonderful little nugget of pure gold. Of much higher quality than lots of triple A games.
It is a game where the only real monster you might actualy meet, depending on your way to play, is yourself. It is a masterpiece from A to Z.
The storyline is really well orchestrated and a real pleasure to discover through your adventures.
The whole game is filled with secrets, puns, references and other jokes that will constantly make you smile.
The soundtracks are by far ones of the bests I've ever happened to hear. Every melody, every note fits its environment and situation perfectly. It is a pure and perfect osmosis.
Every charachter has his own unique and strong personality, each and every one of them is amazingly attaching by his own way. You will feel truly happy for some, deeply sad for others. And some will terribly miss you...
At the end of my journey I only have one regret: knowing that this world and these wonderful charachters that I've met and love so much are finaly nothing more than bunches of pixels and lines of code. That truly breaks my heart, and that's why Toby Fox can really feel proud of what he has accomplished.
I couldn't recommand this game more, once again, it is a pure masterpiece.

The whole game is filled with secrets, puns, references and other jokes that will constantly make you smile.
The soundtracks are by far ones of the bests I've ever happened to hear. Every melody, every note fits its environment and situation perfectly. It is a pure and perfect osmosis.
Every charachter has his own unique and strong personality, each and every one of them is amazingly attaching by his own way. You will feel truly happy for some, deeply sad for others. And some will terribly miss you...
At the end of my journey I only have one regret: knowing that this world and these wonderful charachters that I've met and love so much are finaly nothing more than bunches of pixels and lines of code. That truly breaks my heart, and that's why Toby Fox can really feel proud of what he has accomplished.
I couldn't recommand this game more, once again, it is a pure masterpiece.

I got rust as a gift in the early parts of the alpha and thought I might give it a go.
So here is my thoughts on it so far.
Rust has the potential to become something great some day.
As it is now it's mostly about building a base as fast as possible to make sure your stuff does not get deleted.
My main issue with this game is that it has been ruined by hackers to many times that I have bothered to count.
Which one of the main reasons I don't play it any more.
Now there has finally been some updates that I value a lot. They have finally added a map and most important of all there is now finally pve servers, which is something I have been looking forward to the most.
That is really thing that bores me the most. There is to little to do. Rust consist of three things if you ask me. Pvp, farming materials for your house and finding a place where players don't bother you so you can actually keep it. They have added more features but I still think there needs to be a lot to be added.
Now the most frustrating thing they added lately is the way to fast degrading on house foundations. I keeps me playing because I don't want to loose my foundations to fast. But on the other hand it's frustating to use tons of my hard earned materials to repair my foundations almost every day.
So as rust now I can't recommend it. With future updates perhaps as it seems the devs are actually working on the game now. I check in my self from time to time so see if they made changes for the better or worse.

First off, this game broke my metaphorical heart. And I love it for that. I've never written a review for a game before, but I knew I had to for Undertale. This game will make you laugh, cry, question your moral compass, and realize that the world is mired in ambiguity. Player choice, or lack thereof, is handled perfectly in Undertale. I don't think I could handle a pure genocide run, knowing what I know now. Pacifism led to some great dialogue and a fascinating perspective on the mindset of a game player. The relationships you build, the bad jokes, the atmosphere, just everything is fantastic. Play the game as you see fit, and reap the consequences of your actions.
Also. Soundtrack. 11/10, would cry again. This game fills me with determination.

This game is really fun. And, while it can get really frustrating, even if you absolutely suck at the minigames, as long as you stay determined, you will be able to even get the true ending. It won't be an easy road, but it will be one full of determination. Trust me, I probably died in the triple digits, but I still made it to the end! I also really liked how there are so many variables covered in this. Many things do many things, and things you did are remembered even when you didn't do them. The story is nice too, albeit a bit shaky at times. The characters are all pretty great. Can't really think of one I didn't like by the end.
And if you don't feel determined enough, there's always the easier way to get to an ending. But, I'd really recommend you to stay determined.
Finally, the music is pretty amazing. Lots of really memorable tracks.
And now for the (more openly) bad:
Some (most) of the boss' clear requirments are just frustrating. Not to do, but to even have a clue that's what you're supposed to do. The game doesn't even give so much as a hint as to many of them, and oftentimes you'll find that you can be too determined, and that's why you're not getting things done right. And every boss is different...kind of. But yeah, it got to be a real pain sometimes.
The MC's sprite is well....about as alive as the MC. I really enjoyed the characters in the world, but hte MC hisself was just kinda...there. I realize this is probably meant to be very self-insert, but I just can't see this as anything but a negative. Still, others might like this feature.
I think that's about everything I have to say about it. Definitely recommend others to give the game a try. It's certainly a different sort of experience.
Feels/10

A strangely endearing and fun game. It's a bit of an anomoly to me for the fact it contains a lot of things I typically dislike or find annoying, but manages to handle them in a way that actually works pretty nicely. Likable and memorable characters, generally great music and battle themes and..."interesting" enemy designs and interesting battles, especially with the bosses.

First of all, skeletons. If you're anything like me I don't need to say anything else.
For the rest of you guys, Let me say that this game is a retro-styled turn-based combat game in which actually fighting is optional. Usually, anyway. Each choice you make in this game has consequences that actually manage to transcend the saving system itself. Obviously, this can work for or against the game's appeal, so I tell you this so you know what kind of game you're getting yourself into. Anyway, this does help bring some depth to the characters in this game. And the characters are great, it can sometimes feel more like you're a protagonist in a sitcom than a video game, all the main ones are three dimensional and almost everyone has something charming to say, the rest don't talk.
Fair warning, this game is very good at provoking deep, melancholic thought, especially in a certain ending. Playing the game one way might just make you not want to play it another way. That said, it's worth a shot. If you like games such as, say, Earthbound, give Undertale a go.

First of all, this is a great game. It is a great consept, and i think it will turn out awesome.
BUT.
I cant recommend it in its current state, as it lacks a feature that i think would make it a lot easier to love. Singleplayer. Of course the game is based on multiplayer, but you simply cant spend less than 5 hours non-stop if your goal is to be able to log out, sleep, and log in the next day with your life and house intact. It is incredibly hard to get materials such as stone, and it is nearly impossible to build a house that wont get captured when you're offline. If it had singleplayer, you could get to know the game and its mechanics, as well as discover what its like to have no need to be online at all times.
Another thing is the fact that when you log off, your character remains on the server, asleep on the floor, and if someone finds it, you're dead. I've built several big houses and fortresses, but none of them survives when i go to sleep. Its just not that much fun.
So until you can build a huge mansion without playing for 12 hours without a break, I cant recommend Rust.

This game is, in my opinion, the best game in existence. Why?
IT MAKES YOU FEEL THINGS.
IT MAKES YOU HAVE FEELINGS.
EMOTIONS EVERYWHERE.
So, now that I've got that off my chest, I can use actual sentences.
Undertale is an experience that must be had to really understand, but I'm going to try and explain it in words.
The basic concept is that you don't have to kill anything. Period. Instead of killing monsters, you can befriend them (or at least make them not want to fight you). Of course, you CAN kill them... If you're, you know... Into that...
So, because of that, there are, obviously, multiple endings. The three main paths are Genocide (kill EVERYTHING), Neutral (kill SOME THINGS), and Pacifist (self-explanitory). Genocide and Pacifist both have only a single true ending, but neutral branches off into a bunch of endings depending on who you kill and what you do.
PROTIP: If you plan on doing them all, do Pacifist first. Just trust me.
Another awesome feature of this game is that it remembers just about every choice you make, even if you "reset" the game. It remembers your deaths. It remembers your past playthroughs if you play it twice. It knows when you restart the game. Yeah, I know, it's just a fancy assortment of numbers and files, but it's so well executed that it can sometimes give you chills when the game references a thing you did in your previous save file.
PROTIP: If, for whatever reason, you want the game to not remember your past deeds, there are ways to manipulate the files to make that possible, for which you can find guides on the internet.
OTHER PROTIP: Speaking of the internet, try not to go there until you finish the game. You have a 99.9% chance of being spoiled if you do.
Also, the music in the game is absolutely perfect. I don't have a very large musical vocabulary, and I've been trying (and failing) to describe it adequately for about ten minutes now, so I think I'll just suggest that you look up the soundtrack and have a listen. You'll get what I'm trying to say.
Undertale's storyline, as one might expect from a story-driven game, is also really freakin' awesome. Without spoiling it, all I can really say is that you should pay close attention to what the characters say and keep an open mind about what is and isn't possible.
PROTIP: Seriously, though, stay the ♥♥♥♥ off the internet until you finish the game. Tumblr, twitter, deviantart, nowhere is safe.
Now, I can't honestly say the Undertale fandom is the best one ever, because really all fandoms have a reeeeaaally ugly side. But there are a ton of talented people who are inspired by this game. Fanart, remixes, musical mashups, medleys, you name it...
...
...Yes...
...Including Rule 34...
...If that's your thing...
What really makes the game shine (for me at least) is the fact that every character is intriguing/cool/funny/someone I would totally be friends with in real life. It's great because, unlike other RPGs where you generally don't want to bother with the townspeople unless you have to, you want to hunt down and talk to everyone and everything, if only to get a few extra lines of dialog or flavor text. And by the end of it, if you're like me, you'll probably end up loving the hell out of every single one of them.
I would easily say this is my favorite game ever. If you have ten dollars and a few hours to kill and an urge to ride an emotional roller coaster...
BUY THIS GAME. PLAY THIS GAME.
This game will fill you with determination.

My shortest review, and it'll be like this on purpose.
Those of you who've read my reviews (few, but I appreciate those few <3 ) know how much I love going into detail about everything, being honest with every single negative thing I could find with a game. I have so much I want to say, but it'd be simply gushing about the game, praising it excessively, and that's almost what drove me away from the game. I'll keep it brief.
The Rating System: Good refers to the obvious positive qualities, the Bad is reserved for nitpicks and gripes that don't necessarily ruin the experience, the Ugly is for the worst parts of the game, meant for serious consideration before purchase.
The Good:
Its music is perfectly executed, it goes quiet when the game needs to give you a moment to take in what's happening, it gives tension to scenes just as you'd expect, and it's very memorable. The 8-bit art style doesn't hinder it whatsoever with me, it actually led to a ton of really well designed and very fun puzzles. The gameplay is sugar simple, easily accessible to any and all, challenging in all the right ways and throwing new ways to tackle each individual enemy in the game at you to keep the game fresh. It never once felt eclecticly designed, despite how often the "combat" would vary between enemy encounters.
The story is very simple surface-wise, but grows richer and deeper the longer you play. The game's true ending moved me to tears.
Every single speaking entity in this game is its own character, with its own likes, dislikes and goals. I wish I could give them all a big hug, and will miss them as I move on to other games.
The Bad:
I guess sometimes the savepoints are weirdly placed, but I think it was intentional, like giving you 5 different save points in the final rooms of the game was a way to heighten tension.
The Ugly:
Not. A. Single. Thing. Maybe you don't like the 8-bit art style, maybe you don't like the idea of bullet shooter gameplay mixed with RPG stats, but I truly believe that everyone could enjoy this game if it's given a chance, should they ignore how often it's been talked about in recent media (like I did, I was sick of hearing the name Undertale by the time I got around to playing it and just wanted to see what the fuss was about).
Final Verdict: 10/10
I award perfect scores to games that aren't necessarily flawless, but whose flaws never take away from the experience or make you wish to stop playing. This is one of those games. I wish I could have played it as a kid, I wish I could go back in time and tell myself to jump on the bandwagon and try it earlier, I wish I could wipe my memory and replay it a couple dozen times more to re-experience the whimsy, the fear, the laughter and the tears this game brought me. It's rare when I find a game that evokes such emotion from me, and I'm so thankful I gave this its fair chance.
Please, I'm begging anyone who reads my review.. give it a fair shot. It's not like FNaF or some other gimmicky fad-game, the love and care that was put into this game has EARNED its popularity, and I'm happy to call myself a fan of Undertale.

Short: This is one of the greatest games I have ever played. Go play it now.
Long: Undertale is a role-playing game in which you do not have to kill anything. As opposed to other RPGs where you kill in order to gain power in order to push further into the story, Undertale gives you inventive alternatives to killing the monsters. It's fitting, then, that although the game uses a turn-based combat system, the enemy's attack phase is more akin to a bullet hell shooter than a different RPG. Dodging patterns is enjoyable in its own right, but what makes the game really tick is its writing, which ranges from the brilliantly ridiculous to the beautifully touching. I have seen the ending three times already, and it's only become more powerful to me.
You can also kill everything, but after you come to know these characters, chances are you won't want to. They really are that good, and I couldn't possibly bring myself to kill them. While avoiding spoilers, I'll just say that each of the game's multiple endings takes what was already a lovely, brilliant game and imbudes it with a level of depth and subversiveness that's only matched by the very best examples of the medium. You could spend days talking about the various layers this game has, or you could just let yourself get engrossed in this joyous, brilliant world.
This is a game made out of love, and at times, it feels like it loves you, the player. Really, you've got to play it. Maybe, just maybe, you'll love it just as much as it loves you.

Rust has the potential to become something great some day.

You can't write about Undertale without speaking about Earthbound.  They share design similarities, pacing, and even a few sound effects.  That being said if Earthbound is a friendly, enveloping blanket keeping you comfortable as you sleep in a comfortable spot then Undertale would be a stranger holding a pillow in your general direction with a creepy smile expecting you to get excited about the reference.
Overall it's not worth the price and it's skippable. I told myself to play to meet the characters like I did before I had ever played RPGs before on the SNES, but ultimately those acquaintances weren't worth getting to.  By far its best feature is a charming battle system that is totally overshadowered with poor direction, strange pacing, and unpolished sequences that suggest its creator couldn't really decide on a genre.
Give it a skip and go play Earthbound. Toby, if you're reading this, this was truly an amazing feat for one person.  I hope to see more from you because after everything said here one thing remains true: this game definitely took perseverence and talent.
Recommended to those that like games like Mother 3/Earthbound and bullet hell games or just about everyone :T

I finally beat Undertale on the TRUE Pacifist mode. This game is going down in my top games of ALL TIME. EVER. It deserves a minimum 9/10, and only if I were to pick it apart and give it the lowest score I could. I actually give it a 10.
It does story well, humor well, the graphics are retro and fantastic, the comic is ingenius and comical, the game isn't too long, nor too short, and has 3 endings. The characters are all very memorable and loveable, and hateable at the same time. The combat is not too overwhelmingly difficult or too easy. The soundtrack is just as amazing, and very reminscent of retro 16 and 32 bit style music with a lot of awesome twists... that definitely set the mood for the game's scenes.
The first hour I played I wanted to go into the game and become the child and live with Toriel. I felt bad leaving the Ruins... and her. Enough to stop playing. Toriel may be one of my favorite characters from a game.
It plays like a retro top down RPG, with a lot of modern twists. The ending is... out there. But amazing.
This game has everything, and does it all justice. Nothing feels overdone or underdone. A perfect game.
I'm sad this game is over. I want to live in this world and eat butterscotch cinnamon pie all day made by Toriel herself. Sadly, I cannot.
I got this game free from a friend but chose to buy this game AND the soundtrack, both for full price after only playing the game for one hour.

Preferably, you should attempt it blindly. No Let's Plays, no guides, none until you have beaten it at least once, and only accept hints on how to progress, no searching on how the ending goes. It is how you can get the maximum experience.

I didn't want to stop playing.
Friend would message me and ask "Up for some games" and I be like, "Nah, I'm playin' Undertale."  Some would consider that a bad thing, but I wasn't rude about it ;P
Now, if there were honest criteque here, the system of combat in this game isn't too complicated, but it relies more on skill than one may think, which I like.  It isn't the kind of 'tap the guy with the sword, run back, and wait for him to tap back' kind of deal.  The system can seem to be repetitive, but the system isn't really what the game is trying to focus on.  If we focused on purely that aspect, this game wouldn't be that good.  Assuming that they didn't keep the system fresh from time to time.  And they manage to do that with unique battles and abilities, making the 'combat' system tolerable from the beginning to the end.  So no issues there.
What keeps the game going is its story.  It is a story driven and slower paced game (depending on how you play it, which I will get to in a bit), but even if you aren't into that kind of stuff (unless you shun the very act of creating story in video games) I still believe you can enjoy this game and experience it like you've experienced no game before.
But even the story is supported by another pillar.  That pillar is concequence.  I wouldn't really call this a 'choice' game as you don't make a multitude of choices on a regular basis.  It is more of an 'act' game... if you act in a particular way, the game will change and mold itself to suitibally respond to what you have done in the game.  Because in the end, there are two routes in the game: Genocidal (No Mercy) and Pacifist (Mercy), that leaves only three possible paths, including the Neutral endings (and excluding all the variants of the Neutral endings).  The game within changes a lot, but again, not necessarily due to choices in the traditional sense of Mass Effect or The Walking Dead, but due to the way one acts.  And this game addresses that really well.  You know how in most games, you kill a hundred or so mobs in a certain area and nobody questions anything?  No families are ruined.  No hatred poured on you for being a mass murderer.  If the game doesn't paint that lifestyle as normal in the game (Fallout is a good example) then you just kill enemies because you need to.  No questions asked.
This game goes beyond and asks that question... Why must we always fight?  And because of that this game isn't entertaining, at least not in the thrill factor or the rush of violence.  Instead it is more enjoyable.  That is what the Pacifist route of the game offers.  Peace, fun characters to hang around, puzzles, and other lighthearted things.
However, the game can take a serious, dark, and even horrifying tone.  It can be cold and brutal and heartless.  That is what the Genocide route offers.  Violence and the thrill of it... or not so much.  There is nothing thrill-envoking about the Genocide run.  It is plauged with dispair and the game will constantly remind you of how much of a horrible person you've become.
Depending on how you act depends on how the game responds, and the game can respond DRAMATICALLY to your actions.  The Pacifist route and Genocide route feel almost like completely different games.  Ironically, the Pacifist route is actually harder and longer than the Genocide route when you exclude all the monster grinding.  But trust me on this one; its worth it.  Both extremes are worth the experience if you can emotionally handle either of them.
One last thing is the fact that you feel important... not just as a main character, but as a person.  It makes you feel like you have responsibility over this game and what happens to it, that your button pressing is more than just useless code.  No game has ever made me feel like I as a person help make this game what it is, that I have a responsibility over it.
Yes, it is worth a buy.  Yes, you should buy it ASAP.  Yes, the soundtrack along with the purchase is worth it.  Yes.  Yes!  YES!  YES!!!

After all this development, DayZ is actually a really nice game. Sure it has its problems, but for the most part it is an experience that no other game can deliver. I mean, in what game are you able to kill someone with a kitchen knife, steal his truck and eat his flesh? 10/10

You will die.. a lot! You might even survive for a week with you character if you're real good and then... 'you are dead' all of a sudden. A sniper saw you, or maybe the game decided to kill you with a random fall damage (wich sometimes happen when you log in, but now it's really rare).
The gameplay isn't quite dynamic and you might get really frustrated when your character can't walk sideways and grab his gun or even can't stop moving straight ahead while doing the same. Oh, the zombies lag so... never trust of them being where you think they are. yeah...
Seriously though apart from the really infuriating bugs that sometimes happen (and they will kill you) the game gives you the feeling of fear of constant death when it may come from anywhere. You might get sick, you might die from hypothermia, maybe hyperthermia, you might starve, become thirsty until death but in these cases your death won't be fast. No. You will suffer all the long way until you die. Fell a little high? Thought you died? Oh, but now you legs are broken... good luck surviving while you crawl for your life... literally!
Finally if you want this game because of zombies just forget it, they are laughing stock. But if you do see a little pixel of something that moves but doesn't look like a zombie... then your heart will skip a beat and then you will get the feeling of what this game is about. We are the apocalypse

DayZ (Standalone) is a Massive Multiplayer Online Sandbox Horror Zombie Survival Game made by Czech game developer studio, the Bohemia Interactive Studio or just Bohemia Interactive. Dayz is a successor after the well known Dayz Mod originally found by Dean ''Rocket'' Hall, for Arma 2 (+ Arma 2: Operation Arrowhead expansion pack required) and because the DayZ mod was very succesful and because of many players, especially me, bought it because of it, the developers decided to take up Dean to their dev team and make a standalone game called DayZ. In DayZ Standalone is no singleplayer or campaign nor co-op, but only just multiplayer, where you can decide if you want to play either as neutral survivor who can help other survivors or just leave them be or defend themselves against survivors who are trying to kill you, or as a hero who tries to help out other survivors as much as he can and defend them agains bandits or play as the enformentioned bandit who kills everyone he sees and doesn't metter if you are a ''fresh spawn'' (you have nothing) or you are a geared badass looking guy with a gun, so that is called ''Kill on Sight''. So Dayz is in the world of Chernarus which is a real part taken from Russia with real existing or fictive cities, villages nad towns. The size of Chernarus is about 120 square kilometres and it's keeping getting larger and larger. You spawn as a survivor with basic shoes, jeans, T-shirt, battery and flashlight, yes there is a night time as well, so far you have 1 character (which you can customize in main menu: you can be either black, white, asian, you can customize your pants, shirt and shoes colour as well) for Regular mode servers (1st/3rd person + crosshair) and 1 character for Hardcore mode servers (1st person, no crosshair) and also there are a Private servers that are not connected so that means that you have a different character on every Private servers, you don't have the same as on Public servers, every Private server has its own character, every server si set either to daylight only, nightime only or both time cycles. Weather affects you as well, you can get cold, you can overheat, then you can get sick from eating rotten or raw food and you can drawn. Every server has it's own restart cycle, mostly every few hours, due to lags and to respawn new loot, but there are servers with ''Persistance'', that means that after restart all items on the ground will be still there and won't disappear and no loot will respawn. There are many items; food, weapons, clothing... Every item has its own condition; Pristine, Worn, Damaged, Badly Damaged and Ruined, but severl items can be repaired by other items; sewing kits, weapons cleaning kits... Unlike in the mod, almost every single building is enterable and items spawn there, there are military bases and arfields for guns and hospitals for medical supplies, but you can find weapon in many other places that in barracks or in a hangar or police station, but there are a ''Crash sites'' (a fallen halicopters with rare loot; M4A1, Steyr AUG, Ammo box..). You can trade items with other survivors, you can interact with themm talk to them using direct commnutaion (chat or talking but only up to 80 metres I believe), but you can use walkie talkies that are effective up to 800 metres. If you have a weapon, you need ammo for it, but unlike in other games, you need weapon mag, but if you don't have any you can still chamber your gun with one bullet, not everygun but most of them. But don't worry, if you don't have a weapon you can punch with you bare hands; 2 hits to the head and you are unconscious, unless you wear a helmet. Weapons have also they maximum shot distance, but can zero it if you are shooting at long distance. You can also craft Bow and Ghillie suit. All signs are in Russian azbuka, but if you play long like me, you will either learn it or you will recognize the place where are you at the moment. There are a few types of animals that you can kill, skin, cook and eat and craft a backpack of their skin, and for those who are interrested in torturing people, you can handcuff them, poison them, MANY THING, and the most interresting part; after killing them, you can also skin, cook and eat them :D , but you will start shaking and your character will either cry or lough every few minutes. If you are bleeding you can tear apart some of the cloathing, especially some shirts into rags and then badage yourself if you don't have bandage (you can do so even with sewing kits). And if have broken legs and no morphine or hatchet to cut down a tree and make a splint, you can crawl into a forest and search for kindling and then craft a spilnt (+ bandage/rag needed).
Well, that's pretty much it, but keep in mind that this game is being worked on, it's in Pre-Alpha stage; bugs, glitches etc. Don't buy it unless you are a big fan and you want to really play this game and support the devs. I highly recommend this game, it's my favourite so far. It's very interactive and enjoyable, but sometimes makes you rage.

I didn't want to stop playing.
Friend would message me and ask "Up for some games" and I be like, "Nah, I'm playin' Undertale."  Some would consider that a bad thing, but I wasn't rude about it ;P
Now, if there were honest criteque here, the system of combat in this game isn't too complicated, but it relies more on skill than one may think, which I like.  It isn't the kind of 'tap the guy with the sword, run back, and wait for him to tap back' kind of deal.  The system can seem to be repetitive, but the system isn't really what the game is trying to focus on.  If we focused on purely that aspect, this game wouldn't be that good.  Assuming that they didn't keep the system fresh from time to time.  And they manage to do that with unique battles and abilities, making the 'combat' system tolerable from the beginning to the end.  So no issues there.
What keeps the game going is its story.  It is a story driven and slower paced game (depending on how you play it, which I will get to in a bit), but even if you aren't into that kind of stuff (unless you shun the very act of creating story in video games) I still believe you can enjoy this game and experience it like you've experienced no game before.
But even the story is supported by another pillar.  That pillar is concequence.  I wouldn't really call this a 'choice' game as you don't make a multitude of choices on a regular basis.  It is more of an 'act' game... if you act in a particular way, the game will change and mold itself to suitibally respond to what you have done in the game.  Because in the end, there are two routes in the game: Genocidal (No Mercy) and Pacifist (Mercy), that leaves only three possible paths, including the Neutral endings (and excluding all the variants of the Neutral endings).  The game within changes a lot, but again, not necessarily due to choices in the traditional sense of Mass Effect or The Walking Dead, but due to the way one acts.  And this game addresses that really well.  You know how in most games, you kill a hundred or so mobs in a certain area and nobody questions anything?  No families are ruined.  No hatred poured on you for being a mass murderer.  If the game doesn't paint that lifestyle as normal in the game (Fallout is a good example) then you just kill enemies because you need to.  No questions asked.
This game goes beyond and asks that question... Why must we always fight?  And because of that this game isn't entertaining, at least not in the thrill factor or the rush of violence.  Instead it is more enjoyable.  That is what the Pacifist route of the game offers.  Peace, fun characters to hang around, puzzles, and other lighthearted things.
However, the game can take a serious, dark, and even horrifying tone.  It can be cold and brutal and heartless.  That is what the Genocide route offers.  Violence and the thrill of it... or not so much.  There is nothing thrill-envoking about the Genocide run.  It is plauged with dispair and the game will constantly remind you of how much of a horrible person you've become.
Depending on how you act depends on how the game responds, and the game can respond DRAMATICALLY to your actions.  The Pacifist route and Genocide route feel almost like completely different games.  Ironically, the Pacifist route is actually harder and longer than the Genocide route when you exclude all the monster grinding.  But trust me on this one; its worth it.  Both extremes are worth the experience if you can emotionally handle either of them.
One last thing is the fact that you feel important... not just as a main character, but as a person.  It makes you feel like you have responsibility over this game and what happens to it, that your button pressing is more than just useless code.  No game has ever made me feel like I as a person help make this game what it is, that I have a responsibility over it.
Yes, it is worth a buy.  Yes, you should buy it ASAP.  Yes, the soundtrack along with the purchase is worth it.  Yes.  Yes!  YES!  YES!!!

So please don't listen to the "minimum requirements" because that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. Recommended is actually the minimum. Oh yes and I almost forgot, do not attempt to play this game alone. This game was once pretty good even if you were solo, but now it's definitely clan oriented and is continuing to do so. Each patch undermines the solo player and helps clan players. Keep that in mind.

What is it: A wonderful RPG, inspired by Earthbound, featuring a bullet hell-like combat mechanic used for dodging enemy attacks, multiple endings, phsyco flowers, and enough emotion to rip your heart asunder and destroy you completly and utterly if you play it wrong.
Pros:
* Great Music
* Fantastic and unique characters
* Multiple endings with an interesting Reset mechanic for starting new playthroughs
* Unique combat mechanics that vary slightly depending on the weapon you're using and the enemy your fighting
* Deep and compelling story
* A character that's like a Mom
* Puzzles
* 7 dogs (I counted and didn't include the boat)
* Good spritework and animation
* Toby's annoying dog
Cons:
* Game is kind of short
* Occasionally feels slightly out of your control in some instances that should be
* Low encounter rate
* Takes a bit to go back to places
* Some items have zero explination for use or incredibly cryptic descriptions
* Toby's Annoying dog
I'm slightly biased in this review, purely due to how much I loved the game and it's writing, as well as some of the very relatable characters. Despite that the game runs great, plays great, and destroyed me emotionally... Good game to be able to do that. Backtracking is kind of annoying, despite the boatman (woman? dog?) taking you between the three main towns, and it's hard to tell whether or not you've missed something. Regardless the attachments you can form with some of the characters will drive you to ignore this and scour the game in an attempt to help them. If that doesn't scream well written then I don't know anymore.
Verdict: If you like having your actions questioned throught a playthrough and all the following playthroughs and you don't mind getting emotionally destroyed, check out Toby's game Undertale!

Wow. Just wow. I never thoght this game was going to be this great. When I first saw the trailar steam I thought, "Huh, this game reminds of Mother 3 alot." (Which another fantastic JRPG you should play.) So I bought it instantly and started playing it. Now, I went into this game completely blind and I tend to have the best time with story based games the majority of the time. My first run was the Neutral run, but I accidently killed Toriel. I actually felt really bad and reloaded my save file to spare her and which I did. Now this is were the game completely blew my mind. After you get done with Toriel you are suppose to meet Flowey after the battle. This game knows when you reset your game and its kinda creepy and brillant at the same time. Now I did get all of the endings in the following order. Neutral,Genocide,and Pacifist. The Neutral ending was the least memorable of the three mainly because the Pacifist and Genocide ending simply outshine it more. Now don't even get me started on the Genocide run. It was terrible. I never felt so bad about killing enemies in a game in my life. The whole story and atmosphere of the game changes completely. There were only two bosses that gave me a difficult time and the people who played the Genocide Route shoudl know who I'm talking about. I literally spent 7 hours on the final boss, but I didn't feel good when I beat it. It left a bad taste in my mouth. Now finally, the Pacifist Run. After doing the Genocide run and then doing the Pacifist Run made me feel a whole lot better know that I can spare my favorite cast of characters. The ending of the Pacifist Run literally had me in tears and its pretty hard for me to cry from a video game, but the game managed to do it. I felt pretty satisfied with ending, I loved ever bit of it.
I don't think we wil get another game like "Undertale" for a very long time.
PROS:
+Fantastic Soundtrack (Never disliked any song in the entire game)
+Great Cast of Characters
+Art Style
+Satisfying Ending (Pacifist/True Ending)
+Fantastic Story
+Quirky and Funny
Mixed:
+The Diffuculty (Espeically on the Genocide Run. Which makes sense since the game is basically punishing you for being an a**hole.
+The Controls (Ugh... You now how hard it is play bullet hell game with a keyboard? I literally had to use my 360 controller for the final boss in the Genocide run.)
Cons:
-You can't stay with Toriel at the beggining of the game. :(
-Can't save
All in all. Undertale is a fantastic RPG where it goes to show that you don't have to be triple a title to be a fantastic game. All it takes is a lot of love and effort... and Temmies.

I originally wasn't going to buy the game. I was going to watch a play through of it, and I was fine with that. But...I had some extra money after buying cosplay stuff, and a friend convinced me that I should play it. I had the money, so why the hell not?
Two days ago, I bought a game I was prepared to laugh and cry over...
Prepared...or so I thought.
Yeah, I laughed like I knew I would. I'd already seen a lot of funny bits from watching a most of a playthrough that hadn't gotten to the end yet. Things were still fairly innocent.
What I wasn't prepared for was sobbing like a friggin' baby.
Last night, I began the "end" of Undertale. I met with the final boss that I was yet again "prepared" to fight. I thought he would be evil and monstrous, despite Papyrus calling him a big pushover. I mean, it's the final boss! He's gotta be awful, right?
HAHAHAHAHAH no. The exact opposite, honestly.
After walking through a house identical to my goat mother's and a grey city while participating in a gut wrenching story session, I walked into the throne room. He almost invited me for tea, and dear God in heaven did I wanna take that offer because I did NOT want to fight this big fluffy papa goat.
I was given the choice to defeat him or give him mercy. Of course, I chose mercy. I really wanted that pacifist ending. And THEN...
Oh...oh lord...
And then...
Nightmare fuel. Everywhere.
Long story short, that wasn't the end of my tears. Oh, no. No no no no no. I thought it was over. I thought everything was okay.
Nothing is ever okay.
Things got sadder, and my tears fell harder.
Another long story short, I loved this game. I didn't think I would love it so much, but I did. My eyes burn from crying so much, and you know what? It was worth it. Worth every single damn tear over each and every pixelated character. I don't think I have the heart do a true reset, or worse, a genocide run. I can't do it. I spent two days building up this love for characters. I'm not going to throw that all away. It sounds silly, but...this game broke me. Broke me in a good way.
I've never cried over any other game so hard in my life.
Damn good job, Toby.

The only thing I can say about this game is that it is sublime. You will finish the game and desire for more. You will want a way to spend more time with your friends. The ones you made in the game.

I can say even with any criticism this game will get for whatever reason, the overall flow of this game is something that should be noted as unique. It's definitely worth a play, no matter what kind of gamer you are. As for my personal rating, I'm gonna rate this on a scale of 100.
Visuals - 16/20
This is literally the only thing I can really criticize about the game. Yeah the graphics seem "old" in a sense. But in some ways this does add to the game itself in quite a few ways. I personally noticed occasional graphical bugs on the way through. But overall, I'd say the retro-styled graphics still fit the game very well.
Music - 20/20
It's pretty cool that this soundtrack was created entirely by Toby himself. I did notice alot of musical references(Primarily Earthbound) which helps suite the classical feel of this game. I would say without a doubt, several different tracks of various musical genres make it especially unique. My personal favorite however, will always be hopes and dreams :P.
Gameplay - 20/20
The puzzles can be both a challenge and fun to solve as well. Plus they are integrated heavily into the story, your individual actions will affect EVERYTHING. This includes every battle, most of the dialogue, and the endings itself. While it's up to you on what actions affect what, this game can easily be a sweep, if you want it to be. The game has a good habit of either making some things seem easier than others, yet in the end, they do come with a price. Truly something unique that gives the overall actions you do in-game so much more meaning.
Story - 20/20
Very unique & based off of your play style. As with the gameplay mechanics, the battle system will heavily influence the story that results. While I'm not going to reveal the different endings, consider how real life is viewed to a video game. Do we lash out against something that "isn't real" to escape our real world issues? As you'll find out, the story can really put really heavy tasks on us. And it's up to you to decide how to handle them.
Characters - 20/20
While cheesy humor is often frowned upon, I can say this game pulls it off well. I found the questions relating to anime & monster dating sims to be absolutely hilarious(You can tell this game is unique). Breaking the fourth wall in a game to some may seem a bit dicey. But this game manages to keep you feeling involved with each character as they all interact with you with their various diverse personalities.
So in the end, i'd give Undertale a rating of 96/100. Too high, too low? That sucks. lol
Overall, it's a really unique & fun to play game. Definitely worth both the game & soundtrack as well.

The warning of it being in Alpha does hold true as you WILL experience bugs and crashes that will leave you facepalming. You will experience players who slaughter you for no apparent reason, and you may even see some game ruining hackers, and you will inevitably run around doing nothing for minutes to hours at a time.
Despite the flaws dayZ sends you into a vst open world were you can create some of the most memorable stories you'll experience in gaming.  It is completely up to you how you play and what experiences you have, well, I guess up to you and the random, random people you come across.
With the additions of Cannibalism and yes even a few trucks DayZ continues to push forward.  It does have potential to keep getting better, but sometimes takes detours adding useless things like hypothermia and such.
Overall this game is a challenge.  Not to be taken lightly, if you're up for it give it a try, if not, stay away.

DayZ is honeslty one of my all-time favorite survival games (notice I didn't say MMO) and I downright enjoy it. With that being said there ARE problems. Whether playing the game or reading most of the negative reviews, you'll see that. BUT, in my opinion, these are problems a game in ALPHA would probably foster.
Pro: This is an amazing game. Hands-down. The world is beautiful, expanisve, and filled (sort of) with towns, cities, and villages alike. Now, I don't know if I'm allowed to mention other games here, but if you're unhappy with this game, may i suggest WarZ- I mean Infestation: Survivor Stories. If you don't like glitching zombies and their buggy AI, go enjoy Infestation: Survivor Stories, where you'll meet even worse zombies and the usuall hacker. Now, back onto topic, DayZ IS INCREDIBLE. I got lost after leaving Svetlojarsk, wandered the countryside for 3 hours, and still managed to have an exceptional experience. It gives me the option to play hardcore (first-person), or regular (first and third-person). I've run into good and bad people, both of which have made the game amazingly interactive, and have experienced starvation, sickness, and border-line hypothermia all in one character who's still alive. Basically, if you want THE zombie-pvp-interaction game, DayZ if your best choice, and if you want to wait for further development, then that is PERFECTLY FINE, there's no reason not to be cautious. Just like in the game, the choice is yours to make.
Cons: Theres obvious problems. I could just slam a list down, but you might have read other negative reviews and kinda get the sense. MY BIGGEST problem is the zombie AI, and its not because its simply a problem, but I haven't seen any notes or logs about fixing it, which concerns me. I'm not saying I'm upset with the developers, but I simply would like to know whether or not I can look forward to actually going through a town unseen by a zombie a half-mile away. That's my biggest problem, and others have their's. PvP is somewhat of a limbo land, stuck between actual firefights and being killed through a wall. I've been through both, so essentially, try to watch out for people. All-in-all, there's going to be problems, even in the blockbuster games that are DONE in development (Battlefield 4 or Grand Theft Auto online anyone?) but these problems WILL (most likely) be fixed, and as I said before, waiting for more development and bug-fixes is understandable.
DayZ is a tremendous game with some bugs that DO make it hard to play. But being in Alpha even almost a year after, it's an amazing experience, and I recommend it to all my friends. So, basically, enjoy the beautful landscape, watch out for annoying out not game-breaking bugs, and experience the interactions you'll have with friends, others, and yourself.
If I was going with an IGN rating, it'd be 7.5.

Wow. Just wow. I never thoght this game was going to be this great. When I first saw the trailar steam I thought, "Huh, this game reminds of Mother 3 alot." (Which another fantastic JRPG you should play.) So I bought it instantly and started playing it. Now, I went into this game completely blind and I tend to have the best time with story based games the majority of the time. My first run was the Neutral run, but I accidently killed Toriel. I actually felt really bad and reloaded my save file to spare her and which I did. Now this is were the game completely blew my mind. After you get done with Toriel you are suppose to meet Flowey after the battle. This game knows when you reset your game and its kinda creepy and brillant at the same time. Now I did get all of the endings in the following order. Neutral,Genocide,and Pacifist. The Neutral ending was the least memorable of the three mainly because the Pacifist and Genocide ending simply outshine it more. Now don't even get me started on the Genocide run. It was terrible. I never felt so bad about killing enemies in a game in my life. The whole story and atmosphere of the game changes completely. There were only two bosses that gave me a difficult time and the people who played the Genocide Route shoudl know who I'm talking about. I literally spent 7 hours on the final boss, but I didn't feel good when I beat it. It left a bad taste in my mouth. Now finally, the Pacifist Run. After doing the Genocide run and then doing the Pacifist Run made me feel a whole lot better know that I can spare my favorite cast of characters. The ending of the Pacifist Run literally had me in tears and its pretty hard for me to cry from a video game, but the game managed to do it. I felt pretty satisfied with ending, I loved ever bit of it.
I don't think we wil get another game like "Undertale" for a very long time.
PROS:
+Fantastic Soundtrack (Never disliked any song in the entire game)
+Great Cast of Characters
+Art Style
+Satisfying Ending (Pacifist/True Ending)
+Fantastic Story
+Quirky and Funny
Mixed:
+The Diffuculty (Espeically on the Genocide Run. Which makes sense since the game is basically punishing you for being an a**hole.
+The Controls (Ugh... You now how hard it is play bullet hell game with a keyboard? I literally had to use my 360 controller for the final boss in the Genocide run.)
Cons:
-You can't stay with Toriel at the beggining of the game. :(
-Can't save
All in all. Undertale is a fantastic RPG where it goes to show that you don't have to be triple a title to be a fantastic game. All it takes is a lot of love and effort... and Temmies.

Whether it's through endearing two of the most abhorred fonts in all of history, romantic shenanigans involving a sentient skeleton, or the creatively sprinkled inclusion of journey-wide pop-culture references, dank memes, or kickass fish lesbians, this game never ceases to amuse, and is truly a work of contemporaneous art to behold for years to come. The music is phenomenal, even by Homestuck's coveted composer Toby Fox's standards, the humor is always jam-packed and on key, typical of what you'd expect from a professional accomplished gagster like Toby 'radiation' Fox, and the satire just wreaks of what you'd expect from such a zany, sporadic, and downright lovable adventure as that of Undertale. Thanks to none other than Toby Fox, who you might know from such famous pieces as a particular Earthbound Halloween ROM hack; this game being a true testament to his excellence in programming.
That being said, the game has some considerable post-launch issues I'd like resolved before I can tenderheartedly wipe from my bosom the cascading tears that now decorate my horrendous Christmas sweater. I seem to be having somewhat of a bad time with one character in particular, and it's wracking my brain to come up with an effective solution to maneuver about their silly, yet frustrating shenanigans. The game is not so bad as is its developement team.
Before the game launched the developers had come out and said they were going to keep the price low on the game, around $10 - $15. The game launched with a $30 starting price, in early access. Typically early access games will have a lower price due to it being unfinished. Then came the price increase to $35, after little had been improved with the game over almost a year. The reason developers gave was that it would help in getting the game complete, but not until 2016. They also said they were going to port the game over to PS4. This news came with the game being far from finished. People became angry with the thought that developers should create a finished product before thinking about spending money to bring the unfinished game to consoles. Then came the news that the head developer, Dean Hall, is to step down from developement and is leaving Bohemia Interactive. His reason was that he realized he was not cut out to be a leader, yet with his leaving he planned to start his own independent game company. And here we are, a year since DayZ's release, and little has been done to improve the game. Most of the updates had been bug fixes. Though these fixes did not seem to fix anything. And with the bugs remaining in the game, the possibility of more features being added died.
But I guess I should talk a little about the game. As of this post the game still has some issues. The only improvements I could find were that the movement and controls now feel smoother and less clunky. Combat is still an issue. For example, I was standing right next to a zombie and tried hitting it several times with a sledgehammer but somehow missed. The combat can be unpredictable and clunky, especially if you don't have a gun. Zombies also seem to be less frequent. They are also the smallest threat in the game. You are more likely to die from a five foot drop than you are to die from a zombie. After getting use to dealing with zombies they begin to become more of an annoyance than anything thing else. Yet not as annoying as the text in the lower left corner of the screen telling you that your hungry and thirsty every two minutes or so. The one thing that will spice things up in the game is an encounter with another player. This can go two ways. It could spur a random yet hilarious event or it will lead to a tense standoff that will leave your palms sweating. The encounters are rare but that is a good thing. When an encounter does happen it feels new and exciting since it does not happen often. But since these are not frequent and the zombie count and threat are low, it will lead you to having an experience similar to the game (walking simulator) "Dear Esther" except without the great narration and stunning views (great game btw). Most of the time you will be scavenging house after house in search of food, and perhaps even a gun which seems to be as rare as a knife from a CS:GO crate. And when you do find this gun, the most you will be able to do with it is to intimidate other players since finding ammo with the gun is highly unlikely. And if you do find a gun and ammo together you will most likely be held up by bandits camping the barracks or airport. And then you have to start all over again. And don't complain when it happens because it is bound to happen to you at one point in the game. Yes it is frusterating but it is how the game came out working being that there is no incentive to be good to get that hero skin. Overall the game is not that great but it can easily be enjoyable if played with good hearted friends, it just might take awhile to find them.
My recommendation is to pass on the game until we see where it stands in 2016, hopefully it will be finished. Try the ARMA 2 mod for now, it is really fun. And only buy this game if you feel the absolute need to play it and if you have friends to play with.

I can say even with any criticism this game will get for whatever reason, the overall flow of this game is something that should be noted as unique. It's definitely worth a play, no matter what kind of gamer you are. As for my personal rating, I'm gonna rate this on a scale of 100.
Visuals - 16/20
This is literally the only thing I can really criticize about the game. Yeah the graphics seem "old" in a sense. But in some ways this does add to the game itself in quite a few ways. I personally noticed occasional graphical bugs on the way through. But overall, I'd say the retro-styled graphics still fit the game very well.
Music - 20/20
It's pretty cool that this soundtrack was created entirely by Toby himself. I did notice alot of musical references(Primarily Earthbound) which helps suite the classical feel of this game. I would say without a doubt, several different tracks of various musical genres make it especially unique. My personal favorite however, will always be hopes and dreams :P.
Gameplay - 20/20
The puzzles can be both a challenge and fun to solve as well. Plus they are integrated heavily into the story, your individual actions will affect EVERYTHING. This includes every battle, most of the dialogue, and the endings itself. While it's up to you on what actions affect what, this game can easily be a sweep, if you want it to be. The game has a good habit of either making some things seem easier than others, yet in the end, they do come with a price. Truly something unique that gives the overall actions you do in-game so much more meaning.
Story - 20/20
Very unique & based off of your play style. As with the gameplay mechanics, the battle system will heavily influence the story that results. While I'm not going to reveal the different endings, consider how real life is viewed to a video game. Do we lash out against something that "isn't real" to escape our real world issues? As you'll find out, the story can really put really heavy tasks on us. And it's up to you to decide how to handle them.
Characters - 20/20
While cheesy humor is often frowned upon, I can say this game pulls it off well. I found the questions relating to anime & monster dating sims to be absolutely hilarious(You can tell this game is unique). Breaking the fourth wall in a game to some may seem a bit dicey. But this game manages to keep you feeling involved with each character as they all interact with you with their various diverse personalities.
So in the end, i'd give Undertale a rating of 96/100. Too high, too low? That sucks. lol
Overall, it's a really unique & fun to play game. Definitely worth both the game & soundtrack as well.

Rust started out great, got better, then they jumped ship and started over. I avoided playing it after that for a long time. I got back into playing. Was having fun with it until I started trying to build a base. The new building interface is much better than the old Rust system. You start out able to build just about anything. My problem came in when I decided to lock my doors. The key system just sucks @$$, there is no better way to put it. You need a different key for every door, which is a major pain, inventory space is limited already and now you have to carry a key that takes up as much space in your inventory as 1000 pieces of wood. If you die and respawn in your base you can't get out of your base now, because you don't have the key.  So to really make the key thing work you need to make extra keys for your doors and stash them in your base. So now you have to have extra storage space in your base also to keep all your keys. I'm not going to say I wasted my money buying this game, because I used to enjoy it. But now, the whole key thing has ruined this game for me. I will no longer play it until something is done about this horrible festering boil on my @$$ that is key management is changed. I will not recommend this game to anyone at this point. Here's to hoping the dev team realizes what a stupid system this is and come up with a better way to lock and unlock doors.

Undertale man, what can I say about Undertale that hasn't already been said? Nothing, it truly is an amazing game that isn't flawed in any shape of form, amazing gameplay, amazing story (for a game), amazing ♥♥♥♥ing music, and very creative level design and boss fights.
In terms of story, it reminds me a lot of a game that surprisingly enough has the exact same name, but with different words, Cave story, but the story is even better, and just like in Cave story, your actions do affect the outcome of the game, only this time there is no ♥♥♥♥ing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t that cannot be completed without a guide.
There really isn't anything I can directly compare Undertale with in terms of gameplay, but if I do have to put in somehow, think of Touhou as regular golf, well then, Undertale is basically mini golf, but not. This may be a good way to describe a few boss fights and regular enemies, but most bosses have a fresh twist to them that can completely alter the gameplay.
For 10 dollars, Undertale is an amazing game that nobody has any reason why not to play, if you like very quirky characters and god tier catchy music, then Undertale is the game for you. One of the best game ever? Meh, maybe if it lasted 20 hours, it could be, but for 10 hours, it is only one of the best games of it's genre. If somebody says they don't like this game, ask them ''Explain why you don't like it'', and if you see the words ''memes'' or ''tumblr'' in that amazing essay, don't even bother to read it and disregard it immediately.
It manages to be a better Earthbound game than Earthbound. While combat is boring, boss fights are awesome and fun and the soundtrack is addictive, would buy again for friends.

So many RPGs, even brilliant ones, have us mindlessly killing monsters for EXP and loot on the principle that they're "evil" and that we need to save the world, but Undertale takes that principle and wipes its♥♥♥♥♥with it. Sure, you CAN kill them if you want, but... maybe the game will make you change your mind? Either way, your decision will heavily impact the course of the game, as there are multiple unique endings.
As you may have noticed, Undertale has received a metric crap-ton of praise for its unique approach to giving players the ultimate choice between befriending or slaying every monster in the game; it has also received praise for its emotionally empowering story, its many interesting (and sometimes downright AWESOME!) secrets and Easter eggs, its rockin' sountrack, its charming yet simplistic aesthetics, and - arguably above all else - its lovable, memorable characters.
When a game can make you enjoy going out on a date with a skeleton who once tried to capture you against your will, it's special. When a game can make you genuinely care about a fish knight who once mercilessly chased you through the rain so that she could rip your soul from your body, it's special. When a game can make you look up a web source to help you obtain friendship with every enemy in the game who tried killing you in various random encounters, it's special. Malboros from Final Fantasy games are hated by almost everyone who has encountered them, but what if we could become best buds with them? Crazy to even think about, eh?
Let's wrap this up before you get bored and scroll down: Undertale is a very "feelsy" game; it makes you give a s*** about 16-bit creatures who originally plotted against you, and I feel that not very many games can bring that out in players. Rust started out great, got better, then they jumped ship and started over. I avoided playing it after that for a long time. I got back into playing. Was having fun with it until I started trying to build a base. The new building interface is much better than the old Rust system. You start out able to build just about anything. You need a different key for every door, which is a major pain, inventory space is limited already and now you have to carry a key that takes up as much space in your inventory as 1000 pieces of wood. If you die and respawn in your base you can't get out of your base now, because you don't have the key.  So to really make the key thing work you need to make extra keys for your doors and stash them in your base. So now you have to have extra storage space in your base also to keep all your keys. I'm not going to say I wasted my money buying this game, because I used to enjoy it. But now, the whole key thing has ruined this game for me. I will no longer play it until something is done about this horrible festering boil on my @$$ that is key management is changed. I will not recommend this game to anyone at this point. Here's to hoping the dev team realizes what a stupid system this is and come up with a better way to lock and unlock doors.

So many RPGs, even brilliant ones, have us mindlessly killing monsters for EXP and loot on the principle that they're "evil" and that we need to save the world, but Undertale takes that principle and wipes its♥♥♥♥♥with it. Sure, you CAN kill them if you want, but... maybe the game will make you change your mind? Either way, your decision will heavily impact the course of the game, as there are multiple unique endings.
As you may have noticed, Undertale has received a metric crap-ton of praise for its unique approach to giving players the ultimate choice between befriending or slaying every monster in the game; it has also received praise for its emotionally empowering story, its many interesting (and sometimes downright AWESOME!) secrets and Easter eggs, its rockin' sountrack, its charming yet simplistic aesthetics, and - arguably above all else - its lovable, memorable characters.
When a game can make you enjoy going out on a date with a skeleton who once tried to capture you against your will, it's special. When a game can make you genuinely care about a fish knight who once mercilessly chased you through the rain so that she could rip your soul from your body, it's special. When a game can make you look up a web source to help you obtain friendship with every enemy in the game who tried killing you in various random encounters, it's special. Malboros from Final Fantasy games are hated by almost everyone who has encountered them, but what if we could become best buds with them? Crazy to even think about, eh?
Let's wrap this up before you get bored and scroll down: Undertale is a very "feelsy" game; it makes you give a s*** about 16-bit creatures who originally plotted against you, and I feel that not very many games can bring that out in players. Is Undertale perfect? Nah, but no game is. As a guy who appreciates Shigesato Itoi's "Mother" trilogy for the NES, SNES, and GBA, I found a lot to like in the quirky little game that Toby Fox and his team so lovingly created; a great deal of effort went into the final product, I can tell.
If I haven't convinced you, look at it this way: it's ten freaking bucks. That's like, what, a couple "Happy Meals" from McDonald's? Please...

AMD FX 8320 Black Edition OctoCore OC'd to 3.76Ghz
Diamond Radeon HD 7970 3GB DDR5 OC'd to 1200Mhz Core Clock/1600Mhz Memory Clock
8GB Corsair Vengence 2000Mhz RAM (2x4GB)
MSI 970A-G46 Motherboard
Cooler Master Seidon M120 Liquid CPU Cooler
How The Game Plays:
Even with my machine, which I can run any game I've ever played at max setting with a stable 60FPS or more, this game runs so incredibly poorly it makes me motion sickness. The screen tears and lags constantly, even with the game on the lowest settings, it makes no difference. This, is a sign of poor development within the engine when they rebuilt it. The engine is quite terrible, it is so terrible, that even after a year, the DayZ developement team has yet to fix the fact that zombies can glitch through walls, become invisible, hit you from 20m away, and can even aggro to you from over 1000m away.
You cannot run from zombies, don't bother running into houses or buildings to try and close the door behind you, because they will just run through the door or the wall and still get to you. Makes no difference. You have no safe place. The game is glitchy to the point you will try and drink water, and it will get stuck and nothing will happen. You will try and pick up an item, in my case I tried picking up ammo for a gun that I had just found, spent 20 minutes running from zombies trying to find ammo for this gun, well I found the ammo and the zombies glitch hit me through the floor and killed me. Had the item gone in my inventory I could have dashed past them and loaded my gun and killed them. Though, the game is so incredibly broken that it makes it impossible to so the simplest tasks.
Why didn't I just melee the zombies? You are probably asking. The melee in this game is so horrible you will punch yourself in the face. The melee is so hard, so glitchy, it is almost impossible. You will dodge a zombies and be 15m away, and you see him swing and somehow, someway, he hits you. You can't get close to zombies at all, or you will get glitch hit and start bleeding out.
The engine is so poorly designed, it makes me think they rushed to rebuild an engine for the sole fact of releasing a DayZ standalone alpha, so they can scam 2 million people or more of their money. This game has been out for quite a while. Sadly no matter what they do to this game it will not be fixed until they fix the engine. Sunlight can go through walls, zombies can go through walls. It'll make you cringe. The game does not run smoothly whatsoever, it's just too sluggish and poorly managed.
If you don't believe me, buy the game for the raised price tag of $34.99, which is absolutely ridiculous for a game in it's current state. By no means is this game worth $34.99.
I understand that this game is in Alpha, however it has been in Alpha for so long, and key issues have not been addressed. The point of an alpha, is to address bugs and issues to better the game so that is can become a finished product, a finished, playable product. Except, the developement team behind this is NOT doing that. They are not suporting the game, and for a team of over 200 people, this is absolutely pathetic. Do you really think players are interested in cannabalism, as opposed to fixing the zombies glitching through walls? Do you really think adding items in the game that have absolutely no use currently, instead of fixing CORE engine problems?
This developement team has their heads up their arses, I tell you. They have made millions off this Alpha alone, it is simply unacceptable how little they have done. You can report the bugs and issues, as you should do participating in the alpha, but they don't take initiative to fix anything. If they truly were going to release this game, they would be eager to fix these core problems, but they haven't, and they aren't.
The community:
The players in this game are some of the worst. Players always shoot on site, even if you're unarmed. It is just a deathmatch. Back in the day, you would hold someone up, press F2 and surrender, get handcuffed, and let go. Now, everyone is a coward, and shoots every player on sight. People don't get the system that is in place in this game neither. I've been well geared, just once, and I was shot in the back multiple times with a shotgun.
I had a backpack full of pristine items, that I had spent hours upon hours gathering. Only to get shot in the back. The players are so nubish, they don't know that when you shoot a player, you can damage their gear depending on where you shoot them. This guy destroyed everything in my backpack, every pristine item, and for what? He didn't kill me to loot me, cause he is now looting the damaged stuff that he shot, that I worked hard to gather, all because he was a coward and shot someone in the back.
This is what you will encounter in this game, time and time again. The players are more of a threat than the zombies, the zombies are nothing in this game besides a big glitchy mess.
The game has so many things right with it, but even more things wrong with it. The players need to stop being psychopathic maniacs and shooting everyone they see on site like cowards. The player interaction is one of the best things, or what USED to be one of the best things about this game. Though it has really lost it's touch and the game is full of people who don't understand it and want to treat it like a call of duty kill-as-many-people-as-you-can game.
I will continue to play this game from time to time, and post videos of all the glitches that are in this game, maybe now that rocket is gone, things will be different. Though, they have not announced that the engine will be rebuilt. Which, if this game is to be successful, it NEEDS to be done.
You are better off playing the DayZ mod with ARMAII, along with the other free mods like Epoch etc. They will give you the experience you want from this game, and it is already there.
This game is a poorly managed alpha with developers that refuse to fix key issues. If the developers were more proactive about fixing things, my review would be different. They aren't, though, and until they prove me wrong I would not recommend getting into this alpha.
Be warned, Buy the alpha if you want, but, I will say "I told you so!"

You can eat people in this game by carving their dead♥♥♥♥♥and baking it in a forest fire while you're being hunted down by the same person you're cooking who just respawned looking to get revenge. That is how awesome this game is.
