Of course it has problems. I'll go ahead and list out the ones I've come across. They should be fixed before the real game comes out. I find these annoying, but it definitely does not impact the amount of fun I have in this game, knowing that it is an alpha:
- FPS problems even on high end PC
- Combat isn't up to par
- You can die in really stupid ways (falling a couple of feet)
- Bugs when picking up and dropping items
- Not being able to move sometimes when spawning in map
- The fact that you can still get killed for a good 30 seconds after you have left a server
- Server lag and ping issues in combat
Weapon variety is perfect, and the overall mood the game sets is gorgeous. You can die from hunger and thirst and it is very realistic. It has a pretty gloomy overall vibe that says "if you don't take care of yourself, these zombies will".
Most fun I've had in a while.

Nowadays, you have games and experiences.
The experiences forego most mechanics and normally present systems for showcasing and storytelling. Beautiful as they may be, often they lack elements of interactivity and a sense of agency.
Games are the interactive media that allows one to test their skill. They rely on mechanics and graphical fidelity to give an experience that closely attached to that of a simulator.
Undertale transcends these classifications.
Its reliance upon simplicity and a unique story-based theme might turn people off. But I find that through its simplicity, it is also honest and through it story, it drags you along for a ride more compelling than most movies, stories and games have in the last 10 years.
Surely there’ll be things about Undertale you won’t like, but one thing you will be, is pleasantly surprised by all the things this game will do.
Of the 200+ games out of my steam list, this is one of the select few that I’d rate with a 9.8/10, even surpassing titles like bioshock (1,2,3), metro (LL & 2033).
Go and freaking get it if you have any interest in story driven games what so ever.

Undertale is easily one of the more charismatic entries into the medium of late and well worth the investment.
The game should be lauded for its excellent use of language. Characters feel alive, fresh and engaging. As a player you care about what these characters think and feel and they are largely what will drive you to complete the game, perhaps even more than once.
A similar amount of care and attention has been placed into the soundtrack and art assets. The world is so brimming with different colours and radically different locations that you really feel like you're moving through a fantastical 16-bit picture book of sorts. A simple, but highly inspiring touch for example is that early on you will see a block of ice floating through river and as you progress so too does the block of ice in the background. With the soundtrack they also opted to not stick entirely to the 8-bit/16-bit schtick and I think this pays out immensely for the more dramatic moments of the plot.
However, with all this said I find myself struggling to embrace Undertale as a great game. Why? Because I'm not sure that the actual gameplay has been properly balanced here. Yes I know, the bullet-hell mechanics are INCREDIBLY original, a stroke of genius almost, but these sequences are not the whole game. When looking back on the gameplay of the game is there any other gameplay element that we can say is quite as original?
For example, despite the excellent environments, the game is essentially one long corridor that only slightly deviates from being a straight path. There are a few secrets hidden here and there but for the most part moving from one screen to the next is the name of the game. Also, when we consider how innovative the bullet hell as a defense mechanism is it begs the question why the attacking system is only marginally more interesting than your average menu-based attack system, and probably more cumbersome.
However, these weaknesses become subtle strengths if we reconsider calling Undertale a game and call it something more akin to an interactive novel with gameplay elements, or (god forbid) an interactive experience.
In the case of the corridor issue, the cramped linear feel might lead the player to understand a little about why someone (or some monsters) might really not want to stay underground. And in the case of the attacking system being boring? Well this just leads to the player being more inclined to try and act and negotiate their way out of a fight because while the gameplay of attacking might be dull, the dialogue of talking out the situation with your enemies is immensely fun to read through. Acts of mercy also of course lead the player towards a predictable, but meaningful and worthwhile moral conclusion.
I suspect that Undertale might be best played when someone is between the ages of 10 and 13. Old age cynacism can easily unravel the emotional tapestry Undertale weaves. Sure there are some dark, and adult implications, themes and motifs dotted around the narrative and design but I only feel like these would serve to challenge a young mind in a positive way and get them to draw parallels with their own life.
With that said I do not think that older gamers should limit themselves to NOT playing this Undertale. It truly is one of the most creative things I've seen come out of the industry in the past while and there are few people that I wouldn't recommend it to.
So check it out already!

I CRAWLED THROUGH THE BUSHES. My hands crept forward slowly as I slid along the ground, the grass rustling as I passed over it like a snake.
My killers lay in sight. They had murdered me, though I was nothing but a defenseless bambi. Now...they were the ones who were defenseless. One of the two killers had a broken leg and was lying in a bush as he talked to his friend. "Go look for a splint, hurry, I need it. Check the houses by the shore. Go!" he pleaded. Little did he know that soon his corpse would lie beneath my feet. His friend nodded once, green motorcycle helmet bobbing up and down as he jogged off towards the shore.
Now was my time of vengeance. I slipped out of my hiding place, a small bush that was only a few feet away. The injured man lay there, unaware of my approach.
I was standing over him now, reveling in my victory. My hand snuck into his backpack, and I took the pickaxe he had.
The pickaxe gleamed in the afternoon sun as I hoisted it over my head. Then
. Blood spurted everywhere as the pickaxe bit through the man's coat and into his soft flesh. He screamed for help...but his friend was too far away to save his life.
Vengeance is sweet.

Does it live up to all the hype? ...No.

It's really hard to try and convince someone to give Undertale a try since it's one of those games where the less you know about it the better.
So, in the spirit of trying to keep this mini review spoilers free, i'll have to be as vague as i possibly can. What is Undertale? It's a classic turn based RPG with the twist that you can possibly win any battle without killing anything. Beyond that, it's better if you take the plunge and give it a try yourself.
At first you might not "get it" why this game gets such praise, chances are, you never will get it, but to those that stick to the end and the game "clicks" with them, then they will surely remember it for a long time. The only way to know, is to try and play the game yourself.
On a more technical side, the game has a lovely soundtrack. Full of memorable tunes. And the sprite work while not impresive, does have it's own charm. Particularly, the style of the sprites used in the battles is very unique. The background tile set does leave a LOT to be desired though. While most of the world of Undertale is very interesting, the very plain tile sets fails to properly represent the world it takes in.
Other than that, i urge anyone that craves something a tad different to give Undertale a try. Even if you feel game doesn't live up to the hype it's getting, at the very least, you'll get to meet a cast of very lovable characters that will brighten anyone's day. Nyeh! heh heh!

Okay, before I start this, I just need to tell you that I JUST finished the true ending. Because of this, I will sound like a crazy maniac. I am so sorry (I'm rewriting this now, so maybe it won't be that bad).
I want this review to be useful, so here are some bullet points of why to buy this game. When I'm looking for a game to buy, and an RPG game comes up in my list, Undertale will be what I will be comparing it to. It was THAT. GOOD.
1.) There was never a time when my computer slowed down because of this game. It is not a game that makes your computer run slow.
2.) The controls are just great. There was never a time when I felt frustrated because of this.
3.) The gameplay is unique. You have surely seen the preview for this game and seen other reviews and heard of "pacifist" and "genocide" playthroughs. Leaving story aside for a little, you can play this whole game without killing anyone. Thoughout 99% of the game, it is possible to use an "ACT" action instead of an attack. After doing the right actions such as consoling, joking, hugging, etc., you can "Spare" your enemy. This is where the true challenge of the game comes in. Many fights have you either doing this, surviving long enough, or some other twist (Mettaton's battle is esspecially memorable). Honestly, you can kill most enemies with one hit, even the bosses (with the exception of 2). Playing this game as a pacifist, howwever, requires skill, as the enemy's attack is done through your soul, represented by a heart, doging attacks. Doing this eans that unless you sleep at a hotel, you HP will never go above 20. Really, this gameplay is the best.
4.) The story is one of best I know. It breaks the fourth wall, it's funny, dramatic, heartbreaking and just full of great, complex feels. It's a story about compassion, humanity, forgiveness, empathy and sympathy..... it's truly a story that you not only witness, but experiance. It's truly a modern epic.
5.) The characters are just fantastic. I won't be too detailed, but if you kill any of these characters, you're a ♥♥♥♥ing heartless monster. I don't even care that they're computer programs. I like and care for them. It's also worth mentioning that the main character is just a perfect medium for the player. Again, this is not just a game or a story, but an experiance.
God it's late... but I MUST persevere... the love of the game fills me with DETERMINATION.
(You'll get it if you play it, I promise).
6.) It's not a terribly difficult game. It's not too casual, but it can be played without raging out. It also rewards you for exploration, but it's not like The Legend of Zelda or Skyrim where that much open world might feel frightening. You can find secrets and they're not too dificult to figure out. Again, this game is meant to give you a good time and immerse you. Oh, and the puzzles are reletively easy as well. Hard enough to make you think, easy enough that you won't be on the same one for hours on end.
7.) The art and attention to detail is great. Everything from the little character noises that are made when dialouge is occuring to their expressions and the world around them, this game feels complete.
8.) The music is EPIC. It's not often in my life where I can listen to a voiceless album for long periods of time. Undertale exceeds ecpectations with its music though. I LOVE this soundtrack. It has many moods to it and fits the game perfectly. And the usage and timing of it is just.... so ♥♥♥♥ing great. Buy the game and soundtrack bundle. There's over 2 hours worth of music on it, so it's definitely worth the extra 8 bucks.
9.) If my brain wasn't so tired, I would probably be able to keep going. All I can say now is that it's under 20 bucks for the Game + Soundtrack bundle. Relative to even to meals at McDonalds, and relative to SO MANY triple A titles, that's cheap. And so many of those big budget games can't even compare to Undertale. So at least buy the game. If you hate it, you spent ten bucks, and you didn't lose much. In fact, if you wanna take the time, you can get a refund. Also, you can listen to the soundtrack on Bandcamp and youtube, and you can download a demo on the game's website. So really, there's so much reward for so little risk.
If you're sitting omn the fence, BUY IT. You won't regret it. I know cause I was the same.
AND NOW, SO TIIPS.
1.) Keep sparing Toriel.
2.) Spare EVERYONE. On your first run, however, it's ok to fight ASGORE.
3. After your first run, load your save and don't fight Asgore. You'll get a call which will start the events that will lead you to the TRUE ENDING, which, by the way, is ♥♥♥♥ing amazing and may make you cry.
4.) Find out more of what tthere is to find!
Thank you for reading this review. Let me know if it helps you!
Oh, also, if you plan on being a massive♥♥♥♥♥♥ do it AFTER your pacifist run. The game will remember what you did on the genocide run and it will ruin the ending. Also, prepare to cry.

It's not "as good" as everyone says it is, but it's very solid.
Pros:
+Excellent Soundtrack with lots of catchy chiptunes mixed with a variety of songs that rarely if ever seem out of place
+The Multiple Endings are great. The neutral ending is so out there that it alone almost makes the game worth the price
+When this game does well with it's writing it does very, very well
+Bosses are memorable and very fun
+Has a loveable charm throughout
+Tsundereplane
Cons:
-Short length, and much of the full experience comes from playthroughs after the first, which I am not a fan of
-Lack of battle options; You have a fight command for damage and that's it, most battles are spent dodging the enemy attacks, and there aren't a lot of useful items and whatnot around
-Writing can be hit or miss, and it misses a decent chunk of the time. At times it can be outright genius, at others it feels tryhard or too memetic and the quirkiness doesn't work. I'll admit I've already played the entire Mother series, which this game feels very inspired by, leaving me comparing the two a lot, but I still feel as if it didn't really leave an impression on me as often I would have expected
-The adventure is very linear and most areas feel like they serve little purpose other than "go here because it's the area after the boss of the last area"
All in all a solid game that is worth the price of admission. And if you see it on a sale, go ahead and grab it right away.

It's not "as good" as everyone says it is, but it's very solid.
Pros:
+Excellent Soundtrack with lots of catchy chiptunes mixed with a variety of songs that rarely if ever seem out of place
+The Multiple Endings are great. The neutral ending is so out there that it alone almost makes the game worth the price
+When this game does well with it's writing it does very, very well
+Bosses are memorable and very fun
+Has a loveable charm throughout
+Tsundereplane
Cons:
-Short length, and much of the full experience comes from playthroughs after the first, which I am not a fan of
-Lack of battle options; You have a fight command for damage and that's it, most battles are spent dodging the enemy attacks, and there aren't a lot of useful items and whatnot around
-Writing can be hit or miss, and it misses a decent chunk of the time. At times it can be outright genius, at others it feels tryhard or too memetic and the quirkiness doesn't work. I'll admit I've already played the entire Mother series, which this game feels very inspired by, leaving me comparing the two a lot, but I still feel as if it didn't really leave an impression on me as often I would have expected
-The adventure is very linear and most areas feel like they serve little purpose other than "go here because it's the area after the boss of the last area"
All in all a solid game that is worth the price of admission. And if you see it on a sale, go ahead and grab it right away.

Yes, review number #1 and it's a mostly negative one at that.
My time with Rust (8 hours) has been mostly fun. So far I've played on a few servers and got to grips with the game. I found a server I liked, started to gather resources and attempt to build a home, on my own. All was well, I had plenty of resources, my home was complete, made from stone, had a furnace and all the goodies to keep me surviving. I was proud.
So once I felt I had enough resources in my base to make me feel safer I decided to go out to deeper explore the surrounding area. My journey lead me to a massive tower build by other survivors and there was somebody home too, so I put away my weapon and said hi etc. We chatted for a while then I went on my way back home only to bump into another player who attacked me and sadly killed me. Now that was all fun, way more fun than I've had with DayZ.
Now for the issue, well actually 2 MAJOR issues. The first being that you can craft a lock and key for the door to your house. Great idea and works well for the most part, for example, while your out looting nobody can get into your house (providing you lock the door).
What happened to me and probably to many more is that once I died I no longer had the key to my house and it only gets more frustrating. Of course, after dying, I then respawned inside my house only to find my door locked with no way to open it or to break it down (made of stone). So now I'm stuck inside my house and my 6 hour playtime today has been for nothing. All that time wasted because of a rather silly key system.
Now the second major issue is that if your someone like me who does not have the ability to play the game every day then your in for more stupid. Let's say for example I wasn't locked inside my house and everything was still going well. I would have logged off as normal only to find out the next time I log in (2 days from now) my entire house will have fallen down! Due to decay. Decay which takes 24 hours.
So Rust seems more like a full time job rather than a game you play for fun. Everything you build requiring constant upkeep. Now it isn't such a big issue for those who play in large groups because there is always likely to be somebody on reparing their base, but for those like me who enjoy playing solo then we are out of luck until they find a better solution than this.
These two flaws have put me off the game entirely. The question in my mind everytime i think of playing is, what's the point in playing now it's all for nothing.
Please be aware before purchasing this. It has unbelievable potential. I hope it improves...soon.

Okay, you're thinking about playing this game. I feel ya. It's got some hype.
But first, go download Unturned the Free to Play on Steam.
Play it for ten minutes.
Realize that is what Day Z is aiming for.
There is smoother graphics in DayZ, but Unturned has smoother gun play, better hit detection, longer draw distances, better layouts of villages and internal buildings, and a wider selection of places to visit and loot to engage the world with. It's everything the Day Z mod was when it was only a Mod, community supported, and its everything DayZ wanted to be as a StandAlone. Unturned has vehicles and Crysis 2 like weapon modding systems (You hold up your gun and add the mods, very nice). Meanwhile, in DayZ, two years of development and interacting with your inventory is a still a chore in this game. I risk losing my equipment just setting it on the ground more than I did when it was a mod.
Basically... its Unturned without any of the features or fun of Unturned, with better graphics, and a ridiculously overpriced tag for the few features it boasts that are limping along in functionality.
I'm keeping an eye on this game, I'll let you know and change my review when it becomes playable.
In the meantime, see you in 7 Days to Die, or Unturned. The only thing this has going for it, to be honest, is its not Call of Duty. There is that.

Yes, review number #1 and it's a mostly negative one at that.
My time with Rust (8 hours) has been mostly fun. So far I've played on a few servers and got to grips with the game. I found a server I liked, started to gather resources and attempt to build a home, on my own. All was well, I had plenty of resources, my home was complete, made from stone, had a furnace and all the goodies to keep me surviving. I was proud.
So once I felt I had enough resources in my base to make me feel safer I decided to go out to deeper explore the surrounding area. My journey lead me to a massive tower build by other survivors and there was somebody home too, so I put away my weapon and said hi etc. We chatted for a while then I went on my way back home only to bump into another player who attacked me and sadly killed me. Now that was all fun, way more fun than I've had with DayZ.
Now for the issue, well actually 2 MAJOR issues. The first being that you can craft a lock and key for the door to your house. Great idea and works well for the most part, for example, while your out looting nobody can get into your house (providing you lock the door).
What happened to me and probably to many more is that once I died I no longer had the key to my house and it only gets more frustrating. Of course, after dying, I then respawned inside my house only to find my door locked with no way to open it or to break it down (made of stone). So now I'm stuck inside my house and my 6 hour playtime today has been for nothing. All that time wasted because of a rather silly key system.
Now the second major issue is that if your someone like me who does not have the ability to play the game every day then your in for more stupid. Let's say for example I wasn't locked inside my house and everything was still going well. I would have logged off as normal only to find out the next time I log in (2 days from now) my entire house will have fallen down! Due to decay. Decay which takes 24 hours.
So Rust seems more like a full time job rather than a game you play for fun. Everything you build requiring constant upkeep. Now it isn't such a big issue for those who play in large groups because there is always likely to be somebody on reparing their base, but for those like me who enjoy playing solo then we are out of luck until they find a better solution than this.
These two flaws have put me off the game entirely. The question in my mind everytime i think of playing is, what's the point in playing now it's all for nothing.
Please be aware before purchasing this. It has unbelievable potential. I hope it improves...soon.

Hello everybody! It's been a while since I've written a review, and this review is certainly late for the party. I've been playing since legacy, so I think my opinions are valid for such a time requiring game. Anyways, off to the review!
NOTE: I will be reviewing experimental, because it has grown enough to be considered the main game.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Optimization: This game is generally well optimized on its own, but it can be unreliable at times because your framerate also relies on the server host. Other than that, this game can run on all current PCs, but to run it on lesser ones you must also lower your graphics(as expected). (9/10)
Graphics: The game looks amazing for what it used to look like back in the 'Legacy' version of the game. I'll find myself completely absorbed and immersed because of the atmosphere this game introduces through the sunsets, the views, and the changes in screen overlay depending on the scenery. However, there are still some shading and shadow issues, which can ruin far terrain sometimes. (8/10)
Gameplay: The game is very fun, don't get me wrong, but I feel that it lacks in certain areas. It is time consuming and difficult to build a base good enough to let you sleep and go about the week, let alone protecting yourself from larger raid-clans and dealing with building decay. From this, it becomes very tedious and the overall result makes you sad to go back to it. In the end, you do have some good memories colaborating with the community, which is why I give this section a (7/10).
Originality: Everyone likes an original game, don't they? Well sometimes you have to borrow assets from other games to make said game original. Rust takes most of its communal elements from concepts used (and poorly delivered) in DayZ, and then combines it with other more sandbox like games to create a truly original game. You'll find yourself in wars, disputes, and towns because of the community colaboration's odd concoction with the sandbox elements. In the end, I think this game gave me some unique memories that I'll never forget. (10/10)
Social Ease and Affect: My special category for this game is social ease and affect. By this, I (of course) don't mean how many players have social deficits. Rather, I am judging how the game allows and effects communication with fellow players. Anyways, the microphone compatability along with other people being able to manipulate you when you're offline really adds a sense of realism when it comes to social interaction. You'll find yourself having similar social disputes you'd have in real life, just on a more paleolithic scale. Social interaction is easy, as it is just the hit of the V button. Also, mouths moving when words come out adds a nice touch. (10/10)
The total score of this game is an 88/100, or about a 9/10. Basically, that means it is rising far above most AAA games and is DEFINETLY worth your time, if you have a lot to spare of course.

I can't leave a proper review due to character limitations.
Above anything else when playing this you need to remember that it's in Alpha. For those of you who don't know this means, it means not remotely done. (The developers predict another two years which is ambitious realistically more like 5ish). When a game (especially a big title game like say Halo or Masseffect) is in Alpha it is generally kept in house where a small group of testers (good luck getting that job. I've tried for a local branch of Atari) look for issues and actually try to break the game so the dev team can work out the issues then fix them. It's also a playground for the developers to add or subtract items that may or may not ruin the game. Where this game is released on Steams early access we the players get to help fund the developers as well as break the game to help it evolve into it's beta form.                                           With that being said you should expect the game to have issues, content that serve no purpose yet and by all means don't get attached to your character for a number of reasons.
In the standalone you get the Chenarus map. A fictional Russian/Eastern European country side containing small towns, cities all the way  down to farms and castles that look to have been abondoned for a few years. I'd like to see maps that have been completely over grown like in the (evil) console game The Last of Us. As far as the standalone  there is no autorun key or choice of vehicles at the moment. The Mod also offers other maps outside of Chenarus which I hope find their way into the standalone.
When it comes to vehicles the mod has a large variaty to choose from. Things like make shift APC's and Dune buggies all the way to slow baggage carts and deadly ATV's (seriously I had one in the mod and it wound up launching me to the top of the map to fall to my death) Despite the variaty of vehicles the Mod only had from my memory two customizable set of wheels. The standalone will make all cars custom builds. To the point where you can put four different tires one the same car.
When it comes to survivability the Standalone really outshines (and will continue more so) the mod. In the mod you had to fend off hunger, hypothermia and if you are foolish enough to drink untreated water a disease. Starvation was staved off by hunting for canned goods but finding huntable game was like hunting for a unicorn. More often than not if you would find a wild amimal om the mod you would either not have the ranged weapon to kill it or not have the very specfic hunting knife to cut the beast apart. In the standalone I have had moments where I find more game animals than I have ammo or loot space. The leather of critters can also be used to craft items in the standalone unlike the mod. In the standalone if you so choose you can also become a cannibal eating the flesh of other players. As far as food goes the easiest way to get food is the most tedious, fishing. The standalone will eventually become tougher as they start to introduce things like wolves, bears and diseases that are trying to kill you in the zompocolyse. This is going to make the game that much more difficult and fun in my opinion.
As far as fellow players goes this game will make you question everyone... ever.. in any circumstance. My sister and nephews play. I like to think they are good people but when thrown into a Dayz scenario they become... well putting it as lightly as possible bandits. They use to be good folk helping new spawns but as people in Dayz betrayed them for one reason or antoher they became more shoot you in the face, loot your still warm cropse and laugh about it sort of folk.
There is no benifit for one mentality over the other. other than knowing that despite the odds you can be a decent person. For the most part the mod had the same reasoning but one of the mods for the mods (gah modception) would effect your housing. This makes me wonder what the dev team has in store knowing that by late 2015 they plan on working in a fortification or player housing system. The mod made it so a heroe (it's how it's spelled in the mods mod) would need more material to build a house or garage but it'd also grant more storage space than a bandits house which cost less but hold less loot.
The mod has a much larger variety of fire power than the standalone.  I honestly have no idea the depth of the mods weapon locker but I know in the standalone it's pretty limited. I had a VSS sniper rifle on me most of the time in the mod. It's a sniper rifle with a built in silencer. Come the zompocolypse what more is there to love about it? There were also things like grenade launchers with various ammo such as flare or smoke rounds and even an Enfield (known as the dinner bell for good reason) The standalone as a meh diversity so far. One of my public characters I have a pump action shotgun on my back and an AK in my hands and a deringer (wich is a .45 btw. Much larger than I'd expect) I also have a pirvate hive charcter that has a pistol grip (smaller, sawn off pump action shotty) and a .357 magnum with no ammo. I really hope they open up more fire power. Given the craft system and items in game one should be able to make a good ol' fasion molotov. Rag+empty container+gasoline=firey doom!.
So after spending hours in both the mod and the standalone my findings are the mods are more "complete" but the end game standalone will have more to offer. I could (and have been able to) keep a character in both but each has it's ups and downs. The standalone has a lot of potential if you don't mind playing in the sandbox of an  unfinished game that everyone and everything is out to kill you. The mod is great too in it's own way. I suggest paying into this if you don't mind supporting potentially hungry down on their luck developers. If you are looking for something more complete I suggest the mod.
Something one needs to remember when buying into a game that is in it's alpha stages is that the dev team may literally be doing their work out of the basement of someones parents house, living off of cheap beer and or energy drinks broken up by the occasional stovetop ramen noodle dish. They tend to live like artists such as Van Gogh lived or a great number of other artists. Every developer dreams it but not all live up to what happend to Notch with Minecraft which was a literal millionaire over night scenario. I would happily buy any dev team a case of beer or ramen and just sit in the background and watch the magic of seemingly smashing on keys and furious clicking to develop different aspects of the same piece of interactive art.
I do enjoy a survival game. As it just so happens a large number of them involve the currently favored zombie hordes for enemies but anything would do. If you are looking for a Zombie Apocalypse game, then DayZ in a current state is not a game for you. Don't get me wrong, there are zombies in this game alas they pose a minor nuisance, something that makes you swap your rifle for a melee weapon once in a while. I bet players would hardly notice if zombies would be removed altogether. This game is more of a special operations or guerilla warfare simulator, where hostile bands players sneak upon one another to take potshots at the enemy, looting settlements in some free time. The game is still being developed but mark my words, whatever they change, it will still be the same gameplay as it is now. All in all it is a lot of fun to travel the breadth of Chernarus with friends, being on constant lookout for danger and gathering supplies in order to die in some meaningless gunfight in a city or on the road.

Undertale is a game with puzzles, a deep story, and silly characters. You make decisions throughout the game that affect the ending. In it, you play as a gender neutral character, already making the game for anyone and everyone! Is the character female? Male? Neither? Both? It’s up to you to decide and in doing so you feel a closer connection to the character by reflecting your gender onto them.
Unfortunately, this game does not have the graphics of MGSV or FF during cutscenes, but I feel it made the right choice in terms of graphics. By having simple graphics and cute little sprites reminiscent of a slightly more detailed NES game rather than detailed backgrounds, character models, huge maps, etc. you’re more drawn towards the story. I mean, let’s be honest: the graphics are♥♥♥♥♥♥ But they aren’t important to a game like this. The graphics don’t drive the game or the depth of this game, it’s the story. If you’re anything like me, you get emotionally invested in the main character, which makes the story all the more enjoyable.
I don’t know what I can say about this game without spoiling the game. It’s just really freaking good! The only thing I’d have to say is that please for the love of anything and everything holy do NOT spoil it for yourself and watch other people do an entire playthrough. If you’ve watched a little bit, that’s fine, but if you’ve had the whole plot and everything ruined then I’m not really sure why you’re debating buying it. Where’s the mystery? Where’s the wonder? Where’s the emotional involvement?
But I mean it’s a good game and there’s really nothing more I can say about it. So I’ll just gush about it. I just love the fact that the main character is gender neutral, it’s amazing. I mean they’re a child so they’re already pretty gender neutral because let’s be honest most children look the same (aside from skin color and whatever but this kid’s skin is literally yellow. No kid’s skin is like that). There’s multiple endings. There’s the good route, the bad route (also known as genocide) and the neutral route. You can go on a murdering rampage and kill everyone, you make friends with everyone and not hurt a single soul. There’s so many options and the story changes drastically based on how you play and what choices you make.
I mean… I just really like this game. I’m in love with a skeleton who makes awful puns and I DON’T know why but I also don’t care. This game is just…. beautiful. Just play it. Do it. I promise you’ll like it.

I am probably the last person that would like this sort of game. It's retro, it's got a fittingly retro-chiptunesque soundtrack, and it's an RPG (although you don't really have to play it as one, sort of).
However, despite my dislike of games with these qualities, I was inexplicably hooked. What hooked me can only be described as Undertale's "charm". The characters, their stories, their personalities, and the story itself. It all feels so charming and warm and youthful, it reminds me of some of the less "violent" movies of Miyazaki.
I like that the game allows you to approach it however you want, it opens up the possible audience. I personally skipped most of my monster fights when possible because I was more drawn to the main story line than the little touches that I'm sure give the game a nice depth and flair to those more inclined to really explore the "woodwork" of a game. But even in my direct, narrow style the game still had a lot to offer me and I appreciate that. I appreciate having the options and not being forced to adapt to how one might think an RPG "should be played". I didn't have to level up or focus on my stats, or care about strategies or talk to people. I could do what I wanted, and I'd still get a rewarding experience of what this game is about. And for me, that was the characters (personal favorites being Toriel and Alphys. Oh Alphys, if only, if only...)
In short, this game is diverse in how it lets you approach it, and rich and rewarding in the story it has to tell. I'd definitely recommend it if you're like me and you don't tend to have much of an interest in these sorts of games. Give this one a chance!

You're best off playing this game blind on the first run through, as your choices will be much more natural for you personally that way and you'll get more out of your initial ending. Undertale is a game with puzzles, a deep story, and silly characters. You make decisions throughout the game that affect the ending. In it, you play as a gender neutral character, already making the game for anyone and everyone! Is the character female? Male? Neither? Both? It’s up to you to decide and in doing so you feel a closer connection to the character by reflecting your gender onto them.
Unfortunately, this game does not have the graphics of MGSV or FF during cutscenes, but I feel it made the right choice in terms of graphics. By having simple graphics and cute little sprites reminiscent of a slightly more detailed NES game rather than detailed backgrounds, character models, huge maps, etc. you’re more drawn towards the story. I mean, let’s be honest: the graphics are♥♥♥♥♥♥ But they aren’t important to a game like this. The graphics don’t drive the game or the depth of this game, it’s the story. If you’re anything like me, you get emotionally invested in the main character, which makes the story all the more enjoyable.
I don’t know what I can say about this game without spoiling the game. It’s just really freaking good! The only thing I’d have to say is that please for the love of anything and everything holy do NOT spoil it for yourself and watch other people do an entire playthrough. If you’ve watched a little bit, that’s fine, but if you’ve had the whole plot and everything ruined then I’m not really sure why you’re debating buying it. Where’s the mystery? Where’s the wonder? Where’s the emotional involvement?
But I mean it’s a good game and there’s really nothing more I can say about it. So I’ll just gush about it. I just love the fact that the main character is gender neutral, it’s amazing. I mean they’re a child so they’re already pretty gender neutral because let’s be honest most children look the same (aside from skin color and whatever but this kid’s skin is literally yellow. No kid’s skin is like that). There’s multiple endings. There’s the good route, the bad route (also known as genocide) and the neutral route. You can go on a murdering rampage and kill everyone, you make friends with everyone and not hurt a single soul. There’s so many options and the story changes drastically based on how you play and what choices you make.
I mean… I just really like this game. I’m in love with a skeleton who makes awful puns and I DON’T know why but I also don’t care. This game is just…. beautiful. Just play it. Do it. I promise you’ll like it.

Undertale surprised me in all the best ways, and is a top contender for my GOTY!
I bought the game on a whim when it released, only because I saw a large group of artists and game designers I follow on Twitter talking about it. That turned out to be a very, very good decision, as it's not only some of the most fun I've had with a game in a while, but also the most invested I've been with a game's story in a while.
The art style might be a little simple for some, but I think it is very charming and perfectly captures the mood that the game is going for. Every chaarcter feels unique and well designed. The gameplay though is where I had the most fun. I opted to spare every enemy and I loved the feeling of every encounter being its own little puzzle. Trying to figure out what combination of actions would let you spare an enemy and seeing the reactions to those actions, all while trying to avoid enemy attacks in a bullet hell-type fashion, it was all so fun and engaging!
In terms of the story, all the dialogue was very quirky and genuinely funny. Reminded me a lot of Earthbound! I loved every character I came across and honestly, after playing through it without killing anyone, I really don't want to go back and change that!
So yeah, if you like fun RPGs with unique gameplay twists and a genuinely funny and heartwarming story, yoooouuuu should check out Undertale!

This is one of the best games I have ever played. This game has so much love and care put into it that as a player it honestly lead to such a magical experience, it gave me hope in games and made me feel much better about my life, it stays with you even after it's over. It's an adventure that will take you through a roller coaster of emotions.
Positives:
-One of the best soundtracks I have heard, each song creates amazing an atmosphere that fits with the scene or fight, incredibly memorable and diverse.
-Some of the best writing I've seen. The game knows how to make you laugh or cry, it's honestly just so charming. If you're a fan of Mother 3 style writing then this is a huge treat.
-In this game you come to really love the characters. They aren't one dimensional, they are full of depth and stay with you throughout the whole game. They all feel important to the plot and by the end of your journey you do come to love and care for them, they are amazingly written.
-Your ACTIONS effect the game.  Honestly the amount that you can change in the game is spectacular, it's not about picking dialogue options, it's about how your actions effect everything. Will you give MERCY or will you FIGHT? Each battle offers a way to completely change the game just by your choice of action.
-The combat of the game is very different from regular RPGs, it keeps you on your toes with bullet hell fights and your need to doge bullets that come near you. It makes fighting a lot less tedious and more interesting.
-Much more, honestly I could gush about Undertale forever so I'll just leave this off saying that the game has: good detail, design, world building, fourth wall breaking, and so much more.
Negatives:
-You can only walk in this game, which means you're kinda slow. Backtracking isn't forced in this game but you get some interesting details of you do so that leads to some veeeery long walking. Which is kinda boring and a waste of effort. This doesn't really effect the game much at all, it's just a bit oh a nitpick though.
Honestly I've bought this game for others because everyone deserves to see such a cute game full of love. I would definitely recommend others to play this game, it's an experience you won't want to miss!

Undertale surprised me in all the best ways, and is a top contender for my GOTY!
I bought the game on a whim when it released, only because I saw a large group of artists and game designers I follow on Twitter talking about it. That turned out to be a very, very good decision, as it's not only some of the most fun I've had with a game in a while, but also the most invested I've been with a game's story in a while.
The art style might be a little simple for some, but I think it is very charming and perfectly captures the mood that the game is going for. Every chaarcter feels unique and well designed. The gameplay though is where I had the most fun. I opted to spare every enemy and I loved the feeling of every encounter being its own little puzzle. Trying to figure out what combination of actions would let you spare an enemy and seeing the reactions to those actions, all while trying to avoid enemy attacks in a bullet hell-type fashion, it was all so fun and engaging!
In terms of the story, all the dialogue was very quirky and genuinely funny. Reminded me a lot of Earthbound! I loved every character I came across and honestly, after playing through it without killing anyone, I really don't want to go back and change that!
So yeah, if you like fun RPGs with unique gameplay twists and a genuinely funny and heartwarming story, yoooouuuu should check out Undertale!

If you are a person that enjoys playing alone or in a small group ~5 people, I would highly suggest not playing on an official server. You have ZERO potential to make a meaningful stand against the 20+ member gangs that go around and raid everything in sight.
You either have to join these gangs or simply play on a low pop server.
I can see the potential this game has, but it's at a really tricky spot at the moment. The game has little balance and less administration (on official servers).
Is it worth the price at this very moment? No. Can I see the developers improving this game in the future? Yes.
If you have $20 to blow and just want a few days of fun, this game is for you. If you think you're going to get more than a weeks worth of replay value, I would highly advise you to wait it out and continue to follow it's development.

This is one of the best games I have ever played. This game has so much love and care put into it that as a player it honestly lead to such a magical experience, it gave me hope in games and made me feel much better about my life, it stays with you even after it's over. It's an adventure that will take you through a roller coaster of emotions.
Positives:
-One of the best soundtracks I have heard, each song creates amazing an atmosphere that fits with the scene or fight, incredibly memorable and diverse.
-Some of the best writing I've seen. The game knows how to make you laugh or cry, it's honestly just so charming. If you're a fan of Mother 3 style writing then this is a huge treat.
-In this game you come to really love the characters. They aren't one dimensional, they are full of depth and stay with you throughout the whole game. They all feel important to the plot and by the end of your journey you do come to love and care for them, they are amazingly written.
-Your ACTIONS effect the game.  Honestly the amount that you can change in the game is spectacular, it's not about picking dialogue options, it's about how your actions effect everything. Will you give MERCY or will you FIGHT? Each battle offers a way to completely change the game just by your choice of action.
-The combat of the game is very different from regular RPGs, it keeps you on your toes with bullet hell fights and your need to doge bullets that come near you. It makes fighting a lot less tedious and more interesting.
-Much more, honestly I could gush about Undertale forever so I'll just leave this off saying that the game has: good detail, design, world building, fourth wall breaking, and so much more.
Negatives:
-You can only walk in this game, which means you're kinda slow. Backtracking isn't forced in this game but you get some interesting details of you do so that leads to some veeeery long walking. Which is kinda boring and a waste of effort. This doesn't really effect the game much at all, it's just a bit oh a nitpick though.
Honestly I've bought this game for others because everyone deserves to see such a cute game full of love. I would definitely recommend others to play this game, it's an experience you won't want to miss!

Alright, I'll give this one a go. Before I dive too far into it, I feel I should be clear: I love this game. It's been weeks since I've finished it and I still catch myself listening to the soundtrack or looking up fan art. An 'undertale remix' search on Youtube is one of the first 'u' urls in my browser (which should be distressing but somehow isn't).
Because I love it though, I want to try to lay out clearly what it is and what it's not. I didn't follow Undertale until the pre-launch trailer went up and it got my attention; I didn't play it until a friend started it up and gave me all the details I needed to know I had to play it. So I want anyone who considers this game to come at it ignoring the hype surrounding it, if that's at all possible.
Pros:
- The soundtrack is pretty rad. I think we can objectively agree on this, right? I guess if a kinda SNES/chiptuney aesthetic turns you off, it might not be for you - Toby, in my experience, obviously goes all in for that stylistically. It's more than that but I'm really not qualified to do music critique.
- I'd be inclined to say the same goes for the visuals. I've seen potshots that it's more of this sort of "you made it in an old-school way because you can't do any better," and while that can hold true if you're burned out by this sort of thing, I think Toby comes by the style pretty honestly. It's artistically sort of like if someone took Earthbound's artistic sensibilities and used it to flesh out a dream-y kind of Yume Nikki aesthetic full of neat setpieces. If that and a general kind of old school look don't work for you, there's not much else I can say.
- Gameplay is more involved and fun than the RPG Maker games I know I had in mind when I was thinking about buying this. There's a standard sort of turn-based menu selection element at play, but the shmup-y gameplay that occurs when you're trying not to get hit is done well. You'll notice it less depending on how you play the game but with boss battles, the game whips out some neat tricks to change how fights operate. I'd be lying if I said it's a profound, fantastic, super great system, but for what it is, it's done well and I believe should keep most people more invested than just clicking a button and smacking things (although you can certainly do that as well).
- The game advertises itself as a game where you don't have to kill anybody, and it takes that idea as far as it can go. Sometimes it even takes it farther than you'd think it could. I don't want to comment extensively on it and risk ruining it, but Undertale plays the implications behind level grinding incredibly straight. The moments where you're figuring out whether and how to spare an enemy are the most praiseworthy parts of how the game is put together. There is at least one encounter I drove myself nuts over because of my absolute unwillingness to fight back and for a game to do that to me is one of the better things I can say.
- This is a vague one, but: Undertale is not afraid to make narrative use of its medium. It's best you find out exactly how for yourself, but I would go so far as to say the particular ways in which Undertale tells its story are THE draw and what distinguishes it from the games it's influenced by.
These all constitute things I have a hard time imagining someone looking to get this game would dislike. What follows aren't exactly cons but they are things I would think about:
- This absolutely feels like a one man kind of show. I don't recall who else was credited, but my understanding is that Toby did more or less anything that isn't Temmie. I personally love this - I've become kind of a crank about how soulless it is for me when I can't feel any distinctive personal touch in a game - but if you don't like Toby's writing voice, you're honestly probably going to have a bad time. I think the game is incredibly funny and I'm clearly not alone in that respect. But Toby is the kind of person that will take a gag and run with it, and isn't afraid of just throwing in random stuff that's meant to be amusing because of how out there it is. If bone puns, dating sim interludes, and having an obscene amount of hot dogs stacked on your head strikes you as stupid, well, don't hold your breath for that kind of humor to ever stop.
- I'm going to go out on a limb here and guess that Toby likes JRPGs. That sounds like a no duh thing, but hear me out. If you've played a JRPG or watched anime at any point and have felt that the reliance on hope and friendship you often get with them is cheesy and/or emotionally manipulative, I don't think Undertale will change your mind. There are clever touches that it sucks I can't mention here really, but when it unloads the power of love on you, you have to have an affection or openmindedness for that sort of thing to appreciate it. If you don't, it's probably just going to leave you cold.
- From a conventional content standpoint, Undertale took me somewhere around eight or nine hours to beat and I may have taken more time than is normal. You could get more out of it depending on what kind of playthrough you do, or whether you play it again to go after a whatever other things you want to (there's a surprising amount of sort of cosmetic variability depending on how you handle sparing or killing monsters), but I had no desire to play any more after the ending I got and I mean that in a very positive sense, believe it or not.
- And staying on content, most of that time is focused on walking around, occasional random battles, easy puzzles, and interacting with a ton of NPCs. I think it's a fair asking price for what I got out of it, but if you're hoping for a low price find with lots of sidequests, replay value, challenges that will hold you up for a long time, you're going to be out of luck. There are somewhere between one to three places I would expect most people to struggle, and you really have to overacheive to run into two of them. This game is largely a brisk narrative straight shot that goes from Point A to Point B that most people should clear quickly. I like not having my time wasted with filler so shortness isn't a flaw for me if what's there is good. I think it is but maybe that won't sell you if your idea of bang for your buck is getting a lot of time out of the games you purchase.
Con:
- Nitpicky, but I want to throw this in here. The game's transition from midpoint to finale is abrupt. I had the definite sense, which I was able to ignore in the spirit of what the game was trying to do, that I was being rushed through the end towards the final set of encounters. Before the endgame, I would say Undertale is paced incredibly well. As you hit the endgame, it starts to feel like some kind of cosmic deadline was closing in. What IS there is good, but I was sort of sad to feel like I was being rushed to the conclusion of something I could have spent more time in. Read a certain way, that's almost kind of a compliment though, isn't it?
It's all kind of pedantic and I regret how poor my cutting room floor instincts are, but I think this covers it. Undertale is a game I think as many people should experience as possible. I strongly recommend it. It's made me think a lot more about what you can do in a video game than I ever have before. It also happens to be more playful and fun than a stuffy sentence like that would suggest, hahaha. I could talk a lot more about what I personally really liked but I think it wouldn't be useful to someone looking to figure out if this is the game for them or not. Whenever it happens to get discounted, if you're someone who happens to be on the fence about it, just get it. At an even lower price than $10, I have a hard time seeing how you could get absolutely nothing out of it.
Oh, and, be good, won't you?

Updated Review as of 12/31/15
The sociopath simulator -- yes, still it is a sociopath simulator.
But this game has become, and is becoming so much more.
The Devs are making great strides in the way of content and optimization. The game has never run better than it does currently, and the Dev Team is close(1.5 months eta) to bringing out:
The New Renderer - which should give us the same current visuals with increased optimization.
The New Player Controller - which will make the whole game feel "new", it will eliminate many glitches and bugs, and it will give our characters more freedom and ability(walking whilst eating, swapping guns on the move, etc).
The game has come a long way since day one, I've had a blast and would now suggest it to anyone, with the following disclaimer:
It is still early access, things aren't perfect yet, they are getting there. You have to understand this game was released at an earlier stage of development than any other game in the Steam Early Access program.  No other game has been released with this early and this raw of content. Many people compare it to ARK, but ark had the opportunity to learn from DayZ's trials and tribulations, they had content that they got ready for a smooth release prior to going to early access.
It is a tough game, you will die, a lot, sometimes it will be your fault, sometimes it will be a bug, most of the time it will be to others with various motives. If you can learn from each death, then you'll get better, if not, then you'll complain a lot.
It's a tough game, don't get attached to your gear. Everyone says this, but not that many practice what they preach. If you can be ok dieing as a freshspawn, and almost equally ok when you die fully geared up in military bling, then you're a real DayZ player.
I hope this updated review will help someone out there with their purchase decision. I truly suggest picking this game up, and getting into the world of Chenarus+.
Good luck, survivor!

Would I recommend it for its innovations in mechanics and the changing dialogue depending on past playthroughs? Possibly.
Would I recommend it for the experience? YES.
Undertale is a game that is more than the sum of its parts. Yes, the gameplay is new and fresh. Yes, it does some cool things with small differences in dialogue depending on your past actions even between saves. Yes, the music can be balls-to-the-wall amazing. But the experience, what you take away from the game as a player, is where Undertale shines. What Undertale is is told through everything Undertale does. The whole game sings as a chorus, the music complimenting the gameplay complimenting the graphics complimenting the story.
You will not regret buying this game.
Oh, also, don't read anything about this game before you buy it. This is one of those games where the impact of spoilers is several times more devestating than normal.

anyways on to the actual game
the games obviously based off the popular arma 2 mod where you lodge lead chunks in fellow players skulls for beans and cola and if youve ever tried the experience for yourself i beg you to keep on doing precisely that for an additional $0.00 surcharge because the only things this version has on it are a small pile of guns and the ability to make survivors wear handcuffs and eat stale capn crunch
they certainly plan on adding even more features than theyve currently got but no matter how many colors of pants i can have the core gameplay remains buggier than a motel in arizona and approximately none of those kinks were worked out
thing is youre still going to get invisible zombies gouging chunks of your face out and the ethereal legions of the dead will happily tear their way through just about any wall in the game and get to you on a whim
youll also have to be wary of the psionic members of the living dead thatll preform an excisional biopsy on you from a good five meters away before closing the distance just to ♥♥♥♥ with you
players can easily get in on the fun and hack to their hearts content since theres precisely jack♥♥♥♥♥♥stopping them from one-upping your three hour gun hunt with a five second national guard armory summoning ritual
ladders continue to be lovecraftian horrors beyond human comprehension and more than capable of shattering bone on a mere whim
even homes wont show mercy since youll be stuck in a wall should you approach it unconventionally
the biggest spoiler i have for you is that the entirety of chernarus is actually an enclosed area meant to train super sayians at a hundred times earths gravity
youll realise this upon falling off of a small rock or a staircase half your height and having your legs turn to splinters
while the melee combats no longer preformed with wands that fire thousandths of themselves at hapless adversaries i havent seen any changes to the fact that the arc of the swing might as well be replaced with you casting soviet hexes on the sentient bean container youre aggressing at the time since the engine that made melee combat a hassle was brought back with few changes overall
so few that i retained my arma profile name and the occasionally effective anticheat softwares still bohemias in entirety
theres a pretty solid amount of weapons overall and instead of filling this entire paragraph with repeated statements of 7.62x51 being different from 7.62x54r ill just mention the types
youve got an admirable assortment of things to hit people in face with and somebody even had the foresight to order an arming sword from the budk catalog and the clumsiness and omnipresence to abandon it at multiple locations
youve also got a pretty good stockpile of arms ranging from four 12 gauge shotguns to three various grenades along with an assortment of rifles and two submachine guns to boot
also available is the highly concealable derringer that could help you out in a pinch if it couldnt immediately be pinpointed by chernarus' resident handcuff wielding aikido masters

not to mention that at this rate duke nukem forevers going to have a shorter alpha period and less game breaking glitches
if you havent purchased either strongly consider going with arma since at the very least it offers no less than three good experiences in one for a fraction of the price
as with starforge im honestly hoping im proved completely wrong on all fronts over the coming months considering that even if you were to omit the core premise of legions of bumhungry zombies thisd easily be the most complete survival experience to date if the devs deliver on at least a good chunk of their promises

There have been games with great stories and writing before, but I can't think of any that take advantage of the medium of the video game as fully as Undertale does. It manages to do a lot of really interesting things with the unique form of games without becoming bogged down in self-reference. It's a comedy, a fantasy, and a morality tale, plus a sci-fi and an odyssey and a dating simulator. I can't compare it to any other game I've ever played (although I've never played the Mother/Earthbound games).
There is absolutely no reason not to purchase and play this game.

This is undoubtably my favorite PC game at the moment and ranks very high amongst my favorite games ever. The game has incredible characters, a beautifully well executed moral choice system, genius humor, a gripping story, a solid combat system which seamlessly blends RPG and Bullet Hell, challenging boss fights, abundant replay value, and more. My only "complaints" are that the game is capped at 30 FPS (no big deal in this case), there's no widescreen (not a huge deal either) and that you can only stretch the window to the screen's resolution via the task manager (and there's no way to do borderless). Aside from that I can't say there's anything particularly wrong with the game at least to me.

This game. Holy crap. I was NOT expecting something so spectacular.  I had heard about Undertale from some friends as well as it being all over the internet.  I thought it was just some silly game that I wouldnt care or worry about and probably never play because of all the hype.  I watched the trailers and still had a meh feeling overall.  However, I still was intrigued to find out what all the commotion was about.  So I bought the game.  I was surprised by how small the download was.  And then I played.  And played. And played.  I fell in love with it.  The story, the characters, the animations, the music.  I was engrossed in the world that Toby Fox created and I never wanted to leave it.  I cried, I laughed, I felt inspired.  This game was made with so much love, time and dedication.  And the idea of not having to hurt anyone or kill anyone is such an interesting and different concept.  Yet the game makes you not WANT to hurt anyone because you honestly end up falling in love and not wanting to hurt anyone.  Each character was crafted with heart and soul.  This game is a masterpiece in itself.  Please, try this game. I promise you, you'll end up loving it as much as I did.

Would I recommend this game for the gameplay? Maybe.
Would I recommend it for its innovations in mechanics and the changing dialogue depending on past playthroughs? Possibly.
Would I recommend it for the experience? YES.
Undertale is a game that is more than the sum of its parts. Yes, the gameplay is new and fresh. Yes, it does some cool things with small differences in dialogue depending on your past actions even between saves. Yes, the music can be balls-to-the-wall amazing. But the experience, what you take away from the game as a player, is where Undertale shines. What Undertale is is told through everything Undertale does. The whole game sings as a chorus, the music complimenting the gameplay complimenting the graphics complimenting the story.
You will not regret buying this game.
Oh, also, don't read anything about this game before you buy it. This is one of those games where the impact of spoilers is several times more devestating than normal.

I personally find RUST fun. The server I am on is relatively small to lessen the chances of getting into an encounter. My Listu:
Pros:
No Zombies, Just good ol' fashioned mother nature and a server filled with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s all to ready to teabag and loot your corpse to contend with!
Once you pick up the basics it becomes easier to follow and understand
Natural land generation makes for beautiful surroundings.
Hunting is fairly realistic (unless said prey is stuck on an invisible wall).
Constant look out on your overall condition and what factors bode ill for you.
Loot is fairly hard to find outside of RAD towns and Airdrops, making them more contended and a definite target.
Cons:
Blueprints are rare as balls, even in places you'd expect to find them.
Forging is a process which takes too much time and way too many resources for minimal turn out, making it a bit of a chore.
Random spawning can sometimes drop you right next to players all too ready to paint the surrounding area with your innards, frustrating for new players.
The building system can be extremely confusing for novice players.
The randomly spawning Prefabs are often just for show outside of RAD towns, making them nothing more than disappointing landmarks.
Often not enough warning about dangerous animals being nearby (They should be louder and growl/bark when they are charging giving you time to react).
You can't see someones name until you're literally close enough to lick them. Making friendly-fire a constant issue as people panic.
Fun

They're not static like in most other RPGs you find- Somehow, they seem more relatable, more alive, more -human- than most humans in other games. Where most games, you have one well-developed character, in this game, you have.... Well, I'm not going to spoil it.
I would go on and on and on, and I easily could... But I will have MERCY and SPARE you the massive review. Suffice it to say this:
While most game dev -teams- struggle to make a compelling game, somehow Tobyfox managed to make a game that eclipses all of them, practically by himself. So put that in your spaghetti. If you need some salt for it, just lean over the plate. The tears this game's storyline will give you will be salt enough.

I really enjoyed DayZ when it was a mod.  Though a little quarky at times, was still playable and fun.  Though the base mode was decent, what made it fun was the mods of the mod, such as epoch.  The addition of base building and economy made the game much more engaging.  When I heard they were making a standalone, I was very excited.  I was glad they were also making it more accessable considering that in order to play the mod, you had to purchase Arma 2 and then download the mod files, which was a bit tricky at times.  Also having to keep both updated, and making sure the server you were playing on was running the proper versions as well was a bit tidious.  The mods of the mod were great even though they were created by community and not the primary developer.
So tell me, what the hell happened.  You would think that the development team behind the origional mod would know what the hell they were doing.  Certainly more so than a bunch of random people who created mods like Epoch.  How can a standalone have less content and be as broken as it is, YEARS after initial development?  It's still essentially a mod of ARMA.  It's practically the same engine, running the same code.  This is being worked on by a full development team and still no working vehicles?  You're lucky if you come across one zombie after an hour of running around.  A broken melee system that worked much better in mod, and still none of the promised base building or fortification that was promised yet fully accessable in epoc which was created by a handful of people who pretty much did this for free.  How much money do you think has been thrown at this game?  Enough to merrit the question of why is this game still no where near being completed? I understand that ARMA has its limitations, but I've seen other mods that were able use it a lot better than this mess.  This is unacceptable.
Don't even get me started on the fall sale fiasco.  They raised the price 15% then lowered it 15% and slapped a sale sticker on it.  What a pathetic attempt to put your game on the sale page to garner more exposure.  There were many other alpha/early access games that legitimently lowered their prices, there is no excuse for that underhanded tactic.
~Update~
How many years has this game been in early access?  I tell you how many... too many.  I doubt it will ever be completed, and even if they announce that it is done, it still will not live up to the hype or promises they created.  As it stands now, it's a broken zombie game, with pretty much no zombies.  If you play it just for the PVP aspect, good lucky trying to find someone to kill, or waiting for hours for someone to cross your path.  When you finally do come across someone, have fun with that "combat" system and latency issues.  Don't get me started with the script kiddies, and "hackers"...
Overall, don't bother, there are several other "Zombie Survival" games out there that do everything that DayZ promises and even do it better.
TL;DR version:
For a game backed by a major developer created from a working mod, with hundreds of thousands of dollars thrown at it, there is no reason for this game to be this incomplete after years of development.  DO NOT PAY FOR LIES.  If you have ARMA 2 or 3, just download the mods.

This game is easily, hands down, the best game I've ever played. Now, if you want to know everyone else's reasons for loving this game, go ahead and scroll down. I challenge you to find a -single- bad review for this game. Why? Because this has everything you could ask for.
The story of this game is remarkably compelling- it merits replay after replay.. Not in spite of the fact that you know the story, but BECAUSE you know the story! It's like a book. The more you re-read, the more you understand, the more secrets you unlock, the more you enjoy it and feel for the characters.
And that's what you do in this game- you feel for the characters. They're not static like in most other RPGs you find- Somehow, they seem more relatable, more alive, more -human- than most humans in other games. Where most games, you have one well-developed character, in this game, you have.... Well, I'm not going to spoil it.
I would go on and on and on, and I easily could... But I will have MERCY and SPARE you the massive review. Suffice it to say this:
While most game dev -teams- struggle to make a compelling game, somehow Tobyfox managed to make a game that eclipses all of them, practically by himself. So put that in your spaghetti. If you need some salt for it, just lean over the plate. The tears this game's storyline will give you will be salt enough.
Ten out of Ten stars. I would give it more, but that's mathematically impossible. Oh well, giving it the highest score of any review I've ever made, and am likely to ever make, is fair enough....

The most satisfying game I've played in recent memory.
With more impactful decisions made in this game than most triple-A titles and a story that honestly made me care more about the characters than any other game I've ever played, you owe it to yourself to play this.
Remarkably, the game's format and 8-bit/16-bit feel lent to its strengths, as the mini-games that take place during battles were unique for every enemy and often with new mechanics introduced as you steadily progress. This shone particularly well in "boss" battles, introducing the player to a new mechanic slowly to start while gradually increasing the difficulty of evading attacks. Combined with memorable and catchy music tracks, and you begin to look forward to fighting bosses for the music as much as for the challenge and thrill of success.
Toby Fox and his team did an amazing job writing the characters and in getting you emotionally invested, regardless of the paths you choose in game. While I have only completed a single paragon run (with a neutral boss fight and then chance at full paragon initially) to date, the cohesion between the other characters and the writing made for a thrilling ride of comedy, drama, and joy. There were definitely tears streaming down my face at one point, all while grinning and feeling happily overwhelmed.
However, while a large part of the game is in "the power of friendship," you can also become the villain of the story by not showing any mercy to your opponents. While I might not be able to bring myself to experience it firsthand, you can leave quite the trail of destruction in your wake, grinding the subsurface's monsters (along with their hopes and dreams) to dust. If you're willing to set aside some emotional investment for a greater challenge in difficulty in fighting a few characters, this run's also worth a go.
Lastly, the subtle (and not so subtle) acknowledgements made by some more powerful characters lend greater impact while playing. I won't spoil it, but it made for all the more powerful an experience.
For $10? This game is a gift.
Play this game. Play with a friend, play by yourself. Do at least a run or two of it, make whatever choices you want. An outstanding ~6 hours of gameplay to be had and memories to be made.
Rest assured, you won't be in for a bad time ;)

The problem with moral choice systems in games is Twofold:
First, they're usually presented as clearly signposted dialogue options in unskippable cutscenes, so the choice system feels like an afterthought that, other than unlocking upgrades, has no real relevance to the gameplay.
Second, there's very rarely any reason to justify a choice other than wanting the good or bad karma from it. They force you to choose early into the game if you want to play as a captain planet bad guy who kills kittens for teh lulz or as some kind of saint that makes ridiculous or strictly pacifist decisions, when you, the player wouldn't neccesarily make those decisions. Let's be honest, we don't mind slaughtering hundreds of computer generated innocents in a sandbox game if it means we get dark side points for it, and the only reason we ever try to protect them is for the good karma.

Even the games where the system is well implemented (usually when it's central to the plot), such as KOTOR or Infamous 2, suffer from these problems to an extent.
But, in my opinion, Undertale addresses both of these issues very well. The moral choice system is incredibly central to gameplay, in fact it forms the basis for the whole game, and the nature of the system itself is such that you don't learn about the way it works untill near the end, which makes the gameplay feel very organic. In my first playthrough, if a monster♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off I destroyed it, but ones that were likeable I spared as much as I could. If I had a high health bar or was confident in dodging attacks, I could afford to be merciful, if not, then it was "Kill or be killed." The decisions I made were because I wanted to make them, and i genuinely felt the consequences of my actions as the story is amazing and the game really makes you care about it characters. When I got this game in early 2014 I thought it would be a great survival. Rust claimed to inherit the best from such giants like DayZ and Minecraft. And it was so until Garry decided to remake the game for Unity.
Let me describe the gameplay of an average daily dose. First, you discover a fine PvP server (PvE is boring, huh?). 40/50 players online. You think it's great: more people - more fun. WRONG. Even if the map is big enough, time to time you, naked, with a rock wielded, will meet people willing to kill you and get that precious rock.
Speaking about rocks. Even this starter item has durability and you don't have a chance to, say, find it anywhere. Also it's the only way for interacting with the surroundings in earlygame. So you have an only one chance to get at least a stone hatchet. ♥♥♥♥ balance, go for the nearest tree, count hits, run like about a mile, smash stones and pray you'll not get wrecked by some of 24/7 playing people.
Fine, you managed to get a hatchet. Now you have to build your base. Stop, how do you suppose to lock it? Sure you have to craft a lock (codelock preferred). But you'll need a blueprint for it. Fine. For a lock you have to get some metal fragments. How will you get them? From the furnace! How will you get a furnace? You will need to get some rocks and a LOW GRADE FUEL. It is made from animal fat, so you'll have to hunt for it. Animals are bugged in Rust so forget about melee weapons. Get a bow and some arrows. Where? Again you'll need recipes for them. But bow is crafted from cloth which is also got from animals. Devil's circle, huh? No. At this point you start to hunt for ♥♥♥♥ing BARRELS. Starter recipes and loot are there. In earlygame you're not supposed to get them from Radtown so you have to run like a retard all over the map hunting for barrels. If you're lucky enough you'll get everything needed for a simple twig house in 2-5 hours.
Spent a whole day gathering stuff, built a fine stone house on a top of a rock, not killed by a miracle. You lay down sleeping in your house and, thinking of newly obtained safety, log out. YOU'RE WRONG. 99% probability next day you'll find yourself laying naked on a shore with a rock in your right hand. Your house is looted and smashed into pieces.
Why? F*ck balance, that's why. 24/7 players are f*cking killing machines. You'll never get into Radtown - they constantly secure it. You'll never get airdrops - they're for ones who play in stacks of 5 people all the time. So you'll never get decent recipes, clothing and weapons. "F*ck you, customer", - says Garry and adds ROCKET LAUNCHERS in the game. "F*ck you, Garry", - I say and uninstall this handful of cr*p from my PC.
3/10 - 3 is for people who don't have a life or like constant butthurt. They might like Rust.
