There is a plethora of words that come to mind that do nothing but praise the amazing work that Toby Fox created before us. Unique. Intuitive. Witty. Emotional. Philosophical. Entertaining. Instense. Heart-touching. I could go on.
Undertale, as a sum of its parts, is a well-balanced video game that takes the player on a journey into the Underground, a fantastical but collapsing society of Monsters that want nothing more than to live their lives with freedom and prosperity. Not only are you being told a story, but with every action you make, you shape it. The developer makes it one of the most attracting features of his game. While one gamer might play it aggressively and without heart, another (and most likely all) will take the road less traveled: Pacifism.
I won't go too much into detail to avoid spoilers. This game touched my heart. After playing through the game and achieving the "true" ending, there is little I can say that would fully compensate the outstanding story-telling and direction the developers took. It plays on the aspect that it is all a game, making sure to break the fourth wall at any given moment without much warning. They also make sure to connect the player with the pixelated characters in a way that is undescribable. Maybe it was Sans' witty jokes, Alphys' shyness, or Mettaton's fabulousness... but I felt for these characters. I have a completed game file that I refuse to reset due to the fact I will "lose" the friendships I've created with these fictional characters...
In the end, the story is inspirational. I urge anyone who enjoys a good story to buy this. This is definitely a must buy game for 2015, and I would go to lengths to say every gamer should have this in their library.

I bought this game knowing pretty much nothing about it's premise, but only knowing it was a RPG and was according to a friend of mine Earthbound'ish. To a certain point it is, but I discovered it was so much more than a simple homage to Earthbound.
The game is about a human falling down to the world of monsters, who are banished after a war between humans and monsters. It's your mission to get back to the surface. That's the short summary of the story, but what makes the story and the game special is that you have two options to do it: Kill everyone or spare everyone. The fighting system when you kill is a typical rythm based attack system. If you are doing it as a pascifist, you can use certain act options according to each enemy and spare them, thus never killing them. This also affects all the boss fights in the game. How you do it is up to you.
Usually I normally end up killing enemies in games that gives me the option of either killing or spare them. In this game, I did never want to murder anyone. Not because it gives a good ending, but because the characters in the game are well written. They all have great characteristics and personalities that makes you get very attached to them. I cried both in the peace route and the genocide route for all different reasons.
Not only is the game an great emotional rollercoaster, but the different locations in the game are splendid, the comedy is quirky, weird and fun! Enemy designs are also on point and never gives you a feeling of getting stale or repetive. And the soundtrack..oh god the soundtrack is just amazing. The variety in tunes are amazing. Replayability is also huge because to get the full scoop of the story, characters and secrets, it's higly reccomended to complete the game a few types in different types of run, even though it is painfull doing the genocide run (unless you are a scumbag by nature).
By far is this my game of the year, and I doubt something else will take the throne. Toby Fox did something amazing with this. A name to follow in the future for sure.
Writing this review and hopefully make someone give this game a chance..it fills me with determination.

This game appears to have potential.  At the moment - and since I purchased it a long time ago - it doesn't seem to me that any advances have been made in the games development.  When I started playing it a long time ago it was exciting at first because of all of the promises made by the game and the game that it is based off of - the Arma series mod.  However - upon meeting your first zombie you will realize that this games idea of melee combat is maybe the worst melee combat I have ever experienced in any game.  Period.  You have to aim about a foot over the zombies head in order to make contact with the head - otherwise everything you do will be bodyshots that take forever to knock one down, meanwhile you will be bleeding profusely and have to use up all of your clothes to bandage yourself.  This bandaging feature is cool - if you only had to use it when you actually screwed up and not because the game is awful.  As for looting - that is pretty much the only fun part of the game.  Searching around the map for empty homes and warehouses and apartment buildings in the dark with only a flashlight - searching for that awesome backpack that more than doubles the size of your inventory.  But unfortunately once you find a few things you really like and actually start enjoying the game - some things happen - mainly you fall 5 feet from something and the game decides that warrants death.  Or you walk into a nice house looking for some items - maybe even find some - and then realize that you can't walk back out of any of the doors.  Or maybe you go to log in to your game and it simply just waits to connect to the host for eternity and never allows you to play in the first place.  I want to LOVE this game.  I really want this game to be my next favorite game.  But I reallyyyyyyy don't feel that ANY development or changes have been made to the game since I bought it.  Also - I hate how the screen loses color when you get hurt, are tired, are hungry, are thirsty, or really anything besides completely comfortable.  Part of what makes this game awesome is the beautiful landscape and scenery that you are running around in - the mixture of terror and beauty makes it cool - but when no matter what you do you start losing color and the game turns into a black and white blurry mess within 20 minutes of playing - it loses its visual draw.
To the developers - Please spend more time developing this game on PC and less time developing it for consoles.  It seems like a cash grab unless you can prove otherwise.

When I got this game in early 2014 I thought it would be a great survival. Rust claimed to inherit the best from such giants like DayZ and Minecraft. And it was so until Garry decided to remake the game for Unity.
Let me describe the gameplay of an average daily dose. First, you discover a fine PvP server (PvE is boring, huh?). 40/50 players online. You think it's great: more people - more fun. WRONG. Even if the map is big enough, time to time you, naked, with a rock wielded, will meet people willing to kill you and get that precious rock.
Speaking about rocks. Even this starter item has durability and you don't have a chance to, say, find it anywhere. Also it's the only way for interacting with the surroundings in earlygame. So you have an only one chance to get at least a stone hatchet. ♥♥♥♥ balance, go for the nearest tree, count hits, run like about a mile, smash stones and pray you'll not get wrecked by some of 24/7 playing people.
Fine, you managed to get a hatchet. Now you have to build your base. Stop, how do you suppose to lock it? Sure you have to craft a lock (codelock preferred). But you'll need a blueprint for it. Fine. For a lock you have to get some metal fragments. How will you get them? From the furnace! How will you get a furnace? You will need to get some rocks and a LOW GRADE FUEL. It is made from animal fat, so you'll have to hunt for it. Animals are bugged in Rust so forget about melee weapons. Get a bow and some arrows. Where? Again you'll need recipes for them. But bow is crafted from cloth which is also got from animals. Devil's circle, huh? No. At this point you start to hunt for ♥♥♥♥ing BARRELS. Starter recipes and loot are there. In earlygame you're not supposed to get them from Radtown so you have to run like a retard all over the map hunting for barrels. If you're lucky enough you'll get everything needed for a simple twig house in 2-5 hours.
Spent a whole day gathering stuff, built a fine stone house on a top of a rock, not killed by a miracle. You lay down sleeping in your house and, thinking of newly obtained safety, log out. YOU'RE WRONG. 99% probability next day you'll find yourself laying naked on a shore with a rock in your right hand. Your house is looted and smashed into pieces.
Why? F*ck balance, that's why. 24/7 players are f*cking killing machines. You'll never get into Radtown - they constantly secure it. You'll never get airdrops - they're for ones who play in stacks of 5 people all the time. So you'll never get decent recipes, clothing and weapons. "F*ck you, customer", - says Garry and adds ROCKET LAUNCHERS in the game. "F*ck you, Garry", - I say and uninstall this handful of cr*p from my PC.
3/10 - 3 is for people who don't have a life or like constant butthurt. They might like Rust.

**UPDATE NOV. 2016: I Have Nominated This Game for The Steam Awards: "I'm Not Crying, There's Something In My Eye" Award. This is a game that I expected to be a simple RPG that hit me hard emotionally by the ending. If any game I have ever played deserved this award, it would be UNDERTALE.**
TL:DR
Like Earthbound? Play Undertale!
Like JRPGs? Play Undertale!
Like Dogs? Pet Them! Er, I mean, Play Undertale!
On to the Review:
Undertale was not interesting to me at first. First glance: the graphics of the game, indie dev I never heard of, I initially ignored this game. Then I heard rumors about it: rumors that you don't have to kill anyone; that it had really good music; that it was just downright fun. So I finally gave Undertale a shot, and enjoyed it thourghly. This game made me tear up; it made me laugh at my screen; and it got me thinking after I was done playing.
What I Did Like:
--This music is just great. Arguably the music is what puts Undertale over the top. Even if it's going retro for the sound and feel: the quality of the music is great.
--The Choose-Your-Path story. You can go full-on pacifist, kill what you need, or kill everything you see. This time, it matters.
--I liked nearly every character in the game and was sad to not to see more of thier dialogue.
--I'm not a bullet-hell gamer, not my taste: but Undertale put it in a framework I really enjoyed. Made me want to give bullet-hells a chance.
What I Didn't Like:
--This game is short, in my playthru I racked up about 11 hrs, which is longer than the average. This left me wanting to play much more. Though, this is less about feeling the story was unfinished but more that I wanted to keep playing.
--I wished the puzzles were harder or as intriging as the story: but, the puzzles are really simple and don't take much thought to solve. I appriciate a game that doesn't have MYST-level of frustrating or tedious puzzles: but too easy means I barely care about them.
What Others Might Not Like:
--Retro asthetic won't be for everyone.
--Child traversing a strange place may be a tale you feel played enough of.
--Tone Shifts may be jarring for some.
Overall:
Would I recommend this ~$10 simple, funny, scary, JRPG-inspired game? Absolutely. Sure it's short, the puzzles are simple, and the retro might not be for you: but this is an interesting experience worth playing through. Get it full price for sure!

If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

**UPDATE NOV. 2016: I Have Nominated This Game for The Steam Awards: "I'm Not Crying, There's Something In My Eye" Award. This is a game that I expected to be a simple RPG that hit me hard emotionally by the ending. If any game I have ever played deserved this award, it would be UNDERTALE.**
TL:DR
Like Earthbound? Play Undertale!
Like JRPGs? Play Undertale!
Like Dogs? Pet Them! Er, I mean, Play Undertale!
On to the Review:
Undertale was not interesting to me at first. First glance: the graphics of the game, indie dev I never heard of, I initially ignored this game. Then I heard rumors about it: rumors that you don't have to kill anyone; that it had really good music; that it was just downright fun. So I finally gave Undertale a shot, and enjoyed it thourghly. This game made me tear up; it made me laugh at my screen; and it got me thinking after I was done playing.
What I Did Like:
--This music is just great. Arguably the music is what puts Undertale over the top. Even if it's going retro for the sound and feel: the quality of the music is great.
--The Choose-Your-Path story. You can go full-on pacifist, kill what you need, or kill everything you see. This time, it matters.
--I liked nearly every character in the game and was sad to not to see more of thier dialogue.
--I'm not a bullet-hell gamer, not my taste: but Undertale put it in a framework I really enjoyed. Made me want to give bullet-hells a chance.
What I Didn't Like:
--This game is short, in my playthru I racked up about 11 hrs, which is longer than the average. This left me wanting to play much more. Though, this is less about feeling the story was unfinished but more that I wanted to keep playing.
--I wished the puzzles were harder or as intriging as the story: but, the puzzles are really simple and don't take much thought to solve. I appriciate a game that doesn't have MYST-level of frustrating or tedious puzzles: but too easy means I barely care about them.
What Others Might Not Like:
--Retro asthetic won't be for everyone.
--Child traversing a strange place may be a tale you feel played enough of.
--Tone Shifts may be jarring for some.
Overall:
Would I recommend this ~$10 simple, funny, scary, JRPG-inspired game? Absolutely. Sure it's short, the puzzles are simple, and the retro might not be for you: but this is an interesting experience worth playing through. Get it full price for sure!

I first heard of the game not long after completing LISA: The Painful (another great game that is heavily influenced by Earthbound's charm), and knowing how positive the reviews were, I decided to add it to my wishlist.
I finally bought it a few days before Halloween, and started playing it without expecting too much. I played and played, and It turns out that I ended up not doing anything at all on Halloween: no party, no hanging out with friends, little to no interactions with relatives due to the immersive attraction of the game's unique style.
Was it worth it?
Hell yes.
Every second of it. The game felt fresh all the way through; every area felt unique as well as the soundtrack that fitted those places. The music really did add enough ambiance to make you feel you're part of the mystical environment, and it succeeded in making the game feel more compelling when comparing it to watching today's best films. The quirky humour entertains the player between serious plot elements and they add up as memorable moments that we can remember and reference to even years after playing the game.
The game's highlight, for me at least, was the battle mechanic. Not only can you fight the monsters you face, but you can also converse with them too. It adds new depths of storytelling within combat, and the best part is how you have the ability to dodge your enemy's attacks when it's their turns, like a bullet-hell. I've seen quick-time events in battles (Paper Mario), nonsensical humour to balance out serious plotlines (Earthbound), avoiding obstacles in bullet hells (Touhou), Close-eyed protagonists (Yume-Nikki), and for sure many more games whose elements I've seen in Undertale.
-- Spoilers --
Playing Undertale without knowing anything in advance made me think of traditional RPGs where all monsters were to be fought and killed, therefore I killed everything on the way. I realized how foolish I was when I found out upon arriving at the very end of the journey that Killing. Is. Bad. I had twice the fun when I played a second time, and it's when I realized how much more content there was left to find.
It is for sure my game of the year, even knowing we're at the last few months.
The thought that someone somewhere might play this great game, it fills you with DETERMINATION.

When I got this game in early 2014 I thought it would be a great survival. Rust claimed to inherit the best from such giants like DayZ and Minecraft. And it was so until Garry decided to remake the game for Unity.
Let me describe the gameplay of an average daily dose. First, you discover a fine PvP server (PvE is boring, huh?). 40/50 players online. You think it's great: more people - more fun. WRONG. Even if the map is big enough, time to time you, naked, with a rock wielded, will meet people willing to kill you and get that precious rock.
Speaking about rocks. Even this starter item has durability and you don't have a chance to, say, find it anywhere. Also it's the only way for interacting with the surroundings in earlygame. So you have an only one chance to get at least a stone hatchet. ♥♥♥♥ balance, go for the nearest tree, count hits, run like about a mile, smash stones and pray you'll not get wrecked by some of 24/7 playing people.
Fine, you managed to get a hatchet. Now you have to build your base. Stop, how do you suppose to lock it? Sure you have to craft a lock (codelock preferred). But you'll need a blueprint for it. Fine. For a lock you have to get some metal fragments. How will you get them? From the furnace! How will you get a furnace? You will need to get some rocks and a LOW GRADE FUEL. It is made from animal fat, so you'll have to hunt for it. Animals are bugged in Rust so forget about melee weapons. Get a bow and some arrows. Where? Again you'll need recipes for them. But bow is crafted from cloth which is also got from animals. Devil's circle, huh? No. At this point you start to hunt for ♥♥♥♥ing BARRELS. Starter recipes and loot are there. In earlygame you're not supposed to get them from Radtown so you have to run like a retard all over the map hunting for barrels. If you're lucky enough you'll get everything needed for a simple twig house in 2-5 hours.
Spent a whole day gathering stuff, built a fine stone house on a top of a rock, not killed by a miracle. You lay down sleeping in your house and, thinking of newly obtained safety, log out. YOU'RE WRONG. 99% probability next day you'll find yourself laying naked on a shore with a rock in your right hand. Your house is looted and smashed into pieces.
Why? F*ck balance, that's why. 24/7 players are f*cking killing machines. You'll never get into Radtown - they constantly secure it. You'll never get airdrops - they're for ones who play in stacks of 5 people all the time. So you'll never get decent recipes, clothing and weapons. "F*ck you, customer", - says Garry and adds ROCKET LAUNCHERS in the game. "F*ck you, Garry", - I say and uninstall this handful of cr*p from my PC.
3/10 - 3 is for people who don't have a life or like constant butthurt. They might like Rust.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Ok, so this game is in Alpha, but its been in Alpha for along time, so this is not an excuse.
1) They removed zombies, I am ok with that, some might not be.
2) When the server has been reset, the game plays great
3) When the server has been played on for 24 hours, it will bring the mightiest rig to its knees, expect 1- 20 fps, 30 if your lucky,making mass gun fights impossible without enourmous FPS lag.
4) People and npcs lag around the map, making it hard to carry out any kind of combat, like disapearing and reappearing 30m away.
5) Alt-tab or minimizing the game in a window or fullscreen creates graphical problems requiring a restart, I am sure it will be fixed.
6) Random crashes to desktop and also can freeze your entire PC, making you need a hard reset.
7) The game is fun, when all of the above issues are not affecting you.
8) You need to play with a group of friends or don't expect to raid anyone, creating enough mats for raiding or raiding alone is nearly impossible.
9) There are plenty of immature griefers, and the occasional cheaters, but they have done a good job preventing cheaters in this new rust.
10)Find a good server with a good admin, the offical servers have no admins and they are ruined after 24 hours of being reset.

Ive played around 600 hours on both Legacy and "New Rust" and I think its safe to say (with a couple of other Open world survival games) That Rust is the best Hands Down.
Pros:
+ PvP is Good, Fun and Intresting.
+ Building is good allowing players to make unique bases.
+ Fun is general always have you on something.
+ Solo can be just as destructive as a group of 4 players.
+ Raids are Good fun Solo or grouped.
+ Updated frequently

Inbetweens:
= The community is alright ( Ik alot of people will hate on me for saying this but not all people kos in my experience)
Cons:

- Can be hard to run if your PC isnt as "high end" you cant run this with a potato.
- Hackers (Its hard to run into these guys but most big servers have one in the biggest clan you can kill them)
- Even with a "high end" PC you can still experience lag in gunfights (sometimes proving fatal)
- On big servers like Rustopia and Offiical servers if you dont have a group it can be impossible to build up ( Thankfully you can go to community servers and type in solo in the search bar for a servers with groups only as big as three people)
- End game gives you nothing but raids, helis and airdrops to do which is still fun but I wish there was more.
Overall I recommend this game to you as it is really fun and can be a even better game as they update it so frequently

Firstly, I do think that 'Dayz' as an experience is unlike anything else that exists in terms of an immersive heart-racing survival experience, but that positive extends beyond Dayz standalone and over to Dayz the free mod for ARMA 2.
As it stands currently, this game just isn't fun. It offers (in my opinion) an inferior experience to that of the mod. The mod has very dedicated teams and server admins which provide hugely superior features and content such as working vehicles of multiple types, base building, trading, currency sytems, custom maps and much much more.
It seems like all we get with DayZ standalone are promises that we hope the devs keep. This is part of early access obviously but I can't help but feel that this game and all it's clunky bone-breaking, easily hacked, badly netcoded game will fail to meet expectations after first hearing that this was transitioning from a mod into a 'standalone' game.
Part of the whole reason this game was converted into a standalone product (according to Dean Hall) was to do things that simply couldn't be done with the mod due to limitations with the engine. Now, over a year later we are still experiencing huge game-breaking bugs that are due to the SAME engine. Being buggy is fine within the context of it being an early access title but I can't help but feel that some of the justification for moving it to a stand alone game was false.
I still have hope for DayZ but I think the inability of BI 'striking while the iron is hot' will lead to superior survival games emerging with a better game engine and more talented development teams that really nail the experience. I hope I'm wrong as this game has huge potential but in it's current state, it can't be recommended.

Firstly, I do think that 'Dayz' as an experience is unlike anything else that exists in terms of an immersive heart-racing survival experience, but that positive extends beyond Dayz standalone and over to Dayz the free mod for ARMA 2.
As it stands currently, this game just isn't fun. It offers (in my opinion) an inferior experience to that of the mod. The mod has very dedicated teams and server admins which provide hugely superior features and content such as working vehicles of multiple types, base building, trading, currency sytems, custom maps and much much more.
It seems like all we get with DayZ standalone are promises that we hope the devs keep. This is part of early access obviously but I can't help but feel that this game and all it's clunky bone-breaking, easily hacked, badly netcoded game will fail to meet expectations after first hearing that this was transitioning from a mod into a 'standalone' game.
Part of the whole reason this game was converted into a standalone product (according to Dean Hall) was to do things that simply couldn't be done with the mod due to limitations with the engine. Now, over a year later we are still experiencing huge game-breaking bugs that are due to the SAME engine. Being buggy is fine within the context of it being an early access title but I can't help but feel that some of the justification for moving it to a stand alone game was false.
I still have hope for DayZ but I think the inability of BI 'striking while the iron is hot' will lead to superior survival games emerging with a better game engine and more talented development teams that really nail the experience. I hope I'm wrong as this game has huge potential but in it's current state, it can't be recommended.

Rust is an interesting concept. Garry and the team at Facepunch have done right by the community in revamping the game and really putting a ton of effort into it.
From my perspective, I think the game looks great, runs much better, and has some cool mechanics. Aside from those points, I really cannot say this is a good game. It simply requires too much time - and no matter how much time you're spending on it - someone else is spending more time than you. It's a neverending circlejerk.
You spawn with a rock and a torch and you have to build up from there. Maybe you make a small hut the first night. Let's just say you wait 2 days between the time you made that small hut and you log in again to continue your progression. Guess what? Your hut is gone and you've been killed. This doesn't just apply to new players - you constantly have to restart because there's always someone who will be on when you're offline.
Rust players will tell you "build on a rock" or "hide your base". Well yeah, that works, except you have to bascially use game breaking stuff to do the first part. People will climb huge rocks by using foundations ( a building element) and then deleting them. As for hiding, some people find cheaty ways to make their houses in a rock or use indestructable stuff to surround it with.
I would love to recommend this game, it has a lot of TLC put into it. But I can't. At its core, it has an awful community and it's impossible to step away from it for a day or two and come back. If you don't mind being attached at the hip to one game every day, then get it. Otherwise, stay away, because this game will just be a huge waste of time and source of anger.

I bought this game nearly a year ago, the day it was released. I absolutely loved the mod and was interested in seeing where this game was going.  The first thing I noticed was the game was buggy. Obviously I expected this, as it CLEARLY says everywhere in the game and on the steam page. Things like zombies killing me through walls were issues I had expirienced in the mod, but given the resources of an actual development company, real progress could be made towards a more polished game.
One year later, the zombies still kill me through walls.  Yes, I understand what "Alpha" means, but do the developers?
On May 1st of this year, Dayz sold its 2 millionth copy. Disregarding any sales and distribution fees, that means that the developers have brought in 60 million dollars.  Yeah, thats a six with TEN zeroes behind it.
They have had 7 months and 60 million bucks and they can't even fix the biggest game breaking bugs like the zombies going through walls???
Let me put it another way, if Dayz were a country, it would be ranked right after the Falkland Islands in GDP. And they still cant fix the most basic of problems??
I can produce no feasible reason why Dayz has been updated and filled with thousands of trivial items and  mechanics before they have at least made decent progress addressing the severe underlying problems with the game. The priorites of this game's development are absolutely absurd and completely tangential to any gaming industry norm. While I do find some of these features amusing, such as being able the read the entire "New Testament" as an in-game book; I would feel much more satisfied if I wasnt reading it to pass the time while I wait for my character to die of starvation after I spawned inside of an inaccessible building with not way out.
I sincerely hope this game is eventually "finished", but due to the amount of missed deadlines, lack of features, and almost zero MEANINGFUL progress of this game. I do not recomend this game to anyone who does not enjoy it in it's current state.  As the saying goes "The best predictor of future performance is past performance", things do not look bright for Dayz.

Let us look at the game so far, from it's realease till now. On realease it was... Okay. Yes, the game is taking ages to get developed but that's to expect; it's Bohemia Interactive after all...
You're all pretty delusional if you expected a relatively small publisher like BI to spit out a finished game after only a year. Hell, not even Activision and EA with their eight digit development budgets seem to manage something like that.
So far the game is no doubt feature poor but at the same time each feature is far more detailed and of a far higher quality than anything from DayZ mod and its other off-shoots.
Although I barely play DayZ SA (because so far there's ♥♥♥♥ all to do after getting geared) I still think it was the right choice to make SA properly from the ground up instead of filling it with half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥features and call it a day. If they would've gone that route then DayZ SA would've just been the DayZ mod with an additional price tag.
It's not necessarily a bad purchase as it's cheaper the earlier in development you buy it but if you're looking for a zombie survival game you want to play
I'd rather recommend just going the Breaking Point route and buying ArmA 3 instead.
You not only get a more feature packed zombie survival game but also everything else ArmA 3 has to offer; anything from handcrafted mil-sim missions to large scale PVP fights in CTI Warfare/KOTH to picking apples for money in the GTA Online styled
Altis Life.
There's just not enough meaningful gameplay features in DayZ currently to recommend it.

Seeing as it is early access I am going to avoid talking about the horrible amount of bugs and focus on core elements of the game. The game is open world zombie game where you start with basically nothing and have to scavenge to find items to help you survive. The world map is rather large and full of places to explore. However, all the locations look very similar and many of the building are just copy and pastes of other buildings. This can be really disappointing when you spent the last 10 minutes just running towards this location. That brings me to my other point, the phrase walking simulator gets thrown around a lot lately but I think no other game is quiet deserving of that title quiet as much as Dayz. You will find yourself running to building to building, running to woods to woods, running to city to city until your finger starts to bleed.
Another problem I have with the game is just how broken the controls feel. You feel so clunky when playing this game, no matter how much I put up my sensitivity it still feels very slow and forced. There is also a noticeable delay between pressing a key and the action happening, it’s not a huge delay but you feel it more than you see it. This problem is most noticeable when using the jump, prone and crouch commands, sometimes they just don’t want to work.
The game is said to be good if you play it with a group of friends but that does not make a good game. I enjoy watching really bad movies with friends, it does not make it a good movie. The problem with this game is the developers keep trying to add more things to an overall broken game. What they should try and do is focus on strengthen the elements of the game they have in first then build up from that.

The concept is great: Survival in a post-apocalyptic landscape with limited resources. Starting off naked with just a rock and a torch and working your way up from there. The graphics are nice and the gameplay feels challenging and exciting. The possibility of death is always near, be it in the form of other players and wild animals. So far so good.
Sadly, many factors make this game an unenjoyable experience for me overall:
- The game has severe framedrops which makes it near impossible to hunt animals and makes even the most mundane    tasks frustrating.
- Advanced players with rifles continuously kill naked starters that only have a rock.
- Resources are incredibly scarce, to the point of frustration. I played for two in-game days without coming across a single stone deposit. Stones are needed to craft even the most basic tools.
-The whole map is completely filled with player built structures. Within hours of a server wipe it becomes virtually impossible to find a place to build a house and call your own, even when walking several hours from your spawn point in a procedurally generated map.
- Russian hackers are everywhere.
Should these issues be addressed, I would love to recommend this game. In the current state however, I simply cannot.

After logging off and back on, all my gear was gone and I was back to my base model.  So the previous hours I had spent gearing up, were just as if they didn't exist.  Ok so one glitch, no big deal, right?  Well after playing for SEVERAL more hours, I happened to stumble across a rifle AND a pistol.  Again, I was ecstatic. The greatest running of all time, Walking Simulator 2013/14...
On a serious note, although Standalone is barely a shell of what the Mod version is I still find it really enjoyable to play. Yes, there are glitches and bugs which will annoy you and I'm not going to use "Its in Alpha" or "Its in Early Access" as an excuse for those, but the problems I've experienced with this game do not even total more than five minutes in terms of time spent dealing with them, which compared to the overal time I've now played this game is miniscule. I agree there isn't enough content at the moment in terms of weapons, vehicles and base construction, but maybe I'm the only person who isn't that bothered...
When playing the game there is always tension in the air, even when you're in the middle of a field in the south-western area of the map where nobody really goes currently. There's always that nagging feeling that although it's only a 40 man server and it's a huge map there could always be a lone wolf crouched behind a tree with the crosshair of their scope on your head while you have no clue that they are there. There is still tension when you think you've come across a friendly player who is quick to say "Hi!", they could be a front to a group of people that you are unaware of who are ready to shoot you down once you let your guard down. When you meet a genuinely nice person you forget all of the issues you've had with other players in the recent past and I've had my fair share of encounters with incredibly funny people who just don't care if they get shot or handcuffed and made fun of. The people who run around tormenting other players who have next to nothing are equally as funny, although mildly annoying. They always fail to realise that they're throwing away their resources and time to, in their minds, annoy someone who will respawn 30 seconds later and probably be a lot closer to their friends anway.
I'm quite a passive player and will generally leave people alone unless provoked or at an airfield. I can't say I've killed many people, but when you pull off 650 metre long-range Mosin shot to someones head while they are looting an ATC tower it is a fantastic feeling, just as much as it is when you only have your fists to defend you against someone with an M4 when the game rewards you with an instant knock-out first punch to enable you to take their weapon before they wake up. Then there's the memorable experience meeting someone in-game who wants to have a rolling race from Nizhnoye to Berizino while some bandits look on in confusion as to why you don't care about them firing shots at you.
Expect occasional glitches, expect a decent number of morons, slow developement progress and fewer weapons and vehicles and you'll know what you're getting in to in comparison to the Mod version. Saying that the Mod is hardly the cream of the crop when it comes to being smooth running and having a friendly userbase either. Taking into consideration the time I've spent playing this vs. the money spent I've not really got much to be negative about. Two distinctly average 21st centuary DVDs lasting maybe a total of four hours, or this game for the same price which offers endless action and amusement with friends; I'd pick this every time without hesitation.

The bottleneck is the spaghetti code within the game engine, which has never be fixed and most probably never will be.
If you're expecting a survival game with a compelling postapocalyptic athmosphere: Well, you should avoid DayZ. Because instead of adding stuff that actually fits into the environment, the devs are obsessed with adding masks from Payday 2, silly hats and unfitting weapons like the Steyr AUG. While this seems to be a minor problem, it just shows once again that the devs absolutely have no base line and common theme.
tldr version: Don't buy. Glitchfest, incompetent devs, significant performance issues which will never be solved, broken game which will most probably never be fixed. Wait for a proper release version, which presumably will come out in 2020. And even then expect it to be broken.
The Alpha excuse is a fallacy. You should also bear in mind that the devs already made bank with this game, while delivering next to nothing.

Essentials: If you purchase this game you're getting an ok game for $20 USD that involves farming, looting, killing, and raiding. There's also frustrations as it is currently in alpha and has been for the past four years with some arguable change. It's definitely had a dramatic face-lift from is first public form-factor, the community has as gotten a major downgrade, and the game has definitely gotten repetitive, increasingly frustrating, and old with the weekly and monthly wipes along with some other issues. I understand frustration might be due to differred interest and entertainment by every player but, I've been playing the entire five years almost and it's only gone downhill. The wipes are of course due to the current state of the game being in alpha but, again it's been four years. Other than the great amount of time they have spent in alpha what matters to me the most is the changes to the game. But, they've only re-done the game by giving it a large facelift and adding some other significant features however, at this point in time all weekly updates are stale and empty of new things. Consider avoiding this game for now unless you found twenty dollars on the ground.
First,
; it hasnt changed much. You hit any tree and get wood and then you hit specific rocks around the map called "nodes". Other than them adding barrels and loot boxes where you can get many things from gear, resources, and components used for crafting.(I'll talk about this later) It's really not that bad how they set it up as on vanilla it works quite well.
Next,
; this topic definitely is near and similar to farming but, they're surprisingly different. Farming resources and looting rad-towns differ in risk and gameplay experience. Looting the rad-towns and landmarks around the map seems fun to explore for the first time yet, it's not worth the risk for most of them. What I've come to find is that looting specific landmarks like harbor. You get rarely any gear and you risk getting killed from many factors including players and no loot. Unless you're looting launch-site don't expect to get anything game changing but, you'll definitely encount large groups of players.(again I'll talk about this later)
Subsequently,
; PVP is defnitely the only way I'd consider playing this game when I see it on the store even though there are RP and PVE servers they're quite under-rated and small population. So, you'll definitely PVP so lets talk about the PVP. Well weapons are definitely unbalanced in their specifications like damage, recoil, spread, and bullet drop. I feel as though every two to three weeks there's at lease two weapons that either get buffed or nerfed in result of poor testing done by the developers. The "Assasult Rifle"(aka AK47) has definitely had many changes done to it and it's currently been buffed to where you get little to no recoil with a silencer. It really confuses me with four years into development and maybe two years with most of the current weapons that they can't figure out this issue.
Final gameplay component,
; raiding is where you can break into someone's base on rust and take their things for your advantage. You'll definitely raid in this game as there's almost no way to advance significantly without doing so. There's different ways to raid for example, you can noob raid with spears and other primitive like tools, use grenades or cheap explosive satchel charges, or lastly get the best gear which includes rockets and C4 to destroy your enemy's base. The decision is yours! This part of the game seems balanced and fun but, they could improve it somehow maybe by changing the way you claim your base and getting on people's bases.
Overall, this game was good and fun in the beginning but now, it's leaving me and some other people in dire disappointment. I still love this game in different ways but, there have been reoccuring issues and frustrations that made me come to writing this negative review. This review is based off of the current state of the game on August 16, 2017. So, I only wrote this review to make others aware that these issues have happened far too long.

Essentials: If you purchase this game you're getting an ok game for $20 USD that involves farming, looting, killing, and raiding. There's also frustrations as it is currently in alpha and has been for the past four years with some arguable change. It's definitely had a dramatic face-lift from is first public form-factor, the community has as gotten a major downgrade, and the game has definitely gotten repetitive, increasingly frustrating, and old with the weekly and monthly wipes along with some other issues. I understand frustration might be due to differred interest and entertainment by every player but, I've been playing the entire five years almost and it's only gone downhill. The wipes are of course due to the current state of the game being in alpha but, again it's been four years. Other than the great amount of time they have spent in alpha what matters to me the most is the changes to the game. But, they've only re-done the game by giving it a large facelift and adding some other significant features however, at this point in time all weekly updates are stale and empty of new things. Consider avoiding this game for now unless you found twenty dollars on the ground.
First,
; it hasnt changed much. You hit any tree and get wood and then you hit specific rocks around the map called "nodes". Other than them adding barrels and loot boxes where you can get many things from gear, resources, and components used for crafting.(I'll talk about this later) It's really not that bad how they set it up as on vanilla it works quite well.
Next,
; this topic definitely is near and similar to farming but, they're surprisingly different. Farming resources and looting rad-towns differ in risk and gameplay experience. Looting the rad-towns and landmarks around the map seems fun to explore for the first time yet, it's not worth the risk for most of them. What I've come to find is that looting specific landmarks like harbor. You get rarely any gear and you risk getting killed from many factors including players and no loot. Unless you're looting launch-site don't expect to get anything game changing but, you'll definitely encount large groups of players.(again I'll talk about this later)
Subsequently,
; PVP is defnitely the only way I'd consider playing this game when I see it on the store even though there are RP and PVE servers they're quite under-rated and small population. So, you'll definitely PVP so lets talk about the PVP. Well weapons are definitely unbalanced in their specifications like damage, recoil, spread, and bullet drop. I feel as though every two to three weeks there's at lease two weapons that either get buffed or nerfed in result of poor testing done by the developers. The "Assasult Rifle"(aka AK47) has definitely had many changes done to it and it's currently been buffed to where you get little to no recoil with a silencer. It really confuses me with four years into development and maybe two years with most of the current weapons that they can't figure out this issue.
Final gameplay component,
; raiding is where you can break into someone's base on rust and take their things for your advantage. You'll definitely raid in this game as there's almost no way to advance significantly without doing so. There's different ways to raid for example, you can noob raid with spears and other primitive like tools, use grenades or cheap explosive satchel charges, or lastly get the best gear which includes rockets and C4 to destroy your enemy's base. The decision is yours! This part of the game seems balanced and fun but, they could improve it somehow maybe by changing the way you claim your base and getting on people's bases.
Overall, this game was good and fun in the beginning but now, it's leaving me and some other people in dire disappointment. I still love this game in different ways but, there have been reoccuring issues and frustrations that made me come to writing this negative review. This review is based off of the current state of the game on August 16, 2017. So, I only wrote this review to make others aware that these issues have happened far too long.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

There's so many things to say I barely know where to start. You might notice I got 900 hours of rust. I know this game since legacy, back when there were still zombies, so I've seen the developement of both the games and Facepunch. 3rd speaking of dev. I'm not gonna compare Legacy with the new Rust, since like people said before, they are kinda 2 different games (altough they are implementing always more stuff from legacy to Rust), so I will speak a bit of both.
Also let me say that I got this game recomended by a RL friend, who said there's a hype about this totally new and innovative game where you have to to survive in a world, eat, craft, hunt and build a house, where there's open PvP, made by a indie company, only catch, its an early access game. I thought I would still give it a try, have fun with my friend and help this company make their goal true, like crowd funding (which I kinda got to regret later). He stopped playing after a couple days.
Game developement itself:
Why is there even 2 versions of Rust? Because the original Rust (Legacy, new rust is just Rust) is a mess, engine and performance-wise. When Facepunch realized that the very foundations were crap, the best solution was to restart and do it right from the beginning instead of reprogramm everything. Rust has and always had troubles with bugs and performance, while graphically not being that impressive, specially in legacy. While the new rust definetively looks much better and can look great in full graphics, dont let the screenshots fool you, its still no skyrim like many ppl like to say, and noone plays like that as the fps drops to an unplayable state. I still always read from people with supercomps that get low fps and lags. Cheaters is another common problem specially in legacy. While they tried to fix that in Rust with EAC (EasyAntiCheat) which indeed did help at first (always more hackers find their way in), it also added half-dozen problems like EAC: DIsconnect, which added to the other half dozen problems of the game itself like some people getting black screen or others not finding server list, made alot of people not be able to play new Rust (me included) till recently and some still not to this day.It is really only recently that the game has become somewhat stable and playable, altough performance still lets wishes open, and usually for every change or fix, there come 3 new bugs which sometimes are released from dev test server even when obviously bugged. And they have changed the whole system so many times one would think they dont even know what they want, which direction they are heading, but it only keeps changing, not evolving (much atleast).Now I perfectly know this is still an EA game and in alpha, far from finished, but alot of people put alot of money in this game, and consindering how they handle developement, their attitude, and after all this time, one cant help but be disappointed in this game and company that call themself hobbysts while having made millions of an alpha game, often not listening to the suggestions of the people but implementing unnecessary stuff noone asked for.
Game itself:
Rust used to be something kinda new (only to be compared with DayZ that time I think) that, altough it originally had zombies (which got replaced later by red animals), is mainly caveman themed, with the radiated towns the only hint of some lost modern society, where your goal is to survive. But while one thinks this is kinda a fallout online, its just mainly a PvP game where you walk alot, because there's not much else to do after having built your fortress and having gotten all weapon and C4. Now while I had my share portion of fun in this game by creeping people in their houses at night with predator sounds (this game LIVES from voice chat and would be dullier than usual without) and laser sight, playing both alone and in groups, playing both pacifically and as raiding bandit, after building a base, getting raided, rebuilding, raiding, server wiped, building, raiding etc and repeating this process a hundred times (if you can't handle people bullying you and robbing/wasting your resources and time, dont play this, many people will backstab you), you can't help but feel this game needs much more to keep it interesting. While the thrill of the hunt (or being hunted while full of loot) can be exciting and make your heart race, there are so many other promising survival games that look better, are more interesting or devs work faster ( zombie survivals, dino surivals, mutant survival. I specially am interested in the co-op PvE of The Forest other EA games coming out, PvE in Rust is just kindergarten). So unless you like being a bandit, murdering and robbing other players, destroying their house and progress, eat their corpse and are ok with people doing the same to you, then I don't recommend paying for this game.
Now with all this said, since I cant sell or trade the game, I'll keep playing it from time to time, hoping that maybe in late future the game will finally be completed. Or until I completely loose hope and C4 it.
Update1: They added now Rocket Launcher. A fun addition, but that means the game becomes even more PvP and less survival. Now newbies and casual games will only "survive"  12 hours instead of 24 hours. Alot of other people complaining about this too saying it becomes Battlefield/CoD.
If you're looking for PvP, play CoD. If you're looking to build, play minecraft. Survive? The Forest.
Looking to troll? Buy Rust.
-Did a little research, just found out the probable cause of all the signs disappearing. It seems like Rust saves every sign, at every stage of the painting, on everyone's local computer folder, resulting in everyone on the server having several versions of everyone's signs.
Update2: Ok I'd like to start with some people blaming me for A) giving an EA game a bad review and B) giving bad review after 1000 hours. A) Yeah its EA. Its been for 2 years. I think that gives me the right to criticize it honestly and fairly. B) yeah it took me 1000 hours and 2 years to come to this conclusion and be able to give a fair review about its developement and features. Oh and btw, how do YOU know if I had fun in all those 1000 hours? Do you realize half of that is AFK crafting and much boring farming???
Now to the updates: the last 10 updates were mainly more PvP and gunz and ammo updates. Only 2 real good things were implemented: Farming crops and female characters (atm only for admins). Oh and some PvE server command that I dont know what good it does. Aside from these 2-3 changes, the rest has been PvP changes. Sure, I guess its nice to have incendiary ammo, but WHERE is the SURVIVAL in that? The survival aspect in this game is the PvP. PvE is still a piece of cake. And unless you got a big active international clan going, you will most probably get raided. Now if Rust intends to be a Troll vs Troll game, thats fine with me, after all they did warn us that game content could change anytime. But please, don't sell it as a "survival" game then if its just a big-map-running PvP game, because that's what the (OLD) trailer is basically telling us what Rust is. I thought I was buying sometihng in the lines of "The Forest" or "Savage Lands" but they removed Zombies and Mutants and you only got players to fight now cause else you bore very quick. I will admit thought, the game's got slightly better in those years since its first steam release.
That is my veridict. If you're a sadomaso and into trolling people and getting revenge this might be your game, else, stay far away from it. This is probably also my last update.
Oh btw, maybe you find this more helpful: Got raided, got mad, went bazinga and got revenge by making whole servers go rage-quit. 3/10 wouldn't do again. (sarcasm intended)

Trying to review this game is like trying to explain the intricate details of Area 51.  Even if you get inside, you won't live long enough to see anything of worth.
And that's the problem here.  I have spent more than an hour attempting to play this game.  However, I never was able to get anything more than the rock that you start with.  Some of this is due to the game's interface itself.  There is no tutorial. No objective. And no way to refer to game controls from within the game to find out what does what.
For most single-player games, this would not be an issue and is sometimes a great strength of "exploration" style games. Much of the fun is finding your way in a barren world, learning to survive on your own.
However, this is NOT a single-player game. This is a game world populated by hundreds of young boys whose only apparent goal in life is to slaughter any new player that dared to purchase Rust.  You will not survive.  The moment you find something interesting to look at or try to craft, you will lose it all because some little brat with his junk hanging out has smashed your head in with a rock.  You lose everything and must start over.
So, do I recommend this?  No.  Not until the developers include a way to at least learn the controls and the crafting systems PRIOR to throwing you to the wolves.

This game is in the process of being revamped.  The developers are really only guilty of taking their time and doing things the right way, despite the venom they receive from the community this is a labor of love from the guys who pioneered the genre.
Is this the game I have been looking for in its current form?  Hell no...but they have shown dedication and persistence in constantly adding pieces to the game.  After playing 5-6 hours with each of the last 5 or 6 updates I am pleased with the progress and excited for the final playable game.  And the new engine hasn't even been deployed yet.  This will likely be the standard by which the genre is defined eventually.  But still, all of that is speculation, purchasing it early (because I'm impatient and patient at the same time) was a gamble, but I think it was pretty good one.  Just don't buy this game and expect the whole kit-and-kaboodle at the moment.  The mod is far more fleshed out at this point, but this will overtake and surpass at some point in the next 6-18 months I'm fairly certain.

DayZ is honeslty one of my all-time favorite survival games (notice I didn't say MMO) and I downright enjoy it. With that being said there ARE problems. Whether playing the game or reading most of the negative reviews, you'll see that. BUT, in my opinion, these are problems a game in ALPHA would probably foster.
Pro: This is an amazing game. Hands-down. The world is beautiful, expanisve, and filled (sort of) with towns, cities, and villages alike. Now, I don't know if I'm allowed to mention other games here, but if you're unhappy with this game, may i suggest WarZ- I mean Infestation: Survivor Stories. If you don't like glitching zombies and their buggy AI, go enjoy Infestation: Survivor Stories, where you'll meet even worse zombies and the usuall hacker. Now, back onto topic, DayZ IS INCREDIBLE. I got lost after leaving Svetlojarsk, wandered the countryside for 3 hours, and still managed to have an exceptional experience. It gives me the option to play hardcore (first-person), or regular (first and third-person). I've run into good and bad people, both of which have made the game amazingly interactive, and have experienced starvation, sickness, and border-line hypothermia all in one character who's still alive. Basically, if you want THE zombie-pvp-interaction game, DayZ if your best choice, and if you want to wait for further development, then that is PERFECTLY FINE, there's no reason not to be cautious. Just like in the game, the choice is yours to make.
Cons: Theres obvious problems. I could just slam a list down, but you might have read other negative reviews and kinda get the sense. MY BIGGEST problem is the zombie AI, and its not because its simply a problem, but I haven't seen any notes or logs about fixing it, which concerns me. I'm not saying I'm upset with the developers, but I simply would like to know whether or not I can look forward to actually going through a town unseen by a zombie a half-mile away. That's my biggest problem, and others have their's. PvP is somewhat of a limbo land, stuck between actual firefights and being killed through a wall. I've been through both, so essentially, try to watch out for people. All-in-all, there's going to be problems, even in the blockbuster games that are DONE in development (Battlefield 4 or Grand Theft Auto online anyone?) but these problems WILL (most likely) be fixed, and as I said before, waiting for more development and bug-fixes is understandable.
DayZ is a tremendous game with some bugs that DO make it hard to play. But being in Alpha even almost a year after, it's an amazing experience, and I recommend it to all my friends. So, basically, enjoy the beautful landscape, watch out for annoying out not game-breaking bugs, and experience the interactions you'll have with friends, others, and yourself.
If I was going with an IGN rating, it'd be 7.5.
+Amazing and beautful world
+Experiences (good or bad)
+That survivor feeling
-Awful and annoying bugs
-PvP needs a fixing

Trying to review this game is like trying to explain the intricate details of Area 51.  Even if you get inside, you won't live long enough to see anything of worth.
And that's the problem here.  I have spent more than an hour attempting to play this game.  However, I never was able to get anything more than the rock that you start with.  Some of this is due to the game's interface itself.  There is no tutorial. No objective. And no way to refer to game controls from within the game to find out what does what.
For most single-player games, this would not be an issue and is sometimes a great strength of "exploration" style games. Much of the fun is finding your way in a barren world, learning to survive on your own.
However, this is NOT a single-player game. This is a game world populated by hundreds of young boys whose only apparent goal in life is to slaughter any new player that dared to purchase Rust.  You will not survive.  The moment you find something interesting to look at or try to craft, you will lose it all because some little brat with his junk hanging out has smashed your head in with a rock.  You lose everything and must start over.
So, do I recommend this?  No.  Not until the developers include a way to at least learn the controls and the crafting systems PRIOR to throwing you to the wolves.

Let me tell you a story everyone, I was playing this game with a friend I recently introduce to Rust, and we had a fairly decent thing going. large 4 story stone house, with code locks on ever door to each floor, enough resources that we didn't have to leave the house and we could focus on building weapons, more floors and storage space etc. then on the same day we came into the server, we had a player at our door knocking, we thought nothing of it and left him alone but he got more aggressive, it started with him knocking more frequently and then started hitting the door with a hatchet, and then after a minute or so we hear MULTIPLE hatchets at our door, there was 3 men inside our home now but we left it because we had an armoured code locked door on every floor up from there so we left it be, but then they ended up getting through every single door we had, they were all locked and not one explosion went off for us to hear, they mowed down my friend with their multiple assault rifles and came for me, I had taken a shotgun from one of the crates we had ealier and headed ot the top floor, one of the men went up the stairs and I shot him multiple times with my shotgun and he fell dead, then a second man came, and the same thing happened, I then went down the stairs and finished off the third, as it turned out afterwards however, those players were a handful of the server admins and so both me and my friend were banned from that server, Rust is a very unsporting game if you enter the wrong server and you do have to spend a lot of your time to learn the ropes and what to do and what not to do, but once you get yourself on a steady way of playing and are living long enough to get a lot of resources and space in your home, it is an amazing game and I 100% reccomend this game, it is definately worth the £15 despite being in alpha as the developers are updating the game frequently and sizeably, just make sure that if you don't think you could defend yourself you join a noob friendly server or non-pvp one, Rust is great, but like most things, it depends on who you play with :)

DayZ in a nutshell: Spend 4 hours running around trying on hats followed by 20 seconds of sheer hand trembling terror followed by a black screen reading "You are dead." Cracking!

As much as I enjoyed bits and pieces of this game, I must say that this game is huge a disappointment so far in its development. I know most of you are going to say "This game is in alpha, what do you expect". The only reason anybody bought this game is because of the Mod ( I bought the standalone within the first 15 minutes of its release) assuming It would be everything the Mod never was.
If you are still planning to buy this game don't. Not yet anyway. All that is going to happen is that you are going to get disappointed and sick of it after a while of playing. There are many other alternatives to this game that are much better and are developing at a faster rate than this game ever did, two of which I'm thinking of getting are H1Z1 or Miscreated.
Mark my words. Don't waste your money on an incomplete product that is going to be outdated and forgotten by the time it is complete.

I would not recommend this game to someone I hated. I really want to like it and keep going back to it after quitting to check up, but I'm always reminded soon after why I quit. A lot of people say it will never be finished and I have to agree. They're making different hats, shoes, and jackets, but you will still die by magically running off a roof even though a second ago you were safely climbing down a latter. You'll spend hours looting, then crouch near a stairway and slide down to your death. I've witnessed people dying just by logging out and I've lost characters after (as the always are) unexpected server reboots. It was funny to see these things happen on youtube when the game was first released on steam. Now it is absolutely pathetic. I'm starting to think this is a HUGE scam.
Bottom line: The developers seem to try and satisfy players with useless, broken items while they take literally years to work out basic functionality. Will most likely not finish the game before better free games come out.

Very enjoyable, but only to a certain extent. A fantastic concept, but a very difficult one to deliver. The world is massive and deeply detailed (save for a few trees in the middle of roads), and graphically the game is up to standard. The survival/needs aspect is rather well done as well. Not very realistic, but still provides a sense of surivial and urgency when you are running low.
The player interactions are variable. Because of the overwhelming amount of banditing in the game, people are paranoid and seldom will trust you if they have weapons. It's unfortuanate, because as the game progresses, more and more cooperation between players will be required. If people cannot find it in them the trust each other, the game wont be able to be enjoyed. I personally have found that announcing yourself, and making yourself visible will increase the likelyhood of the other players not shooting you. That being said, it is still damn likely that they will.
Overall, the bugs are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥and have not been dealt with as swiftly as they should have been. The game is far from complete, but is definitely worth atleast trying it. I am sure that in the future the game will be what it advertises as, but for now, it is still an incomplete yet fun survival game.

Upon yet another game restart and connection to a different server, I finally managed to play the game, only to realize I haven't a clue what I'm doing - regardless of the fact I still couldn't read any text onscreen, there is absolutely no assistance or guide to what you're supposed to do, no direction, nothing - Still I haven't got a clue, so I instead just ran around for a good 15 minutes looking at the scenery and trying to figure out what the blob of text that appeared at the bottom left of the screen every few seconds actually meant.
Bugs and lack of guide aside, the games graphics and environmental details are superb. I imagine the game in a more stable state and possibly a tutorial of some sort or even just first-time tips for new players, would make this game excellent, but due to the terrible experiences I had and the high cost of this game, I would not recommend it for the price offered. I may come back and edit this review at a later stage of the games development, but for now I do not believe this game is worthy of its price tag.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Leaving a review for both parts of the game.
TLDR: two games for the price of one, hell yeah! (Quit complaining oldies. Sincerely, a fellow oldie.)
Rust Legacy review: Perfect for nostalgia, not so perfect for actual playing. The servers are far too unpopulated for my liking, but if that's your thing than it could still be a great game. The gunplay and fighting in general is definitely more intense in the Old Rust, however since hackers flooded into the game it's hard for people (myself included) to not call hacks at times. This game is honestly amazing IMHO. 10/10 would reccomend Naked Man Rock Smash Bros. to anyone. I could an entire game on this day and still have a great time.
New(Current) Rust: If you played Legacy Rust back in the day, the transfer over to this version can be hard, and almost intolerable. Don't give up though. It gets really fun once you adjust to the differences and accept the fact that it's a different game. The graphics are obviously vastly greater than Legacy graphics, and the Official servers are actually moderated (HALLELUAH). The gunplay is slightly less intense, but it's honestly more realistic. You can't get shot 3 times in real life, and just run behind a rock and use a green box to heal yourself back to Superman Mode. No, in New Rust every shot matters.If you get sprayed, chances are you're dead, if not then you're hobbling off with next to no health hoping that they took pity on your poor poor soul. The building on this version is far more customizable and complex, which is a double-edged sword to the community. Honestly I enjoy it though, it brings so many more tactical options into the game. A HUGE, and yes I mean huge difference in the game is that food is actually important in this one. "Hold up wait, food can be important?" Yes, and it is. In old Rust, you would find yourself with hundreds of "chicken" breasts and the occasional cat food can. On this version you will find yourself actually having to hunt for animals instead of seeing a crowd of them out in the field. The maps on this version are procedural as opposed to the same map. This can make finding your buddies harder, and getting lost easier. But that's awesome. It truly ups the survival aspect by a lot. All in all, this game is just as great as old Rust as long as you weren't an old Newman, or if you bear through the beginning critiques that you will have. 10/10 would reccomend New Naked Man Rock Smash Bros. to anyone.

Dayz standalone has a consideral amount of bugs and issues. some are ALMOST gamebreaking like dodgy internet connections with servers and uncertain hitbox locations on zombies. The Basis for the game however is the unique Human interaction which draws me back for repeated gameplay. Even if the game was zombie free and just human interaction based i would have a hard time.
Finding shelter in a populated server is terrifying. Every city is the goldmine filled with gas. you almost NEED to visit cities to find the supplies you want and need. decent weapons, clothes, repair supplies, food and shelter are abundant in city's but at the same time so are other players and zombies and you often find yourself forced to improvise a weapon from something as simple as a stick or hammer in order to find the fire axe or Mosin Nagant
There are several times where i have found myself breathing quietly and hiding in a cupboard or a small room by myself as the voices of several players talk nearby. i have been held prisoner on numerous occasions and on several occasions beaten to near death and abandoned. I have also been saved by players from players given food, weapons and ammo and set free. The interaction with players can range from instant surrender to violent aggression meaning every encounter starts the same way.
is it zombie?
have they seen you?
are you armed?
is he/she armed?
do they talk?
are they agressive or are there hands up? and for the more agressive among you
do they have any valuables?
and all this has to be decided in just moments where you know hesitation can kill you.
I'd rate the game highly for stunning and massive visuals 8/10
simply requiring some polishing and some extra side affects of the apocolypse you would expect such as suicide couples. burned piles of corpses and crashed vehicles.
I'd rate the game as OK for gameplay 5/10
while the human interaction part is unique and brings a refreshing level of difficulty, server connections are spotty and often plauged with timeout errors. the servers are also sparesley populated with an average of 20/30 players in an area that takes 2 days to cross at full pelt.
for POTENTIAL i'd rate the game 10/10
being early access means the game is still BOUND to be buggy and full of issues. However set that aside and it becomes quickly apparent that this game is LOADED with the potential to be a massive hit. with vehicles and a fully fledged survival system, appropriate immersion and fixed zombies the game promises to be the Resident evil players wet dream.
