Leaving a review for both parts of the game.
TLDR: two games for the price of one, hell yeah! (Quit complaining oldies. Sincerely, a fellow oldie.)
Rust Legacy review: Perfect for nostalgia, not so perfect for actual playing. The servers are far too unpopulated for my liking, but if that's your thing than it could still be a great game. The gunplay and fighting in general is definitely more intense in the Old Rust, however since hackers flooded into the game it's hard for people (myself included) to not call hacks at times. This game is honestly amazing IMHO. 10/10 would reccomend Naked Man Rock Smash Bros. to anyone. I could an entire game on this day and still have a great time.
New(Current) Rust: If you played Legacy Rust back in the day, the transfer over to this version can be hard, and almost intolerable. Don't give up though. It gets really fun once you adjust to the differences and accept the fact that it's a different game. The graphics are obviously vastly greater than Legacy graphics, and the Official servers are actually moderated (HALLELUAH). The gunplay is slightly less intense, but it's honestly more realistic. You can't get shot 3 times in real life, and just run behind a rock and use a green box to heal yourself back to Superman Mode. No, in New Rust every shot matters.If you get sprayed, chances are you're dead, if not then you're hobbling off with next to no health hoping that they took pity on your poor poor soul. The building on this version is far more customizable and complex, which is a double-edged sword to the community. Honestly I enjoy it though, it brings so many more tactical options into the game. A HUGE, and yes I mean huge difference in the game is that food is actually important in this one. "Hold up wait, food can be important?" Yes, and it is. In old Rust, you would find yourself with hundreds of "chicken" breasts and the occasional cat food can. On this version you will find yourself actually having to hunt for animals instead of seeing a crowd of them out in the field. The maps on this version are procedural as opposed to the same map. This can make finding your buddies harder, and getting lost easier. But that's awesome. It truly ups the survival aspect by a lot. All in all, this game is just as great as old Rust as long as you weren't an old Newman, or if you bear through the beginning critiques that you will have. 10/10 would reccomend New Naked Man Rock Smash Bros. to anyone.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Leaving a review for both parts of the game.
TLDR: two games for the price of one, hell yeah! (Quit complaining oldies. Sincerely, a fellow oldie.)
Rust Legacy review: Perfect for nostalgia, not so perfect for actual playing. The servers are far too unpopulated for my liking, but if that's your thing than it could still be a great game. The gunplay and fighting in general is definitely more intense in the Old Rust, however since hackers flooded into the game it's hard for people (myself included) to not call hacks at times. This game is honestly amazing IMHO. 10/10 would reccomend Naked Man Rock Smash Bros. to anyone. I could an entire game on this day and still have a great time.
New(Current) Rust: If you played Legacy Rust back in the day, the transfer over to this version can be hard, and almost intolerable. Don't give up though. It gets really fun once you adjust to the differences and accept the fact that it's a different game. The graphics are obviously vastly greater than Legacy graphics, and the Official servers are actually moderated (HALLELUAH). The gunplay is slightly less intense, but it's honestly more realistic. You can't get shot 3 times in real life, and just run behind a rock and use a green box to heal yourself back to Superman Mode. No, in New Rust every shot matters.If you get sprayed, chances are you're dead, if not then you're hobbling off with next to no health hoping that they took pity on your poor poor soul. The building on this version is far more customizable and complex, which is a double-edged sword to the community. Honestly I enjoy it though, it brings so many more tactical options into the game. A HUGE, and yes I mean huge difference in the game is that food is actually important in this one. "Hold up wait, food can be important?" Yes, and it is. In old Rust, you would find yourself with hundreds of "chicken" breasts and the occasional cat food can. On this version you will find yourself actually having to hunt for animals instead of seeing a crowd of them out in the field. The maps on this version are procedural as opposed to the same map. This can make finding your buddies harder, and getting lost easier. But that's awesome. It truly ups the survival aspect by a lot. All in all, this game is just as great as old Rust as long as you weren't an old Newman, or if you bear through the beginning critiques that you will have. 10/10 would reccomend New Naked Man Rock Smash Bros. to anyone.

Dean Rocket has a pretty nice plan with this project, but by the looks of it. He just got his fat paycheck and left the project(Or so it seems). The most common problems with this game is that it borrows some of the most annoying bugs from the mod version.

-Zombies still walk through walls.
-Zombies have an inhuman sense(Seeing/smelling you miles away despite being hiden)
-Broken limbs can appear out of nowhere when running or walking into/out of buildings.
So it may seem that the dev team behind this standalone did it all for a cash n' grab and do barely any updates at all.

24 Hours in and I love the game already. When you're playing on a low pop server its all about the loot bout the loot bout the loot... lol It gets funner and more interesting as you go trough the game picking out gear that you really like and more intense when you're on the verge of loosing it. Than once you got your self some experience and loot(including weapons) its time to go help others on their adventures or be a billy badass and just straigh up a lone gun slinger. While it is fun hunting people (so i hear). It just seems like you mind get more enjoyment out of just making friends and talking tasks and adventures together, not to mention its quite helpfull to have a buddy with you when you get lost or are running low on supplies... or even more importantly when you encounter a player or a group that aren not as frienly as you are!
The fact that this game is in ALPHA never even crosses your mind(ok maybe once, or twice) simply because you are emmersed into this beautiful post apocaliptic world of what seems like eastern europe (or russia). The atmosphere and landscape is just breath taking. I am not sure if people apreciate how much time and effort goes into these things. Understandably the patters are repeated and once you've seen one village you almost have certainly seen them all, with the exception of a few land mark buildings that are located in some cities. However, there is nobody that will not agree that this game is just straight up beautiful. You find your self constantly just apreciating the scenery (when you aren't jumping at every noise you hear). As mentioned the villages do look very similar in the sense that the buildings don't vary too often. I have not obviously been to the whole map so maybe i should even not speak on the subjet but so far i have visited most major cities and quite a few small villages, as well as about 3 or 4 military bases and 3 air strips.
Your biggest problem here wont be rampant lone wolfs who are out to kill a few noobies(or bambies as they are known in the UK servers). The biggest problem you will have is knowing or being lucky to get loot quick once you spawn as a fresh survivor. If you dont not get a decent weapon right away you can almost certainly expect to get killed by a zombie (Unless you run away, but they seem to chase you forever. After a while you just get bored and want to make a stand, just to find out that it takes about 5000 punches or theres a whole herd of zombies now after you, they just dont give up!). To kill one you have to be either good with a weapon or just good at dodging. Once you dodge their initial attack (you will see que's) you have a second or two to line up a blow to the head). Ofcourse different weapons will have different hit points. I found the AXE to be the best mele weapon. Followed by the pickaxe, than the shovel. But this isn't a survival guide. I just want to share a few points.
Over all the game seems to have been in development for quite some time. However it has established quite a loyal fan base already. Once you play it for a little you can tell why. Its quite addicting, but more so when you play with friends. It trully is an adventure. Right now the game has a few things that it needs to fix and quite alot of things that it needs to add to become more appealing to a wider crowd of gamers. If you want a decent explorer game where the game mechanics are quite decent, graphics are beautiful and you can play with others this one is for you. I know some people will not like the action as it is right now, but it is worth it. Considering the game will be double the price when its finished(whenever that is). You could save your self 30 bucks in the future and buy it for 30 today. Maybe you wont play it 24/7 but you will find your self going back once in a while and spending a few hours just exploring stuff.

While still in Alpha, Rust is a blast! Kind of a cross between Minecraft and Skyrim (though no high-fantasy elements). Rust is real. You're put in the middle of the woods with a bunch of sticks and stones, and it's up to you to survive given the resources that are around you. COOL GAME - BUT!
Epic game, I love the atmosphere of the game and how any mistake can end your life. I played Rust before in its original state on my friends computer but recently I brought a gaming PC myself and playing the new version of Rust, currently called Experimental - I had a lot of fun.
The game is progressing quickly, the devs are constantly working on the game and changing aspects that might not fit the game very well, this can also be a problem but I will get to that later.
The game spawns you in different locations of the map, with nothing but a rock and a torch- you are then free to run around like a headless chicken hitting everything and everyone OR using your time wisely to build tools and shelter and progress from there to survive.
Survivors in Rust will find that it’s better to survive together, finding your friends can be quick if you are lucky or an absolute pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ Do not trust players, who don't have microphones, it never ends well.
Rust is very unique survival game, no zombies, just the player vs the environment and whole bunch of naked dudes swinging rocks- or bandits going around "practicing" shooting.
_____________________________________________________________________
BUT!!!
Rust is an early access game so watch out what you purchase, watch latest YouTube videos because the game changes very quickly, features get fixed and broken, fixed again or removed. this is a massive problem with Rust, as much as Devs are caring for the game, they change and remove features as they please meaning that in future the game might now be what it is now.
For example my problem lays with removal of the Building Walls Removing option which allowed people to remove walls later on when they want to expand on their homes or fix errors they made by accident. the devs removed the features as they found that player raiding shelters (which is a normal part of Rust implemented by the community and Devs) would take down house when they get access to build in the area by authorising themselves to use the tool cupboard (an object which placed in a house forbids other players to BUILD on and around the building). I guess what Devs have not figure out that the raiders can build in the player's house and completely make it unusable by for example placing a staircase on the doors and upgrading it to stone, this would make it near impossible to break through with standard tools- near equivalent to the house being destroyed.
Other problems include the performance issues, the devs are fixing those problems and trying to make the game run smoother with every update, but often lag comes from the number of players in servers and abandoned, raided shelters (that are now not destroyed by raiders) - even though those things such as destroyed abandoned houses in Rust give it its unique atmosphere it can be the game's curse.
I have little performance issues when playing Rust other than a little lag every 20 or so seconds which makes FPS drop to 30. This is because I'm running Rust on NVidia GTX 980 oc Video card, i7 4790K processor and 8 GB RAM. I have around 80 to 70 FPS when running around, but in highly builder up areas it can drop.
Overall the game is cool, I'm enjoying it very much right now, and I really hope the Devs will listen to the community as the new version of Rust progresses further. If you feel like trying Rust try finding cheaper Steam keys on websites such as♥♥♥♥♥and help out a charity at the same time.

This is what I said back in 2014. The Arma 2 mod was the whole reason I got into PC gaming, and I still play the mod from time to time. Me and my friends enjoy the aspect of team gameplay without the confines of a small map, but a large, open world.
I remember waking up one morning in October of 2013, checking some social media before school, and saw that DayZ standalone was set to release in December. Thank God! All I could thinnk about at school that day was the realease of this game. At this time, I would be about halfway through my 8th grade year.
It is now July 2017, a month before I begin my senior year. I always check the BI twitter for updates every week to see if theres anything going on with development. "Updates to Zeleogorsk", "Bug Fixes", and "Stability updates" are all i've seen the past few months. I watched a video this morning, where two guys were comparing this game to Playerunknown's Battlegrounds. Some points that they brought up were pretty good, but I still couldn't figure out why they were comparing the two.
The way I see it, PUBG is a simple copy and paste from an Arma 3 mod to the Unreal 4 Engine, and is a great way to put out a product early on, but will limit what they can do with the game later down the line. DayZ, on the other hand, tried to make it's own engine based off of the Arma engine. Although this engine is great for Arma games, it was a poor choice on the original BI dev team due to how buggy it is, and is the reason wh ythe current DayZ team is recoding the entire engine, which should push this game into 0.63, or beta. On top of that, while they are recoding the engine, the game is still techincally playable. If PUBG had to recode an engine, it would easily double the time it took to develop. PUBG also hasn't had the mastermind behind it up and leave a dev team to figure out what to do on their own.
Three and a half years is a long time for a game to be in development, but for a game on this scale, it's doing relatively well, especially with all the problems BI has encountered. But, to this day, I still have hope for this game. One reason is for the fact that BI has usually done what it said it would do. I mean, Arma 3 is trucking along fine and well with its road map, and its on the smaller side of companies. Rockstar Games took five years to make GTAV with at least ten times the amount of devs working for them, and the game doesn't even have half the mechanics that DayZ has (Realistic ballistics, carry weight, etc.)
I refuse to let this game crash and burn. The mod has made some of my best gaming memories, and i've sunken countless hours into both the mod and standalone. It's the basis for tons of other copies (H1Z1and State of Decay, i'm looking at you two) and still has a fairly large player base on both the mod and standalone. As the famous rapper G-Eazy once said in an interview about his career, "The longer it takes, the longer it lasts." I think we should all just let BI do its thing, pass it into beta, and put all of this crap behind us. I mean, come on, nothing can be more of a disappointment than No Man's Sky.

Look, I bought this game almost a year ago now, and I barely play it. The simple fact is, nothing has changed. The game has implimented a few new clothing choices, weapons and re-modeled cities that should have been in there since day one. The game was rushed into Early Access way too fast. And while I realize that it is in fact, an Early Access game, there is no excuse for not adding anything meaningful to the game after 2 years.
And I would even say that there are more bugs in this game than there originally were two years ago.
And if you're a person that can handle bugs and glitchs and can take all that in stride, the community is the next problem. I have recently finished watching all of FrankieIn1080p's videos on his DayZ story, and the mod is so much further along than this game is, and the community are 4x better as well. Everyone in the stand-alone WILL shoot you on site. At least in the original mod you had a 30% chance they would not. And trust me, that 30% seems a whole lot better than spending 10+ hours getting gear all over such a huge map (which still does not have vehicles, but the mod does) only to be sniped from somewhere you can't even see.
The big thing that annoy's me about this game, is that the 4 year old mod, is still so much further along than this game. Like I said, I can respect that an Early-Access game has its fair share of bugs and glitchs, but when the original mod still has more stuff and is more stable than this game, there is definitly something wrong.
That, and the lead dev is leaving to make some other game when he has not even finished this Alpha.
It's your call if you want to buy it, but I really did try to like this game and it wasn't for me... or anyone else I know. The concept is there, it just could have been executed better.

Do not buy this game, and heres why.
The gameplay is tense and fun, it will always keep you on your toes provided you don't play on empty servers like a casual so you can gear up. Theres not a whole lot of action going on, but when there is, it gets difficult as one wrong decision will mean the death of you and all your gear is gone, back to gearing up and finding food again. As of time of writing, the Zombies are a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ they are more of an annoyance then something you will watch out for. Their detection seems to be buggy as some zombies wont detect you when you're close but some zombies will detect you from a mile away. Don't even bother trying to kill them with a melee weapon as the hitbox registration seems to be a bit broken and trying to even kill them with a melee weapon will take a few tries as they are super laggy and you will probbably end up bleeding. The game also offers Third Person and First Person servers so if you want more of a challenge, you can join the First Person only servers which will require you to be more careful due to limited view.

The hacking and the glitching in this game currently makes it unacceptable. Dispite the new EULA for BattleEye being able to do whatever they want to your computer, and have removed all liability for damage, hackers are still not being detected and eradicated. If you are on a medium-populated server then there will be a hacker around who will be able to detect you from 2000m away, headshot you with an aimbot, be invisible and just ruin your experience as you've put in a good 10hrs of gameplay to get your character up to scratch.
The problem is that the hacks are very easy to come by. A quick good search will reveal very profitable websites that for a subscription fee will hold your hand and tell you how to inject the hacks which my mother could do. As a result of it taking no skills and the fee being around $10/m a lot of people use them. It's prevalent and destroys the game. It makes playing it organically pointless as you will be killed by a teenager using these easy hacks if you have any weapon at all. Also, as you can buy stolen Dayz keys from the same websites, there is no comeuppance at all for people willing to pay a couple of bucks a month. I accept that some hacking will opccur in all online PC games, it's the nature of the beast, but I object to the ease of hacking within this game and the lack of effective solutions against it.
Eugine Harton boldly said that the hacking problem is fixed. It isn't. Until they start banning by computer it wont be fixed. The problem with that is that it then reduces the revenue stream. There is no incentive to ban anything except the key for Dayz as then it forces the player to buy another copy, which is more money for the development team.
Zombies are a huge problem as well. They can currently walk through walls, and have been able to for the past 2 years. If you run inside a building, your hitbox will often be left outside the building, so the zombies will be smashing you when you're nowhere near them. The annoyance is exacerbated by the constant introduction of superflous items in the game. Petticoats, ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Derringers, batons are being created, yet players are still being killed by a glitch that occurs when walking up a set of stairs. It's like trying to apply icing to cake batter. The cake sponge hasn't been made yet! Sort out the big, gamebreaking, glaring problems before introducing useless, but fun items. We can farm tomatoes, but we can't lock zombies in/out of rooms because they walk through the walls! WTF!
I would strongly reccomend people do not buy this game. Although the youtube videos are cool, bear in mind that one short video is a result of around a month of gameplay and 90% of the videos are staged by other players colluding with the youtube to set the conditions. It's not organic, they're staged.

I've been following this game since it originally came out, and I can say that I'm honestly impressed.
The original Rust had a good concept... Misguided, uninspired, sure. But a good concept.
The Facepunch team has been working to expand it ever since, and not kept the community in the dark while doing so. That's something that I can admire. Updates are frequent, often significant, and have all around made this game worth the money that I originally paid and much much more. It will only get better from here, I'm sure.
People who say that the devs have abandoned this game or have no idea what to do with it are, in my opinion, misguided.
Things have been changed and moved around, removed entirely, or given new aspects and that's what you have to expect out of an early release game but the direction the devs are moving is a truly unique one and it offers a great experience to you if you enjoy survival games and want a realistic experience.
All in all, I'd give it an 8/10 and would definitely recommend giving it a shot. Especially if it's on sale.

DayZ is not the zombie survival game you think it is.  As you can see by my play time, I have spent weeks learning the nuances of how to best approach whatever this is, which is pretty much entirely limited to understanding PvP combat.  This is honestly all the game has to offer.
After your first 40 hours or so it gets to the point where zombies pose virtually no threat to you whatsoever regardless of what gear you have.  There are only two types, walkers and crawlers, and both of them simply charge at you and swing their arms at a set range after a short delay.  No matter how many zombies there are after you, they aren't going to get you.  That being said, there are only 4 or 5 zombies per town, with the numbers skyrocketing to a whopping 10 in major cities, assuming other players haven't already cleared them out. Little did I know that the minute the game was installed I had already beaten it.
So what's left is the epic firefights.  You are fighting for your life against other humans to defend the two hours worth of gear you have strapped to your back.  This is where DayZ actually shines.  The guns handle extremely well, the players are all willing to kill each other because honestly there isn't anything better to do, and the group or individual with the best tactics can often beat somebody with better equipment.  These skirmishes give me shots of adrenaline every time, because so much is at stake.  Because I know... I know that if I die I have to go through that two hours of excruciatingly boring♥♥♥♥♥♥all over again.

DayZ is not fun.

the clue is in the name 'standalone' only those who trust nobody will get far, its you vs the bandits, zombies and other horrors of this frozen deathland that is chernarus.
the plot is this- you wake up usually on a bit of coast in the south and east or in a small woodland area in the far north. all you have is the shirt and pair of jeans you are wearing and a flashlight with a battery. no tutorial, no helpful signs, nothing.
you are alone. and the rain will be coming soon and its getting dark, your old friends W,A,S,D and the mouse havent changd in terms of controls so the first thing to do is find food and a weapon and a town for supplies.
then survive
in this game loot is everything, even your common everyday items will be akin to a gift of life helping you struggle through every minute of this place that makes purgatory look like a picnic.
YOU WILL BE SHOT IF YOU HAVE SOME ITEMS. and thats if you are lucky, if not it will be rotten food and poisonous substances rammed down your throat and your limbs broken just because you found a can opener.
playing with friends is good but not always advised, you never know if they will turn on you for their own survival, making friends is valuble but the same applies. sharing equipment is vital at the cost of less for yourself. an ally can be invaluble but also risky, but another gun is always useful if you can manage it.
speaking of guns in this game guns and ammo are rarely found in the same location and if they are chances will be that the ammo was in a box and not a magzine so you will be restricted to one bullet at a time then having to rechamber your weapon, knowing your weapon is paramount to using it-you could find a farmers shotgun fresh off the bat but not find ammo for it until you reach the opposite corner of this massive world.
melee weapons on the other hand are easy to find but can be tricky to use. the best are the machete and wood axe. the axe does more damage but the machete drops less food when opening cans and has less of a profile allowing for better stealth.
you can use almost anything as a melee weapon, i have beaten bandits unconcious with a medical bag before, i dont reccomend trying that though i did it in an emergency.
overall a great game to play both with and without friends, each time of playing either day or night has benefits and drawbacks, the day its easier to get around but more risk of players finding you, at night more loot as fewer players around, but it requires more care especially in a zombie infested town as they are a pain to see.
i reccomend this to anyone who wants a challenge, starting off is harsh and you lose everything upon death, and if you fall unconcious without a friend or a rare helpful hero, you are dead anyway.
10/10 although not a full game technically its being updated every week or 2 weeks and each month has a substantial update. vehicles arent in as of time of writing (15th november 2014) but they are close to being implemented. a warning for when they do- dont drive a quadbike on a bridge near elektrozavodsk- it will randomly flip you.

First and mostly: I'm a FPS and Tactical Shooter enthusiast. I met Arma 2 before the DayZ Mod and I enjoyed both very much; keep it in mind, the DayZ Mod, which I managed to get over 10+ Steam Buddies to buy this game play along it with me, is a solid 9/10 in my book.
Regarding the DayZ Standalone I'll be quite blunt: it came out almost a year ago on December 13th and, out of myself and about 20+ friends who came from the DayZ Mod, NONE of us is actively playing it. The main reason is the obvious feeling: it's not, by a longshot, a game in full-development or progress; there are bugs in basically EVERYTHING, hackers and such are all over the servers and, even after numerous updates and patches, the game doesn't seem to be improving. Yes, we all know the game is in Alpha but, quite honestly, the game seems worse than it was at it's launch.
Another crappy point: I have a medium-valued RIG (last upgraded on 2012) and my FPS drops drastically playing this game. Some of my friends have top of the market RIGS and guess what? They get the same performance issues that I have.
There are, however, a couple of pros to this game: it has MASSIVE potential once things get on track with the developer team and one can have lots of fun playing it with friends and/or being a lone wolf. That is, of course, if you have no objections with getting frustated at something that's supposed to be fun.
My verdict? Do not buy this game. Not until it's fixed and, trust me, that will take a long time. It's simply not worth the money for it (not the 30 dollars or 20 euros or 70 reais, the currency here in Brazil).

I've probably had DayZ for well over a year now. In the beginning, the game was literally unplayable. Insufferable lag, numerous bugs (such as items unable to be picked up, invisible zombies, etc.) Granted, the developers provide an initial warning stating that the game is still in its Alpha stages, hence why I have stopped playing it shortly after purchasing it.
Now that a significant amount of time has passed since I had last played DayZ, I was hoping that the developers made some progress on making the game a more enjoyable experience with less problems, especially because I had originally bought the game because I felt that it had potential to be a very entertaining. However, this is far from the case. I am still experiencing the same problems that I was  before, except for the lag issue slightly improving, all though there are moments where your fps suffers for a bit.
Regardless, save yourself the money and don't even think about buying this cruddy game that is most likely doomed to be forever stuck in alpha. If you want to give it a go, I suggest purchasing ARMA instead and playing the DayZ mod from there, instead of investing in buying the standalone.

*DISCLAIMER*
***Before bum rushing me with hate mail, one thing needs to be understood, I enjoy this game. It has the potential to be one of the best if not the very best game in the zombie survival genre. This review is meant only to poke fun at some of the very real problems in Dayz. While my opinion is 100% true, I admit it was somewhat dramaticized for the sake of a fun review. If you are uber-defensive of this game DO NOT READ THIS REVIEW. If you share my zucchini ridden struggles, have a read, you may get a laugh out of it. Enjoy!***
At this point in time upon writing this review, I have 172 hours in the game. From those 172 hours of experience I have indeed kept in mind that this game is an alpha. However, there are some issues that MUST be worked on if the DayZ community would like to survive. There is mainly one subject in particular that I feel is one of the killing factors in this game:
The Zombies:
Quite frankly, take them out of the damn game for now. I know, I know, this sounds like blasphemy. What's Dayz without the Z? Yes I completely understand that point of view, but anyone who has played Dayz would know that these indestructable excuses for zombies have the potential to render the game unplayable at times. A simple solution is the fire axe, best zed killer I know of. However, for a fresh spawn who does not own such a prized possession, life is hell. Over the course of the past few weeks I have logged onto Dayz only to meet another broken leg as zombies repeatedly slap my fresh spawn character to death. Did I mention you can't actually see the zombies? Oh yes, in this game, for some damned reason, zombies have telepathic powers in which they can use their keen zombie senses to murder some freshie who has nothing but a zucchini THROUGH A ♥♥♥♥ING WALL. I cannot tell you how many times I have been slightly geared, with no fire axe mind you, and have broken my legs via stairwell slap zombies. Upon breaking my legs, I submit to my imminent death as zombies are IMPOSSIBLE to outrun in this game, let alone with broken legs. My main point here is that the zombies, in my opinion, NEED to be worked on ASAP. This should be one of the first things touched up before adding an extra type of ♥♥♥♥ing canned food.
I will end this review with a bit of a prompt for any other reviewers out there:
If you had one thing to mention to the devs, what would it be?
My answer:
I don't know if I am speaking for everyone, but personally I DONT WANT ANY MORE ♥♥♥♥ING FRUITS AND VEGGIES ADDED TO THE GAME. FIX YO DAMN ZOMBIES KIDDO. FIX EM NOW.
Unfortunately in this current stage of the game, I will have to give it a negative review.

This is a hard game for me to recommend; though it is just as hard not to recommend.  The idea of the game and the feel of an open world is brilliant.  Tons of items, fun player interactions, and well.... zombies!  But there is a downside.  The game just does not run well.  I have an asus laptop with 8GB of ram that I was unable to efficiently play this game on.   I do, however, have a desktop computer that has 12GB of ram, NVIDIA Geforce, Blah Blah blah... its a gaming pc.  It runs the game beautifully with the optimization offered by NVIDIA, yet I still find the game is riddled with glitches and hiccups, which is normal for any Early Access Game, of course.  A critical gamer may have a hard time with this game.  Another issue is the fact that one feels "glued" to the ground, due to the lack of a realistic jump button.  Also, the audio for zombies is extremely annoying and loud.  I pray that I don't encounter a zombie solely because I don't want to hear that poorly recorded audio track Dean used for the zombies.  Also, even though there are tons of items and uses for items, there is a lack of features in certain areas.  For instance, say you get clawed by a zombie once and you start bleeding.  If you can't find bandages, you will proceed to bleed to death and die.  In reality, one could stop the bleeding with a number of things: shirts, cloth, pant legs, etc.  Perhaps this could even introduce wound infection.  Fun game, definitely worth a try if your computer is capable.  Gaming computers recommended!

I put tons, and I mean
of hours in to the orignial mod. I was there from the early days of the first map, and continued to play in to the many community maps. In its core, Dayz is a great idea, and even works out pretty well. Zombies are more of an annoyance then a real threat, unless you get stuck in a room with the zombies clipping through the walls, breaking your legs, and losing all those beans you collected. The mod was great, so many awesome stories, so much to do, and endless hours of fun. Hell, most people bought Arma 2 because of the popularity of the dayz mod, and the community has kept the mod going to this day.
So how excited when we heard that the creator of Dayz, Rocket, was going to do a stand-alone release? It was everything we hoped for, an actual
version of Dayz, no longer would we be pray to hackers making the whole server gangam style, no longer would be victems to invisible zombies flying through walls. We were going to get an actual game of one of the best mods ever to be made. But we didn't, not yet at least.
Dayz Standalone was in closed alpha for a few months two years ago, with a planned full release in January of 2013(?), information was very limited. Around this same time WarZ (Now Survival Stories) was released in December with massive backlash due to the unfinished product, only a week or two later did we get an announcement DayZ release would be pushed back so we could get a supirior product. We all cried a little in dissapointment, but we trusted they knew what they were doing.
Skip forward to June and Rocket annonced that the initial release would be bare bones, the game itself would be updated over time to introduce more content. This troubled some people, but the majority of the community (myself included) shrugged it off, how would this team let us down? Now its December, the relase, its here, we can play it. Its amazing... to some.
On initial release the complete LACK of content that was even in the original mod was staggering, I mean no vehicles? No mod maps? Wasn't running around for 4 hours to find a tire to throw on to your shaggy van the point that got most of us to keep playing? On top of that, my frame right was down right awful, hovering around 10-20 fps on my gtx 660 ti. I dropped out at this point, waiting for more content, letting others enjoy the game in its Early Acess stage.
Almost a year later now, with an announcement of a PS4 port, and the development progress is abismal to say the least. I think I can speak for most the comunity to say what a dissapointment this has all been. Yes its early access, but the
that started it all has more content than this. Hell, the
that the comunity made has had better updates than DayZ Standalone.
What a pity for a game with so much potential. I can see why they pushed their release date back after the WarZ fiasco, not wanting to follow in their shoes. Go play the mod, at least its buggy for a reason.

The game is good but not brillient. It has many glaring issues and bugs that have not been addressed after a year of development.
Pros
Gameplay:
The game is fun! Lots of content and cool things you can find. If you hook up with a few mates taking to the big city is great. I love how major loot zones have become play for a lot of player versus player action. There is an element of risk, do you play it safe and avoid these areas or do you take the plunge for greater reward? They've done this nicely and the map feels like it's well thought out.
Sounds:
Some sounds could use an overhall but the ambience of it all is fabulous.
Mapping and graphics:
Very well thought out and they look great, I can see they've spent a lot of time creating a vast landscape. Denser zombie hordes can easily be spotted in major cities where country areas are less likely to contain zombie life. You know if you loot in a military base you will find weapons.
Cons
A.I:
Namely the zombie A.I and mechanics need a major overhaul. The concerns of zombies are:
-Their innate ability to home in on you from vast distances, dispite doing complex movements to dodge, outrun and loose  them they can still track you well after your out of sight.
-Invincibility, the damage system really is unclear and more so impossible to predict. How it happens is a mystery but some zombies simply cannot die. So not only do zombies home in on your position from miles away they can sometimes come immune to damage which is not really helpful at all.
-They can clip through walls. one might think hiding in a house or bunkering down is a good idea (after all that is what nearly every other zombie game promotes). However Zombies if they do not have a clear path to your location will default to passing through walls to reach you. This is the longest and indeed the most glaring bug the game has to offer. Not much has been done to fix/address this issue.
Playability:
The game is brutal and is not forgiving to new players at all. All loot that you need to build up/survive is in places that are riddled with zombies. For a new, freshly spawned player, no weapons at all and sheer speed of zombies, it's purely a game of luck as to whether or not you can get going. If your lucky you might find a weapon, however most weapons do poor damage to zombies and you won't start dealing damage untill you get some form of axe which is not easy to get if your far from a major city and getting swamped by zombies.
Progesssion:
Usually you can find yourself dying to zombies, starvation, bleeding, thirst, hypothemia, exposure 75% of the time you spawn before you actually make any kind of progression. The game promotes an environment that has a player dying often in any case. Even more geared out players can easily die so there is not much in the way of progressing through.
It has innumerous cool features and things you'll love to play with... But the likelyhood of ever being able to play with a gun, fit it with some sweet attachments or paint it for camo is very unlikely if your going solo.
Efficiency:
I haven't got anything fancy, just a store bought computer and it is quite able to run most games. But for Dayz I can expect a top of 20 fps when I turn all settings down to minimum or turn them off. It's just not very efficient and for someone who can't afford to make a gaming system or simply can't justify spending money on one this is a bit of a turn off for me.
---
The game itself promises a lot, and indeed it looks like it's going in a good direction. But the developers need to spend less time adding features and more time fixing these problems. In it's current state they ask for $30, I can honestly say I do not think it is worth nearly that much not with all these glitches and bugs so glaringly obvious. I would say wait for a while untill these bugs are fixed, perhaps pick-up the game if it's on sale for $15 or so.

If you are not into the development and workings of games, do NOT buy DAYZ prior to v1.0. Much can be said for the development process taking time, effort, money and feedback. This game needs much more of the first two at the moment. Rather than fix buggy rendering, physics errors, connection failures with battleEYE and incredibly long load up times, the developers have recently lumped in multiple new ways for you do be well on your way to dying far before you are even aware of your surroundings. Dying to cold after spawning in the rain, waiting ~10 minutes to gain control over the character, and finally bugging your way around enough to find out that no fire starting supplies are left in your area is now a VERY real occurance. This game will be a masterpiece when the developers mature enough to work on the problems present in the game, rather than adding feature after feature to an already unstable framework. At one point I was excited for the addition of vehicles to the huge map, but now I can only cringe at the thought of riding along and glitching inside of buildings at freeway speeds, after spending days(weeks, or months if you played at a point where the game was stable enough) building up gear, weapons, ammo and food. If you do pick it up before release, don't expect to leave with the same hairline that you began with.

It's in alpha still, so we've got a long way to go.
The idea of the game is fantastic, and what they've got so far is excellent.
However, if you're looking for a full game that can hold you attention for more than a few hours, you might look elsewhere.
Currently, when you start a new character on a server with a decent amount of people (You don't really want to run around on an empty server either, that's no fun), you'll see quite a few buildings, some very large. What you'll probably notice about most of the small (3x3 or less) buildings is that they've been broken in to. This is the hardship of a new player on any of the servers. As soon as you've made your first home there'll be a roaming band of people with guns and ammunition to hunt you down and take your stuff.
The best way to survive this onslaught is to try and upgrade to stone immediately, and have a sleeping bag in your hut along with some extra tools. Then, you'll want to try to upgrade to metal immediately after that. Anything less than a metal house will most likely be demolished by the time you log back in next.
TL:DR
The game is great, but the lack of protection for new players and general difficulty in protecting your stuff ruins it.
If they increase the defense of wooden structures to the same level as stone, and then stone up to metal, and metal to an even higher level, that'll fix the game. (in my opinion).

This game has a lot of great moments in it's alpha stage. There's plenty to do and explore, and it's sufficient enough to feed anyone's hunger for adventure. There are parts of the game that are unforgiving to new and veteran players (i.e. radiation poisoning, predatorial wildlife, and even other players).
The main objective of the game is hunt and gather to stay alive, so the excitement really stems from interaction with other players.. however, the notion of 'kill on site' runs rampant on almost all servers (it's best to assume everyone is hostile). There's a good variety of weapons and consumables in the game. You'll find yourself running out of the good tools quickly, so crafting is a key part of surviving. Protecting your loot is hard as all you can really do is lay down bear traps and surround your stash with walls (wooden, stone, or metal). It would be nice to see something that really bites back when an intruder knocks down a wall or attemps to unlock your doors.
Visually, Rust does a great job of capturing the imagination. Landscapes can range from deserts, plains, beaches, and snowy mountains. There are only a handful of critters that roam the map, so I would only assume that adding more wildlife is in the plans for future development. Wolf meat is the main source of protein in the game. In the future I would hope to see options to fish near lakes or farm within your base.
I really can't wait for this game to ramp up with more features and players. It would be interesting to see tribes/groups develop and navigate standoffs with other groups. The feeling would be similar to TWD, but minus the zombies.
$20 well spent.

DayZ is undoubtedly one of the best games I have ever played, in fact strike that, it is THE best game I've ever played. Whatever I play in the future I can't see this game ever moving out of my top games list.
But longevity wise it is flawed.
Having clocked up 150 odd hours of play I'm at the point of having visited every point on the map, and able to spawn fresh and equip myself with everything I need to survive. I've spent countless hours exploring and looting, as well as countless more in the early days running across the massive map  with no idea where I am or where I'm going.
And I've loved every minute.
But now I've seen just about everything there is to see, and after gearing up find myself standing around thinking 'what now'.
I'm not interested in PvP, I play lone wolf and steer clear of other players. I've no interest in finding friends to travel with - for me that just means two of us standing around saying 'what now'. I'm happy to help when I can but that's rare as  more often than not I'll get killed for my trouble.
And that's the problem, for me at any rate. There's nothing else to do now I know how to survive.
That said, the 100 odd hours it took to get me to the point of wondering what to do next represents around 20 UK pence an hour, that has got to be value for money surely? I've still gone on to notch up another 50 odd hours on top of that, before reaching the point of saying 'that's enough'.
I'll keep an eye on the updates, and probably poke my nose in from time to time for a fix, but I've had my moneys worth as far as I'm concerned  - and if you buy this game you will too.

This game has a lot of great moments in it's alpha stage. There's plenty to do and explore, and it's sufficient enough to feed anyone's hunger for adventure. There are parts of the game that are unforgiving to new and veteran players (i.e. radiation poisoning, predatorial wildlife, and even other players).
The main objective of the game is hunt and gather to stay alive, so the excitement really stems from interaction with other players.. however, the notion of 'kill on site' runs rampant on almost all servers (it's best to assume everyone is hostile). There's a good variety of weapons and consumables in the game. You'll find yourself running out of the good tools quickly, so crafting is a key part of surviving. Protecting your loot is hard as all you can really do is lay down bear traps and surround your stash with walls (wooden, stone, or metal). It would be nice to see something that really bites back when an intruder knocks down a wall or attemps to unlock your doors.
Visually, Rust does a great job of capturing the imagination. Landscapes can range from deserts, plains, beaches, and snowy mountains. There are only a handful of critters that roam the map, so I would only assume that adding more wildlife is in the plans for future development. Wolf meat is the main source of protein in the game. In the future I would hope to see options to fish near lakes or farm within your base.
I really can't wait for this game to ramp up with more features and players. It would be interesting to see tribes/groups develop and navigate standoffs with other groups. The feeling would be similar to TWD, but minus the zombies.

This game has a lot of great moments in it's alpha stage. There's plenty to do and explore, and it's sufficient enough to feed anyone's hunger for adventure. There are parts of the game that are unforgiving to new and veteran players (i.e. radiation poisoning, predatorial wildlife, and even other players).
The main objective of the game is hunt and gather to stay alive, so the excitement really stems from interaction with other players.. however, the notion of 'kill on site' runs rampant on almost all servers (it's best to assume everyone is hostile). There's a good variety of weapons and consumables in the game. You'll find yourself running out of the good tools quickly, so crafting is a key part of surviving. Protecting your loot is hard as all you can really do is lay down bear traps and surround your stash with walls (wooden, stone, or metal). It would be nice to see something that really bites back when an intruder knocks down a wall or attemps to unlock your doors.
Visually, Rust does a great job of capturing the imagination. Landscapes can range from deserts, plains, beaches, and snowy mountains. There are only a handful of critters that roam the map, so I would only assume that adding more wildlife is in the plans for future development. Wolf meat is the main source of protein in the game. In the future I would hope to see options to fish near lakes or farm within your base.
I really can't wait for this game to ramp up with more features and players. It would be interesting to see tribes/groups develop and navigate standoffs with other groups. The feeling would be similar to TWD, but minus the zombies.

DayZ... Where do I begin?
The game was made originally made a mod for Arma II: Operation Arrowhead about 3 years ago, and during its mod days I totally enjoyed the game, had constant fun of running around the map with stable game mechanics, lots of content and numerous updates coming very regular. Sniping people in Stary Sobor at like 4am on highly populated servers was the life, setting up car traps (Hence the word, CARS.) and it was so fun I could sit there for hours picking off unsuspecting victims. The DayZ where you could get into helicopters, cars and have a wide variety of different weapons, a working system and it was absolutely bliss. Then the developers announced it was going to be made into a standalone game.
DayZ Standalone  came out on the night of the 16th December 2013, I bought it within 15 minutes of release, thinking it was going to have a sufficient amount of content considering they was developing it for a long period of time. Yet upon loading and playing the game for some time, I was quite dissapointed by lack of effort actually put into the game. Their was like 2 guns, the hand held weapons didnt even work, zombies could run through walls, no vehicles not even a peddle bike and their wasn't even a proper loot table let alone respawning loot. So today is 09/11/2014 and I am going to say that, literally, the only thing that has probably changed is the following;
- 5 ish new zombie annimations.
- 3 to 4 new guns added.
- A semi-working loot table.
- Countless amounts of clothes added (When zombies are still running through walls and under the ♥♥♥♥ing floor).
- A couple of towns added.
I mean, every time DayZ gets updated, Im like "Oh my god, its been three months and there is finally an update! OMG. What is it? Vehicles? Guns? Zombies fixed from breaking my legs from under the floor? Actual working hit detection system with melee weapons? Im so excited!!!" Followed by... "In update 0.xx, we have added... WATERPROOF CLOTHES!!!" and then people like going mental as if they've fixed the entire game in the comments. Like really? Waterproof ♥♥♥♥ing clothes? Rust is a game about survival. But that takes time. Initially, it's just about death. It's about freezing to death, and starving to death, being shot to death and getting bitten to death; occasionally mixing things up a little by slipping on a warm radiation coat and fading faster than your faith in humanity after being stabbed in the back by a supposed friend's hatchet. Sometimes you get gored to death. Other times, bored to death. It's not easy, surviving post-apocalyptic civilisation with nothing but a rock - especially when your enemies have guns, and double-especially in a game that makes you work just to earn a pair of basic trousers.
Even this early into development, Rust's mix of DayZ and Minecraft (the easiest comparison, though Wurm Online is more apt) has won it no shortage of fans - some of them not even psychopaths, hackers and trolls on the hunt for new victims to murder and mock over voice chat. It's the kind of game that's less a shooter than an engine designed to tell stories. Those stories are mostly, as ever, in the field of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥om, but there's scope for some humanity amongst all the pranks and murder. It's also a world that focuses on demanding effort rather than promising to reward it: starting players out naked and hungry and alone, dangling the potential of going on to build forts, craft weapons, and finally savour the air at the top of the food chain.
Crafting is the most important part of this, though there are loot crates - both in radioactive remnants of civilisation and regularly dropped from passing planes - that provide free toys to play with and blueprints for advanced gear that, unlike your inventory, survives death. Early on, the priority is making basic tools like a stone hatchet, a bow, a hut and a sleeping bag by beating supplies out of trees and rocks and animals... usually cloth, for some reason. Later, blueprints, furnaces and workbenches offer more advanced gear like metal doors that other players can't so easily get through, and armour capable of protecting against bullets and lingering radiation fields, as well as keeping you warm and covering up your naughty bits.
Building a solid place to call your own is by far the most important thing to focus on - ideally backed up by friends, because on default rules, your character becomes an unconscious, vulnerable sleeper rather than vanishing on log-out. Not all servers use this though, with some even going for pure co-op. It's not a very fun mode to play, though, odd as missing the gankers might seem. Too quiet. Too much time grinding without distraction.
As far as game completion goes, all the basic components here are in place and fully playable, including wildlife to hunt and be hunted by, a range of weapons to craft, and a decent-sized map that's more than capable of handling over a hundred players in its valleys, forests and ruins. Current stress tests are cranking that up to 300 for true Spartan madness.
That said, most of the details are very rough, with much work left in everything from making combat mechanically satisfying, to putting proper sound effects in, to generally finding the balance between Rust's various inspirations. The map, for instance, is far blander than DayZ's Chernarus, and mostly filled with generic forestry and plains and space left empty to give players scope to develop each server in their own image. This sounds cool, but at the moment, the primitive components don't offer anything like enough freedom to create interesting things. On a Minecraft server, absolutely anything could be waiting around the next corner in all its blocky glory. Here, it's almost always going to be a generic wood shack or tower, usually long abandoned or fiercely guarded by a proprietorial player who thinks himself a post-apocalyptic badass but acts far more like Cletus the Slack Jawed Yokel.
That side of things being so prominent also makes the basic goal underpinning the action - "Survive!" - feel somewhat unambitious, as well as depressingly acting as license for a player-base of social Darwinists to be on their worst behaviour. The same can be said of DayZ, of course, but in that game the setting and mood go hand in hand with the brutality - ruthless scavengers picking through a broken world gone long past the point of no return. Rust presents something with more possibilities, and in doing so often feels like it should be offering more to actually survive for. At least, something more than finally scraping together the explosives to go kick over other kids' sandcastles.
Simply getting to that point offers plenty of challenge, however, not least because the resource economy is currently completely broken - especially on busy servers. Survival requires food, but you can easily starve to death without even seeing an animal to extract life-saving chicken breasts from. (For the moment, it's always chicken, even if it's a pig, though other foods are available elsewhere.) It can also take several lives just to luck into enough stone to construct the most basic hatchet for gathering supplies, or a single piece of the cloth you need to construct a sleeping bag that acts as a respawn point, only to lose it all after being spotted by a player with a gun or getting too close to a wild animal or zombie. Speaking of which, yes, Rust has zombies. Of course it does. They're not around in huge numbers though, and thankfully not long for the world, hanging on for the moment as placeholders for something that can't help but be better simply by not being more bloody zombies.
Provided you're in the mood for a player-versus-player game that makes you work to not simply be a victim, and ideally have a few friends to band together and scare off passing opportunists, Rust's challenge already offers enough of a survival experience to be worth a look. It's as primitive as its rock-smashing cavemen in many ways, and lacks both DayZ's atmosphere and the raw punch of its setting, but the focus on building and crafting does make for a notably different experience. It's worth waiting for a few more patches, though, so that the developers at Facepunch can fix the resource lottery that makes getting started such a chore - and even then, you should take time to find a server where operators are watching for hackers instead of letting them have their fun.
Rust is firmly a base for what might be a great game later on rather than a great one right now. It's seen best in quiet moments, when players aren't around to troll and murder, and crafting and raw survival take the focus. There's more than enough here to suggest great things in Rust's future as it evolves its crafting, its combat, and clears out the zombies to further find its own niche in 2014's upcoming war of survival games. It has the tools to become something very special, and hopefully will provide players with enough to do the same.

Let's get a couple things out of the way before I begin this:
1: Most things I say now will be pretty moot in about a year.
2: It’s hard for me to review this game objectively, since I've been so invested and supportive of it. This I cannot deny, I shamelessly bought this game upon release. However I will try my best.
Most of the helpful reviews here have been heavily criticizing both the game's developers and the community. On these topics I feel it is best to hold no opinion, and I don't think that they should influence your decision in purchasing or not purchasing this game. What you need to consider is if you are prepared to deal with the almost unplayable state that this game is in. DayZ, in its current state, runs well on most computers and looks very nice. I have an HP laptop from two years ago and here it's going fine. A friend of mine has a much worse laptop and he can pull off medium settings at a tolerable framerate as well. Most problems that I've seen have originated with either poor or broken graphics cards, but this is only from experience. You will most likely encounter a fair amount of rubberbanding if you have a poor connection, like me. This is honestly one of the things that makes me turn the game off the most, but as far as I can see it doesn't have much to do with the game's servers. As far as how the game plays, it's pretty much like a slightly more streamlined ARMA II. Sure, you’ll have cheap deaths like always, and at times it’s really pretty hard to get immersed.
With that said, you may be thinking, “How can he still recommend this game?”
My reasoning is this: I am a very faithful and forgiving person. As a reviewer of a product like this, maybe that’s a horrible trait. Actually, it is a horrible trait. Nonetheless, I will stand by this game until the end. DayZ is fun, and some people honestly have a hard time accepting that after what they feel was them being cheated. People like to hate things for the sole reason that other people hate them, and that’s fine. We’re human; I like to hate things too! Criticism is fun! Some of these feelings are based in truth, I can’t deny that. I would even call the game overpriced given its current state. However, for $30 I got at least as much fun as I paid for and this game isn’t even finished yet.
One last thing to acknowledge and that is the, “It’s been in development for two years” complaint. What you are seeing now is not the direct result of a full two years of straight up, uninterrupted development. What you are seeing is the ARMA II engine having been revamped after the developers thought that simply releasing a fixed-up DayZ mod was cheap. What you are seeing is the developers answering the wants of the community relentlessly through active, transparent development. The only reason I think that this game was released in the state that it was in was
It’s silly to think that Bohemia Interactive is trying to scam you when you take into consideration all of the thoughtfulness that has went into this product so far. And yes, development will be slow because that is Bohemia’s way of doing things. They are ambitious. They either plan big and go for it or don’t do anything at all.
In closing, I consider DayZ a fun and worthwhile game to be taking part in the development of. Please consider purchasing this later on if you think you can be patient enough. I guarantee if you wait you will get a much, much, much better game. However, if you don’t want to wait you may as well buy now and enjoy the updates as much as you can bugs and all. Thank you for reading if you did, and please feel free to critique.

I must say that to this point this game has been an utter disappointment - the only thing that makes it even remotely enjoyable is playing with a group of friends. Beyond that this game has so many flaws and bugs, especially everything netcode-related. Every action is so singlethreaded and the lag on every server is unplayable. Not to mention the fact zombies still teleport through walls and are near impossible to hit melee-wise. Graphics and video-wise, this game lags horribly in this aspects, I played BF3 with top settings and lagged less than this game even when running through small towns.
The damage scaling (if any) is complete and random BS - hit a dude with a pick in the face 3 times, shoots you once in the leg and you pass out 1 second later to eventually be fully killed.
Suggestion to the devs, rather than adding features and items, why don't you spend those efforts fixing the necessities, e.g. netcode and client-server information exchanging, adding fluidity to actions, fix the broken pathing and zombie AI + clipping, damage scaling, hunger and thirst, healing, item spawning, and the list goes on.
I can't say that going forward I will be supporting early access games. I've been disappointed by enough of them to this point but this one has definitely been the final straw.

Rust originates from Gary (of Gary's Mod) deciding he could make a finished DayZ-like game in only a month. A year and a half later, we still have a game in its alpha. Before I say don't buy this game, let me talk about the good things that it does have. First (and most importantly) the game is being actively updated, unlike many of the early access survival games. In fact, a little while ago the game was completely rebooted in a newer gaming engine. So the game is always getting better, and has a lot of potential to be a really good survival game.
Now let's get into the bad. Like I said, the game has a lot of potential, but Gary is asking you to pay 20 dollars now, for a game that could be really good in 3 years. As Gary has stated, most games go through a development process that last several years, but most studios don't start allowing players to play it until the end of the beta stage, which ensures that you stay excited for the product. Imagine if only a moth after development began Nintendo allowed players to start playing a new Metroid game. The players would be furious that the game is so unfinished and would not be happy that they paid for the game now, even though it's no where near done. Interviews with Gary show he has a hard time understanding this concept, and he get's upset when players ask for more now. On a more technical level, the game is obviously not finished. Glitches are quite common, there is only one player model and map, cheating has not been reeled in it, the crafting system is still pretty bare bones, animals are barely programmed (animals drop random meat and some meat doesn't actually do anything), the hunger system is (at the time I played the game last) broken, textures for buildings look bad and unpolished, and there is very, very little PVE in the game. If not for other players, you could easily survive forever once you get your initial base set up and your first gun made. Rather than the game balancing threats from a hostile environment and other players, the game simple relies on other players being threatening enough to give you a sense of fear for your life. The main menu is broken as well. The game doesn't remember what servers you've been on, and the favorite server list doesn't work yet, which means you have to remember the name of your server in a sea of server names. There is also no easy way to turn down game volume, making it hard to hear people you're steam chatting with. I also have experienced framerate issues unless I play on pretty low resolutions, and as I have a pretty powerful PC I'm going to assume it's that the game is not properly done right.
In conclusion, this could perhaps be a really, really good game one day, but one day is not too day. I regret paying 20 dollars for a game that's barely been developed. With the switching of the game engine (which in theory is good since it shows that Gary is still working on his project) the development process will be set way back as well. If you like survival games, and you think this one looks good put it on your wishlist and keep an eye on it. When it's much, much closer to being finished it could be worth the 40, 50, or even $60 price tag it will have, but it's just not worth 20 in its current state.

The rust I first bought  (legacy/ old version) was amazing. It had it's bugs and hackers, but the game worked, and I spent countless hours playing it, well over 100. Ever since the newer version had arrived, I almost immediately stopped playing. I'd always find myself playing legacy because I was familiar with it, and it was very addicting. the legacy version now is full of cheaters, and makes the game nearly impossible to play without hacking it be juself. I'm hopeful that the newer edition of rust will be just as playable and fun as the version before it. I'd give it another year or two before I attempt to play again.
I wouldn't reccomend buying rust in this current stat. However given it was still in legacy, I would most definitely reccomend the purchase, because it was truly addicting and very fun.
Would I reccomend Rust legacy? Hell yeah! (if they still kept it up to date/ no cheating. it's not up to date, and it's full of them.)
Would i reccomend Rust today? No, it's currently "playable" to say the least. The graphics are great, the frame rate isn't. The core gameplay seems buggy still, yet progressively getting better. I definitely believe rust can achieve what it had done before, but facepunch has some work todo before I'd reccomend someone handing them their money.
A few suggestions from an absolute fan of rust legacy, (and hopefully your newer version).
1. More/stronger wildlife needs to happen.
2. 360/Xbone controller support. [That's a major plus in my book. Pinnacle has one for legacy, but the newer version is broken.]
3. optimization, it's gotten better since you first released the newer version, but it still has some way to go.
4. Rad towns, I haven't seen any, but i want to. they are kind've what kept people in a certain area. Made going into that
area a risk.
5. [just a general thought] What made rust so fun to begin with, was weighing out the pros and cons of doing certain tasks. should I stay warm by my puny fire and shelter tonight, or should I go for that air drop? Should I open the door and kill this ♥♥♥♥♥♥, or is he hiding something? This is what your game was arguably built around, and you should find ways to keep that in. Risk taking should be rewarding, and challenging, that is what I loved about rust.
Hope this helped someone's opinion, and if facepunch took a read, then thanks for listening to your customers!
UPDATE:
The game has much improved since I first wrote this review. I was skeptical that the team could make me enjoy the new rust as much as I had the original, but they've been diligently working the past year or so to prove me wrong.
The game is still a bit buggy, but It's still in early access. Aside from some weird lighting with the campfires in your own shelter, and server latency, the game is coming along perfectly.
I would now recommend the new rust to anyone borderline buying it, it is worth your money, and the devs do listen to your complaints. This is the only review I've ever re-written, and it deserved it.

Its been in Alpha for 2-3 years now. Its not getting better. Was a few months since I last played, and now its more laggy, characters gets wiped almost every relog.
Its still a fun game in essence, but I fear it will never be complete at this backwards rate. Which makes me sad since all the alternatives out there are going for the more arcade-feel.
I like the harsh and rugged reality of DayZ SA, I really do.
But when the character wont even stay saved for 6 hours, it feels like such a hug waste of time.
I literally only have time to loot up some basic clothes and a damaged melee weapon. It takes such long time to start a character, and whenever I need to go eat, or do some groceries, its all wiped.
I wasted half a day now, looted so much stuff, did not die once. And I have nothing to show for it.
Its an alpha yes, but even that has a limit before it gets tiresome. I would be fine with wipes if I could at least see some progress.
But for every new item they add I feel they break equally many lines of code. I just don't understand how the game can feel less optimized and less stable every time I return in hope of seeing something new.
Don't get me wrong, they do work on it, and they do add a lot of stuff, but its only large new areas, new items and a lot of energy spent into creating animals and cooking.
But I feel that in the midst of all that, they loose track on making the base game stable and playable.
Adding zones and loot comes later, right now it feels like they are desperatly trying to keep the players interested instead of putting focus on finishing the code and engine.
If they cant keep the characters saved or the servers running smoth and laggfree, dont spend months on adding veichles just because other games have them. Its like their plan is dividing into way to many sidetracks and time is lost.
Maybe I just had a bad day, and maybe I'm just butt-hurt for loosing my char 3 times in a day without dying.
But I know I'm not the only one feeling frustrated about it. And I know many share my feeling that way to much time and effort are spend on adding bling instead of finishing the ground.

The new version of Rust is cool and all but it still has some pretty devastating problems.
One is that bases are horrendously underpowered. You basically spend hours building up your base, just to have someone axe down your walls and steal your loot while you're sleeping. (Yes I said axe down your walls, a few minutes of cutting at a wall will break it).
Another thing is that the coding is bad. This game has been in early access for over a year now, and they have not addressed any of the serious bugs. In the older version (Rust Legacy) the game was well optimized, and had all of the serious bugs addressed. In this newer rebooted version, it is plagued with optimization problems. My computer is pretty strong for a gaming computer, I can run games like Crysis 3 and Battlefield 4 and Ultra settings at around 60 FPS. However on Rust, despite being on Unity my computer will have framerate drops, and my components would be working on overdrive just to run the game. People with not as powerful computers find just navigating the start menu a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ The best part is that instead of addressing these game breaking bugs the dev team just keeps releasing skins, textures and items.
I was excited for a Rust reboot and gave it a chance multiple times but I can no longer recommend this newer version to anyone. If I were Gary I would scrap the reboot and just continue building up Rust Legacy. For now on Rust Legacy will be the game I play. The only reason I'm giving this a thumbs up is because I believe the old version alone is worth the $20 you spend.

Before I say anything else, I need to say this- Rust is not for the faint of heart. The game will be extremely difficult, even more so if you have nobody else to play with. You will kill, and you will be killed. Everything you have will be stolen, and all your hard work will occasionally be lost. But if you can get past that...
The game is INCREDIBLE.
Never before in a game have I felt such fear and excitement. The graphics are incredibly beautiful, the  building system is phenomenal, combat feels great, and the game is actually difficult- Whereas other games hold your hand, this game lets you figure it all out. I find this a positive, but others may find it a negative.

My story.
Here I am, the desoalte land of DayZ. I have nothing but the clothes on my back and a flashlight, I imediatly realise that I need to get off of the beach. I sprint, taking refuge in a hangar. I find myself an army jacket and pair of gloves. After another 20 minutes of sprinting building to building I finally stand a chance against a zombie. My equipment was comparable to a bargan Navy Seal, full camo, chest rig, helmet and all the rotten fruit I could eat. I even found a pistol with 4 rounds. As I was looting a barn, I find a corpse of a fellow human. As I am checking the body for loot I am barely missed with a rifle round. I run to cover, a nearby house. I begin to look for the source of the gunfire only to see 3 running, clipping, unfinished zombies sprinting towards me. I ready my weapon. As they clip though the door and stairs I hear another gunshot. I luckilly was missed, but then another *You are dead*    4/10 loots dificult, bandits are lame, and zombies are garbage.
