It's basically a running simulator with snipers... and a really, really bad game engine.  If you somehow think the Arma game engine is good, or even the least bit smooth, you might not get a headache trying to play this.
However, horrible terrible attrocious... did I say horrible?  Anyway, the game engine aside it is actually an awesome game to play.
You'll start out alone, somewhere near the coast about 2 clicks from a town.  You'll follow the road till you get to some houses, you'll start rooting through the houses and before you know it you're toting some meelee weapon, possibly a rifle without a magazine (because you'll NEVER find a rifle WITH a magazine.  I guess zombies run around unloading every weapon and eating the magazines.)
You'll find a really awesome rare gun, then you'll see a msg on your screen "No message received for xx seconds".  The server reset about 30 seconds ago, and that awesome thing you just found... it's gone.
So you reconnect and keep rooting.  You run - for an hour - to the next town.  You find some tactical bacon.  That's bacon in a can.  You'll open it with a can opener if you're lucky to find one, otherwise you'll jab it with your kitchen knife or some other random sharp object to open it.  You'll eat it, you'll be happy.
Then your screen will go black and it will say "YOU ARE DEAD".
Was the bacon bad?   Did your arm hurt so bad from that last zombie attack it killed you?  Or did you get sniped from 600 meters away by jim-bob?  You never even heard a shot...  There's no global chat, so you'll just never know.
You'll start out alone, somewhere near the coast, about 2 clicks away from the nearest town.  You'll go the -opposite- way, get all that cool gear back again, and as you're running from 3 zombies you'll see a msg on your screen that says, "No message recieved for xx seconds".  The server just reset as you were being chased by zombies - and guess what - those zombies ate your face while you were in connection limbo.
You'll start out alone, somewhere near the coast, about 2 clicks away from the nearest town.  You'll hit esc, click "Exit", and about 3 hours later you'll do all of this all over again.  And again.  And again.  And....again.
Did I mention the game engine is terrible?
If you haven't baught this yet, don't bother...  no amount of coolness can make up for this terrible game engine.  Don't get me wrong... I play it, I like it, it IS fun.  But with H1Z1 right around the corner, being built with a legitament game engine....  Don't waste your money on this.

Now, I'm assuming you want an honest opinion - no fanboys trying to kiss the♥♥♥♥♥of 'Rocket-senpai', but no random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ saying 'I didn't read that the game will have major problems in its alpha state because I'm a dumb-dumb'. So I will take this through in steps. Also, to make it a fair review, I will only be comparing this game to other 'zombie' games.
Engine:
It runs on a modified ARMA 3 engine, a game which I had a very large amount of issues with, but still found myself able to enjoy it to an extent. This game definately smoothens some of the ♥♥♥♥♥ier aspects of the engine, which was essential to keep the core gameplay solid. Many of you may be familiar with the DayZ mod, which ran on the ARMA 2 engine, and - while I adore ARMA 2 - the engine was trash. So gameplay is significantly improved in terms of accessability and ease of use. This is especially good for people new to ARMA or the engines.
Connection: My internet is close to being a pile of trash that even a hobo wouldn't want to touch, so my connectivity is poorer than an Ethiopian child. However, I am aware of people with good internet experiencing problems with servers not appearing and semi-frequent lag spikes, so be warned - you could be in for a bumpy ride.
Actual Gameplay: This can be quite different depending on the kind of person playing the game - people who decide to sit in a house with a lamp to live off of 3 cans of beans and a bottle of water won't find adventure, whereas people who go out looking for it probably won't find it either. However, there are times that make you feel like you actually achieved something, or that you're a badass, or that you should have actually got a job as a torturer. There will also be moments that make you scream curses at the game, but this is to be expected of most 'action' games - I definitely use that word LIGHTLY - but I can honestly say I have felt more awesome on this game than on plenty others that offer the same experience. For example, I single handedly defeated 3 bandits in an all-out melee combat brawl using nothing but my wits and a really underpowered crowbar. Freeman would have been proud... As you are probably aware, there aren't any real objectives to this game, however, staying alive by finding food, weapons and medical supplies seems to be a popular thing. Nearly every building in the game is enterable, which is a vast improvement from the mod. This allows the player to enter towns that actually feel abandoned and deserted expect for the charming zombie nature. Finding supplies can be hard unless you really know where to look, but I should think that you'll not experience too much hassle. However, if a server restarts every 4 hours, and you join 3 hours in, loot will be incredibly scarce in the areas near the coast. This is because the player always spawns at or near the coast (I am unsure when or even if this will change) and so the nearest town is usually the desired looting spot. You also now have to take in consideration fatigue, injuries and ammunition conservation, not to mention hunger, thirst and illness. This all sounds well thought out, but the execution can appear poor, as glitches result in injuries and sometimes death, ammo can randomly appear and dissapear, hunger can be INCREDIBLY hard to get rid of, especially due to its frequency. The developers should have perhaps implemented this after some of the other bugs were tested and rid of.
Scavenging: This is one of the core elements of the game, and I needed to break off the chunk of text that I had just written. If you can enter a building, there is a chance that some random loot will spawn in there. However, it is not as simple as finding a bazooka in the toilet, as there are loot tables for every building (medical, residential, military etc.) that consist of different items that have a percentage of spawning in. This allows for replayability, but can mean that if you want to find one particular item, it can be infuriating if it doesn't spawn. There is also an element of 'inventory tetris',
meaning that different items can take up a greater amount of slots than others. This can sometimes mean that you have to decide which takes priority - medicine, ammo or food. Other times it just makes you♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥that you can't carry 50 cans of bacon. Different backpacks and clothing can store different amounts of items, but all of this does have an effect on how quickly you get fatigued, so be smart (and don't talk to strangers. No, seriously, don't).
Stranger Danger: Among the internet are many *ahem* interesting people, who's goals can vary. However when it comes to DayZ, all that can go out the window, and bronies can become merciless killing machines, much to my heart's dissmay, and nazis can become your new best friend. If you're like me and have tried to approach a player, don't expect a warm welcome. However, if you need to know more, there are plenty of well-detailed guides to help spot who gives free candy, and who gives free bullets. To the face.
Zombies: Ah, yes, the most desirable feature right? Wrong. The zombies currently are a mess. Its as if they tried to make a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chimp copy Shakespeare, and they used the script as code for the zombie AI. And the script was literally just smeared in♥♥♥♥♥♥ Clipping through walls, nearly invulnerable to melee weapons and terrible navigation, they are seriously buggy. Nothing more to say.
Clothes: So many clothes! Yay! That's what we want in the next update, to dress like a ♥♥♥♥ing hipster! How merry!
Clothes (serious): You can look dapper.
Melee Combat: Hah. The weapons are so underpowered that the best choice is to run from the zombies - honestly. Aiming your weapon is also very clunky, which adds to how terrible they are. And while all weapons have a condition, it isn't needed for the melee weapons because of how ineffective they are. This will hopefully be fixed in a future update.
Running Simulator: As there are not any vehicles currently implented in the game, the player is forced to run everywhere - this can be quite a few kilometers if you are going to meet a friend. Couple this with the stamina and fatigue system, and you can see why people like me ♥♥♥♥♥ about the much needed vehicles.
Updates: This is gonna upset people, I just know it. Firstly, the updates are not as frequent as I think they should be for a game backed by so many customers. I understand that it can be very difficult to add new content, and that delays should be expected, but to wait a couple of months for some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ update introducing a broken mechanic and some new shoes? That brings me to my second point - the content of the updates. FrankieOnPCIn1080p is a filthy asslicking fibber. The amount of (or lack of) content that is currently in the game is appaling. Now, some may argue that there are quite a lot of things in the game at the moment, but I beg to differ. So many of the things currently in the game are useless! It makes it quite pointless having them in.
Graphics: They are suprisingly nice, as long as you don't look at the textures too closely, with delightful lighting effects and a realistic skybox.
Conclusion: If I were you I would take a long, hard look at the bit that says 'YOU ARE PREPARED TO HANDLE ISSUES AND PROBLEMS'. Then look at it again. And one last time, because I can tell you this game has an extremely large amount of flawes. However, it can still be fun if you look past them, despite some of them being quite game-breaking. The reason I am saying I DON'T reccommend the game is that I have lost a lot of hope in the game's current state. Please don't base your opinion solely on this review, or on a youtube video of Frankie-the-liar, because it is really up to you to decide if you like it or not. Also, the asking price of an EARLY ACCESS game is very steep, which should have driven away a lot of customers. This is one review, so please look at some other to make up your mind. Thanks!

The rust I first bought  (legacy/ old version) was amazing. It had it's bugs and hackers, but the game worked, and I spent countless hours playing it, well over 100. Ever since the newer version had arrived, I almost immediately stopped playing. I'd always find myself playing legacy because I was familiar with it, and it was very addicting. the legacy version now is full of cheaters, and makes the game nearly impossible to play without hacking it be juself. I'm hopeful that the newer edition of rust will be just as playable and fun as the version before it. I'd give it another year or two before I attempt to play again.
I wouldn't reccomend buying rust in this current stat. However given it was still in legacy, I would most definitely reccomend the purchase, because it was truly addicting and very fun.
Would I reccomend Rust legacy? Hell yeah! (if they still kept it up to date/ no cheating. it's not up to date, and it's full of them.)
Would i reccomend Rust today? No, it's currently "playable" to say the least. The graphics are great, the frame rate isn't. The core gameplay seems buggy still, yet progressively getting better. I definitely believe rust can achieve what it had done before, but facepunch has some work todo before I'd reccomend someone handing them their money.
A few suggestions from an absolute fan of rust legacy, (and hopefully your newer version).
1. More/stronger wildlife needs to happen.
2. 360/Xbone controller support. [That's a major plus in my book. Pinnacle has one for legacy, but the newer version is broken.]
3. optimization, it's gotten better since you first released the newer version, but it still has some way to go.
4. Rad towns, I haven't seen any, but i want to. they are kind've what kept people in a certain area. Made going into that
area a risk.
5. [just a general thought] What made rust so fun to begin with, was weighing out the pros and cons of doing certain tasks. should I stay warm by my puny fire and shelter tonight, or should I go for that air drop? Should I open the door and kill this ♥♥♥♥♥♥, or is he hiding something? This is what your game was arguably built around, and you should find ways to keep that in. Risk taking should be rewarding, and challenging, that is what I loved about rust.
Hope this helped someone's opinion, and if facepunch took a read, then thanks for listening to your customers!
UPDATE:
The game has much improved since I first wrote this review. I was skeptical that the team could make me enjoy the new rust as much as I had the original, but they've been diligently working the past year or so to prove me wrong.
The game is still a bit buggy, but It's still in early access. Aside from some weird lighting with the campfires in your own shelter, and server latency, the game is coming along perfectly.
I would now recommend the new rust to anyone borderline buying it, it is worth your money, and the devs do listen to your complaints. This is the only review I've ever re-written, and it deserved it.

Seems like the reviews tell pretty much all there is to tell, so I'll just share a recipe for a Strawberry Banana smoothie:
Ingredients:
-1 Banana
-4 to 8 plump Strawberries
-4 to 6 Ice Cubes
-1 Spoonful of Greek Yogurt (Whatever kind of yogurt works, Greek is just my preferred choice.)
-2/3 Cup of Milk
-1/4 Cub of Water
-1 squirt of Lemon Juice
Instructions:
Put the banana in the blender, preferrably in slices. Proceed to place the strawberries in after that. Next, Chuck the spoonful of yogurt into the blender (minus the spoon, of course). Then, carefully place the ice cubes in on top of the bananas, strawberries, and yogurt. Pour the milk, water, then lemon juice into the blender. Start blending on a low setting to crush the ice, then gradully increase speed until you are content with the smoothness of the drink. Pour into a glass and enjoy!

So many negative reviews for this game, which I don't understand.
Yes it's been in Alpha for 4 years, however not with the same Devs!!
Roughly 2 yrs ago, it was picked up by Dean Hall and his crew, who started fresh, and they're slow at releasing updates.
However when they do, you know it was worth the wait, after .62 update became stable just a matter of days ago, the game has become beautiful, and I love the new effects.
The gun play is amazing, harder than most games, actually takes some skill, it's a huge map, and there is a lot of places to loot.
However finding a car and driving to where you want to go is a good option, cars have improved and the game mechanics have too.
If you like a good variety of weapons, clothes and scenery. And a game that can be more of a challenge, then try it out, I would say wait for a sale, just not sure I've ever seen it on sale.
I have played for over 800 hours and would say I got my monies worth, and I will keep playing as I love this game.
Devs have made great improvements as of late. No, it is still not a 100% bug free optimized game but I enjoy it much more at this stage of development. Kudos to you dev team!

As a solo player, I've spent many hours playing Rust Legacy, and it was quite fun.
My review is focused on solo gameplay, and I'll just explain why the new Rust ruined lonewolf fun.
1. Farming, it's now 75% of a solo player gameplay, chopping trees all day isn't fun.
2. It is still a weapon race game, survival is just an excuse to fight with big guns, but in Legacy you could easily find good weapons, farm zombies and fight against big teams, now you need hours and hours of barrel farm to find this good stuff, considering you die and retry a lot because you are chased by others while farming, so you have to secure any good thing to your house before going back farming more barrels.
3. Communication : the game has a good ingame voice communication, but players tend to use teamspeak so they can easily approch your house without you knowing it. How unfair is that.
4. Hiding you base, in Legacy playing solo had this only one advantage, the capability of hiding a small 2x1 or 2x2 base in the mountains which was the only place where you could rest and craft new weapons before going back to the fight.
Now it is impossible for a solo player to hide, they will find you, rip your base and all your hours of investement in this game. Because you have no weapons, you are weak.
5. Moreover, now you can help a mate to revive, so if you killed one, he will just ask for help to his friends, and repeat until they finally catch and kill you... twice, ez pz.

I would absolutely recommend this game. I've been playing since early in the mod days.
I bought the standalone as soon as it was released and since that point I've seen substantial improvement.
The standalone started out SUPER buggy, but now it is only a little buggy and the framerate is much improved. the development team has added many weapons and items to spice the game up.
Like in the show The Walking Dead, it turns out that the biggest threat in the zombie apocalypse is not zombies- it is hunger, and other people. you have to decide weather to kill a stranger on sight (to get what little food he is carrying) or risk communicating to potentially open trade. Also since you have only limited space on your person and there are so many weapons and ammo, the game forces you to make hard decisions on whether to keep ammo for the gun you really want, or have extra ammo for the crappy weapon you are carrying now.
I met one of my college buddies I havent seen in a long time (in real life) in a barn north of one of the big cities in the game. He set up a camp fire, gave me an extra jacket, and cooked me a boar steak.
This game really shines when playing with your friends. Come for the open world MMO survival horror, stay for the whacky encounters that make the community in this game one of the best I've experienced.

I bought DayZ on day 1 and have played quite a bit for the last year. While it is fun at times, it is certainly not complete at this paint...and it remains to be seen whether the dev team can deliver on the final product one it hits release.
For a long time, I was a big proponent of the game often shooting down naysayers among my friends and on the forums. However, lately I feel that the dev team may be straying from the goal of having a fun and emersive game.
Of course, it is still in alpha with a large part of the road map still unfulfilled. I do not regret making the purchase as I knew that I was buying into an early release.
However, if anyone were to ask me if they should purchase the game, I would tell them to at least wait until the project reaches the beta stage...and if they can wait longer, wait until release. I don't doubt that the game will be be good onc eit has been released (after all, they have the DayZ mod to use as a model...and it was successful), but the question remains as to how good the release will be. Will it be well-optimised or a disappointment? Will Bohemia work hard to quash bugs and prevent hacking, or will they let things slide?

I'd only recommend this game to the most patient of players. The updates come out extremely slow, especially for a game that has such success as far as sales are concerned on Early Access Alpha games. There is a major lack of content in the game, and therefor very little for the player do except to focus on constant PvP. The game also utlizes a ton of your PC's resources, so better ensure you have a high-end PC to get good frames and make it worthwhile for you to play.
Other than the above, you get quite a rush from the PvP aspect of the game. Looting is also quite nice to do, but at current the persistent servers seem to have an issue with the loot spawning mechanic. The zombies are few and far between (quite ez killz really) even though they should be the main focul point in any 'zombie apocolypse survival game' in my opinion. There is zero base building thus far (for those whom come from Arma 2), you will have to be satisfied with tents for now. There is more weapons and clothing than anything else in this game, which is probably only put there to entertain us while they slowly work on the other more important things (such as vehicles). The game engine is also not optimized yet even though they claim to have done so in a past update.
There is a great future for this game, but at current it does not even fit the price tag it comes with. Maybe we'll see the Beta version in the next few years, but until then I'd rather stick to Arma 3. At the end of the day it's just a matter of to each their own. Don't hate my review. Kthnxbye!
